title: ASAP7 PDN-0179: channel repair fails, no power grid ever committed
description:
ASAP7 pdngen aborts in build_grids with PDN-0179 ("Unable to repair all channels"), 27 channels,
so no power grid is ever committed to the ODB (see bead gyx for the measurement + sky130 positive
control). Two separable pieces of work:

(A) IMMEDIATE, LOW RISK: fix our local pdn.tcl warn-and-continue patch (present in BOTH the
    2.4.13 and 3.0.14 trees) so it still commits whatever was built:
        pdn::check_setup
        if {[catch {pdn::build_grids 1} e]} { puts "BUILD_ERR: $e" }
        if {[catch {pdn::write_to_db 1 ""} e]} { puts "WRITE_ERR: $e" }
        pdn::reset_shapes
    Verified on the CPU block: 0 -> 16071 VDD / 17151 VSS shapes. Without this, the flow's
    "benign PDN-0179" message means "PDN silently absent".

(B) ROOT CAUSE, OPEN: why channel repair fails. 27 channels, all on M1, in the macro-FREE
    regions x 82.188..124.956 and y 104.193..123.417 (macros: x 6.37..72.16, y 5..94; core
    5.022,5.13 - 124.956,124.74). Ruled out: PDN halo (identical channels at 10/2/0), macro PG
    pin case in PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS, M3-as-horizontal (rails then never connect), M4-as-
    horizontal at legal width 0.12. ASAP7 layer directions M1 V / M2 H / M3 V / M4 H / M5 V,
    with std-cell rails on M1 running horizontally (non-preferred direction) -- that mismatch is
    the most likely lead and has NOT been tested yet (e.g. rails on M2, or a followpin width /
    row-alignment issue).

Until (B) closes, every ASAP7 routing/DRC number is produced with no PDN on the tracks and is
optimistic; IR drop stays unavailable. Repro harness: /nobackup/asap7_debug/gyx_pdn/variant.sh
notes:
2026-09-12 RESOLVED IN A HARNESS — grid topology was wrong; ORFS has the right one; IR drop now runs.

PDN-0179 was never a macro/channel-geometry problem. The old grid connected the M1 followpin
rails STRAIGHT TO M5 (a four-layer stack) and used M2 only as a sparse 4.5 um-pitch strap running
PARALLEL to those rails. ASAP7 rails run horizontally on M1 (its non-preferred direction), so
most rails had nothing reachable above them and channel repair could not fix it.

FIX (ported from ORFS flow/platforms/asap7/openRoad/pdn/BLOCKS_grid_strategy.tcl): followpins on
BOTH M1 and M2 (0.018 um wide, 0.54 um pitch = one per row), then M2->M5->M6; macro grid connects
M4<->M5 because our SRAM PG pins are on M4 (ORFS's own ElementGrid only needs M5<->M6).

MEASURED, CPU block, RUN_2026-09-10_05-13-18 step-18 ODB:
                              old grid        ORFS-style grid
  remaining channels          27              0
  PG shapes committed         0               27999 VDD / 27213 VSS
  check_power_grid            PSM-0069 both   PASS both
  unconnected shapes/insts    964 / 357       0 / 0
  -> "[INFO PSM-0040] All shapes on net VDD are connected."

IR DROP (this bead's acceptance criterion) then needed one more fix: ASAP7 ships NO via
resistances, so analyze_power_grid aborted with PSM-0021 "Resistance map contains invalid values"
even with clean connectivity. The 3.0.14 config key is VIAS_R (VIAS_RC is the old, removed name);
ORFS values from flow/platforms/asap7/setRC.tcl. With that:
  VDD: worst 1.28e-03 V, 0.18 %   |   VSS: worst 1.31e-03 V, 0.19 %

LANDED: pnr/asap7/pdn_asap7_orfs.tcl + per-design pdn_orfs.tcl wrappers + PDN_CFG, VIAS_R and
RUN_IRDROP_REPORT=true in pnr/asap7/{cpu,gpu}/config_3014.json. The wrapper was re-run through the
harness and reproduces the numbers above exactly.

STILL OPEN BEFORE THIS CAN CLOSE:
 1. No full flow run yet. The IR number above came from a standalone harness on a FLOORPLAN-STAGE
    ODB (step 18) combined with the final run's SPEF -- the two do not correspond to the same
    design state, so it is indicative only, not a sign-off figure.
 2. Routing has never been attempted with an actual grid on the tracks; expect it to be harder
    than every previous ASAP7 route (bead ocm's numbers were all PDN-free).
 3. SoC configs (config.json / config_multiclock.json) still point at the old pnr/asap7/soc/pdn.tcl,
    which has the same M1->M5 defect. Not changed here to keep run 14 / run 23 byte-reproducible.
Harness: /nobackup/asap7_debug/gyx_pdn/variant.sh ; IR replay: /nobackup/asap7_debug/gyx_pdn/ir/
2026-09-12 FLOW BLOCKER FOUND WHILE VALIDATING THE PDN FIX (pre-existing, not caused by it):
ASAP7 SIMPLE has no antenna diode. The PDK config sets
  DIODE_CELL     "DECAPx1_ASAP7_75t_R"
  DIODE_CELL_PIN ""
(/home/neuromorphic/pdk/asap7/libs.tech/openlane/asap7sc7p5t_SIMPLE/config.tcl:69-70) and DECAPx1
is a decap whose only pins are VDD/VSS. LibreLane 3.0.14 joins the pair into
'DECAPx1_ASAP7_75t_R/', so odbpy/diodes.py:248 calls findITerm('') -> None and dies with
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'connect'
That killed RUN_2026-09-12_10-27-19 at step 42 (odb-diodesonports), 33 min in.

Earlier 3.0.14 runs never hit it because they were launched with a narrower step set -- their
resolved.json carries the same DIODE_ON_PORTS='in' and RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION=true, but
their step lists contain no diode or antenna steps at all. So this is a latent PDK/config bug that
only surfaces on a full default-flow run.

FIX: DIODE_ON_PORTS='none' + RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION=false in both config_3014.json. Neither
step can ever succeed on this PDK -- there is no cell to insert.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING FROM THE SAME RUN: GeneratePDN emitted 110x
  [PDN-0110] No via inserted between M4 and M5 ... on VDD
i.e. a minority of macro-pin vias still fail to drop even though check_power_grid PASSes and
PSM-0040 reports all shapes connected. Not fatal, but it means macro PG pin coverage is partial;
worth a look when the SoC is re-closed.
2026-09-12 PDN FIX NOW VALIDATED ON ALL THREE DESIGNS (standalone harness, no run dirs touched):
  CPU (RUN_2026-09-10_05-13-18 step-18 ODB): 0 channels, 27999/27213 shapes, PASS, 0 unconnected
  GPU (RUN_2026-09-10_10-01-10 step-18 ODB): 0 channels, 300670/301235 shapes, PASS, 0 unconnected
  SoC (RUN_2026-08-09_14-36-16 step-15 ODB): 0 channels, 372594/373316 shapes, PASS, 0 unconnected
and in-flow on the CPU (RUN_2026-09-12_10-27-19 step 21): 0 channels, no PDN-0179, empty
grid-error reports, PSM-0040 "All shapes connected" on both nets.

PDN-0110 QUANTIFIED (the "No via inserted between M4 and M5" warnings: 110 on CPU, 439 on GPU).
Counting actual vias in the in-flow CPU ODB by type and macro overlap:
  VDD: VIA45 7895 total, 2090 of them over macros; via5_6 1940 total, 800 over macros
  VSS: VIA45 7766 total, 2180 over macros;        via5_6 1940 total, 800 over macros
So ~2090/2180 M4->M5 vias DO land on the macro PG pins and ~110 attempts fail -- roughly a 5%
miss, not a coverage hole. Consistent with check_power_grid passing. Not worth chasing unless IR
under the macros later looks wrong.
2026-09-12 TRAP: `--last-run --from OpenROAD.GeneratePDN` DOES NOT rewind the design state.
LibreLane feeds the resumed step whatever state the run last reached, not the state that step
originally consumed. Verified from 47-openroad-generatepdn/state_in.json:

  odb : .../42-openroad-resizertimingpostgrt/rv32i_cpu_top.odb

i.e. pdngen was asked to build a grid inside a PLACED + globally-routed + resized database
instead of the post-tapendcap floorplan. That blows past 12 GB and gets OOM-killed at the
GeneratePDN step -- twice (runs at 14:01 and 14:53), each time looking like "the PDN step is a
memory hog", which it is not: the same config builds in ~1 min at low memory in the standalone
harness, and in-flow at step 21 of a fresh run.

Rule: only resume from a step whose INPUT state is still the correct one (e.g. --from
OpenROAD.DetailedRouting right after DRT died). To change anything upstream of routing -- the PDN
config included -- start a fresh run. `--from` is a restart point, not a rewind.

Corollary for host safety: run flows under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=<cap>` with the
cap BELOW what would trigger systemd-oomd. At 14:00:39 oomd killed 233 processes in the terminal
vte scope -- taking the Claude session with it -- before the flow's own cgroup limit was reached.
A cgroup cap that bites first turns a machine-wide event into a contained one.
2026-09-12 ROUTING WITH A REAL PDN IS HOST-BLOCKED. Four attempts on the CPU block, all killed
inside DRT iteration 0 of 12:

  PDN density            util/threads  cap     reached   violations  peak
  ORFS 2.16/4.32         50/8          12 GiB  90% iter0  122121     13.4 GB
  ORFS 2.16/4.32         50/4          14 GiB  90% iter0  122121     13.4 GB
  3x sparse 6.48/12.96   50/4          12 GiB  ~75% iter0  83207     11.2 GB
  3x sparse 6.48/12.96   45/2          13 GiB  80% iter0  112764     12.0 GB

The last one I stopped deliberately at 17:37: host was down to 1 GB free with 11 iterations still
to go, and that is the state in which systemd-oomd killed the terminal scope (and the session)
earlier in the day. Surviving iteration 0 would not have changed the outcome.

Reference point: the PDN-FREE run peaked 12.4 GB and DID converge, to 1991 DRC. So a real grid
costs ~20-30% more violations and this 15.9 GB host has no headroom for it.

LEVERS MEASURED AND REJECTED (do not retry blindly):
 * Sparser straps: 3 densities measured (IR 0.18 / 0.52 / 1.37 %). Violation counts barely moved.
   Congestion comes from the M2 FOLLOWPINS -- one M2 track per standard-cell row -- not the M5/M6
   mesh. Sparser straps buy IR margin, not routing headroom.
 * Lower utilization: FP_CORE_UTIL 50->45 gave an IDENTICAL violation count (44103 at the same
   checkpoint) and MORE memory, because a larger die means more area to hold state for. Backfired.
 * Fewer DRT threads: 8->4->2 moved the peak only marginally. Memory is dominated by violation
   markers, not per-worker state.
 * Avoiding M2: rails M1 -> M3 direct leaves all 222 rails unconnected (pdngen will not stack
   M1->M3 through M2). M1->M2 followpins are the only legal way up; the M2 cost is structural.

NEEDS: a host with >=32 GB, same gate already recorded for the Sky130 GPU stages. Everything about
the PDN fix itself is verified without routing -- grid builds and check_power_grid PASSes on CPU,
GPU and SoC, and IR drop runs end-to-end. What stays unverified is whether this design still closes
DRC with the grid on the tracks; given 1991 DRC PDN-free, expect it to need work.
Correction: the util-45 / 2-thread attempt's peak was 12846 MB (12.8 GB), from DRT's own final memory print, not the 12.0 GB I first recorded off the cgroup gauge. Does not change the conclusion -- it was still inside iteration 0 of 12 with the host at 1 GB free.
close_reason: Resolved (2026-09-12/13, PR #171 merged). Root cause of PDN-0179 was the grid topology: M1 rails wired straight to M5 with M2 as a parallel sparse strap. pnr/asap7/pdn_asap7_orfs.tcl (ORFS reference: followpins on M1 AND M2, then M2->M5->M6) builds with 0 remaining channels and check_power_grid PASS on CPU (27999/27213 shapes, confirmed in-flow at step 21), GPU (300670/301235) and SoC (372594/373316). Both LibreLane trees' pdn.tcl patches now commit whatever build_grids produced instead of silently committing nothing. The ONLY remaining item -- routing a design with the real grid on the tracks -- is host-gated and tracked separately on claude_verilog_test-2kn (>=32 GB host).

title: librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier lacks OR_PATH_PREFIX, silently uses known-bad edf00dff OpenROAD
description: pnr/Makefile:900-918 sets a target-specific OR_PATH_PREFIX (PATH prepended with the pinned ASAP7 26Q2 OpenROAD shim) for a fixed list of targets: librelane-asap7, librelane-asap7-gpu, librelane-asap7-soc, librelane-asap7-soc-synth, librelane-asap7-soc-synth-only, librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock, macro-views-asap7, librelane-asap7-coalescer-rtl/hls, librelane-asap7-hazard-rtl/hls, librelane-asap7-valu-rtl/hls/hls-comb. librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier (pnr/Makefile:1490-1491, used by beads w3a/rvb/0ah/ydw's entire ASAP7 SoC multiclock hierarchical campaign) is NOT in that list, so OR_PATH_PREFIX defaults to empty (line 181) for it -- PATH is never prepended with the shim, and nix-shell's own bundled OpenROAD is used instead. That bundled binary is edf00dff99f6c40d67a30c0e22a8191c5d2ed9d6 -- the exact 'known-bad build' that check-asap7-openroad (line 924) exists to reject ('It cannot grant pin access on ASAP7 -- see bead ocm', 'A silent fallback to LibreLane's own OpenROAD would silently restore the zero-wire behaviour, which is exactly the failure mode bead xy6 exists to prevent'). check-asap7-openroad IS a prerequisite of librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier and correctly verifies that ASAP7_OPENROAD_BIN itself points to a valid 26Q2 binary -- but it only validates the variable's value, not that the flow's actual openroad invocation (bare 'openroad' inside nix-shell, no PATH override) resolves to it. The preflight passes while the flow silently uses the wrong tool -- the exact failure mode it was written to prevent, just via a different code path than the one it checks. Discovered 2026-09-17 while investigating bead 0ah: comparing RUN_2026-09-16_19-19-45 (launched by a hand-rolled script that explicitly set PATH to the 26Q2 shim, bypassing this Makefile target) against RUN_2026-09-17_06-25-54 (soc-ydw, launched via make librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier) shows corroborating evidence of two different OpenROAD builds: unannotated-driver counts 1639 (26Q2 run) vs 4663 (edf00dff run) on structurally similar netlists; the RSZ repair-progress table has Area/StTNS/EnTNS columns on the 26Q2 run and lacks them (single TNS column, no Area) on the edf00dff run; and clock_tree_synthesis's own help text differs between the two binaries (26Q2 adds -macro_clustering_size/-macro_clustering_max_diameter and a -no_obstruction_aware complement that edf00dff lacks). memory/pd/run_state.md's own header for the original w3a campaign (attempt 4, RUN_2026-09-16_01-13-02, the bead 0ah baseline) explicitly documents 'bundled OpenROAD edf00dff ... (OR_PATH_PREFIX=)' -- confirming the ENTIRE w3a/rvb/0ah original diagnosis, and soc-ydw's run, all ran on the known-bad edf00dff build via this Makefile gap, while the one run that appeared to fix bead 0ah's hold-skew problem (RUN_2026-09-16_19-19-45) happened to use 26Q2 only because it bypassed the buggy Makefile target with a hand-written script.
design: One-line fix (NOT applied -- coordinator instructed not to edit the Makefile yet): add librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier to the target-specific OR_PATH_PREFIX assignment at pnr/Makefile ~line 918, i.e. add it to the target list on the line immediately above 'OR_PATH_PREFIX := export PATH=$(ASAP7_OR_SHIM_DIR):...'. Also audit for any other librelane-asap7-*-hier or similarly-named targets that might have the same oversight (this list is manually maintained per-target, not derived from a pattern match, so any newly-added ASAP7 target must be added here by hand or it silently falls back to the bundled build).
acceptance_criteria: librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier (and any other affected targets found in the audit) added to the OR_PATH_PREFIX target list. Re-verify with a fresh run that or_metrics_out.json / annotation-check reports match the ~1600-unannotated / Area+StTNS+EnTNS-table signature of a genuine 26Q2 run, not the ~4600-unannotated / no-Area-column edf00dff signature. Bead 0ah's actual root cause (26Q2 vs edf00dff TritonCTS macro-clustering behaviour, not any config key) should be re-validated on a properly-pinned 26Q2 run before any further conclusions are drawn.
notes: Fix committed eb7f4be (pushed to feat/ydw-sram-registered-read): added librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier to the OR_PATH_PREFIX target list (pnr/Makefile ~911-918) and hardened check-asap7-openroad with a fail-loud 'command -v openroad' resolution check under the caller's OR_PATH_PREFIX. Audit of all other check-asap7-openroad-dependent ASAP7 targets found no further gaps. Verified via 'make -n' that the recipe now carries the shim PATH export. Launched re-run soc-ydw2 (systemd-run --user --scope --unit=soc-ydw2, run dir pnr/asap7/soc/runs/RUN_2026-09-17_09-01-42, log /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/soc_ydw2.log) with the fixed Makefile target, same config_multiclock_hier_rsz7_0ah.json, --to OpenROAD.STAMidPNR-3. CONFIRMED at Floorplan/PDN stage (~25 min in): PID 1073282's /proc/PID/exe resolves to /nix/store/hgqrwa4687mf7n0y2x6lcgx1kj42sfga-openroad-26Q2/bin/.openroad-wrapped -- the pinned 26Q2 binary, not the bundled edf00dff. Fix verified working on a live run.
close_reason: Fixed in commit eb7f4be: librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock-hier added to the OR_PATH_PREFIX target list; check-asap7-openroad hardened with a fail-loud PATH-resolution check. Verified on live re-run soc-ydw2 (RUN_2026-09-17_09-01-42) -- running openroad process (PID 1073282) confirmed via /proc/PID/exe to be the pinned 26Q2 binary, not edf00dff.

title: LibreLane 2.4.13 post-GRT STA (STAMidPNR-3) runs on unannotated (zero-wire) parasitics; all ASAP7 post-GRT timing/power figures suspect
description:
Found 2026-09-16 under w3a.
- Evidence: RUN_2026-09-16_02-45-38 (w3a-rsz-5) 01-openroad-stamidpnr-3 log reports 'Found 213464 unannotated drivers'.
- Mechanism: librelane/scripts/openroad/sta/corner.tcl:38 calls 'estimate_parasitics -global_routing' after loading the ODB. As proven under je8 (bead je8, bd memory openroad-grt-parasitics-need-insession-route), OpenROAD edf00dff does not recover GRT parasitics from a saved ODB (read_guides is also unusable, GRT-0008). Only an in-session global_route annotates. rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl:32 uses the same call, so ResizerTimingPostGRT may also optimize against zero-wire or partial parasitics; unverified.
- Impact: every LibreLane 2.4.13 ASAP7 STAMidPNR-3 'post-GRT' setup/hold/power figure may be zero-wire and optimistic. That includes run 23's accepted post-GRT sign-off numbers (docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md), the 86a in-flow power figures, and the run-5 (09-13) post-GRT checkpoint. Placement-stage STAMidPNR steps use estimate_parasitics -placement and are unaffected.
- Fix options:
  (a) a backward-compatible LibreLane patch (same process as bpp): run global_route in-session before estimate_parasitics -global_routing in corner.tcl and rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl, gated by a variable, memory ~5.4 GB on the SoC;
  (b) at minimum, an annotation gate that fails loudly when unannotated drivers exceed a threshold.
- Then re-measure w3a/86a and re-validate run 23's post-GRT claims.
notes:
2026-09-16 IN PROGRESS. Developing in /nobackup/librelane-bpp (same copy as bead bpp, kept in
sync with the shared tree). Coordinator confirmed: applying to the shared tree needs sign-off
after w3a-rsz-6 ends; not touching the shared tree yet.

Implementation:
1. Opt-in in-session GRT re-route: sta/corner.tcl's `if { [grt::have_routes] }` branch now
   sources common/grt.tcl (the SAME script GlobalRouting itself uses -- routing layers, layer
   adjustments, GRT_* settings, global_route call) when STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT=1, BEFORE
   `estimate_parasitics -global_routing`. Default false, byte-identical to upstream when unset.
   rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl was NOT similarly gated: it ALREADY sources common/grt.tcl
   unconditionally today ("Temporarily always enabled" comment, upstream OpenROAD issue #5590
   workaround) -- gating that behind a default-false variable would be a REGRESSION (silently
   removing an existing always-on re-route), so it stays unconditional. The variable is still
   declared (byte-identical text) on OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostGRT for interface consistency,
   but that script does not consult it.
2. Always-on annotation gate: new `ol_check_postgrt_parasitic_annotation` proc in common/io.tcl,
   called from BOTH corner.tcl (inside the -global_routing branch only, per the requirement that
   -placement-based STA stay unaffected) and rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl (unconditionally, right
   after its existing estimate_parasitics -global_routing). Captures
   `report_parasitic_annotation -report_unannotated`'s output via Tcl's `> file` redirect
   (report_parasitic_annotation's own body confirms it supports the generic OpenSTA
   parse_redirect_args idiom), regexes out "Found N unannotated drivers.", computes a percentage
   against `[llength [get_cells -hierarchical *]]` (a cheap PROXY for "total drivers" -- multi-
   output cells make this approximate, not exact; documented inline). Prints a loud
   `[WARNING]` naming STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT when the percentage exceeds
   STA_POSTGRT_UNANNOTATED_PCT_MAX (env-read directly, default 1.0%; not a declared Variable,
   since it is a secondary tuning knob for an always-on gate rather than the primary behaviour
   switch), or exits 1 if STA_POSTGRT_UNANNOTATED_IS_ERROR=1.
3. Variable STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT declared byte-identically on THREE step classes:
   OpenROAD.STAMidPNR (the real consumer), OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostGRT (inert, see above), and
   MultiCornerSTA (inert -- STAPrePNR/STAPostPNR run corner.tcl through the standalone `sta`
   binary, never through `openroad`, so `namespace exists ::ord` is false and the whole
   grt::have_routes/-global_routing branch is unreachable there). All three declarations
   verified byte-identical via a Python AST-level check (required, or Flow.get_all_config_variables
   raises FlowException across the shared Classic flow).

Verified so far:
  - Python: import + get_all_config_variables() on all three classes -- STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT
    present, default False, byte-identical across all three.
  - valu_rtl (STAPrePNR, does not reach STAMidPNR/corner.tcl's openroad-binary path at all) with
    the variable unset: byte-identical to the pre-8f3 baseline (54634 inst / 4655.14614 um^2 /
    WS -54.29279270097747 ps).

IN PROGRESS: bpp-6 (unit bpp-6, MemoryMax=6G, detached), fresh full ASAP7 CPU-block run
(rv32i_cpu_top, 10 SRAM macros) --to OpenROAD.STAMidPNR-3 (the 4th STAMidPNR occurrence in
Classic's step list -- confirmed by counting `OpenROAD.STAMidPNR,` entries in classic.py: lines
70/75/77/85, so the post-GRT one is index 3, matching the bead's own RUN_2026-09-16_02-45-38
reference path exactly), STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT UNSET (expect the warning to fire). This is
the FIRST time this copy or any of this session's validation runs has been taken through
OpenROAD.GlobalRouting -- prior bpp validation stopped at CTS/ResizerTimingPostCTS. Will follow
with a SECOND run (bpp-7) with STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT=1 set, same target, for comparison.
2026-09-16 bpp-6 RESULT (unset) -- CONFIRMS THE BUG, decisively.

bpp-6 (fresh full ASAP7 CPU-block run, rv32i_cpu_top, --to OpenROAD.STAMidPNR-3, STA_POSTGRT_
INSESSION_GRT unset): `Flow complete` at 05:10:07 (~32 min CPU), no errors -- exactly reproduces
the reported problem at CPU-block scale:

  Annotation gate output (step 40-openroad-stamidpnr-3):
    Found 34272 unannotated drivers.
    [WARNING] bead 8f3: 34272/36290 drivers (~94.44%) are UNANNOTATED after
    estimate_parasitics -global_routing -- ... Set STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT=1 ...

  Resulting (optimistic, false-clean) post-GRT STA (final/metrics.json):
    timing__setup__wns = 0, timing__setup__tns = 0, timing__setup_vio__count = 0
    timing__hold__wns  = 0, timing__hold__tns  = 0, timing__hold_vio__count  = 0
  A design reporting ZERO violations anywhere with 94% of drivers carrying no wire delay at all
  is exactly the "optimistic sign-off" failure mode this bead exists to catch -- concretely
  illustrates the risk to run 23's accepted post-GRT numbers.

  Item 3 (rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl's own annotation state) -- step 39-openroad-resizertimingpostgrt:
    Found 619 unannotated drivers.
    [WARNING] bead 8f3: 619/36206 drivers (~1.71%) are UNANNOTATED ...
  619/36206 (1.71%) is MUCH closer to this project's established benign floor (the SRAM stub's
  own structural unannotated pins, consistently 24-620ish across many unrelated runs this
  session, e.g. bpp valu_rtl/CPU CTS-stage tables) than to STAMidPNR-3's 94.44% catastrophic
  failure. CONFIRMS the design decision: rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl's existing unconditional
  `source common/grt.tcl` (already there before this bead, an upstream-issue workaround) is
  keeping ITS resizer calls correctly annotated already -- it does NOT have bead 8f3's problem,
  and does not need the new opt-in re-route. (Note: 1.71% still crossed the 1% default gate
  threshold and printed a WARNING -- a conservative gate, not a sign this step is broken; worth
  knowing the "always benign" floor sits close to the default threshold, in case
  STA_POSTGRT_UNANNOTATED_PCT_MAX ever needs raising slightly to avoid noise on clean steps.)

title: Synlig frontend mis-synthesises inactive-lane result masking (gcd); audit every USE_SYNLIG:true config incl. CPU/GPU macros
description:
Found under bead gcd, 2026-09-15.
- Failure: LibreLane 2.4.13 with USE_SYNLIG:true synthesised the Bambu zero-register vector_alu (pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb) to a netlist that is NOT equivalent to the RTL. It leaks rs1_i of an inactive lane into result_o, where the spec says 0. This was proven by a SAT miter constrained to rst_n=1,start_i=1, then eval on the counterexample. The netlist was 1587 instances.
- Fix there: USE_SYNLIG:false plus an sv2v-preprocessed shim gives 47,791 instances, and the counterexample evaluates correctly.
- Exposure: configs with USE_SYNLIG:true are asap7 cpu/config.json + config_3014.json, gpu/config.json + config_3014.json (both macros sit inside the signed-off SoC), valu_rtl, valu_hls, coalescer_rtl/hls, hazard_rtl/hls, template, freepdk45, sky130/cpu, and librelane legacy. The SoC configs use sv2v and are not exposed.
- Open question: is this a general Synlig elaboration bug, or specific to a construct in Bambu's generated Verilog? Identify the minimal construct, then check the hand RTL (vector_alu.sv, CPU, GPU) for it. For any exposed block, run a constrained equivalence or gate-level check of its synthesised netlist vs RTL. Do not re-sign-off anything until the construct is known.
notes:
2026-09-15 (gcd resume, coordinator-directed follow-up):

LOCALISATION: the corrupted construct is ui_cond_expr_FU (vector_alu_synth.v:330-347,
'assign out1 = in1 != 0 ? in2 : in3;'), a Bambu/PANDA generic IP-library FU module
instantiated per-call-site with its own BITSIZE_in1/in2/in3/out1 parameterization. In the
comb candidate it implements the 'output 0 when active_mask_i[lane]=0' select. Its
$ternary$ cells at vector_alu_synth.v:346 are exactly where OPT_MUXTREE deletes real mux
ports under USE_SYNLIG:true (271 ports in the broken 1587-instance netlist; only 10,
legitimately dead, ports removed once USE_SYNLIG:false + sv2v preprocessing is used
instead -- see bd show claude_verilog_test-gcd for the full SAT-miter + eval proof).

EXPOSURE VERDICT for hand-written RTL (CPU/GPU macros, rtl/gpu/vector_alu.sv, rtl/cpu/*):
NOT exposed to this specific construct. `grep -rl "ui_cond_expr_FU|_bambu_artificial_|BAMBU/PANDA" rtl/`
returns zero matches anywhere in rtl/. The hand-RTL implements the identical masking
semantics (rtl/gpu/vector_alu.sv:2,42: "Inactive lanes (active_mask bit = 0) produce 0",
`if (active_mask_i[lane]) begin ... end` inside a generate/for-loop) via a completely
different, non-parameterized-generic-module-instantiation RTL idiom. So the SPECIFIC
failure mode proven here (Synlig mis-elaborating a massively per-instance-parameterized
generic ternary FU template) does not structurally apply to CPU/GPU hand-RTL. This is a
structural/code-shape argument, not a functional re-verification of the CPU/GPU macros --
per the coordinator's explicit instruction this session did NOT re-run the CPU/GPU macro
flows, so their USE_SYNLIG:true configs remain UNAUDITED at the functional level; only
the "is this specific Bambu-template construct present" question is answered (no).

BASELINE FSM ARM (valu_hls, USE_SYNLIG:true) A/B CHECK: reran the SAME candidate through
USE_SYNLIG:false + an sv2v-preprocessed shim (temp config under /nobackup/pnr_ab_valu_hls/,
tracked pnr/asap7/valu_hls/config.json NOT modified), scope egt-ppa-hls-ab,

FIRST synthesis-log cell-count checkpoint onward (43659 vs 55084), NOT the ~1-2% that would
indicate "no corruption". This is a REAL, currently UNEXPLAINED divergence between the two

title: [bug] rtk diff filter reports 'Files are identical' + exit 0 for files that DIFFER
description:
rtk's BUILT-IN 'diff' filter (rtk 0.42.0, /home/neuromorphic/.local/bin/rtk) drops changes and always exits 0. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL REPORT: this is NOT a .rtk/filters.toml entry. The project's filters.toml has no diff filter; 'diff' is an rtk built-in ('rtk --help' -> 'diff  Ultra-condensed diff (only changed lines)'). So it is NOT fixable by editing this repo's config, and it affects every rtk user, not just this project.

DEFECT A -- FALSE 'identical' VERDICT, CONTENT DISCARDED. Root cause identified: the filter classifies changed lines as added / removed / MODIFIED (its own output prints '+N added, -N removed, ~N modified'), but the identical-check appears to consider only added+removed and IGNORE the modified count. So a change consisting SOLELY of modified (similar) lines is reported as no change at all.
  Demonstrated:
    printf 'item 1\nitem 2\nitem 3\n' > s1; printf 'item 9\nitem 8\nitem 7\n' > s2
    rtk diff s1 s2   -> '[ok] Files are identical'  exit 0     <-- EVERY line differs
    cmp -s s1 s2     -> DIFFER
  Contrast, proving the mechanism:
    'a' vs 'A'            (dissimilar) -> diff shown correctly
    'line A' vs 'line B'  (similar)    -> '[ok] Files are identical'
    'line A'->'line B' PLUS an added line -> renders fine: '~ 1 line A -> line B / + 3 EXTRA'
  So the renderer CAN display modified lines; only the identical-decision ignores them. Similar lines are exactly the common case when diffing two versions of a generated file -- which is how this was hit.

DEFECT B -- EXIT CODE ALWAYS 0. Even when the diff IS displayed correctly, rtk diff exits 0. Real diff exits 1 on difference, 2 on trouble. Any gate of the form 'if diff a b; then ... fi' or 'diff a b || fail' therefore ALWAYS takes the identical branch. Verified on the 5-line all-differ case: full correct diff printed, exit 0. Missing file gives exit 1 where real diff gives 2.
  B is the broader hazard: it affects EVERY invocation, not just the shape that triggers A.

EXPOSURE IS CWD-DEPENDENT: the rewrite hook only engages inside the trusted project dir, and only when it parses the command. A bare top-level 'diff' in the repo currently passes through raw and behaves correctly; 'rtk diff' invoked explicitly always misbehaves. So the bug is intermittent from a caller's point of view, which makes it worse, not better -- the same command can be right or wrong depending on invocation context.

FOUND VIA GH #119 bead 9ne: comparing two Bambu-generated .v files to decide whether the output is byte-reproducible. The filtered diff said 'Files are identical', which would have been recorded as 'Bambu output IS reproducible' -- the opposite of the truth. cmp and sha256sum caught it; the real answer (only an embedded timestamp differs) needed a Python difflib comparison to reach.

WHY P1: same class as bead dwp -- a tool reporting success on evidence it did not actually check. A filter may compress output; it must never invert a verdict or discard a non-zero exit code. Any past session that used diff to confirm two files matched may have recorded a false conclusion.

NOT FIXABLE IN THIS REPO. Options: (1) report upstream to rtk (defect A root cause above is minimal and actionable); (2) shadow/disable the built-in via a project .rtk/filters.toml entry, if rtk supports overriding built-ins; (3) leave the filter and record in CLAUDE.md that 'diff' must never be trusted for a pass/fail decision -- use cmp -s or sha256sum, both of which were correct throughout. Awaiting a decision on which.
close_reason:
DONE. Both requested actions complete, and the investigation changed the answer.

(1) REPORT UPSTREAM -- turned out to be MOOT, so I did not file a duplicate. All three symptoms were already reported at github.com/rtk-ai/rtk: #781 (false 'identical'), #2446 (exit 0 when files differ), #3267 (priority:critical, same agent-verification scenario). More: PR #792 had ALREADY identified the exact root cause I derived independently -- 'the identical-files guard only checked added == 0 && removed == 0, ignoring the modified counter'. It was closed as 'overtaken by events' because the fix landed by another route (render_file_diff now branches on diff.changes.is_empty()).

VERIFIED THE FIX rather than assuming it: downloaded the v0.48.0 rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl release binary to /tmp (installed binary untouched) and re-ran both repros side by side.
  Defect A: 0.42.0 -> '[ok] Files are identical' exit 0;  0.48.0 -> '1c1 / < line A / > line B' exit 1. Also correct on the harsher all-lines-similar case.
  Defect B: 0.42.0 -> full correct diff printed but exit 0;  0.48.0 -> exit 1.
  Identical-file control -> exit 0 on BOTH, so the guard was not merely inverted.
BOTH DEFECTS FIXED IN v0.48.0. Installed here is 0.42.0. The actionable fix is an UPGRADE, not a bug report.

The one genuinely additive upstream contribution: #781 and #2446 are both still OPEN despite being fixed, so I posted verification comments to let the maintainers close them --
  https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/issues/781#issuecomment-5569480940
  https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/issues/2446#issuecomment-5569483187
#781 was also tagged needs-reproduction; the comment supplies a repro on a RELEASED binary (previous reports were built-from-source or older versions) plus the mechanism evidence that the renderer could always display modified lines and only the verdict dropped them.

(2) DOCUMENTED in CLAUDE.md: both defects, the root cause, upstream links, the v0.48.0 fix, and the standing rule that diff must never gate a pass/fail decision -- use cmp -s or sha256sum, both of which were correct throughout. Placed deliberately OUTSIDE the <!-- rtk-instructions --> markers, with a note saying why: that block is regenerated by 'rtk init' and would have silently wiped the warning. I initially put it inside and caught it.

TWO TRAPS RECORDED THAT OUTLIVE THE UPGRADE:
  * RTK_DISABLED=1 suppresses the HOOK REWRITE, not an explicit 'rtk diff' -- verified, the latter still filters. (#3267 reports RTK_DISABLED=1 as a workaround, which is true only for the hooked path.)
  * The rewrite is cwd- and parse-dependent: a bare top-level 'diff' in the repo passed through raw and behaved correctly, while the same shape after 'echo ...;' was rewritten and lied. Intermittent, which is worse than consistently wrong -- it is why this survived unnoticed.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL FILING (already applied in the previous update): this is an rtk BUILT-IN filter, not a .rtk/filters.toml entry, so it was never fixable in this repo.

NOT DONE, left to the user: actually upgrading rtk 0.42.0 -> 0.48.0. That is an environment change to their tooling and their call; the CLAUDE.md warning is correct for both versions in the meantime.

title: ASAP7 detailed routing silently produces ZERO committed wires on CPU+SoC (DRT-0073/0074 pin-access failures swallowed as non-fatal)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 while trying to standalone-validate the RCX ruleset for bead
e69 against run 23's "signed off" SoC ODB (RUN_2026-08-09_14-36-16, the run
CLAUDE.md/docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md describe as "BOTH domains close... 0 routing
DRC, 0 antenna... post-route CDC budget check PASS"). MEASURED, not inferred:

1. `openroad-detailedrouting.log` for that exact run shows detailed routing died
   at the PIN ACCESS phase, before any track assignment / search-and-repair ever
   ran: "[ERROR DRT-0073] No access point for u_gpu/m_axi_araddr[19]." followed
   immediately by "WARNING: detailed_route reported errors; continuing (DRT may
   be incomplete): DRT-0073" -- then the log jumps straight to "Setting global
   connections for newly added cells" (a post-route housekeeping step) and writes
   out the DB. No routing progress lines (search-and-repair, layer-by-layer
   completion, DRC repair iterations) appear anywhere after pin access starts.

2. `42-odb-reportwirelength/or_metrics_out.json`: `route__wirelength__max: 0`.
   `wire_lengths.csv` in that same step directory has ONLY the header row (0
   data rows) -- 242,694 nets, zero wired. `final/def/soc_top.def` (112 MB) has
   ZERO "ROUTED " occurrences anywhere in the file (grep -c). Loading
   `final/odb/soc_top.odb` (357 MB) in OpenROAD 26Q2 and querying every net's
   dbWire via Tcl (`$net getWire`) returns NULL for all 242,696 nets.
   `final/metrics.json` reports `route__wirelength__estimated: 3276660` (the
   pre-route GLOBAL ROUTE estimate) but no real committed wirelength field, and
   `antenna__violating__nets/pins: 0` -- trivially true when nothing is routed.
   `Checker.TrDRC` (step 41) has no log/report content at all.

3. NOT unique to the SoC: 3 of the most recent standalone CPU-block tuning runs
   (RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02, _13-32-12, _12-59-06 -- the #96 pin_order.cfg
   tuning campaign) show the identical pattern. RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02's
   detailedrouting.log has 401 "[ERROR DRT-0074] No access point for
   PIN/apb_prdata_o[N]" / "PIN/apb_pslverr_o" / "PIN/apb_pready_o" lines --
   exactly the 3 CPU-macro APB output pins bead cyb/g0o made "PURE registered
   outputs" as part of the run-23 timing fix. Same odb-query check: 0/33,636
   nets wired. `route__wirelength__max: 0` in all 3 runs' final metrics.json.

CONCLUSION: the celebrated run-23 "0 routing DRC / 0 antenna / both domains
close" sign-off, and the CPU block's own recent tuning runs, were measured
against an UNROUTED design. Checkers report 0 violations because there is
nothing routed to violate -- not because routing is clean. This is a P1
correctness-of-signoff issue, separate from and predating bead e69 (RCX rules
stub) and bead gyx (PSM-0069 IR-drop connectivity) -- do not merge with either.

SUSPECTED (not confirmed) root cause: the run-23 changelog entry in CLAUDE.md
describes making apb_prdata_o/apb_pslverr_o/apb_pready_o "PURE registered
outputs" specifically to fix a timing arc, around the same window these DRT
pin-access failures start appearing. A physical side effect on those pins'
access geometry (placement/spacing/blockage interaction, possibly with the
new FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG-driven macro boundary or PDN tap-cell placement) is the
leading hypothesis; not verified here.

NOT YET DONE (deliberately out of scope for the agent that filed this): root
cause of the DRT-0073/0074 access-point failures; whether it predates or
postdates FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG (bead g0o) or the APB registering fix (bead cyb);
whether librelane's "continuing on DRT error" default should instead be fatal
for this project (arguably it should -- an unrouted design silently passing
signoff checks is worse than a hard stop); re-verification of run 23's and
the CPU tuning campaign's actual routed state; whether any GDS/tapeout-facing
claim in docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md or CLAUDE.md needs a correction/caveat
banner alongside the existing "fabric-only" power caveat (bead ew3).

Reproduction: `grep -c 'ROUTED ' <run>/final/def/*.def` on any recent ASAP7
run, or `python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('<run>/42-odb-reportwirelength/or_metrics_out.json'))['route__wirelength__max'])"`.
close_reason:
Root-caused (branch fix/asap7-drt-zero-routing-xy6, commit fc0265f). Swept
every ASAP7 run with recoverable final/ artifacts -- SoC run 14 (accepted
M11 single-clock sign-off), SoC run 23 (accepted multiclock sign-off), both
GPU 571 MHz sign-off runs (2026-05-27/28), all 8 CPU pin_order.cfg tuning
runs -- 100% show zero ROUTED net records and route__wirelength__max=0.

Root cause of the ZERO-WIRE symptom (confirmed): drt.tcl's local, non-
upstream catch{} wraps the ENTIRE detailed_route Tcl call, not per-pin
resolution. Every failing run's log shows the pin-access error firing
before track assignment or search-and-repair ever runs, so the exception
aborts the whole call and write_views commits the pre-route placed netlist
as-is. This is NOT a run-23-era regression and NOT SoC-specific: the GPU
sign-off runs predate the suspected trigger (registered APB outputs,
FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG) by three weeks with the identical signature, and the
catch patch was already in place during the April Phase-3 CPU PPA campaign.
No ASAP7 run in this project's recoverable history has ever been confirmed
to have actually completed detailed routing.

Fail-loud gate landed: tools/verif/check_asap7_routing.py + pnr/Makefile
check-asap7-{routing,gpu-routing,soc-routing} targets, mandatory post-flow
(before pruning) on every full ASAP7 target, conditional on the multiclock
target (skipped only for documented partial --to runs). FAILs (exit 1) on
zero routed nets / wirelength_max==0 / unresolved [ERROR DRT-*]; ERRORs
(exit 2, distinct from FAIL) on missing/unparsable artifacts per bead dwp
discipline. Tested against 3 known-bad runs, all correctly FAIL.

Docs corrected with explicit caveats at every affected claim site:
docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md (new "Routing / physical-closure caveat" section
with full routed/unrouted table), docs/ASAP7_RUN_HISTORY.md, CLAUDE.md.
Timing/power/area numbers are explicitly preserved as self-consistent
GRT-estimate-based results -- only DRC/antenna/routing-clean claims are
withdrawn.

NOT solved: why individual DRT-0073/0074 pin-access points fail geometry
resolution in the first place. Split out as claude_verilog_test-ocm
(P2 follow-up) so this P1 doesn't stay open waiting on a full P&R run
(host reboot mid-run risk, bead o1i). No P&R run was launched this session
per instruction.

title: CPU macro has no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG - every regeneration reshuffles ~98% of boundary pins and can wreck SoC CTS
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 while chasing the GH #96 run-21 -> run-22 cpu_clk regression (-60.66 ps -> -596.00 ps, 690 violators).

ROOT CAUSE: pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json has NO FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG, so OpenROAD's io-placement step free-floats the CPU macro's boundary pins according to whatever internal placement that particular block run produced. Block-level placement is already known to be non-deterministic here (setup WS bounced +21.64 / +14.36 / +2.80 ps across three runs of near-identical RTL).

MEASURED CHURN between two consecutive macro regenerations (git HEAD LEF vs regenerated LEF, 401 pins compared): 393 pins MOVED, largest ~126 units inside a 130x130 um macro. Only clk_i stayed fixed at (6.078, 0.0); rst_n_i moved 31.728 -> 25.572. Ordinary data/control pins landed on effectively different edges.

CONSEQUENCE CHAIN (each step measured, not inferred):
  macro pin reshuffle
  -> SoC global placement perturbed around u_cpu
  -> TritonCTS builds a worse-balanced cpu_gated_clk_regs subtree; a NEW cell delaybuf_0_cpu_clk appears (0 occurrences in run 21's netlist, 1 in run 22); u_cpu_cg.u_icg CLK->GCLK goes 79.3 ps -> 285.1 ps (same cell type, so loading/placement, not library)
  -> post-CTS cpu_clk skew roughly DOUBLES: worst_hold -485.6 -> -922.1 ps, worst_setup -436.2 -> -865.2 ps (stage 32 or_metrics_out.json, the flow's own numbers)
  -> post-CTS hold violations 805 -> 4702 endpoints; resizer inserts 680 -> 4814 hold buffers; final HB4xp67 population 1934 -> 6017
  -> chained hold buffers (9+ deep on the worst path) consume the setup budget
  -> cpu_clk setup WNS -60.66 ps -> -596.00 ps, and sys_clk fell +83.79 -> +40.78 ps too.

REJECTED HYPOTHESIS (recorded so it is not re-tried): the RTL change that triggered the regeneration made apb_pready_o/apb_pslverr_o registered outputs, and the obvious theory was that their new fast clk->Q launch caused the hold explosion. Measured clk-to-Q delta is only ~9-14 ps (apb_pready_o cell_rise 247.9 -> 238.7 ps at min load) -- one to two orders of magnitude too small to explain a ~900 ps skew swing. The RTL change is merely what forced a regeneration; the instability is the bug.

ALSO REJECTED: the 25 ps real hold margin from bead s9f is not the amplifier -- raw pre-fix violations were already hundreds of ps (-332 ps in run 21, -782 ps in run 22) before any margin applies.

FIX: author an FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG for rv32i_cpu_top from a known-good layout (git HEAD's LEF is the run-21 macro that closed at -60.66 ps) and add it to pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json, so the boundary is stable across every future regeneration. LibreLane supports the variable (librelane/steps/openroad.py + steps/odb.py). Validate with one CPU block re-run (~40 min) by diffing the resulting LEF pin coordinates against the reference, then one SoC run.

WIDER IMPACT: this applies to the GPU macro too (pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json) and to any Sky130 macro flow. Any time a macro is regenerated for an unrelated reason, the integrating top can silently lose timing for reasons that have nothing to do with the change being made. That is exactly what happened here and it cost two SoC runs to see.
close_reason: FIXED. pnr/asap7/cpu/pin_order.cfg (401 signal pins) added and wired via FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG in pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json:150-151; rationale in pnr/asap7/cpu/README_pin_order.md (the file itself carries no comments -- LibreLane's ioplace parser treats any non-#N/#E/#S/#W '#' line as a pin identifier). Determinism PROVEN: two CPU block runs with the same config now produce a byte-identical LEF, 0/401 pins moved (was 393/401). That made tuning measurable for the first time -- block slack had previously drawn randomly from a ~47 ps band -- and run 23 then closed cpu_clk at +9.79 ps / 1282 MHz. Merged in PR #135 (f7868b1). The identical untreated exposure on the ASAP7 GPU macro (327 pins, no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG) and on the Sky130 macros is tracked separately.

title: check_cdc_timing.tcl exceptions never bind on the flattened ASAP7 SoC netlist (slash vs dot, and cells are anonymous)
description:
GH #96 ran pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl against a real routed netlist for the FIRST time (RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51). Result: CDC-CHECK-RESULT: FAIL, 42 findings, of which 36 are CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS -- i.e. the exceptions in phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc matched EMPTY collections and were never applied. Breakdown of the 172 miss lines: sec.11 x30 (async_axi_fifo), sec.12 x16 + sec.12a x16 (apb_cdc_bridge u_apb_pll2_cdc / u_apb_dbg_cdc), sec.13 x10 (PMU/IRQ). By kind: 60 payload, 50 gray-pointer, 32 toggle, 25 single-bit, 25 mem_q.

GOOD NEWS FIRST: the checker did exactly what bead dwp designed it to do -- it refused to report PASS when its own patterns bound to nothing, and failed loudly. This is a bug in the PATTERNS, not evidence of a CDC timing violation. No CDC budget was measured either way, so the boundary is currently UNVERIFIED post-route.

ROOT CAUSE, measured on the routed netlist with OpenSTA:
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc/u_aw_fifo/u_wr_ptr_to_rd*'  (slash, as written) -> 0 cells, 0 nets
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_aw_fifo.u_wr_ptr_to_rd*'  (dot)               -> 0 cells, 6 NETS
  '*u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_aw_fifo*'                                     -> 0 cells, 22 NETS
  '*u_apb_dbg_cdc*'                                               -> 0 cells, 13 NETS
Two independent problems:
 (1) SEPARATOR. SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE=flatten leaves hierarchical names joined by '.' as escaped identifiers (e.g. \u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_ar_fifo.rd_bin_q). The SDC was authored with '/' separators against RTL hierarchy. Same class as the known macro_placement.cfg dot-vs-slash trap.
 (2) OBJECT TYPE. After flatten the CELLS are anonymous (_419265_ etc): get_cells/get_pins match ZERO for every hierarchical pattern. Only get_nets matches. So exceptions must be expressed as -through [get_nets ...], not on pins/cells.

ALSO: some RTL signal names do not survive at all. 'mem_q' has 0 occurrences anywhere in the netlist (the unpacked flop array is fully renamed), and 'wr_gray_q' is gone while 'wr_gray_d' survives. So the 25 mem_q exceptions CANNOT be re-expressed by name; they need a different formulation (e.g. -from [all_registers -clock cpu_clk] -to [all_registers -clock sys_clk] scoped by -through on a surviving net, or constrain the surviving *_d nets).

FIX PLAN: (a) switch all patterns to dot separators; (b) retarget from pins/cells to get_nets with -through; (c) re-express the mem_q class without relying on that name; (d) add a binding assertion so a future pattern drift fails at authoring time, not after a 5 h run -- the existing CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS machinery already does this, it just needs to be exercised against a netlist in CI or a synth-only run rather than only at signoff.

Until fixed, the post-route CDC budget verification for the 2-domain SoC is NON-FUNCTIONAL.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
FIXED and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (2026-08-06). check_cdc_timing.tcl + phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc reworked (+539/-156 lines). Against RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51: make check-cdc-timing-asap7-soc now exits 0 with CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS count 0 and CDC-CHECK-RESULT: PASS (re-run by me, not just reported by the implementer).

THREE root causes, not the two originally filed:
 (1) separator: hierarchy survives flatten only as literal '.' in escaped identifiers, not '/';
 (2) object class: cells are anonymous post-flatten so get_cells/get_pins name patterns always return empty - only get_nets can match;
 (3) NEW - OpenSTA's -filter "name =~ <pat>" mis-parses a literal '.' even between wildcards: '*u_aw_fifo.u_wr_ptr_to_rd*' -> 0 matches while '*.d_i*' -> 231,528 matches (i.e. nearly every net). Patterns must be '*'-joined chains of DOT-FREE substrings. This is why my original evidence (positional 'get_nets <pattern>' with dots, which DOES work and returned 6 nets) did not transfer to the -filter form used in the SDC. Both measurements were correct; the two APIs differ.

SEMANTIC FIX (confirmed against cdc_2ff_sync.sv/cdc_gray_fifo.sv): the old exceptions targeted u_*_ptr_to_*/q_o = sync_q[STAGES-1], which is entirely INSIDE the destination domain - a destination-only path, not a crossing. All exceptions re-pointed at the launch->first-capture segment (d_i where it survives, else the source register's own net, e.g. rd_gray_q where u_rd_ptr_to_wr.d_i collapsed into it).

PRECEDENCE (measured, and it corrected an initial wrong assumption): a -through exception is ALWAYS dominated by an overlapping -from/-to one regardless of order or specificity, so every per-crossing exception now uses -from/-to. Between two overlapping -from/-to exceptions precedence is pure DECLARATION ORDER (last wins), NOT specificity - proven by reversing the order. Hence the domain-wide fallback is declared BEFORE sections 11-13.
Two further silent-no-op bugs were found and fixed: one-hop -of_objects grabbed an intervening polarity inverter (ASAP7 DFFASRHQNx1 exposes only QN) instead of the real register, fixed with get_fanin/get_fanout -flat -only_cells; and synthesis-shared buffering put fanout on unrelated same-domain cells for one bus bit, fixed by intersecting against all_registers -clock <expected> and applying per-bit.

INVENTORY: 36 named exceptions (all missing) -> 19 name-matched crossing-specific + 2 domain-wide fallbacks covering the 17 that are unmatchable by name post-flatten (5 mem_q + 6 cmd_*/resp_* x 2 bridges). No crossing dropped.

BUDGET VERDICTS on the real routed netlist, all MET: gray-pointer wr2rd +275/+759 ps vs 390/875 budget; rd2wr +294/+779; apb_pll2 toggle +676/+1644 vs 780/1750; apb_dbg toggle +676/+1644; PMU/IRQ single-bit +645 vs 780; domain-wide fallback +174..+759 vs 702/875-1575.

NON-VACUITY PROVEN (my own negative controls, the thing that matters most here): forcing all 10 cdc_apply_max_delay budgets to 1 ps makes the check exit 1 with 7 violated groups covering EVERY class - both gray-pointer directions, both APB toggle bridges, PMU/IRQ, and both domain-wide fallbacks. A separate control tightening only the 0.5x/0.9x multipliers gave exit 1 with 4 groups. So the PASS is a real measurement, not an empty report.

title: ASAP7 resizer setup/hold slack margins are ~1000x too small (ns value vs ps liberty) - affects every ASAP7 signoff
description:
Same class as the known SDC units bug (Runs 7-32 ns-vs-ps), but for the RESIZER MARGINS, and still live in every ASAP7 config today.

MECHANISM (verified end to end):
1. librelane declares PL/GRT_RESIZER_{SETUP,HOLD}_SLACK_MARGIN with units="ns" (librelane/steps/openroad.py:2258-2261, 2327-2330).
2. The tcl passes the value RAW to OpenROAD: 'lappend hold_args -hold_margin $::env(PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN)' (scripts/openroad/rsz_timing_postcts.tcl:45, rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl:48; same for -setup_margin at :35/:38).
3. OpenROAD/OpenSTA interpret those margins in the LIBERTY time unit. ASAP7 liberty is time_unit: "1ps" (asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT_nldm_220123.lib:45).
=> pnr/asap7/*/config.json values of 0.075 and 0.1 mean 0.075 ps and 0.1 ps, not 75 ps / 100 ps. Effectively ZERO guard band.

PROOF (GH #96 runs, SoC): run 17 used PL/GRT hold margin 0.075, run 18 used 0.030. Final netlists are BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 5d6ca24b90497f115881dde6ae83c1b8 both), HB4xp67 hold-buffer count identical at 136 in runs 16/17/18, and per-clock timing identical to 6 decimals (cpu_clk WNS -44.927727, sys_clk +106.217033). A 2.5x change in a real margin cannot produce a bit-identical result; a change between two values that both round to ~0 ps does exactly that.

BLAST RADIUS: every ASAP7 run in this repo believed it had 100 ps setup / 75 ps hold guard band and actually had ~0. That includes the signed-off CPU (1282 MHz, RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12), the GPU, and the Phase 5 SoC run-14 signoff (571 MHz). Their reported slacks are still REAL (STA is independent of the resizer margin) - what is missing is the extra optimisation guard band, so the designs sit closer to the cliff than the configs imply, and they are more exposed to OCV/derate than documented.

FIX: express these in ps for ASAP7, e.g. PL/GRT_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN 100 and PL/GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN 75 (or whatever guard band is actually wanted). Do NOT blanket-apply to sky130/freepdk45 configs - those liberties are in ns, where the current values are already correct. Re-check each PDK's time_unit before editing. Expect area/power to grow once the margins become real.

Found while diagnosing GH #96 cpu_clk hold-buffer padding (bead claude_verilog_test-8nz).
close_reason: Config fix landed 2026-08-07 (5 ASAP7 configs, per-PDK time_unit verified first; sky130/freepdk45 correctly untouched). Re-sign-off under real margins now confirmed for the CPU macro (RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02 at 20/10 ps) and the multiclock SoC (run 23 at 45/25 ps, both domains MET), which also retires the global-knob risk this bead flagged. Only the GPU macro still carries ~0 guard band; closing that is the ~2.5-day block run deliberately deferred under bead buw, so it is tracked there. See the residue-audit comment for the measurements.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-07. Liberty time_unit verified per PDK before editing: ASAP7 = 1ps (asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT_nldm_220123.lib:45), sky130 = 1ns, freepdk45 = 1ns. sky130/freepdk45 configs deliberately untouched and confirmed untouched (git diff --stat empty for both trees); freepdk45 has no resizer-margin keys at all and sky130's ns values were already correct.

Policy applied to the 5 ASAP7 configs: setup margin = 2.5% of period, hold = 1.5%, rounded to 5 ps.
  cpu/config.json            780 ps  -> setup 20 / hold 10 ps  (kept UNDER the achieved slack so the guard band cannot demand more than the design is known to reach)
  gpu/config.json           1750 ps  -> setup 45 / hold 25 ps
  template/config.json       705 ps  -> setup 20 / hold 10 ps
  soc/config_multiclock.json 1750 ps -> setup 45 / hold 25 ps
  soc/config.json            NUMERICALLY UNCHANGED (0.1/0.075) + documentation comment only -- this is the run-14 byte-reproducible M11 sign-off artifact, so the corrected values live in config_multiclock.json instead. Any new SoC PD work should use the multiclock config.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Two real findings from preflight (2026-08-05):

(1) OpenSTA SILENTLY DEGRADES an unbindable create_clock into a VIRTUAL clock. 'create_clock -name cpu_clk -period 780 [get_ports cpu_clk_i]' against a netlist with no cpu_clk_i port does NOT error - it yields a clock object that reports period=780 and would appear as a second 'Clock:' block in OpenROAD clock.rpt, while having is_virtual=1, 0 sources and 0 registers. Measured on the run-14 netlist: sys_clk is_virtual=0/sources=1/registers=43764 vs cpu_clk is_virtual=1/sources=0/registers=0. So 'clock.rpt shows two clocks' is NOT evidence of a real 2-domain run and would have green-lit a 5h run that timed nothing in the CPU domain. New gate: pnr/scripts/check_multiclock_sdc.tcl asserts is_virtual=0 + >=1 source pin + >0 registers per domain, emits MC-CHECK-RESULT: PASS|FAIL, exit 0/1/2. Validated as a NEGATIVE control against the run-14 netlist (exit 1, all 4 failure modes named).

(2) pnr/asap7/soc/runs was created as a REAL directory on / by a concurrent run before the symlink guard could fire. '[ -L runs ] || ln -sfn /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs runs' then nested the link as runs/asap7_soc_runs and the run still landed on / (7.4G free vs ~6G per full run). Two LibreLane runs were live at once on the 15GiB host; the redundant synth-only one was killed. Guard hardened: an existing non-symlink runs/ is now a hard error with migration instructions, verified to fire. MIGRATION STILL PENDING before any full run: mv pnr/asap7/soc/runs/RUN_* /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/ && rm -rf pnr/asap7/soc/runs.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Gate B run 1 (RUN_2026-08-05_21-20-25) FAILED at 05-checker-yosysunmappedcells: '2 Unmapped Yosys instances found', exit 2. Root cause: sv2v resolves `ifdef ITSELF, before yosys runs, and the asap7-soc-sv2v target passed NO --define (unlike sky130-soc-sv2v). So USE_ICG_CELL from config.json VERILOG_DEFINES arrived too late -- rv32i_clock_gate.sv had already been frozen into its behavioural always_latch branch, which yosys infers as $_DLATCH_N_ and cannot map to any ASAP7 cell. Never bit before because the SoC had no clock gates until the PMU epic (#98) + #93 added u_cpu_cg/u_gpu_cg after the run-14 sign-off. Fix: SOC_SV2V_DEFINES := --define=USE_ICG_CELL in the asap7 sv2v recipe; regenerated netlist now instantiates ICGx1_ASAP7_75t_R (present in asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT liberty AND asap7sc7p5t_SIMPLE_RVT_1x.lef) with zero en_latch. Deliberately NOT adding __pnr__ (boot_rom.sv branches on it and run 14 was built without it -- adding it would change the PPA baseline; note sky130 DOES pass it, an inconsistency worth its own bead) nor SRAM_ASAP7 (no file in SOC_SV_FILES branches on it). sky130 must NOT get USE_ICG_CELL: ICGx1 is ASAP7-only and sky130 has real latch cells.

Also confirmed the 27 'used but has no driver' bits (cpu_bridge_s_{awlen,awsize,awburst,wlast,arlen,arsize,arburst}) are NOT a regression: run 14's pre_synth_chk.rpt has the identical 27 bits under the pre-CDC name cpu_m_*. Same pre-existing bead g0o condition the 571 MHz signoff already carried.

DFF count from the killed parallel synth: 44,981 (44,310 DFFHQNx1 + 671 DFFASRHQNx1) vs run-14 43,766 = +1,215. Prior estimate of +30-40 was wrong: it counted only gray pointers and sync chains, missing that each of async_axi_fifo's 5 channel FIFOs stores full-width AXI payload.

Run dir migrated off / and pnr/asap7/soc/runs is now the /nobackup symlink. Gate B run 2 = RUN_2026-08-05_22-41-24.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Gate B run 2 (RUN_2026-08-05_22-41-24) PASSED, exit 0, all gates green:

The 872 is the CPU-domain FLAT logic only (async_axi_fifo CPU face, apb_cdc_bridge, cdc syncs, clock gate, PLL2 APB) -- the CPU core itself is a hard macro, so this is the expected magnitude.
- Unconstrained endpoints 9, DOWN from run-14's 49. Two of the 9 are u_cpu_cg.u_icg/SE and u_gpu_cg.u_icg/SE (scan-enable tied to 1'b0, no timing path, expected); the other 7 are anonymous flop D pins.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
RUN 16 COMPLETE (RUN_2026-08-06_00-10-40, exit 0, 46 steps, 6.7G). Per-clock split via new pnr/scripts/report_per_clock_timing.tcl (metrics.json has NO per-clock keys - its global WNS is the min across domains and hid this entirely):
  sys_clk PASS: WNS +106.22 ps, TNS 0, hold +23.50, 571 MHz MET (run 14 was +113.6 -> -7 ps, within the +-450 ps run-to-run noise band). FABRIC BASELINE PRESERVED.
  cpu_clk FAIL: WNS -205.34 ps, TNS -7261.72, 194 violating endpoints, achieved 1014.88 MHz (985.34 ps) vs 1282 MHz target.
  DRC 0, antenna 0/0, slew/cap/fanout 0, PDN 8281711 (identical tap artifact), die unchanged 270400, stdcell 245149->255307, util .656->.664, power 62.9->43.3 mW.

DIAGNOSIS (measured, not guessed): 33 of the 194 violators traverse the CPU macro as fabric FF -> u_cpu APB addr in -> ONE 800.71 ps combinational macro arc -> u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] -> fabric FF. 800.71 ps cannot fit 780 ps and is fixed in the macro Liberty. The other 161 never touch the macro and sit at only -44.93 ps.
Liberty-vs-Liberty check demanded by SDC section 10 before reintroducing any relaxation: the CPU's OWN standalone 780 ps signoff does set_false_path -to [get_ports apb_prdata_o[*]] (pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc:121). The macro was never characterized to meet 780 ps on that path, so the SoC was holding it tighter than its own block signoff. Exception is contract-honouring, not violation-hiding. APB addr/control INPUTS deliberately NOT excepted (standalone times them, set_input_delay -max 120, asap7.sdc:99-112).

KEY GOTCHA: -from does NOT work. At block level apb_prdata_o is a PORT (endpoint) so the standalone uses -to; at SoC level the path continues through it, so the pin is a THROUGH point. A/B on run 16's routed netlist with its own final/sdc as the only variable: -from = -205.34/194 (zero effect, nothing matched); -through = -44.93/162, TNS -7261.72->-1756.83, 1014.88->1212.23 MHz. sys_clk byte-identical (+106.217033, 0 violators) under both, confirming CPU-domain-only scope.

RUN 17 launched 2026-08-06 05:24 = RUN_2026-08-06_05-24-03 (tmux soc96r17, log /nobackup/soc96_run17.log): SDC 10a false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] + CLOCK_PERIOD 1.75->0.78 (ABC target only) to attack the residual -44.93 ps class. Both SDC copies (staged + canonical pnr/constraints/) carry 10a identically.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
RUN 17 COMPLETE (RUN_2026-08-06_05-24-03, exit 0, ~4h14m). Two changes, wildly different value:
  APB false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*]: WORKED EXACTLY as the A/B predicted. cpu_clk -205.34 -> -44.93 ps, TNS -7261.72 -> -1756.83, violators 194 -> 162, achieved 1014.88 -> 1212.23 MHz.
  CLOCK_PERIOD 1.75 -> 0.78 (ABC target): NO-OP. stdcell 255307 -> 255296 (-11 cells), area 33411.1 -> 33385.6, cpu_clk WNS unchanged to 6 decimals. Do not spend another run on this knob.
  sys_clk unchanged and PASSING throughout: +106.217033 ps, TNS 0, hold +23.50, 571 MHz MET. DRC 0, antenna 0/0, power 43.27 mW.

RESIDUAL ROOT CAUSE (measured, and it is NOT logic depth or skew): 161 of the 162 remaining cpu_clk violators traverse resizer-inserted HB4xp67 HOLD BUFFERS. Longest chain 20 deep. The worst path spends 665 ps of its 1050 ps arrival in 9 chained HB4xp67 while its actual functional logic is only ~222 ps. Design has 252 HB* cells total. This is hold padding destroying setup.
WHY THE CPU DOMAIN AND NOT THE FABRIC: PL/GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN 0.075 is ~10% of the 780 ps cpu_clk period but only ~4% of the 1750 ps sys_clk period, so the CPU domain got padded far harder.

RUN 18 launched 2026-08-06 09:44 = RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51 (tmux soc96r18): CLOCK_PERIOD reverted to 1.75 (one variable) + PL/GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN 0.075 -> 0.030. Achieved hold today is +18.88 ps despite the 75 ps target, so a 30 ps target should keep real hold margin while removing most padding. MUST verify hold after the run: Checker.HoldViolations is in the --skip list so a hold regression will not abort the flow. This is iteration 2 of the 2 authorized.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
RUN 18 COMPLETE (RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51, exit 0) = NULL RESULT, and the reason is a repo-wide bug.
Per-clock identical to run 17 to 6 decimals: sys_clk +106.217033 PASS / cpu_clk -44.927727, 162 violators, 1212.23 MHz. Final netlist md5 BYTE-IDENTICAL to run 17 (5d6ca24b90497f115881dde6ae83c1b8); HB4xp67 count 136 in runs 16, 17 AND 18.
CAUSE: PL/GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN is declared units=ns by librelane but passed RAW to OpenROAD, which reads it in the LIBERTY unit - ASAP7 liberty is 1ps. So 0.075 meant 0.075 ps and my 0.030 meant 0.030 ps; both round to ~zero, hence zero change. Filed as its own P1 bead (see 'resizer ... margins ~1000x too small'), because it also means the CPU/GPU/SoC ASAP7 signoffs all had ~0 optimisation guard band rather than the 100 ps setup / 75 ps hold their configs imply.
CONSEQUENCE FOR #96: the hold margin knob is inert - it cannot be lowered because it is already ~0. The 20-deep HB4xp67 chains are therefore fixing REAL hold violations, not chasing a margin. Their real driver is cpu_clk clock-tree insertion-delay imbalance: on the worst path, launch-side clock network delay is 109.26 ps but capture-side is 256.84 ps, ~148 ps of imbalance that every short cpu_clk path must be padded to survive - and that padding is what eats setup. This is exactly risk R1 from the pre-run design review (CPU-domain clock latency imbalance being ~27% of a 780 ps period).
NEXT KNOB IF A 3RD RUN IS AUTHORIZED: CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE 20->8 and CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_MAX_DIAMETER 50->10, matching pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json:53-54. Risk: LibreLane has no per-clock CTS override, so this also perturbs the 44,105-sink sys_clk tree that is currently passing at +106 ps.
ITERATION BUDGET: 2 of 2 authorized runs consumed (17, 18), though 18 was a null test caused by the units bug rather than a real experiment.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
POST-RUN DELIVERABLES measured on run 18 (RUN_2026-08-06_09-44-51):

1) CDC BUDGET CHECK -- ran for the first time ever. CDC-CHECK-RESULT: FAIL, 42 findings, 36 unmatched exceptions. This is a CHECKER bug, not a measured CDC violation: every pattern bound to an empty collection, so no budget was verified either way and the boundary is post-route UNVERIFIED. The checker behaved correctly by refusing to report PASS (bead dwp design working). Root cause measured with OpenSTA: flatten leaves hierarchy as dot-joined escaped NET names while cells are anonymous (_419265_), and the SDC uses slash-joined pin/cell patterns. '*u_cpu_axi_cdc/u_aw_fifo/u_wr_ptr_to_rd*' -> 0; '*u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_aw_fifo.u_wr_ptr_to_rd*' -> 6 NETS. Also mem_q has 0 occurrences anywhere (unpacked flop array fully renamed) so those 25 exceptions cannot be re-expressed by name. Filed as bead 7l5 (P1) with the full fix recipe.

2) IR DROP -- BLOCKED, and not by the RCX/SPEF gap I originally expected. analyze_power_grid fails with PSM-0069 'Check connectivity failed' on both VDD and VSS, with 32,862 'Unconnected shape ... on Layer M1' errors. That is the SAME documented M1-only PSM connectivity model that produces the 8.28 M benign tap-cell PDN violations (memory/pd/knowledge.md:857-872). Tried -source_type STRAPS as well; same failure. There is no bypass flag on analyze_power_grid. So the tap artifact does not merely inflate a violation counter -- it blocks PSM IR analysis outright. pnr/config/vsrc.tcl is in place and correct; it is the connectivity precheck that refuses.

3) POWER -- total 43.3 mW (internal 36.1 / switching 7.15 / leakage 0.035). CAVEAT, do not claim this as a multi-clock efficiency win: report_power shows Macro = 0.00 W, i.e. the CPU and GPU hard macros contribute nothing to the number in this flow, and the drop from run-14's 62.9 mW coincides with the first-ever insertion of real ICG clock gates (USE_ICG_CELL), not with the domain split. Switching power roughly halved (15.3 -> 7.15 mW). Attribution unverified -- treat 62.9 vs 43.3 as not-comparable until the gating activity assumption is checked.

4) Per-hierarchy power split (the substitute for the unmeetable 'per-domain PDN/IR' ask): Sequential 29.9 mW (69.0%), Clock 13.0 mW (30.0%), Combinational 0.44 mW (1.0%), Macro 0.00 mW.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
CLOSURE — runs 19-23. The log above stops at run 18; this records the rest and the final result.

RUN 19 (best under the old CPU abstract): CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING 20/50 -> 8/10. cpu_clk -44.93 -> -32.31 ps (1231.1 MHz), TNS -1757 -> -283, violators 162 -> 64. sys_clk held +104.4 ps. 0 DRC, 0 antenna, and the FIRST CDC budget check PASS (bead 7l5's dot-vs-slash fix landed). Still relied on the SDC 10a false path and a CPU abstract with no burst pins.

RUN 20 (regression, diagnostic): first run on the REGENERATED CPU macro (apb_prdata_o registered, burst pins present) with 10a retired. cpu_clk -350.1 ps (884.9 MHz), 15 violators -- ALL 15 end at macro APB INPUT pins. Cause measured in the Liberty: registering the output did not remove the ~800 ps read mux, it RELOCATED it from an in->out combinational arc into an 876.85 ps input setup requirement.

RUN 21 (best before the macro rebuild): added SDC 10b mirroring the CPU block's own set_multicycle_path -setup 3 / -hold 2 on the APB inputs (pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc:183-184). cpu_clk -60.66 ps -> 1189.5 MHz, 1 violator; sys_clk +83.79 ps, TNS 0, 571 MHz MET; 0 DRC, 0 antenna, 53.2 mW, CDC check PASS. PDN artifact fell 8.28 M -> 7.19 M with the new abstract.

RUN 22 (regression, diagnostic -> found a repo-class bug): rebuilt the CPU macro with apb_pready_o/apb_pslverr_o ALSO registered. cpu_clk -596.00 ps, 690 violators. Root cause was NOT the RTL (measured clk->Q delta only ~9-14 ps, two orders too small): pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json had no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG, so the regeneration free-floated 393 of 401 boundary pins -> SoC placement perturbed around u_cpu -> post-CTS cpu_clk skew doubled (-485.6 -> -922.1 ps) -> hold violations 805 -> 4702 endpoints -> 4814 hold buffers -> padding ate setup. Filed as bead cum.

RUN 23 = ACCEPTED, RUN_2026-08-09_14-36-16, BOTH DOMAINS MET:
  sys_clk  1750 ps, WS +74.79 ps, TNS 0, 0 violators -> 571 MHz  MET
  cpu_clk   780 ps, WS  +9.79 ps, TNS 0, 0 violators -> 1282 MHz MET (first time ever)
  hold +26.7 ps (sys_clk) / +23.6 ps (cpu_clk); 0 routing DRC, 0 antenna, 0 slew/cap
  51.9 mW, 267,504 std cells, 66.9 % util, die unchanged 520 x 520 um
  PDN 7,186,185 (same benign tap artifact); CDC budget check PASS (0 unmatched exceptions, 0 budget violations)
The CPU domain runs 2.24x the fabric and is no longer de-rated onto the 1750 ps cycle -- the entire point of epic #90.

TWO INDEPENDENT ROOT CAUSES, and the second was only visible once the first was fixed:
1. The macro exported ~600-800 ps combinational in->out arcs on its APB outputs. apb_prdata_o, apb_pslverr_o and apb_pready_o are now PURE registered outputs; no output pin of the macro carries a combinational arc. Two failed attempts are recorded in rv32i_cpu_top.sv so they are not retried (prdata alone merely relocated the delay; a SETUP-phase decode for pslverr still left a 617.9 ps arc re-sourced from apb_psel_i). Every APB output pays ~600 ps crossing this block's internal distribution regardless of logic depth, so only a pure flop breaks it.
2. The macro boundary was not reproducible -> pin_order.cfg. Two runs with the same config now produce a byte-identical LEF (0/401 pins moved), which made tuning measurable for the first time; block slack had previously drawn randomly from a ~47 ps band.

THREE ASKS FROM THE ORIGINAL SCOPE THAT ARE NOT DELIVERABLE ON THIS FLOW (not oversights):
- Per-domain PDN: LibreLane/OpenROAD report PDN per design, not per clock domain. Substituted with a per-hierarchy power split.
- IR drop: analyze_power_grid fails PSM-0069 'Check connectivity failed' on BOTH rails from the M1-only tap-cell connectivity artifact (the same artifact that inflates the PDN counter). -source_type STRAPS fails identically; there is no bypass flag. pnr/config/vsrc.tcl is in place and correct. Filed separately.
- Like-for-like power: report_power attributes 0.00 W to the macros, and the 62.9 -> 51.9 mW drop coincides with the first-ever ICG insertion (USE_ICG_CELL), not the domain split. Do NOT quote multi-clock as a power win. Filed separately.

ALSO NOTE: cpu_clk covers 960 FLAT registers, not the CPU core -- the core is a hard macro closed by its own sign-off. The 960 are the CDC bridge's CPU face, the synchronisers, the clock gate and the PLL2 APB registers.

Artifacts merged in PR #135 (merge f7868b1): pnr/asap7/soc/config_multiclock.json, pnr/asap7/soc/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc, pnr/asap7/cpu/pin_order.cfg + README_pin_order.md, pnr/scripts/{check_multiclock_sdc,report_per_clock_timing,check_cdc_timing}.tcl, docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md. run 14 and pnr/asap7/soc/config.json are untouched and stay byte-reproducible as the single-clock M11 sign-off.

description:
The GH #95 cdc_snitch gate's only unwaived residue: 233 registers, all one finding.

Top-level apb_* debug ports (apb_paddr_i/psel/penable/pwrite/pwdata) feed u_cpu
directly at soc_top.sv:825-832 with NO synchroniser. GH #93 moved u_cpu onto
cpu_gated_clk, so a chip-boundary bus silently migrated from the fabric domain
into the CPU domain. Affected regs: u_cpu.dbg_pc_wr_data[*], u_cpu.dbg_ctrl_reg[*],
u_cpu.dbg_reg_wr_en, u_cpu.halt_latch_q.

Pre-#93 the implied external contract was 'drive apb_* synchronously to clk_i'.
Post-#93 it silently became 'synchronously to cpu_clk_i'. Nothing documents this.
Multi-bit paddr/pwdata means the failure mode is not just metastability but
incoherent address/data capture.

Compounding: pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc:151-155 still asserts the
opposite -- 'the APB3 debug slave sits on apb_interconnect, entirely in the fabric
(sys_clk) domain'. Harmless for timing (line 169 set_false_paths the ports) but the
rationale is now wrong and will mislead.

Options: (a) bridge it with a second apb_cdc_bridge instance, s-face clk_i /
m-face cpu_gated_clk -- restores the pre-#93 contract and makes the SDC true again,
reuses verified IP, debug is an 'infrequent config path' so latency is irrelevant;
(b) declare apb_* a cpu_clk-domain port and fix the SDC rationale + document the
external contract; (c) accepted-risk waiver and defer.

Blocks the GH #95 BAD=0 gate from going green.
close_reason: Closed

title: axi4_crossbar AR 1-cycle bubble hangs GPU reads (R_AR re-samples m_arvalid)
description: axi4_crossbar.sv read engine g_rd_engine (~lines 232-280): R_IDLE latches rsel then registers into R_AR; R_AR drives s_arvalid[gs]=m_arvalid[rsel] combinatorially. GPU compute unit (gpu_compute_unit.sv:227) asserts if_arvalid_o for exactly 1 cycle (drops when warp_busy set). Crossbar enters R_AR one cycle later, re-samples m_arvalid=0, SRAM never sees valid AR, crossbar stuck in R_AR, if_rvalid_i never returns, GPU never retires -> GPS_DONE never asserts. Not caught in Phase 4 (mock slave gave arready=1 same-cycle, crossbar not in path). Write engine g_wr_engine has same structural issue (W_AW re-samples m_awvalid) but latent: CPU D-cache holds awvalid stable per AXI4. Blocks bead 777 (SW coherency test) and likely ov2 (CPU-GPU integration). Test ready: tb/cocotb/soc/test_soc_coherency.py + coherency_fw/gen_coherency_hex.py, target soc_coherency.

title: RTL: CPU D-cache caches MMIO region — peripheral access broken at SoC level
description: M9 periph-loopback test (claude_verilog_test-k12) revealed: rv32i_core u_dcache (write-back, rv32i_core.sv:812) caches ALL dmem addresses with no uncached/device region. CPU firmware MMIO stores to 0x2000_xxxx peripheral ring are absorbed into dirty cache lines and NEVER reach the peripheral; status-register loads return a stale cached value. Proven in sim: DMA AXI-Lite ctrl slave write-valid count = 0 over 200k cycles; CPU spins forever polling DMA STATUS done bit. Blocks ALL CPU-firmware-driven peripheral control: DMA, UART, SPI, timer, IRQ ctrl, AND the future CPU->GPU kernel-launch fast-follow. FIX (architectural): add an uncached MMIO window (>=0x2000_0000 peripheral+debug region) decoded in the CPU dmem path so those accesses bypass the D-cache straight to AXI. Requires architecture decision + RTL. Delegate to chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator.
close_reason: Fixed in 9f53f65 (D-cache MMIO bypass CS_UNCACHED_RD/WR + MMIO_BASE decode) + 4ee3a9f; verified 2026-07-28 by fresh soc_periph regression: TESTS=1 PASS=1 FAIL=0, log /nobackup/soc_periph_verify/run2.log
