title: sram_controller flat mem[] read mux (r_idx-driven, 1024:1) is now the dominant ASAP7 SoC setup violator class post-rvb
description: Found 2026-09-17 during bead 0ah's combined re-run (soc-rvb-0ah, RUN_2026-09-16_19-19-45, config_multiclock_hier_rsz7_0ah.json, real in-session-GRT STAMidPNR-3). After rvb's Path A (sram_controller word_sel_q registered one-hot write pre-decode) and Path B (axi_lite_interconnect r_dvalid_q/r_ddata_q registered read stage) fixes, the SoC's #1 worst-slack setup violator class is no longer either rvb target. Worst path: u_sram._276653_/QN (a flat mem[] read-data storage flop) -> combinational 1024:1 read mux (assign s_rdata = mem[r_idx], rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv:359, selected by the registered read index r_idx declared at line 315 and captured at line 330) -> u_bus.u_xbar -> u_dma.*/D, worst slack -1144.52 ps (setup WNS at STAMidPNR-3). This class accounts for 9259/40202 (23%) of all setup violators in the final STAMidPNR-3 violator_list.rpt, the largest single class (u_dma capture-side aggregation aside). This is the module's own documented characteristic (sram_controller.sv:6-8, 20-22): 'the flat array synthesizes to ~32K flip-flops plus a huge combinational 1024:1 read mux' -- pre-existing, not introduced by rvb; rvb's fixes simply removed the two paths that previously masked it (Path A/B slacks were worse: -2084 ps and comparable pre-rvb).
design: Candidate fix (NOT applied, needs human architecture approval): register the SRAM read data and/or the read-index pre-decode inside sram_controller.sv's flat-array (ifndef SRAM_SKY130) branch, mirroring the SRAM_SKY130 branch's existing 2-3 cycle registered/skid-buffered read path (sram_controller.sv:20-37). Adds read latency (currently 0 extra cycles per the module header, 'RDATA is valid the cycle RVALID is asserted') -- the AXI4 read FSM and any timing-sensitive cocotb tests assuming 0-latency reads would need review. Alternative: swap to a real ASAP7 SRAM macro for the ASAP7 SoC flow the way SRAM_SKY130 already does for Sky130 (reopens the locked Phase-5 behavioral-SRAM decision, larger effort, consistent with bead rvb's own remedy #2 for Path A). Do not implement without explicit approval -- physical-design-orchestrator has no RTL-change authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed (this bead) via violator_list.rpt + RTL file:line citation. Closed when either: (a) a human-approved RTL fix (registered read pre-decode or SRAM macro swap) is implemented and re-measured to remove this class from the worst-path list, or (b) an explicit decision is recorded to accept it as a residual/architectural limitation of the flat behavioral SRAM model for ASAP7.
notes:
RTL fix implemented on branch feat/ydw-sram-registered-read, commit 339f83a.

Design: registered the flat-array read (ifndef SRAM_SKY130) mux output into a
single head register (r_data_q/r_valid_q/r_last_q) instead of driving s_rdata
combinationally off mem[r_idx]. Read FSM (R_IDLE/R_BUSY):
  r_issue_now = r_active && (!r_valid_q || s_rready)
fetches mem[r_idx] into the head whenever it's empty or draining this cycle.
Select path: r_idx is a plain register (set on AR-accept, incremented in the
sequential block) -- never a live rready-gated expression in front of the
1024:1 mux, so the mux's only fan-out is the one head register.

Latency: burst-start latency 1 cycle -> 2 cycles (+1 cycle, first beat only).
Sustained throughput unchanged: continuous RREADY still streams 1 beat/cycle
(next word lands the same cycle the old one is consumed, no bubble).
RVALID/RDATA/RLAST hold stable under RVALID && !RREADY (verified by test,
no drop/dup). FIXED vs INCR, SLVERR, MEM_WORDS wraparound unchanged.

Read-after-write analysis: checked axi4_crossbar.sv (not assumed) --
write/read engines are independent, depth-1-outstanding per slave, with NO
ordering interlock between a concurrent AR and in-flight AW to the same slave
(axi4_crossbar.sv:9, 22-27: "a master that requires read-after-write
ordering... must wait for B before AR"). So a write landing on an address
already prefetched into the stalled head is a reachable race, not one ruled
out by the fabric. Conclusion: not fixed with a bypass -- AXI4 defines no
ordering guarantee for this case either way, this SoC's coherency is
entirely software-managed (CPU flushes/invalidates D-cache around GPU
launches per CLAUDE.md), and a same-address forward-compare bypass would
need to index the MEM_WORDS-wide one-hot write-select vector, reintroducing
the class of wide mux this fix removes. Documented in-RTL as an accepted,
pre-existing-class residual, with a narrow one-hot AND/OR-reduce bypass
sketched (not implemented) for future use if a hardware guarantee is ever
needed.

title: cpu_clk clock-tree skew regression post-GRT: -823ps (post-CTS) -> -1688ps at u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo
description:
On the ASAP7 SoC (current RTL, deferred_flatten, w3a's fixed CTS + bounded repair, bead w3a), the worst hold clock skew regresses substantially between post-CTS-repair and honestly-annotated post-GRT STA, isolated to the cpu_clk domain:

  checkpoint                                worst hold skew   worst-skew instance                    source latency   target latency
  attempt4 07-openroad-stamidpnr-2 (post-CTS repair)  -823.51 ps   u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo._2812_/CLK      148.53 ps        -962.04 ps
  w3a-sta-7 (honest post-GRT STA, in-session GRT)    -1687.92 ps  u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo._2786_/CLK      188.71 ps       -1866.63 ps

(Both from the flow's own skew.min.rpt at each checkpoint -- no live diagnostic session needed, direct read of existing reports.)

KEY OBSERVATIONS:
1. The regression is CONFINED to the cpu_clk domain. sys_clk's own worst-skew reference sink (u_gif_adapter._505_/CLK, chosen by the same report as the "other" clock's entry) actually IMPROVED over the same interval: +237.07 ps (post-CTS) -> +442.08 ps (post-GRT), both benign/positive.
2. Source latency (the domain's best-case clock arrival, from u_cpu_iso_en_sync._7_/CLK in both reports) is roughly stable (148.5 -> 188.7 ps) -- the regression is entirely in the TARGET latency (how late the clock arrives at this specific cluster), which nearly doubled (-962.0 -> -1866.6 ps).
3. The worst instance moved from u_w_fifo._2812_ to a different flop in the same submodule (u_w_fifo._2786_) -- consistent with a whole CLUSTER (the CPU-side write-FIFO's clock branch inside u_cpu_axi_cdc, the CPU<->fabric async_axi_fifo CDC bridge) getting uniformly worse, not one outlier flop.
4. This was ALREADY the worst cpu_clk hold-skew site post-CTS (-823.5 ps, itself a real, un-zero residual) -- post-GRT does not introduce a new weak point, it makes an EXISTING one substantially worse once real routing (rather than a placement-based Steiner-tree estimate) is used for the same clock branch.

READING: most consistent with a genuine ROUTING DETOUR revealed by real GRT routing to reach the u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo cluster (e.g. routing around the CPU macro's blockage, or through a congested channel) that the placement-based CTS estimate did not predict -- NOT the same "TritonCTS Skipping" mechanism already fixed by DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS (that was sys_clk-specific and is confirmed still fixed: cpu_gated_clk_regs's H-tree is intact and this instance IS part of that tree, just its worst branch). Also not fully explainable as a placement-estimate-vs-annotated-parasitics artifact alone, since the effect is isolated to one physical cluster and moves the WRONG direction relative to sys_clk's own estimate-to-real transition (which improved).

CANDIDATE NEXT STEPS (not evaluated in detail -- flagged for whoever picks this up):
- Floorplan-level: review u_cpu_axi_cdc's placement relative to the CPU macro and the cpu_clk source/PLL stub; a macro-halo-driven detour is plausible given the CPU hard macro's known boundary-pin exposure (see docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md's macro-related caveats).
- CTS-level: CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE/MAX_DIAMETER for cpu_clk are already at aggressive settings (8 / 10 um, tuned once before per config_multiclock_hier.json's GH96_COMMENT_4 for a different cpu_clk imbalance) -- further CTS-only tuning may have diminishing returns without addressing the underlying physical detour.
- Accept as a residual hold-timing risk requiring targeted hold-buffer padding on this branch specifically, if floorplan/CTS changes are not pursued.

Linked to bead w3a (this was found during w3a's honest post-GRT STA close-out) but filed separately since it is a timing-only, non-convergence issue -- w3a's own acceptance criterion (every repair stage terminates, reaches honest post-GRT STA) is unaffected by this residual.
design: Read-only finding from existing skew.min.rpt files at two checkpoints (attempt4 07-openroad-stamidpnr-2 and w3a-sta-7's 01-openroad-stamidpnr-3) -- no live diagnostic session was needed since both reports already existed on disk.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of the routing detour (or alternative explanation) confirmed via placement/routing visualization or a targeted incremental floorplan experiment, AND either a fix applied that restores skew to closer to the post-CTS -823ps baseline or lower, OR an explicit decision recorded to accept it as a residual hold-timing risk with hold-buffer mitigation.

ROOT CAUSE of the reference run's clean hold, re-investigated (read-only:
diffed 31-openroad-cts/openroad-cts.log and 30-openroad-detailedplacement/soc_top.def
between RUN_2026-09-16_19-19-45 [reference] and RUN_2026-09-17_06-25-54 [soc-ydw,
same config, ydw RTL = reference RTL + 36 new sys_clk-domain flops for registered
SRAM read data]):

- Macro placement is IDENTICAL in both runs (u_cpu FIXED (365000,15000), u_gpu FIXED
  (15000,15000) -- confirmed byte-identical DEF coordinates). Macro movement is ruled
  out.
- clk_i (sys_clk) sink count: reference 45305 (1 macro + 45304 regs, SPLIT);
  soc-ydw 45340 (NOT split, single tree). The +35 delta is consistent with ydw's
  +36 new sys_clk flops (off by one, plausibly one flop lands on a different net/
  domain). This net's sink-count change is real and RTL-driven.
- cpu_clk_i (cpu_clk) sink count: IDENTICAL in both runs, 172 (reference: 1 macro +
  171 regs, SPLIT; soc-ydw: 172, NOT split). cpu_clk_i's own sinks did not change
  between runs (no CPU-domain RTL changed), yet its split behaviour changed anyway.
  This rules out "this net's own sink count" as the per-net trigger and points to a
  SESSION-WIDE (not per-net) internal mode selection in TritonCTS -- i.e. whatever
  decided to skip the macro/regs split affected the whole clock_tree_synthesis
  invocation, not just the net whose sinks actually grew.
- Direct log evidence of a different internal code path: reference prints
  "blockages from hard placement blockages and placed macros will be used"
  (CTS-0201) six times (once per net) and NEVER prints CTS-0200 at all. soc-ydw
  prints a DIFFERENT message pair, "0 placement blockages have been identified"
  (CTS-0200) followed by "placed hard macros will be treated like blockages"
  (CTS-0201), four times (once per net). Same message ID (CTS-0201) with two
  different message strings, on the exact same OpenROAD 26Q2 binary (bundled shim,
  verified identical in both runs) -- this is strong evidence TritonCTS has (at
  least) two internal blockage/macro-handling branches and the two runs took
  different ones.
- "Repairing long wires on clock nets" also differs (reference: 3 buffers in 1 net;
  soc-ydw: 5 buffers in 3 nets), consistent with a genuinely different clock-tree
  topology, not a cosmetic logging difference.

HYPOTHESIS (medium confidence -- log-evidence-based, NOT confirmed against
TritonCTS source, which is not available locally for this closed-source-packaged
nix build; no bisection/empirical test was run per the no-new-runs instruction):
OpenROAD 26Q2's TritonCTS auto-selects between two internal macro/blockage-handling
algorithms based on an internal, undocumented threshold -- most plausibly tied to
total sink count/density on the clock net(s) it processes in a given
clock_tree_synthesis call (clk_i's sink count grew from 45305 to 45340, crossing
whatever that threshold is) -- and the selection is made ONCE per invocation/session
rather than per net, which is why cpu_clk_i's unchanged-sink-count net was still
affected. clock_tree_synthesis takes no explicit seed/randomization flag in this
build's help text, so the tool itself is very likely deterministic given fixed
inputs (ODB+SDC+config) -- the run-to-run difference is best explained by the real
RTL/netlist/placement difference between the two runs (ydw's +36 flops), not by
tool non-determinism.

CTS_MACRO_CLUSTERING_MAX_DIAMETER), and register four corresponding Variable
objects (two Optional[bool], two Optional[Decimal], mirroring the existing
CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE / CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_MAX_DIAMETER pattern already in
this file's Config schema) in the CTS step's class so the config validator accepts
the keys instead of warning "unknown key" and silently dropping them. Explicitly
forcing obstruction-aware mode plus macro-clustering size/diameter (matched to the
existing sink-clustering size/diameter values, 8/10) would make the macro/regs
split + latency-balancing behaviour explicit and deterministic, rather than left to
TritonCTS's undocumented internal sink-count-driven default -- reproducing the
reference run's good behaviour reliably regardless of incidental RTL-size changes
elsewhere in the design.

2. So the actual comparison this whole investigation has been making is:

  OpenROAD.CheckAntennas        antenna_check.tcl           N/A (no estimate_parasitics call)

Direct log evidence, attempt4's actual run

openroad-repairdesignpostgrt.log): a real global_route ran before repair_design --

against it: "[INFO RSZ-0038] Inserted 535 buffers in 1996 nets", "[INFO RSZ-0039] Resized 430
instances". No annotation-gate output is in that log because the gate (bead 8f3) had only been
added to rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl at the time. FIXED: added the same
ol_check_postgrt_parasitic_annotation call to repair_design_postgrt.tcl (report-only, no new

common/io.tcl proc) so the next run confirms this numerically rather than by code+log inference.

git apply --check clean). NOT applied to the shared tree -- awaiting go-ahead; it's independent

title: sram_controller flat per-bit write decode + u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid 18.5k fanout makes post-CTS setup repair non-terminating on deferred_flatten netlist
description:
ASAP7 SoC (current RTL, config_multiclock_hier*.json, SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE=deferred_flatten) cannot complete OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostCTS in reasonable time. Three attempts (bead w3a) all converge on the same worst endpoint, u_sram._244155_/D, oscillating rather than closing:

- Run 8 (default resizer settings): 30039->23374 violators by iter ~1200, then frozen (no progress) for 140+ logged iterations, then >1h silent hang. Stopped.
- Attempt 1 (w3a-rsz-1: buffer budget 15%, gate cloning off): violator count never moved off 30039 through iteration 540. Strictly worse than run 8. Stopped.
- Attempt 2 (w3a-rsz-2: gate cloning restored, buffer budget 50%, setup slack margin 45->5 ps): ran 73 min / 1040+ iterations. Best WNS -435.092 ps at iteration 490 (best TNS ~-3.167e6 near iter 710); by iteration 1040 WNS had drifted back to -523.763 ps. Violator count frozen at exactly 27550 for the ENTIRE run -- never repairs even one endpoint. WNS/TNS visibly OSCILLATE in a band (e.g. -519.823/-3375780 <-> -523.763/-3197678 <-> -529.856/-3241155, repeating) rather than converging. Stopped by coordinator.

KEY COMPARISON: run 5 (run 23's FLAT netlist -- SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE=flatten, not deferred_flatten -- with the ORIGINAL unmodified resizer config) COMPLETED this same step normally, finishing at WNS -389.8 ps / 34085 violators (resized 304, inserted 54, cloned 191 actions). So the non-terminating behaviour is specific to the deferred_flatten netlist, even though the sram_controller / u_gpu-m_axi_wvalid structure exists identically in both netlists' RTL source.

ROOT-CAUSE PATH EVIDENCE (read-only OpenSTA session on run 8's post-CTS ODB, report_checks -to u_sram._244155_/D): at the pristine post-CTS baseline (before any resizer action) this endpoint is MET at +192.89 ps. Full path: Startpoint u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid (GPU macro's AXI write-valid output register, sys_clk) -> crossbar arbitration/decode logic (AOI31/NOR3/AND5 gates) -> bus_mem_wvalid -> sram_controller's write-enable/index-decode chain (AND5/NAND5/OAI22 gates) -> u_sram._244155_/D, one of ~32768 individual per-bit flops in the flat behavioral `mem[]` array (rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv:128, `logic [DW-1:0] mem [0:MEM_WORDS-1]`, MEM_WORDS=1024, each byte lane gated `if (s_wstrb[b]) mem[w_idx][b*8+:8] <= s_wdata[...]` inside `if (s_wvalid)` at lines ~191-197). This is the module's own documented characteristic (header comment, sram_controller.sv:6-8: "the flat array synthesizes to ~32K flip-flops plus a huge combinational 1024:1 read mux" -- the write-side per-bit decode is structurally the same class of problem, not previously called out by name).

u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid is the SAME net bead je8/86a's 2026-09-14 diagnosis found fanning out to 18584 endpoints post-repair (37.6x run 23's 494) -- present in BOTH flat (run 5/run 23) and deferred_flatten (run 8) synthesis, so hierarchy mode alone does not explain the fanout SIZE, but it evidently changes the resizer's ability to converge on it (run 5 flat completes; every deferred_flatten attempt oscillates on the same endpoint).

CONCLUSION: this endpoint only becomes the frozen/oscillating worst violator DURING repair, not at baseline. The setup-repair algorithm's own buffer/resize actions on OTHER endpoints sharing this physical buffer tree collaterally degrade this endpoint's slack, and it then oscillates trying to re-fix it without escaping (every local fix perturbs the shared tree's loading and can un-fix a sibling endpoint on the same tree) -- specifically on the deferred_flatten netlist, not the flat one. This is a genuine single-cycle sys_clk->sys_clk functional path (s_wvalid gates a real write commit), not an SDC exception candidate.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES (require human architecture decision -- RTL changes are out of scope for the physical-design-orchestrator's authorisation on this task):
1. Register/pipeline the write-enable/index-decode path in sram_controller.sv so the huge per-bit fanout tree has a natural pipeline stage to land in, instead of being one long combinational decode from s_wvalid/w_idx all the way to each of the 32768 bit-flops' write-select.
2. Use a real SRAM macro instead of the flat behavioral array for ASAP7/FreePDK45 flows, the way SRAM_SKY130 already does for Sky130 (rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv already has the `\`ifdef SRAM_SKY130` structure and an existing stub/macro pattern for the CPU/GPU caches to follow -- would need an ASAP7-side SRAM macro or stub equivalent).
3. Flatten sram_controller specifically (a targeted, not global, hierarchy-mode change) while keeping deferred_flatten elsewhere, if LibreLane's SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE can be scoped per-module -- unconfirmed, needs investigation, and still doesn't explain why run 5's FULLY flat netlist has the same underlying 18.5k-fanout structure yet converges (may be a flattening-ORDER or ABC-optimization-pass difference between deferred_flatten's two-phase synth and single-phase flat synth, not flatness per se).
4. A max_fanout constraint targeted at this net/class of net (MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT is already 16 globally and evidently insufficient to prevent the aggregate endpoint-count blowup, since each individual buffer stage IS within the 16-fanout limit -- the problem is tree depth/breadth in aggregate, not any single illegal-fanout node).

Immediate mitigation being tried in parallel (bead w3a, does not require RTL changes): LibreLane hook PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES (wiring OpenROAD's native `repair_timing -max_passes`, which LibreLane 2.4.13 never exposed) to bound the repair step's wall time and accept a residual, honestly-reported violation rather than hang. This unblocks the PD flow pipeline but does NOT fix the underlying timing -- with a passes bound, the design will not actually meet timing at this endpoint (and likely its whole shared-tree family), so signoff-quality closure still requires one of the four remedies above.
design: Preferred order pending human review: (1) register/pipeline the write-enable decode -- smallest RTL delta, preserves the flat-array model, most likely to also help correctness/EM in other domains, but adds a cycle of write latency the AXI protocol/FSM must account for. (2) SRAM macro swap -- most robust long-term fix and consistent with the Sky130 precedent, but adds macro characterization + PDN work (see bead 86a's experience with macro power/timing view generation) and is the largest effort. (3) targeted hierarchy-mode scoping -- cheapest to TRY but unproven and doesn't have a clear mechanism given run 5's flat netlist has the same fanout structure. (4) fanout constraint -- unlikely to help alone since the existing 16-fanout cap is already respected locally; listed for completeness.
acceptance_criteria: Human/architecture decision recorded on this bead selecting one of the four remedies (or another), OR an explicit decision to accept the PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES-bounded residual violation as a known, documented limitation of the ASAP7/FreePDK45 flat-SRAM-array PD flow going forward.

- Path B (post-GRT, u_bus.u_periph_bridge.*_/D): gpu_top.sv:298-321 is a purely combinational ~15-arm case-mux for s_axil_rdata (no output register) -> soc_bus.sv wiring -> axi_lite_interconnect.sv:237,254 (second combinational ring mux, m_axil_rdata=s_axil_rdata[rsel]) -> axi4_to_axilite.sv:239,251,262,282 (rdata_q <= m_axil_rdata, the first register in the whole chain). Path A (rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv, option A2 - registered one-hot word-select pre-decode):
- Declarations (ifdef SRAM_SKY130 vs ifndef split, ~line 162-193): added word_onehot() decode function and a MEM_WORDS-wide word_sel_q register (ifndef SRAM_SKY130 only; w_idx kept as-is under ifdef SRAM_SKY130, untouched).
- FSM always_ff (~line 198-249): W_IDLE now registers word_sel_q <= word_onehot(word_index(s_awaddr)) on awvalid accept (same cycle w_idx used to be captured -- no new cycle). W_DATA's burst-increment branch rotates word_sel_q by 1 bit (equivalent to +1 mod MEM_WORDS since MEM_WORDS is required power-of-two) instead of incrementing w_idx, under the identical `!w_err && w_incr` gate as before.
- New block (~line 257-284, ifndef SRAM_SKY130): w_commit = (wstate==W_DATA) && s_wvalid && !w_err (identical gating to the original nested if); word_we = word_sel_q & {MEM_WORDS{w_commit}} (MEM_WORDS AND2 gates -- s_wvalid's fanout reduced from every storage bit to MEM_WORDS gates); a generate-for loop of MEM_WORDS independent always_ff blocks does the actual mem[gw] byte-strobed write, gated by word_we[gw]. w_err/wstrb/wlast semantics unchanged -- verified by the full 11/11 test_sram_controller.py suite (flat-array target), including burst writes, wstrb partial, back-to-back bursts, and read-after-write-no-gap.

- SRAM_SKY130 branch untouched (mem_addr0=w_idx path unchanged); verified via lint_soc_sky130 target (0 errors, no new warnings).

Path B (rtl/soc/axi_lite_interconnect.sv, option B2 - register m_axil_rdata inside the interconnect):
- Added a registered stage (r_dvalid_q/r_ddata_q/r_dresp_q, ~line after r_hs decl) capturing the rsel-based mux's output (r_dvalid_d/r_ddata_d/r_dresp_d, renamed from what used to drive m_axil_r* directly) one cycle later. r_dreg_ready = !r_dvalid_q || m_axil_rready (accept-into-register qualifier) gates both the register load and the new _s_rready[rsel] drive (replacing the old direct m_axil_rready passthrough) -- depends only on the registered r_dvalid_q and the external m_axil_rready input, so no combinational READY->VALID loop.
- Read FSM (R_IDLE/R_AR/R_DATA) and r_hs definition unchanged; since this ring is single-outstanding (depth-1), R_DATA does not return to R_IDLE until r_hs (m_axil_rvalid && m_axil_rready, now measuring the *registered* beat's drain) fires, so there is no overlap hazard between back-to-back transactions and the 1-deep register.
- Latency impact: +1 cycle of AXI-Lite read latency on the ring->CPU leg (RVALID/RDATA appear one cycle later than the prior direct passthrough), for both mapped-slave and DECERR responses. AXI4-Lite's VALID/READY handshake has no fixed-latency requirement -- protocol legal. This ring has exactly one master (the CPU config path, per this module's own "SINGLE-MASTER ONLY" design note) which by definition tolerates arbitrary RVALID latency (that's the AXI-Lite handshake contract), so every master on this ring tolerates it.
- gpu_top.sv NOT touched -- no GPU macro re-harden, per instruction.

UPDATE (bead w3a closed, 2026-09-16): the RTL agent has published docs/design/RVB_FANOUT_FIX_PROPOSAL.md (commit 5ddc87d), which formally covers BOTH fan-out paths this bead's history touched on:
  - Path A (post-CTS setup) = this bead's original finding: u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid -> sram_controller write-enable/index-decode fan-out.
  - Path B (post-GRT setup) = u_gpu AXI-Lite s_axil_rdata -> u_bus.u_periph_bridge register fan-out, a missing pipeline register at/near a macro boundary on a long, physically-distant net.

Path B is CONFIRMED as a real, current-RTL, honestly-measured residual by w3a's final honest post-GRT STA (w3a-sta-7, in-session GRT parasitics, annotation proven ~0.7% unannotated): post-GRT setup WS -2084.08 ps, TNS -2.19e7, 41864 violators, with the worst endpoints on exactly this u_gpu-s_axil_rdata-to-u_periph_bridge path (matching the earlier w3a-rsz-4/rsz-6 diagnostic finding in full: buffers removed by repair_timing's own internal buffer-removal step on this specific wide-fanout net caused a 5x WNS blowup before -skip_buffer_removal was applied as a bounded mitigation -- the mitigation stops the divergence but does not close the underlying gap, which the RTL proposal's Path B analysis explains structurally). Cross-referencing rather than duplicating -- no new bead filed for Path B; it is already the proposal's B.2 section.

DOES THE POST-CTS SETUP OSCILLATION (Path A) STILL REPRODUCE with the real clock tree? NO -- it does not reproduce as originally observed. With DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS=true (the w3a CTS fix) giving TritonCTS a real, balanced sys_clk H-tree, attempt 4's post-CTS ResizerTimingPostCTS (config_multiclock_hier_rsz4.json, bounded MAX_PASSES=1 + "-repair_tns 5") COMPLETED NORMALLY in ~16 min via RSZ-0062, with real progress: WNS -737.319->-656.523 ps, TNS -5581166->-3114485 ps (-44%), violators 27550->20453 (-26%) -- and the FOLLOW-ON post-CTS-repair checkpoint (attempt4 step 07) reported setup WS -323.4 ps / TNS -1.128e6 / 16680 viol, which already BEATS run 23's -384.3 ps / -1.772e6. So the non-terminating OSCILLATION this bead documented (attempts 1/2/run8, all on the BROKEN clock tree with core_clk never CTS-treed) does not reproduce once the clock tree is real -- the bounded repair converges instead of oscillating. The underlying Path A fan-out STRUCTURE (sram_controller's ~32K-flop write decode) is unchanged and still real per the RTL proposal's analysis, but its PD symptom changed from "non-terminating oscillation" to "a real, honestly-repairable partial violation" -- a meaningfully different (and less severe) failure class than originally filed. This bead's title/description describe the OSCILLATION specifically; that symptom is resolved. The underlying RTL-level Path A structure remains open pending the proposal's approval (bead's own acceptance criterion: human architecture decision on B.1's shortlist) -- recommend keeping this bead open for that RTL decision, now correctly scoped as "Path A structural fix pending approval" rather than "PD flow cannot terminate."

Diagnosis (2026-09-15): openroad -no_init -exit 'help repair_timing' (edf00dff, this host) confirms OpenROAD's repair_timing supports -max_passes, but LibreLane 2.4.13's scripts/openroad/rsz_timing_postcts.tcl (shared tree ~/Downloads/Github/librelane, out of scope to edit for this task) never wires that flag to an env var -- so there is genuinely no LibreLane-level iteration cap for ResizerTimingPostCTS, confirming the bead description. Only two setup-phase levers exist in that script: PL_RESIZER_SETUP_MAX_BUFFER_PCT (-max_buffer_percent) and PL_RESIZER_GATE_CLONING (-skip_gate_cloning). Run 8's frozen state (192 buffers/186 clones, unchanged for 140+ iterations, then total silence >1h) is far short of the default 50% buffer budget, so gate-clone oscillation on the pathological endpoint (u_sram._244155_/D, sram_controller behavioral flop-array D pin) is the leading hypothesis, not budget exhaustion.

Attempt 1 LAUNCHED 21:15 UTC+7, detached, unit w3a-rsz-1.scope (MemoryMax=9500M, MemorySwapMax=0), run dir /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/RUN_2026-09-15_21-15-05, log /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/w3a_rsz_1.log. comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
ATTEMPT 1 RESULT (stopped, worse than run 8): w3a-rsz-1 (MAX_BUFFER_PCT 15, GATE_CLONING false) never moved violators off 30039 through iteration 540 (~1 min); run 8 with default GATE_CLONING=true DID improve 30039->23374 before plateauing. Disabling cloning was the wrong call -- stopped via systemctl --user stop w3a-rsz-1.scope.

ROOT CAUSE (read-only OpenSTA session, run 8's post-CTS ODB 31-openroad-cts/soc_top.odb, same libs/SDC/RC, estimate_parasitics -placement, report_checks -to u_sram._244155_/D): at the pristine post-CTS baseline (no resizer action yet) this endpoint is MET at +192.89 ps -- NOT violating. Full path: Startpoint u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid (GPU macro AXI write-valid reg, sys_clk) -> crossbar arbitration/decode (AOI31/NOR3/AND5) -> bus_mem_wvalid -> sram_controller write-enable/index-decode chain (AND5/NAND5/OAI22) -> u_sram._244155_/D, one of ~32768 per-bit flops in the flat behavioral `mem[]` array (rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv:128, MEM_WORDS=1024, per-byte gated writes at lines ~191-197). This is the module's own documented characteristic (header comment: "the flat array synthesizes to ~32K flip-flops plus a huge combinational 1024:1 read mux" -- the write-side per-bit decode is structurally the same class of problem).

u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid is the SAME net bead je8/86a's 2026-09-14 diagnosis found fans out to 18584 endpoints post-repair (37.6x run 23's 494) -- present in BOTH flat (run 5) and deferred_flatten (run 8) synthesis, so hierarchy mode is not the primary driver.

CONCLUSION: this endpoint only becomes the frozen worst violator DURING repair, not at baseline -- the setup-repair algorithm's own actions on OTHER endpoints sharing this physical buffer tree collaterally degrade it, and the algorithm oscillates trying to re-fix it without escaping (every local fix perturbs the shared tree and can un-fix a sibling). This is a genuine single-cycle sys_clk->sys_clk functional path (s_wvalid gates a real write commit) -- NOT an SDC exception candidate, would hide a real path. Synthesis hierarchy change (flatten sram_controller) is not well-supported: the fanout blowup already existed in run 5's flat synthesis vs run 23's flat baseline, and a resynthesis experiment is too slow for this iteration. If neither resizer-setting attempt converges, the true fix is architectural (RTL: more buffering headroom on the write-enable/index decode, or move ASAP7/FreePDK45 off the flat per-bit-flop array the way SRAM_SKY130 already does) -- out of scope here (no RTL edits authorised); would need to be reported, not worked around.

ATTEMPT 2 LAUNCHED 21:47 (UTC+7), unit w3a-rsz-2.scope (MemoryMax=9500M), run dir /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/RUN_2026-09-15_21-47-49 (pending confirm), log /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/w3a_rsz_2.log. Same seed/stop points as attempt 1 (--with-initial-state run 8 step 32, --from OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostCTS --to OpenROAD.STAMidPNR-2).

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
HOLD-PHASE DIAGNOSIS (read-only, w3a-diag4/4b.scope, 4G, foreground, run 8's PRISTINE post-CTS ODB 31-openroad-cts, flow's own libs/SDC/RC -- w3a-rsz-3 NOT touched).

CONFIRMS ATTEMPT 3 STATUS: setup repair genuinely TERMINATED via RSZ-0062 after ~36 min (real progress: WNS -737.319->-656.523 ps, TNS -5581166->-3114485 (44% reduction), violators 27550->20453 (26% reduction) -- best result of any attempt so far). Hold repair then started (RSZ-0046: 45405 endpoints), and as of this diagnosis (27+ min of log silence, past the coordinator's 00:49 stall flag) it is genuinely STALLED at iteration 0, same failure class as the setup-phase oscillation.

1) HOLD VIOLATOR BREAKDOWN (async SETN/RESETN vs real D-pin data paths):
Scanned every RESETN/SETN pin on every *rst_sync*-named register (je8's own cdc_reset_sync_async_pins pattern) across both clocks: 36 pin objects exist, but only 14 have an actual timing arc (report_checks -to; the other 22 report "No paths found" -- RESETN vs SETN is mutually exclusive per instance depending on active polarity). Of those 14 real checks: 10 PASS (+5.43 to +728.36 ps) and exactly 4 VIOLATE:
  u_apb_dbg_cdc.u_m_rst_sync._12_/SETN   -703.63 ps
  u_apb_dbg_cdc.u_m_rst_sync._13_/SETN   -703.64 ps  <- attempt 3's reported worst hold endpoint
  u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_s_rst_sync._12_/SETN   -671.41 ps
  u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_s_rst_sync._13_/SETN   -671.62 ps
So the async-pin class is 4 out of 45405 violators -- 0.0088%. The other 45401 (99.99%) are ordinary D-pin / real data-path hold violations, e.g. u_spi.u_regbank._2356_/D at -850.17 ps and a async_axi_fifo D pin (u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_b_fifo._210_/D) at -675.01 ps -- comparable to or WORSE than the async pin's own -703.64 ps. Worst-10 min-path dump (report_checks -path_delay min -group_count 10) independently found u_spi.u_regbank._2287_/CLK's D-pin check violating -845.88 ps.

2) SKEW DOMINATES, NOT LOGIC DEPTH: the flow's own report_clock_skew -hold (reproduced live in this diagnostic, bit-identical to run 8's real skew.min.rpt from step 32-openroad-stamidpnr-1) shows:
  sys_clk worst hold skew: -1165.02 ps, target latency at u_spi.u_regbank._2313_/CLK (source latency 331.07 ps, target latency -1486.09 ps)
  cpu_clk worst hold skew: -941.24 ps, target latency at u_apb_dbg_cdc.u_m_rst_sync._13_/CLK (source latency 260.57 ps, target latency -1191.81 ps)
-1165 ps is 66.6% of the 1750 ps sys_clk period; -941 ps is 120.7% of the 780 ps cpu_clk period. These are not ordinary CTS imbalance -- they are extreme, and the WORST-SKEW instances are the SAME instances (u_spi.u_regbank, u_apb_dbg_cdc.u_m_rst_sync) that dominate the violator list. This is a genuine CTS clock-tree-construction defect on specific branches (u_spi and the u_apb_dbg_cdc/u_cpu_axi_cdc CDC bridges), not a fundamentally unfixable logic/architecture problem the way the setup-side SRAM issue (bead rvb) was. Hold buffering can typically only absorb tens of ps per stage; closing an 850-1165 ps deficit per path, across tens of thousands of paths sharing the same defective branch, is why a single bounded pass (MAX_PASSES=1) is still not converging -- this matches the shared-tree hook's own amendment-comment warning (rsz_timing_postcts.tcl:50-59) precisely.

3) WHY RUN 23/RUN 5 DIDN'T HIT THIS: run 23's hold repair started with only 4232 violating endpoints (vs 45405 here, ~10.7x) and closed cleanly to +25.000 ps / TNS 0. Run 5 (flat, same original config) started with 4735 and also closed cleanly. Both are flat-synthesis runs; this run (run 8's seed) is deferred_flatten. Combined with the setup-phase finding (bead rvb: run 5's flat netlist completed setup repair normally, deferred_flatten's did not, on the identical RTL), this is now the SECOND independent symptom pointing at deferred_flatten's two-phase synth (or its resulting CTS behaviour) producing meaningfully worse post-CTS timing than flat synthesis on this design -- not just for the one pathological SRAM endpoint, but for hold skew broadly.

4) RECOMMENDATION for the smallest correct change:
(a) SDC exception for the 4 real async-pin violators -- CORRECT and justified (exact same RTL classification already proven in pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc:518-598, "sec.10a cdc_reset_sync async set/reset pins... excluded from domain-wide max_delay fallback", currently applied ONLY to the CDC-checker SDC, not the PNR_SDC_FILE actually used during resize/hold-repair). Should be applied (mirroring the same set_false_path -to [cdc_reset_sync_async_pins] pattern into phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc) regardless of what else is decided -- but by itself fixes 4 of 45405 endpoints (0.0088%) and will NOT unblock the stall.
(b) Bounding hold effort via PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT / PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN: unlike setup (where a 15% buffer cap was proven NOT binding, since only ~190 buffers were ever used), hold repair's fix mechanism (buffer insertion in series along each violating path) is the mechanism actually being exercised at scale, so a buffer-budget cap is much more likely to be the FIRST thing hit for hold specifically -- worth trying (e.g. lower PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT well below the current default 50%, never explicitly set in any w3a config) to force an earlier RSZ-0062-equivalent bail rather than an unbounded pass-1 thrash. Trade-off: still leaves the vast majority of the 45401 non-async violators unrepaired (honest residual, matching the acceptance criterion), and does not address the root cause.
(c) Accept post-CTS hold repair cannot meaningfully close at this skew magnitude and treat it as informational only, relying on post-GRT resizer for hold: risk -- post-GRT repair_timing gets the SAME PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES bound but does NOT get PL_RESIZER_TIMING_EXTRA_ARGS spliced onto ITS hold call either (confirmed: EXTRA_ARGS is setup-only in both rsz_timing_postcts.tcl and, per the shared-tree pattern, presumably rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl too), and the underlying skew defect is a CTS-stage property that persists into GRT unchanged -- so post-GRT hold repair is likely to hit the identical stall, just later in the flow after global routing's own ~8 GB / lengthy cost has already been paid.

NONE of (a)/(b)/(c) fixes the root cause, which is CTS-stage: the u_spi and u_apb_dbg_cdc/u_cpu_axi_cdc clock-tree branches are enormously under-buffered/imbalanced relative to the rest of their domains. That is a 4th class of fix (CTS retuning, e.g. CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE/MAX_DIAMETER, which this project has tuned before for a related cpu_clk imbalance -- see config_multiclock_hier.json's GH96_COMMENT_4) and was explicitly out of scope for this diagnosis. Recommend treating it the same way as bead rvb: file for architecture/PD-lead review rather than keep bounding resizer knobs against a CTS-level defect.

Given the pattern (setup: deferred_flatten-specific non-convergence on one pathological structure, closed via max_passes+repair_tns; hold: deferred_flatten-specific ~10x worse violator count from extreme CTS skew, not closeable by the same bound), my overall read is that config_multiclock_hier*.json's SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE=deferred_flatten (adopted for host-RAM reasons, bead je8/2kn) may be producing a CTS input netlist/floorplan meaningfully worse than flat synthesis for THIS design, independent of and in addition to the SRAM write-decode issue in bead rvb. Not conclusively proven (no controlled deferred_flatten-vs-flat CTS comparison exists on current RTL), but both independent symptoms point the same direction and are worth flagging together when this goes to human review.

No changes launched or made to any file (read-only diagnosis per instruction). w3a-rsz-3 untouched throughout.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
CLOCK-TREE ROOT-CAUSE (read-only, w3a-diag5.scope, 4G, foreground, run 8's post-CTS ODB 31-openroad-cts + its own netlist/logs -- no run launched, no files changed).

DEFINITIVE FINDING: TritonCTS built a real H-tree for ONLY ONE net in this entire design -- "cpu_gated_clk_regs" (787 sinks). Proof, three independent lines of evidence:
1. CTS log (31-openroad-cts/openroad-cts.log) is unambiguous: "[INFO CTS-0008] TritonCTS found 2 clock nets" total = cpu_gated_clk (1 sink, the u_cpu macro) + cpu_gated_clk_regs (787 sinks). "Total number of Sinks: 788" = exactly 1+787. Zero sys_clk-domain sinks were ever handed to the H-tree builder. sys_clk's chain (clk_i -> core_clk -> gpu_gated_clk) is entirely marked "[WARNING CTS-0105] ...already has clock buffer... Skipping" / "[WARNING CTS-0041] Net gpu_gated_clk has 1 sinks. Skipping" -- no "core_clk_regs" or equivalent net is ever found or logged.
2. Netlist grep for CTS's own buffer/net naming convention (clkbuf_*/clknet_*) confirms it exactly: 1184 matches for "*cpu_gated_clk_regs*", ZERO matches for any core_clk/gpu_gated_clk pattern, anywhere in the post-CTS netlist.
3. Live clock-path traces confirm the mechanism differs structurally, not just in scale. The well-behaved cpu_clk sink (u_apb_dbg_cdc._1487_, picked at random from the H-treed group) reaches its CLK pin via a properly hierarchical hand-built tree: cpu_clk_i -> PLL stub -> u_cpu_cg ICG -> cpu_gated_clk -> clkbuf_regs_0_cpu_clk -> delaybuf_0_cpu_clk -> cpu_gated_clk_regs -> clkbuf_0/1_1_0/2_3_0/3_6_0/leaf_99_cpu_gated_clk_regs (level 0->1->2->3->leaf, fanout 1,2,2,2,13,7 -- a real, hierarchically-branching H-tree, ~7 real CTS stages). The pathological sys_clk sink (u_spi.u_regbank._2313_, the flow's own worst hold-skew instance) reaches its CLK pin via clk_i -> PLL stub -> ~29 buffers ALL individually named "load_slew<N>"/"wire<N>" (the generic repair_design/resizer slew-repair naming convention, NOT TritonCTS naming) with roughly CONSTANT fanout (34-68) at every single stage -- a long, unbalanced, flat daisy-chain, not a tree, accumulating 1486 ps of insertion delay by the time it reaches u_spi. This is architecturally the wrong KIND of structure, not merely "more levels of the same tree" -- it's what generic fanout/slew repair from OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGPL (step 28, runs BEFORE CTS) produces when a clock net's massive fanout needs legalizing and CTS itself never touches it afterward.

ICG / clock-gating structure is NOT the root cause: run 8's netlist has exactly 2 real ICGx1_ASAP7_75t_R cells (matching u_cpu_cg/u_gpu_cg), correctly mapped -- USE_ICG_CELL was defined for synthesis (confirmed in 04-yosys-synthesis/config.json), and the RTL directly instantiates the library primitive (rv32i_clock_gate.sv:20, no inferred-gating pattern to mis-synthesize). yosys-synthesis.log shows rv32i_clock_gate processed correctly as its own module during the FIRST (hierarchical) synth pass. Not the mechanism.

Config comparison (item 4): confirmed via diff, config_multiclock.json (flat, works) vs config_multiclock_hier.json (deferred_flatten, broken) differ in EXACTLY ONE key -- SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE. No CTS_*, clock-gating define, or sv2v define differences exist.

WHY cpu_clk succeeds and sys_clk doesn't: NOT FULLY RESOLVED mechanistically (would need OpenROAD/TritonCTS source access this session doesn't have, or a side-by-side flat-vs-deferred_flatten CTS log diff on current RTL -- run 23/run 5's directories are pruned, unavailable). Best-supported hypothesis, consistent with bead je8's own independently-established finding ("deferred_flatten... submodule input-port nets... merge into their driver nets"): deferred_flatten's two-phase synth (hierarchical ABC pass, then flatten+re-synth) produces a netlist where sys_clk's ordinary (non-macro) fabric register fanout ends up merged into the same "core_clk" net with no surviving distinctly-named sub-partition, whereas cpu_clk's much smaller domain (787 registers vs sys_clk's tens of thousands, spanning far fewer RTL hierarchy levels) happens to retain (or produce) a separately-named net TritonCTS's auto-discovery can find. Not proven; flagged as uncertain.

RECOMMENDATION (item 5), checked against the actually-exposed LibreLane config surface:
(a) Synthesis-side keep_hierarchy/blackbox-preserve on rv32i_clock_gate: NOT ACHIEVABLE without an RTL attribute or a shared-tree change. This LibreLane version's SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE is a single global flatten/deferred_flatten/keep flag (librelane/scripts/pyosys/synthesize.py) with no per-module exclusion list or config-driven keep_hierarchy hook exposed. Ruled out under this task's constraints (no RTL edits, no shared-tree edits).
(b) A CTS config change: NOT ACHIEVABLE either. Read cts.tcl in full: `clock_tree_synthesis` is called with NO `-clk_nets` override (which is the actual OpenROAD arg that could force additional clock-net roots) -- LibreLane only exposes CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE/MAX_DIAMETER, CTS_CLK_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH, CTS_DISABLE_POST_PROCESSING, CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS, CTS_CORNERS, CTS_ROOT_BUFFER, CTS_CLK_BUFFERS -- all tune HOW a discovered tree is built, none influence WHICH nets get discovered as roots. comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
GRT DIVERGENCE ROOT-CAUSE (Task B, w3a-diag7, read-only, foreground, in-session global_route + estimate_parasitics -global_routing on attempt 4's 09-openroad-repairdesignpostgrt ODB -- bumped scope to 6G, not the suggested 4G, per memory bead openroad-grt-parasitics-need-insession-route's documented ~5.4GB peak for in-session GRT on this design; completed faster than that bead's ~24min estimate. Parasitic annotation: 1553 unannotated drivers of ~245k total, 0 partially unannotated -- acceptable coverage, gate passed).

MECHANISM FOUND directly in attempt 4's own log (w3a_rsz_4.log, table starting line 49298, 41930 total setup violators): WNS degradation from -2084ps to -10389ps (the reported 5x) correlates EXACTLY, iteration-for-iteration, with the table's "Removed Buffers" column incrementing -- NOT with resize/insert/clone counts. Concretely: iter 7 (Removed=0, WNS=-2083.075) -> iter 8 (Removed=1, WNS=-4570.571) -> iter 9 (Removed=2, WNS=-5034.002) -> iter 13 (Removed=5, WNS=-6412.615) -> iter 14 (Removed=6, WNS=-6481.518) -> ... eventually Removed plateaus at 15 and WNS freezes at -10388.959 for the remaining 850+ iterations, DESPITE resized/inserted/cloned/pin-swap counts continuing to climb heavily (195/272/199/352 by iter 874) -- i.e. massive subsequent repair effort cannot undo the damage from those 15 removals. This is repair_timing's OWN internal buffer-removal optimization (enabled by default in both rsz_timing_postcts.tcl and rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl -- neither passes -skip_buffer_removal), NOT the earlier, separate DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS pre-repair_design pass (that one already ran successfully back at step 01 and is unrelated to this).

Confirmed via live path trace (item 1) why removing a handful of buffers here is catastrophic: both the iteration-0 worst endpoint (u_bus.u_periph_bridge._1819_/D) and the final pinned endpoint (u_bus.u_periph_bridge._1844_/D) are on the SAME structural path class -- Startpoint u_gpu (the GPU macro)'s AXI-Lite slave read-data bus, s_axil_rdata[5] and s_axil_rdata[30] respectively (different bus bits, same shared distribution network) -- through 4-6 chained buffers (wire836/wire828/wire18141/wire526/wire522/wire18140 for bit 5; wire866/wire863/wire18149/wire505 for bit 30) with EXTREME capacitance at every stage (686-1430 fF, vs the 10-50 fF typical of an ordinary buffer input elsewhere in the design) -- into u_bus.u_axil_ic (AXI-Lite interconnect mux) -> u_bus.periph_axil_rdata[N] -> 2 more gates in u_bus.u_periph_bridge -> D. This is a genuinely wide-fanout shared GPU-readback distribution network (same general class of problem as bead rvb's SRAM write-decode and the earlier m_axi_wvalid finding): removing even a few of its buffers dumps their load onto the survivors, ballooning delay across every downstream bit/instance sharing that tree -- explaining both the magnitude of the jump and why the worst-endpoint identity keeps changing across many different periph_bridge instances/bits (_1819_/_1818_/_1816_/_1832_/_1827_/_1829_/_1830_/..._1844_) as different bits take turns being worst while the underlying shared damage persists. Clock path itself (both endpoints) is a clean, healthy TritonCTS H-tree (clkbuf_*/clknet_* naming, proper hierarchical levels) -- confirms the CTS fix is holding at the post-GRT stage; this divergence is unrelated to the CTS mechanism, a separate resizer-behavior issue.

WHY post-CTS's repair (same missing -skip_buffer_removal) didn't show this: post-CTS uses PLACEMENT-based (Steiner-estimate) parasitics, typically less accurate/more optimistic than GRT's real-routing-based estimate for long or congested nets -- plausible that the same buffer-removal decision looked safe under the post-CTS estimate but is genuinely unsafe once real GRT parasitics reveal the true load on this wide-fanout net. Not proven definitively (would need a controlled placement-vs-GRT parasitic diff on the identical action), but consistent with all evidence.

RECOMMENDED FIX (item 3), in order of justification strength:
1. Add "-skip_buffer_removal" to PL_RESIZER_TIMING_EXTRA_ARGS -- directly targets the confirmed causal mechanism (repair_timing's own buffer-removal step), a real, valid repair_timing flag (confirmed present via `openroad -no_init -exit` help text), and the EXISTING, already-validated passthrough (no shared-tree edit needed). CAVEAT: EXTRA_ARGS is ONE env var spliced onto the setup_args of BOTH rsz_timing_postcts.tcl and rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl -- adding -skip_buffer_removal would apply to the ALREADY-WORKING post-CTS repair too (which converged to -323ps under the current "-repair_tns 5" value). Post-CTS's own table showed its own nonzero Removed-Buffers activity too (not diagnosed in detail here) without visible catastrophic effect there, so skip_buffer_removal is unlikely to regress it, but this is an UNTESTED combination and should be validated, not assumed.
2. PL_RESIZER_TIMING_EXTRA_ARGS "-skip_gate_cloning" for post-GRT: NOT well justified. Cloned-gate count was 0 through iteration 7 (before the WNS collapse) and only grows AFTER the buffer-removal damage was already done -- cloning is part of the (unsuccessful) recovery effort, not a contributing cause here. Disabling it also previously made the post-CTS setup stall WORSE in attempt 1 (bead w3a history) -- not recommended.
3. GRT_RESIZER_* buffer-budget/margin settings: not well justified -- the failure mode is buffer REMOVAL, not insufficient buffer INSERTION budget, so tightening or loosening an insertion-side cap doesn't address the mechanism.
4. A max-wire-length/max_fanout repair_design pass: already happens (step 09/repair_design_postgrt.tcl runs `repair_design -max_wire_length ... -slew_margin ... -cap_margin ...` immediately before repair_timing) -- the problem is repair_timing's OWN subsequent internal buffer removal undoing/exceeding what that legalization pass established, so a stronger repair_design pass wouldn't prevent it.
5. "limiting remove_buffers to clock nets": does not apply here -- that refers to the EARLIER, separate DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS pre-repair_design pass (step 01), which already ran successfully and is unrelated to this divergence (a different mechanism, a different step, already confirmed working).

Not fixed/validated in this PR (per instruction) -- to be filed as a new bead once w3a-rsz-5 (Task A, the honest post-GRT skip-repair result) completes.

comments.text:
CLOSING. Acceptance criterion met: every repair stage now terminates, and the flow reaches an HONESTLY ANNOTATED post-GRT STA (w3a-sta-7, RUN_2026-09-16_05-52-48, STAMidPNR-3). Annotation proven: 1553 unannotated drivers (0 partial) of ~213464 total (~0.7%) -- vs 213464 unannotated under the unpatched stock path (essentially all of them) -- well within the CPU block's own 1.71% validated floor.

FINAL HONEST POST-GRT RESULT (current RTL, deferred_flatten, nom_tt corner):
  setup WS -2084.08 ps, TNS -2.19e7 ps, 41864 violators
  hold   WS -917.23 ps, TNS -392273 ps, 718 violators
  worst hold skew -1687.9 ps, worst setup skew -1604.8 ps
  power total 258.48 mW (internal 215.33, switching 37.69, leakage 5.47)
  instances 235520
This agrees with the resizer's own independent annotated view from w3a-rsz-6 (WNS ~-2078.5 ps, TNS ~-16.7e6, 41891 violators) -- the two tools now line up, which is itself a validation of the STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT fix. w3a-rsz-5's earlier "-426.262 ps / clean hold" result stays WITHDRAWN (computed on ~94% unannotated drivers, falsely clean). Run 23's historical post-GRT figures are themselves unvalidated pending bead 0p6.

TIMING IS NOT CLOSED AT POST-GRT. Stating this plainly: the setup gap is real and large (~-2.08 ns, 41864 violators), concentrated on the GPU s_axil_rdata -> u_bus.u_periph_bridge fanout path (bead rvb / docs/design/RVB_FANOUT_FIX_PROPOSAL.md Path B). The hold gap (-917ps, 718 violators) is smaller but also real, tied to a cpu_clk-domain clock-skew regression at u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo (see below, filed separately).

FIXES THAT GOT THE FLOW THIS FAR (all four required, none alone sufficient):
1. DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS=true -- fixed the CTS mechanism: removed the pll_clkgen_stub module-boundary buffer that made TritonCTS treat core_clk/cpu_core_clk as "already buffered" and skip building a sys_clk tree entirely (was 2 clock nets/788 sinks total; now 4 clock nets with a real 44266-sink H-tree on clk_i).
2. Bounded post-CTS repair -- PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES=1 + PL_RESIZER_TIMING_EXTRA_ARGS="-repair_tns 5" (bead bpp) -- turned an unbounded, non-terminating setup-repair oscillation into a real, terminating repair (RSZ-0062 after ~36 min, WNS -737->-656ps, viol 27550->20453) with an honestly partial result.
3. -skip_buffer_removal added to the same EXTRA_ARGS for the post-GRT call -- fixed a SEPARATE mechanism: repair_timing's own internal buffer-removal was stripping load-bearing buffers off the GPU s_axil_rdata distribution network under real GRT parasitics, causing a 5x WNS blowup (-2084->-10389ps) that no amount of subsequent repair could undo. With the flag, Removed Buffers stays 0 -- no divergence, though the underlying violation (a real, largely un-bufferable fanout problem, see rvb) remains only marginally improved by the one bounded pass.
4. STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT=true (bead 8f3) -- fixed a THIRD, independent mechanism: the stock post-GRT STA step never re-routed in-session, so it reported off mostly-missing parasitics and produced a falsely clean result. This is what makes today's numbers trustworthy at all.

Filed claude_verilog_test-* P2 bead for the cpu_clk skew regression (post-CTS -823ps -> post-GRT -1688ps at u_cpu_axi_cdc.u_w_fifo) -- see next comment / linked bead for detail; not folded into this bead since it is a distinct, timing-only (not repair-convergence) issue.

Config history (chronological): config_multiclock_hier_rsz.json (attempt1, reverted) -> rsz2 (attempt2) -> rsz3 (attempt3, max_passes) -> rsz4 (attempt4, +DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS, the CTS-fix milestone) -> rsz6 (+skip_buffer_removal) -> rsz7 (+STA_POSTGRT_INSESSION_GRT, the FINAL validated config for this bead's scope). rsz/rsz2/rsz3/rsz6 removed as superseded (commit 88b6e5d, coordinator); rsz4 and rsz7 remain as the two load-bearing milestones.

title: Port LibreLane 2.4.13 STA scripts to OpenROAD 26Q2 (corners->scenes API renames)
description:
Port LibreLane 2.4.13's OpenROAD scripts to the OpenROAD 26Q2 binary that pnr/Makefile's
check-asap7-openroad shim (added 2026-09-08, bead ocm) puts on PATH for every ASAP7 target.

The 2.4.13 scripts were never updated for 26Q2. An ASAP7 SoC run on that combination on 2026-09-13
failed four times, three of them on script/binary mismatches:
  1. GeneratePDN: get_psm_error_count() could not parse 26Q2's tab-indented grid-error report
     (yaml ScannerError). FIXED (memory/pd/patches/librelane2413_psm_report_parser_26q2_format.diff).
  2. IOPlacement: ioplacer.tcl passed -random_seed 42 unconditionally; 26Q2 treats it as obsolete
     (PPL-0113) and places NO pins, so GlobalPlacement died with GPL-0326. FIXED
     (memory/pd/patches/librelane2413_ioplacer_26q2_random_seed.diff).
  3. STAMidPNR: corner.tcl called rsz::check_corner_wire_cap -> "invalid command name". NOT FIXED.

A sweep of every namespaced internal call in librelane/scripts/openroad (28 distinct) against 26Q2's
`info commands` found exactly four missing, all with a 1:1 renamed equivalent in 26Q2:

  2.4.13 call                    26Q2 equivalent               call sites
  rsz::check_corner_wire_cap     est::check_corner_wire_caps    sta/corner.tcl:39
  sta::corners                   sta::scenes                    sta/corner.tcl:47, common/io.tcl:463,474 (write_sdfs, write_libs)
  sta::set_cmd_corner            sta::set_cmd_scene             sta/corner.tcl:48
  utl::metric_int                utl::metric_integer            common/io.tcl:519 (write_metric_int)

Note even LibreLane 3.0.14's spelling (est::check_corner_wire_cap, singular) is absent from 26Q2.

RISK -- this is NOT a blind rename: OpenSTA 26Q2 moved from "corners" to "scenes". corner.tcl then
calls methods on the returned objects ([$corner name], -corner [$corner name] on report_checks /
write_sdf / write_timing_model). Verify each against 26Q2 before trusting any STA number. Also note
26Q2's est::check_corner_wire_caps returned 0 on a post-GPL ODB before set_wire_rc -- confirm it
returns 1 after set_rc.tcl, or estimate_parasitics -placement is silently skipped and mid-PnR STA
degrades with no error.

Also recorded: 26Q2 tends to WARN AND SKIP rather than error (items 1-2). Before trusting any 2.4.13
step on 26Q2, grep its log for obsolete|deprecated|Skipping|not supported.

Why deferred: for the 86a/je8 SoC run the flow was switched back to LibreLane 2.4.13's bundled
toolchain (OpenROAD edf00dff + OpenSTA 2.6.0) -- the exact toolchain run 23 used -- because the
shim exists for DRT pin access, which this 15.9 GB host cannot reach anyway (see 2kn). The port
matters once a >=32 GB host makes real routing possible.
notes:
2026-09-15 VALIDATION PART A (valu_rtl, small design) -- PASS on both toolchains, byte-identical.

Sweep of every namespace-qualified Tcl call (28 distinct names) under librelane/scripts/openroad/
in a fresh worktree copy (/nobackup/librelane-bpp, detached at the live tree's HEAD 3562a8d, with
the live tree's uncommitted local patches -- PSM parser, ioplacer -random_seed, pdn.tcl decomposed
build_grids, drt.tcl catch-wrapper, Synlig/UHDM hierarchy-check + lib-sort + SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES
fixes in synthesize.py/steps/pyosys.py/steps/odb.py -- carried over) against 26Q2's `info commands`
found EXACTLY the four already-tracked missing commands, no more:
  rsz::check_corner_wire_cap, sta::corners, sta::set_cmd_corner, utl::metric_int
(est::check_corner_wire_cap, singular, is ALSO absent from 26Q2 -- only the plural
est::check_corner_wire_caps exists, confirming 3.0.14's spelling doesn't help either.)

Fixed with namespace-existence guards (info commands <new-name>) in common/io.tcl
(ol_compat_corners / ol_compat_set_cmd_corner / ol_compat_check_corner_wire_cap procs,
used by the three sta::corners call sites at lines ~488/499/516 and by write_metric_int) and
sta/corner.tcl (the two call sites at the old line 39/47-48). No hard version switch.

Additional finding beyond the four (bead ocm's pin_access/-bottom_routing_layer note, checked as
requested): confirmed via `info body detailed_route` / `info body pin_access` on the 26Q2 binary
that -bottom_routing_layer/-top_routing_layer are now unconditional utl::error (DRT-509/DRT-510,
"deprecated, use set_routing_layers instead") on BOTH commands -- 2.4.13's drt.tcl uses exactly
these flags on detailed_route. Fixed drt.tcl with the same info-commands-sta::scenes guard,
switching to `set_routing_layers -signal <min>-<max>` + bare detailed_route for 26Q2. NOT
validated by an actual DRT run this session (out of scope -- see below); logic-checked only.
Also checked make_tracks/place_pin ordering (bead ocm's other note): already correct in 2.4.13's
Classic flow -- OpenROAD.Floorplan (sources TRACKS_INFO_FILE_PROCESSED / make_tracks) is flow
position 53, OpenROAD.IOPlacement is position 64. No fix needed.

Validation runs (both foreground, <3 min each, small design):

  2. SAME copy, SAME config, bundled OpenROAD edf00dff + OpenSTA 2.6.0 (no shim on PATH) ->

     match to the last printed digit) -- confirms every guard is a true no-op on the old
     toolchain, not just numerically close.

tree's current dirty state, i.e. stacks on the existing local patches rather than re-supplying

awaiting coordinator confirmation no run is active).

[ERROR RSZ-0089] Could not find a resistance value (gpl.tcl:79). Root cause: the coordinator's
carryover list (PSM parser, ioplacer, pdn.tcl) was not exhaustive -- set_rc.tcl's ASAP7
RC-injection fallback (knowledge.md's very first, oldest-tracked entry) is ALSO an uncommitted
live-tree local patch, and valu_rtl's --to OpenROAD.STAPrePNR (Part A) never exercises the
GlobalPlacement codepath that needs it, so Part A's PASS did not catch the gap. Carried
set_rc.tcl over; general lesson recorded in knowledge.md: enumerate a live tree's local patches
from `git status`/`git diff --stat` directly, don't trust a bead-description-derived list, and
don't call a copy's patch set complete until a run has exercised every stage the validation needs.

bpp-2 (relaunch with set_rc.tcl carried, 26Q2): reached OpenROAD.STAMidPNR (first real exercise
of sta/corner.tcl under the actual 26Q2 `openroad` binary -- NOT the same code path valu_rtl's
STAPrePNR validated, see below) and FAILED: `Error: corner.tcl, 60 invalid command name
"nom_tt_025C_0p7V"`. ROOT CAUSE (a second, distinct scenes-API defect beyond the four renamed
commands): under 26Q2, `sta::scenes` returns plain scene-NAME STRINGS, not command objects --
unlike `sta::corners`'s corner objects, which support method-call syntax (`$corner name`).
Calling `$corner name` on a 26Q2 scene string makes Tcl try to invoke a command literally named
after the scene (e.g. "nom_tt_025C_0p7V"), which does not exist -> "invalid command name".
This affects 45 call sites in corner.tcl + 2 in common/io.tcl (write_sdfs/write_libs), all of
the form `[$corner name]` or `-corner [$corner name]`. This is exactly the risk the bead's own
RISK paragraph warned about ("corner.tcl then calls methods on the returned objects... verify
each against 26Q2") -- and it only surfaces via a real openroad-binary-driven STAMidPNR run,
never via valu_rtl's STAPrePNR (STAPrePNR/STAPostPNR are MultiCornerSTA, which invokes
corner.tcl through the STANDALONE `sta` binary -- ASAP7_STA_BIN, pinned to OpenSTA 2.6.0,
NOT 26Q2, regardless of ASAP7_OPENROAD_BIN -- so that path always takes the OLD sta::corners/
object branch and never touches scenes at all). STAMidPNR is a plain OpenROADStep run through
`openroad` itself (26Q2, real `ord` namespace), which is the only place scenes semantics apply.

FIX: added `ol_compat_corner_name` proc (same info-commands-sta::scenes guard style) to
common/io.tcl; replaced all 47 `[$corner name]` call sites (45 in corner.tcl, 2 in io.tcl) with
`[ol_compat_corner_name $corner]`.

Verified the fix in two steps:
  1. `--only OpenROAD.STAMidPNR --last-run` (reruns just that one step against bpp-2's saved

0.129 > 0.91". Lesson: `--from X --last-run` does NOT rewind to "the state before X's first
historical occurrence" -- it continues from wherever the run's linear history currently ends,
so switching toolchain mid-run-directory only works if the ODB format is compatible. This is
an ODB-schema incompatibility between the two OpenROAD builds themselves, unrelated to this
bead's Tcl patch -- worth keeping in memory/pd/knowledge.md as a general caution against
resuming a run directory across different OpenROAD binary versions.

Second patch file: memory/pd/patches/librelane2413_resizer_timing_bounds.diff (PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES
