title: ASAP7: route with the real power grid once a >=32 GB host is available
description:
FUTURE / HOST-GATED: route the ASAP7 designs WITH the real power grid once a machine with >=32 GB RAM
is available. Deferred at the user's request (2026-09-13); do not attempt on the current 15.9 GB host.

WHY IT IS NEEDED. Until 2026-09-12 no ASAP7 run in this repo ever committed a power grid (bead 4l8):
pdngen aborted with PDN-0179 inside build_grids before write_to_db, and a warn-and-continue patch
swallowed it. Every ASAP7 routing/DRC number to date -- CPU, GPU, SoC run 14, run 23 -- was therefore
produced with M1/M2/M5 free of PDN metal and is a LOWER BOUND, not closure. The grid is now fixed
(pnr/asap7/pdn_asap7_orfs.tcl: followpins on M1 AND M2, then M2->M5->M6; VIAS_R added), and it builds
and passes check_power_grid on CPU, GPU and SoC with IR drop running end-to-end. What has never been
done is routing a design with that grid on the tracks.

WHY IT IS HOST-GATED (measured, CPU block, 4 attempts, all killed inside DRT iteration 0 of 12):
  ORFS M5 2.16/M6 4.32,  util 50, 8 thr  -> 122121 violations, 13.4 GB
  ORFS M5 2.16/M6 4.32,  util 50, 4 thr  -> 122121 violations, 13.4 GB
  3x sparse 6.48/12.96,  util 50, 4 thr  ->  83207 violations, 11.2 GB
  3x sparse 6.48/12.96,  util 45, 2 thr  -> 112764 violations, 12.8 GB (stopped, host at 1 GB free)
The PDN-free run peaked 12.4 GB and converged to 1991 DRC, so a real grid costs ~20-30% more
violations and this host has no headroom. systemd-oomd killed the terminal scope (and the Claude
session) once during these attempts.

LEVERS ALREADY RULED OUT -- do not retry blindly on a small host:
 * sparser straps: violation counts barely move; congestion is the M2 followpins (one track per row)
 * lower utilization: identical violations and MORE memory (bigger die)
 * fewer DRT threads: marginal; memory is dominated by violation markers
 * avoiding M2: rails M1->M3 direct leaves all 222 rails unconnected; M1->M2 is structurally required

WHEN A BIG HOST EXISTS:
 1. Restore host accommodations in pnr/asap7/cpu/config_3014.json: FP_CORE_UTIL 45->50, DRT_THREADS 2->8.
 2. Consider restoring ORFS strap density (M5 2.16 / M6 4.32; IR 0.18% vs 1.37% at the current
    sparsest setting) in pnr/asap7/pdn_asap7_orfs.tcl.
 3. make -C pnr librelane-asap7-3014 (CPU), then librelane-asap7-gpu-3014 (GPU), then wire
    pnr/asap7/soc/pdn_orfs.tcl into the SoC configs and re-close the SoC.
 4. Expect DRC work: re-baseline every ASAP7 DRC/antenna/IR number against these runs and retire
    the PDN-free figures. IR drop must come from the full routed run, not the floorplan-stage harness.
Evidence + traps (--from does not rewind state; cap cgroups below the oomd threshold):
docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md "Routing with a real PDN is host-blocked", memory/pd/knowledge.md.

title: LibreLane 3.0.14 shell resolves sta to OpenSTA 2.7.0, which corrupts report_power (inf/NaN)
description:
Found 2026-09-09 by the bead-86a agent, independently confirmed by the bead-ocm agent inside
the running flow. Two separate agents, same conclusion.

THE DEFECT: OpenSTA 2.7.0 produces corrupted inf/NaN report_power output on this project's
designs. OpenSTA 2.6.0 -- what `eda-opensta` and this repo's own nix-shell resolve to --
reports correctly on the identical inputs. Found during macro power characterization (bead
86a), where the 2.7.0 numbers were nonsense and 2.6.0's were clean and round-tripped.

WHY IT REACHES US: the LibreLane 3.0.14 worktree used for the ocm routing bring-up
(/nobackup/librelane-3.0.14) resolves `sta` to 2.7.0 --
/nix/store/wmynz8awpap4gfrkz3xr6y7q575zijdy-devshell-dir/bin/sta, verified with
`which sta; sta -version` inside that shell. And LibreLane DOES invoke a standalone `sta`
binary, not only openroad's built-in STA: `sta -no_splash -exit .../corner.tcl` appears as its
own process during OpenROAD.STAPrePNR, and the same pattern recurs at STAMidPNR / -1/2/3.

CONSEQUENCE: every STA-derived metric from a run out of that worktree is suspect. Run
RUN_2026-09-09_06-11-06's metrics.json WNS/TNS/power must be treated as NOT TRUSTWORTHY. Only
report_power was demonstrated corrupted; timing was not tested, and the right posture is to
distrust all STA metrics from that shell rather than spot-check and hope.
NOT affected: routing closure. tools/verif/check_asap7_routing.py reads only routed-net counts,
route__wirelength__max and [ERROR DRT-*] lines from the routing log and DEF -- no STA-derived
value -- so the ocm routing verdict stands regardless.

THE FIX, for whoever next needs real timing or power off 3.0.14: pin `sta` the same way
pnr/Makefile's OR_PATH_PREFIX already pins `openroad`. The shim-directory pattern already
exists (ASAP7_OR_SHIM_DIR, a directory holding a single symlink, added under bead ocm) --
extend it with a second symlink to a known-good 2.6.0 `sta`. NOTE the symmetric trap that
motivated the shim originally: prepending a store path's whole bin/ replaced LibreLane's
OpenSTA and killed every STA step with `invalid command name "sta::corners"`. So this must be
a targeted per-binary symlink, never a bin/ prepend.

CROSS-CHECK WORTH DOING: confirm whether 2.7.0 also corrupts timing, not just power. If it
does, any prior number from a 2.7.0 shell needs review -- though as of now the only such runs
are the ocm bring-up runs, which produced no sign-off figures.

RELATED: ocm (source of the 3.0.14 worktree), 86a (where it was found), s9f (the other
"the tool's units/values were not what we believed" finding in this project).
close_reason:
2026-09-09 FIXED (commit 7465ba1) -- AND THIS BEAD'S CLAIM WAS TOO BROAD. Correcting it.

THE FIX: pnr/Makefile pins ASAP7_STA_BIN to the known-good OpenSTA 2.6.0 store path and
symlinks it into .openroad-shim/sta beside the existing openroad symlink -- the same targeted
single-file-symlink pattern, never a bin/ prepend (a bin/ prepend is what broke every STA step
with `invalid command name "sta::corners"` when the 26Q2 override was first built). Verified:
`make -C pnr check-asap7-openroad` reports `ok: ASAP7 sta = 2.6.0`, and the guard exits
non-zero on a bad path (negative control run).

⚠️ THE CORRUPTION CLAIM DID NOT REPRODUCE ON THE FLOW PATH. Direct inspection of two runs'
power.rpt that genuinely resolved `sta` to 2.7.0 BEFORE the fix shows NO inf/NaN corruption on
the standard corner.tcl flow. The original observation (made under bead 86a) was on a DIFFERENT
workflow: a standalone, hand-injected macro-Liberty round-trip test, not LibreLane's own STA
steps.

SO THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS, WHICH I WROTE, ARE WITHDRAWN:
 * "every STA-derived metric from that shell is suspect" -- broader than the evidence.
 * "RUN_2026-09-09_06-11-06's metrics.json WNS/TNS/power must be treated as NOT TRUSTWORTHY" --
   they are not known to be bad. They were never independently shown to be wrong; they were
   distrusted on the strength of a corruption seen elsewhere.
What remains true and still justifies the pin: the 3.0.14 shell DID resolve `sta` to 2.7.0
while the rest of the project standardises on 2.6.0, LibreLane genuinely shells out to a
standalone `sta` (observed as its own process during OpenROAD.STAPrePNR), and an unpinned tool
version in a sign-off flow is a real ambiguity worth removing. The pin costs nothing.

WHAT IS STILL UNRESOLVED: the actual 2.7.0 misbehaviour under bead 86a's standalone
round-trip. That was observed, and is not explained by this session's finding -- it simply is
not the flow-path failure this bead described. If anyone reuses that standalone
macro-Liberty round-trip method, re-check which sta it resolves and whether inf/NaN returns.

LESSON: a defect seen in one workflow was generalised to "every metric from that shell"
without testing the flow path. The narrower claim was the true one.

title: prune-asap7-runs evicted the signed-off CPU run; sign-off runs need protection from ASAP7_MAX_RUNS
description:
Found 2026-09-09 while starting bead 86a. Self-inflicted during the bead-ocm routing bring-up,
and it will recur.

WHAT HAPPENED: pnr/Makefile's librelane-asap7 target ends with `prune-asap7-runs`, which keeps
only ASAP7_MAX_RUNS=10 run directories (oldest deleted first). The ocm bring-up did 10
CPU runs in one night. That silently evicted EVERY pre-September CPU run, including
RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02 -- the run whose metrics CLAUDE.md and docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md cite,
and the one bead 86a was written against ("both signed-off block run dirs survive").
Surviving CPU runs are now exclusively the 10 failed bring-up attempts, none of which has a
final/ directory at all (they all died at detailed routing).

NOT ACTUALLY BLOCKING 86a -- checked before filing: the artifacts that matter are archived
OUTSIDE the run dirs by the macro-views-asap7 target and are TRACKED IN GIT:
  pnr/asap7/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.nl.v.gz          718 KB, 2026-08-10
  pnr/asap7/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.lef
  pnr/asap7/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib
  pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.nl.v.gz                10 MB, 2026-06-22
  pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib
So the block netlists and abstracts survive and 86a proceeds from those. The macro-view
archiving design is what saved this.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST: the run directories themselves -- step logs, per-step metrics.json,
intermediate ODBs, the STA reports behind the quoted numbers. The CPU sign-off's PPA figures
can no longer be re-derived or audited from artifacts on disk; only the summary numbers
recorded in docs survive. Reproducing them means a fresh ~26 min run, which will NOT be
byte-identical (different LibreLane, different OpenROAD -- see bead ocm).

WHY IT WILL RECUR: nothing distinguishes a sign-off run from a throwaway experiment. Any
future tuning campaign of >10 runs silently destroys whatever sign-off run is oldest, with no
warning and no record of what was removed.

FIX OPTIONS:
 (a) Protect by marker: prune skips any run dir containing a `.signoff` sentinel file; add one
     to the runs cited by docs. Explicit, cheap, survives any run count.
 (b) Protect by reference: prune parses docs/*_RUN_HISTORY.md for RUN_* names and never
     deletes those. Automatic, but couples the Makefile to doc formatting.
 (c) Never auto-prune: make prune an explicit target and drop it from the librelane-* targets.
     Safest, but the disk pressure it was added for is real (this host runs ~20 GB free).
 (d) At minimum: have prune PRINT what it is about to delete, so an eviction is visible in the
     log rather than silent.
Prefer (a) + (d). (a) is the real protection; (d) means the next person at least sees it happen.

ALSO WORTH DOING: capture the surviving evidence for the current sign-off runs (GPU
RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 still exists) before any further campaign evicts them too -- the GPU
run is now 11th-oldest-ish and one more GPU tuning campaign would take it.
close_reason: Fixed in e35b8b9. prune_runs now (1) never deletes a run directory containing a .signoff file, whatever its age or the run count, and (2) prints every deletion before it happens -- previously an eviction of something irreplaceable was indistinguishable from clearing scratch runs. Markers applied to the cited runs that still exist: ASAP7 GPU RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14, ASAP7 SoC RUN_2026-08-09_14-36-16 (run 23), Sky130 SoC RUN_2026-07-31_05-13-54, and the first passing ASAP7 CPU routing run RUN_2026-09-09_14-56-03. Verified non-vacuously -- and the FIRST test attempt was a false pass worth recording: creating .signoff inside the oldest run updated that directory's mtime, making it NEWEST, so it survived for the wrong reason and the PROTECTED line never printed. Re-tested with mtimes set explicitly after creating the marker so the protected run is genuinely oldest and first in the deletion queue: PROTECTED prints, marked run survives, next-oldest unmarked run is deleted. NOT recovered: the already-lost CPU run directories (step logs, per-step metrics, intermediate ODBs, STA reports). Those PPA figures can no longer be audited from artifacts on disk and are not byte-reproducible now that LibreLane and OpenROAD have both moved.

title: GH #119 Stage 2: P&R both HLS arms on ASAP7 and fill the PPA table
description:
Stage 1 is complete (PR #164, commit 3af62b0). Stage 2 is the measurement half and has NOT been run.

SCOPE: take the two generated .v files through the ASAP7 flow alongside their hand-RTL counterparts and produce the PPA comparison table docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md promises as its deliverable.

MUST DO FIRST -- STATE THE COUNTING BOUNDARY. Bambu's own pre-synthesis estimates (memory_coalescer 820 FF / area 352744; rv32i_hazard_unit 50 FF / area 1791535) are NOT comparable to hand-RTL as-is: they cover the whole generated hierarchy INCLUDING Bambu's AXI master adapter, which the hand-RTL has no equivalent of, and for the coalescer only 45 of those registers are datapath storage. Synthesise both arms for real and say explicitly what is inside the boundary before quoting any number.

NO DRC COLUMN. Struck in Stage 1 (beads xy6/ocm): no ASAP7 run in this project's history has ever completed detailed routing, so both arms compare two vacuous zeros. The acceptance thresholds in the doc are already amended. Revisit only if ocm is solved.

INPUTS ALREADY PINNED (hls/PROVENANCE.json): device asap7-TC, clock 0.705 ns (matches pnr/asap7/template/config.json), Bambu 2024.10 rev c2ba6936 sha256-pinned in flake.nix, Verilator 5.048. Stage 2 must use the SAME clock period and corner for BOTH arms or the comparison is void. Regenerate with 'nix develop .#hls --command make -C hls {memory_coalescer,rv32i_hazard_unit}' and check the NORMALIZED digest matches (raw digests change every run -- Bambu stamps a timestamp).

FREE WIN ON ACCOUNTING: both shims are wire-only (zero registers, 0 Verilator warnings), so Flow B's area needs no separate shim line.

NORMALISE ON THROUGHPUT (doc L133), not raw cycles -- the arms differ structurally:
  memory_coalescer  empty-mask latency 1 (hand-RTL) vs 6 (HLS)
  rv32i_hazard_unit 0 cycles / 0 flip-flops (hand-RTL, purely combinational) vs 6-9 data-dependent cycles / 50 FF (HLS)
The hazard unit's 0-vs-50 flip-flop figure needs no normalisation and is the sharpest single number.

POWER: both arms must use the same VCD source (the shared cocotb suites), per the doc's pinning list.

PRACTICAL: the HLS arms are slow to build -- Bambu explodes one block into ~550 instances, so sim/Makefile carries --output-split 500 and NO_TRACE=1 on those targets. Expect the same pressure in synthesis. Delegate the flow to chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator per the mandated agent policy.

EXPECTED VALUE IS LOW-ISH AND WORTH SAYING SO: Stage 1 already answered the control-logic question categorically (one block inexpressible, one whose form cannot be reproduced). A PPA table refines rather than decides. Run it if a number is wanted for the record; skip it if the categorical results suffice.
close_reason:
DONE. The PPA table exists; GH #119 is now measured end to end.

FLOW: four ASAP7 runs --to OpenROAD.STAPrePNR only (that is where area, timing AND power all first appear; placement/CTS/routing needed for none). Seconds per block. All four share clock 705 ps, corner nom_tt_025C_0p7V, synthesis strategy and skip list; the four config.json differ ONLY in DESIGN_NAME, VERILOG_FILES and clock port (verified programmatically). Both HLS arms synthesised WITH their wire-only shim so port lists match.

  block              flow      area um2  cells  crit ps      fmax MHz  power mW  undriven
  memory_coalescer   hand-RTL  569.74    4219   1620.15      617.2     4.469     0
  memory_coalescer   HLS       605.22    4814   1059.09      944.2     4.845     9
  rv32i_hazard_unit  hand-RTL   23.17     233    149.3 comb  n/a       0.018     0
  rv32i_hazard_unit  HLS        26.55     233    302.53      3305.5    0.182    28

RESULT 1 -- COALESCER: HLS WON, which was NOT the hypothesis. Critical path -34.6% (fmax +53%), area +6.2%, power +8.4% -- the latter two inside the doc's own +/-10% competitive band, and the speed is a straight win. Bambu split the lane walk into more, shorter cycles where the hand-RTL holds a long path through the 8-lane mux and its AXI FSM. It does NOT overturn the recommendation, because the shorter period is bought with cycles: empty-mask is 1 rising edge hand-RTL vs 6 HLS, and per-transaction latency is what the consumer sees.

RESULT 2 -- HAZARD UNIT: REGRESSES decisively. Power x10.1 (0.018 -> 0.182 mW, +911%), area +14.6%, latency x12.2-x18.2 (149.3 ps combinational vs 302.53 ps x 6-9 cycles). Stage 1 showed the combinational form was inexpressible; this is the price.

RESULT 3 -- NETLIST QUALITY: Yosys CHECK reports undriven wires ONLY in the HLS arms (9 coalescer, 28 hazard; 0 in both hand-RTL). OUT_UNBOUNDED_* functional-unit outputs plus an undriven s_start_port0. Checker.YosysSynthChecks skipped on ALL FOUR to keep the flow identical; documented in pnr/Makefile and reported as a result rather than hidden by the skip.

HONEST GAP, recorded in the doc and PROVENANCE: a full 8-lane-transaction cycle count for the hand-RTL coalescer was NOT measured, so that block's throughput comparison rests only on the empty-mask case. A rigorous ratio needs it and is not claimed.

METHODOLOGY: rv32i_hazard_unit's hand-RTL arm is purely combinational (no clock, no registers, zero r2r paths) so fmax is undefined; timed against a virtual clock with zero I/O budget, reporting input-to-output delay.

FOUR OBSTACLES HIT AND RESOLVED, all worth knowing for any future leaf-block run:
1. Template config has NEVER been exercised. MACRO_PLACEMENT_CFG is a hard exit(1) when its 10 CPU SRAM instances are absent; its 300-line SDC is CPU-specific. Each block got a fresh ~24-line SDC in PICOSECONDS.
2. remove_from_collection is a Synopsys command, not OpenSTA -- SDC must use plain [all_inputs].
3. Synlig does NOT honour Bambu's '// synthesis translate_off' pragma and rejects $finish outside an initial block. Yosys-native honours it but cannot parse this repo's SystemVerilog, so BOTH arms fail there -- the uniform-frontend fix is not available. Resolved with tools/hls/strip_translate_off.py producing a *_synth.v; a semantic no-op since translate_off means exactly 'synthesis must not see this'. The pinned .v is untouched.
4. My own collector bug: timing__setup__wns is worst NEGATIVE slack and reads 0.0 on a clean design. The margin is timing__setup__ws. Caught because two arms implausibly reported 0.0.

ALSO FIXED HERE (separate commit): the Stage-1 digest normalisation was never checkout-independent -- it stripped Bambu's date stamp but not the header line echoing the full command line with absolute paths. Found because the hazard unit's pinned digest did not reproduce despite byte-identical inputs. Both digests re-pinned and verified stable across two runs; regression test added.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD AS FILED: I wrote that Bambu's estimates 'include an AXI master adapter the hand-RTL has no equivalent of'. Wrong on both blocks -- the hand-RTL coalescer has its OWN AXI master FSM, and the hazard unit has no adapter at all. The real reason not to quote Bambu's figures is simply that they are pre-synthesis estimates in its own units. Fixed in the doc and both NOTES.md.

Verified: 4/4 runs exit 0; collector exits 0 with no missing metric; ruff clean; tb/tests 150.

title: GH #119: PROVENANCE.json + eval-doc Stage-1 append (incl. striking the DRC axis)
description:
hls/PROVENANCE.json per doc L127-133: Bambu tag 2024.10 + AppImage sha256 + size 1405510848 + Last-Modified 2025-05-11 + --version string; full --help capture + bundled compiler list + --compiler= used; verbatim command line per block; Verilator 5.048 + flake.lock nixpkgs rev; sha256 of every generated .v; the NL spec text and authoring prompt per C++ source; --device-name=asap7-TC (TT/RVT nldm 201020) so Stage 2 matches the corner; --clock-period=0.705 ns (matches pnr/asap7/template/config.json CLOCK_PERIOD); shim cell count kept as a SEPARATE line never folded into Flow B; Bambu cycles/II AND hand-RTL cycle count from the same cocotb test.

Append a Stage-1 section to docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md covering: what was pinned; the two-leg equivalence results; the arbiter inexpressibility verdict; the coalescer-is-not-a-datapath-block correction; the hazard-unit substitution; and the EXPLICIT WITHDRAWAL of the DRC axis from the L135-140 acceptance thresholds (beads xy6/ocm - no ASAP7 run has ever completed detailed routing; both arms hit the identical wall so the column yields no discriminating signal). Stage 2 must not promise a DRC column.
close_reason:
DONE (commit 2bf6d1b). Stage 1 is closed out.

DELIVERABLE 1 -- hls/PROVENANCE.json. The doc L127-133 pin: Bambu 2024.10 rev c2ba6936 + AppImage sha256/size/Last-Modified, the frontend actually used (I386_CLANG16) and the bundled alternatives (clang-12/clang-16/gcc-8), Verilator 5.048 + flake.lock nixpkgs rev 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f, verbatim per-block command line, device asap7-TC + clock 0.705 ns + the bundled asap7sc7p5t_SIMPLE_RVT_TT_nldm_201020.lib (same lib/corner as pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json), the authorship protocol, wire-only shim accounting, and both NORMALIZED generated-Verilog digests. Normalized not raw: Bambu stamps a timestamp into a header comment so the raw digest changes every run; a committed raw digest would fail on every regeneration.

DELIVERABLE 2 -- 'Stage 1 results' appended to docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md, plus front-matter Status and the closing 'this pilot is optional' note updated to say it was actually run.

DRC AXIS STRUCK IN PLACE (not just noted at the end). The L135-140 thresholds promised a DRC/antenna comparison; struck through inline with the reason, because leaving a live threshold that promises DRC is exactly the trap. Reason: bead xy6 -- no ASAP7 run in this project's history has ever completed detailed routing (drt.tcl's bare catch{} around detailed_route swallows DRT-0073/0074 pin-access failures; write_views commits the pre-route netlist; 100% of recoverable runs show zero ROUTED nets). Both arms hit the identical wall so the column compares two vacuous zeros. Bead ocm owns the unsolved cause. Stage 2 must not promise a DRC column.

WHAT STAGE 1 RETURNED: designed to produce a PPA delta, it returned two categorical results out of three blocks.
  - memory_coalescer: equivalent on both legs; one measured 6x latency penalty on the empty-mask control path (1 rising edge vs 6).
  - rv32i_hazard_unit: DOUBLY negative -- form inexpressible (combinational/0-FF reference becomes 9-state/50-FF/6-9-cycle data-dependent FSM, proven not an authoring artefact by a branch-free rebuild that scheduled identically) AND 254/2000 differential mismatches, all confined to forwarding outputs with zero stall/flush mismatches.
  - rv32i_cache_arbiter: inexpressible, no C authored.

The top-of-doc recommendation STANDS and is strengthened on its control half: not 'HLS produces worse control logic' but 'HLS cannot express these blocks at all', for reasons following from the C execution model and therefore not fixable by pragma tuning.

TWO HONEST CORRECTIONS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED:
1. The doc named memory_coalescer the 'datapath-ish, HLS-favorable' pole. It is not a datapath block (214 lines of lane-walking FSM + AXI handshakes, zero arithmetic, GPU_ENABLE_COALESCE=0 so nothing is coalesced).
2. Therefore THE DATAPATH HALF OF THE RECOMMENDATION REMAINS UNTESTED. Neither measured block is a datapath block, so nothing in Stage 1 supports or undermines reserving HLS for datapath accelerators -- that hypothesis is exactly as evidenced as before the pilot ran. rtl/gpu/vector_alu.sv (81 lines, 8x 32-bit multiply + shift/logic) is named in the doc as the block that would actually test it. Worth a follow-up bead if the datapath claim matters.

VERIFIED AGAINST ARTEFACTS, not my own summary: both normalized digests cross-checked PROVENANCE.json vs NOTES.md; gpu_coalescer 5/5, cpu_hazard_unit 28/28, mem_cache_arbiter 14/14 all re-run; comparator re-run exit 1 with mismatch_count 254 / total_vectors 2000; tb/tests 149 passed.

REMAINING FOR #119: Stage 2 (P&R + PPA table) is a separate issue and has not been run. It must synthesise both arms for real and state the counting boundary -- Bambu's own estimates (coalescer 820 FF / area 352744; hazard 50 FF / area 1791535) cover the whole generated hierarchy including its AXI master adapter and are NOT comparable to hand-RTL as-is.

title: GH #119: rv32i_cache_arbiter INEXPRESSIBLE.md verdict + the missing standalone TB
description:
TWO separable deliverables.

(a) hls/mem/rv32i_cache_arbiter/INEXPRESSIBLE.md - Bambu emits AXI MASTERS only, and only as a side-effect of pointer dereference (InterfaceInfer.cpp::create_resource_m_axi); no AXI-slave/s_axilite in the 2024.10 interface-mode whitelist (plugin_ASTAnalyzer.cpp:1366-1400); every design wrapped in start_port/done_port. The arbiter is three INCOMING AXI channel sets with grant-hold-until-RLAST and no invocation semantics -> any C++ equivalent pushes 100% of the design into a hand shim. Cite sources, enumerate alternatives, state why a shim-based attempt would be measurement fraud. NO C++ AUTHORED.

(b) tb/cocotb/mem/test_cache_arbiter.py + sim/Makefile:mem_cache_arbiter - the block has NO unit test today; worth fixing regardless of #119. Coverage: I$-only 4-beat read burst; D$-only read burst; D$ writeback burst + B response; priority (simultaneous D$-write + D$-read + I$-read -> D$-write wins); grant-hold (I$ granted, D$ raises mid-burst -> I$ keeps bus until axi_rlast_i); write grant released only on dc_bready_i && axi_bvalid_i; the documented GRANT_NONE one-cycle AR-forwarding delay asserted not accidentally relied on; back-to-back grants no bubble loss; read-data routing isolation. cocotbext-axi already a dependency.
close_reason:
DONE (commit f8988d5). Two separable deliverables, both complete.

(a) hls/mem/rv32i_cache_arbiter/INEXPRESSIBLE.md -- NO C authored, and none should be. This is a RESULT of the pilot, not a concession in it: for this block the answer is not a worse PPA number, it is that the flow cannot express the block at all.

EVIDENCE IS PRIMARY AND LOCALLY REPRODUCIBLE (deliberately not the GitHub source-line citations from the early research pass, which I could not verify -- the AppImage ships binaries, not C++ source):
  * 'mode = s_axilite' is rejected outright: 'probe_slave.c:2:34: error: Invalid HLS interface mode'
  * accepted mode names are compiled into the shipped clang plugin. strings clang16_plugin_ASTAnalyzer.so -> acknowledge/array/axis/handshake/m_axi/ovalid; grep -iE 's_axi|axi.*slave' -> ZERO hits. Same over usr/bin/bambu: zero s_axi, one m_axi.
  * --generate-interface accepts exactly MINIMAL, INFER, WB4 (bambu --help). Under MINIMAL/INFER every top module carries clock/reset/start_port/done_port -- the C execution model made structural (invoke, compute, return). Confirmed on all 3 designs built this pilot.
  * An AXI master is only ever produced as a SIDE-EFFECT of pointer dereference (Bambu's memory-access mechanism). There is no way to ask for AXI channels the design RESPONDS to.

WB4 ADDRESSED HEAD-ON rather than ignored, because it genuinely does emit a slave port. Probed it: produces a memory-mapped CONTROL interface (write args, start, poll done) in Wishbone, still wrapped around a function invocation. No way to express 3 incoming AXI channel sets, per-burst grant retention, or RLAST-terminated release.

WHY NOT FORCE IT: the only way to get the arbiter's port list is a hand-written shim holding the grant register, priority encoder, burst-hold logic and response routing -- the ENTIRE design -- around an HLS core contributing nothing. That comparison would be hand-RTL vs hand-RTL reported as hand-RTL vs HLS. The two measured blocks have wire-only shims precisely so their numbers mean something. This would not be a weak result, it would be a false one.

FOR THE EVAL DOC: upgrades one named case from 'HLS produces worse arbitration logic' to 'HLS CANNOT EXPRESS bus arbitration in this class at all'. Categorical limit -- unlike a PPA number it needs no re-measuring per tool version, only re-checking that the mode list still lacks a slave. Scope stated honestly in the file: about Bambu 2024.10, about permanently-reactive multi-channel bus arbitration, and NOT a claim that the algorithm is hard in C. The obstacle is entirely the interface.

(b) tb/cocotb/mem/test_cache_arbiter.py + sim/Makefile:mem_cache_arbiter -- the block had NO standalone unit test (soc_all reached it only indirectly through full-SoC traffic). Worth closing independently of #119. 14 directed tests: burst grant-hold to RLAST; D$-write > D$-read > I$-read priority; write-grant release on B and NOT wlast; read-data routing isolation both directions; back-to-back hand-off with no lost beats; the one-cycle AR-forwarding delay out of GRANT_NONE asserted EXPLICITLY (so removing the register would be caught, not tolerated); plus AW forward delay, response-code passthrough, reset-mid-burst recovery, idle sanity.

TOOLING DISCREPANCY FOUND: cocotbext-axi could NOT be used on the memory side despite being a repo dependency. Its AxiBus/AxiRam hard-require id-bearing channels (awid/arid/bid/rid non-optional; AxiSlaveRead/Write unconditionally does len(bus.awid)), but this arbiter's master port is deliberately id-less per axi_pkg.sv while still burst-capable -- neither AxiLite- nor AxiBus-shaped. test_icache.py and test_dcache.py hit the same wall and hand-roll their slave; this suite follows that established pattern and documents why at the top of the file.

NON-BLOCKING RTL OBSERVATION (recorded in code comments, no bug filed): the GRANT_DC_WR entry condition is (dc_awvalid_i || dc_wvalid_i) -- an OR, not an AND -- so W-before-AW stimulus would seize the write grant. Harmless under AXI-compliant D-cache behaviour; not given a dedicated test because provoking it requires illegal stimulus. Header comment and FSM/mux logic otherwise agree; no RTL bugs found.

VERIFIED: mem_cache_arbiter 14/14. Assertions proven LIVE by deliberately inverting the priority expectation (13/14, failing exactly there) then reverting. phase3_all 7/7 + 8/8 + 5/5 no regression. tb/tests 149 passed. ruff clean.

title: GH #119: rv32i_hazard_unit C++ + shim + new standalone cocotb TB (control pole)
description:
rtl/cpu/core/rv32i_hazard_unit.sv, 427 L, PURELY COMBINATIONAL (verified: zero clk/rst_n/always_ff), ~30 scalar in -> ~15 scalar out, no protocol. Literally named in the eval doc's own control-heavy list (L20-21 'hazard/forward unit'). All-scalar C++ with mode=none everywhere; no AXI; shim is a pure rename + start_port/done_port tie-off.

EXPECTED CAVEAT: HLS cannot emit pure combinational logic - Bambu will wrap a zero-cycle function in a start/done FSM. That IS the measurement; normalize on throughput at matched fmax per doc L133 and report Bambu's cycle count alongside hand-RTL's 0.

Needs a NEW standalone cocotb TB - test_pipeline_hazards.py is full-core level, nothing drives this block in isolation. It is the shared oracle both arms are scored against. Commission from chip-design-verification:verification-orchestrator.
close_reason:
DONE (commit 5931407). The control pole. Two headline results, both stronger than a PPA delta.

RESULT 1 -- HLS CANNOT EXPRESS THIS BLOCK'S FORM. Reference is purely combinational (no clock, no reset, ZERO flip-flops). Bambu wraps every design in a start/done handshake: 9 FSM states, 50 flip-flops, 6-9 cycles per evaluation, DATA-DEPENDENT latency. For a block whose job is resolving hazards within one cycle, that is not a drop-in replacement at any clock period -- and no pragma tuning converts a multi-cycle FSM back into a combinational cloud.
NOT an authoring artefact: the author rebuilt the stall/flush logic branch-free (no priority chain at all) and got an IDENTICAL schedule (9 states, 6-9 cycles, area within 0.3%). It is Bambu scheduling a 32-bit comparison network against 0.705 ns. That ablation was run unprompted and is what makes the claim solid.

RESULT 2 -- NL->C SPEC DRIFT BIT HERE (it did not on the coalescer), AND IS PRECISELY LOCALISED.
  hand-RTL: 28/28 directed spec-derived tests. HLS: 26/28. Cross-arm differential: 254/2000 vectors mismatched (12.7%).
  Root cause: the two failing vectors set ex1b_mem_rd=1 and ex1c_mem_rd=1, so those producers are LOADS whose data is not ready and those forwarding tiers must be excluded. The HLS version gates only the EX2 tier on mem_rd, not the EX1b/EX1c tiers, so it over-forwards from in-flight loads. Symptom: fwd_a_sel expected 0, got 3.
  THE AUTHOR PREDICTED THIS BEFORE ANY TEST RAN -- ASSUMPTIONS.md residual risk #3 says the gate is 'unreachable in any legal pipeline state... it will only ever fail under random-vector equivalence, never under a trace.' Exactly what happened.
  ALL 254 mismatches land on fwd_* outputs or their *_pre counterparts. NO stall/flush/load-use output EVER mismatched -- the 9-item priority ladder, which the spec states explicitly and completely, transferred perfectly. The drift is confined entirely to what the spec left to inference. Spec-STATED behaviour transferred; spec-IMPLIED behaviour did not. That is the sharpest form of this pilot's result and belongs in the doc.

The divergence is deliberately NOT fixed. It is the measurement.

HARNESS: the arms genuinely differ (combinational vs handshake). Rather than inject RTL into the reference arm to make them uniform, tb/cocotb/cpu/test_hazard_unit.py detects the arm at runtime and branches in exactly ONE place; vectors, expected values and assertions are identical. Two layers: (a) 27 directed tests whose expected values were derived BY HAND FROM THE SPEC -- deriving them from the reference would make the suite a tautology that can only confirm whatever the RTL does; (b) a seeded 2000-vector cross-arm differential diffed by tools/verif/compare_hazard_traces.py, which refuses to pass vacuously on a missing/empty/length-mismatched trace (bead dwp; exit codes 0/1/2 all verified). New standalone coverage for a block that had NONE -- worth having independently of #119.

The verification agent also pushed back correctly on my prompt: I wrote the tier order as EX1b2 > EX1c; the header actually says EX1b2 has 'priority between the EX1c and EX2 tiers', so EX1c > EX1b2. My text was wrong.

SHIM: wire-only, zero registers -- only zero-extension of 26 inputs (5-bit/1-bit -> 32-bit), truncation of 28 outputs (32-bit -> 2-bit/1-bit), plus the four handshake ports the reference lacks. No tie-offs needed (this core exposes no cache_reset, unlike the coalescer). 0 Verilator warnings.

TWO TOOLCHAIN FINDINGS, now encoded in sim/Makefile:
1. Bambu REFUSES to inline ordinary 'static' C helpers. With the forwarding cascade factored into a static function called 5x, Bambu made it a shared 1-resource submodule with 80 bytes of internal DISTRAM and FAILED the build: 'clock constraint too tight: BRAMs for this device cannot run so fast (0.8129 > 0.7050)'. __attribute__((always_inline)) did NOT change the decision. Only preprocessor macros worked. Ordinary C factoring is not available in this flow.
2. Bambu's ~550-instance hierarchy is pathological for Verilator: it emits a symbol-table constructor of ~4000 giant statements in ONE 1.2 MB translation unit, and g++ spun on that single file at 99.9% CPU for 32 MINUTES at -O0 before being killed. Fixed with --output-split 500 on the HLS arms; they also set NO_TRACE=1 since waveform tracing does not scale to that module count either. Both harness-only, no functional effect. OPT_SLOW is NOT the lever -- Verilator already compiles Slow files with no -O flag.

FOR STAGE 2 / bead cge: pin verilog_sha256_normalized = 397eb1ce38e3619a3f0072daa90035b88283fb87216eaf4444512faae593aeda. Bambu estimates (50 FF, area 1791535, 11 control steps, est. fmax 1857 MHz) are not comparable as-is; Stage 2 must synthesise both and state the counting boundary. The one figure needing no normalisation: 0 flip-flops (reference) vs 50 (HLS), for a block the spec describes as combinational.

title: GH #119: memory_coalescer C++ (NL-authored) + shim + two equivalence legs
description:
C++ authored from the NATURAL-LANGUAGE spec (header comment rtl/gpu/memory_coalescer.sv:1-15 + port list), RTL BODY WITHHELD - transliterating the SV would measure transliteration, not the flow. Commit the exact prompt in NOTES.md (part of the reproducibility pin).

Leg 1: Bambu C/RTL cosim (source->RTL) via wrap-bambu.sh.
Leg 2: the EXISTING tb/cocotb/gpu/test_memory_coalescer.py (275 L, 5 tests) reused UNCHANGED against the shim. New sim/Makefile target gpu_coalescer_hls beside gpu_coalescer (sim/Makefile:864-874).

Shim (chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator - hand-written SV, not inline) absorbs 4 obstacles:
 1. module name -> --top-rtldesign-name=memory_coalescer_hls_core, shim named memory_coalescer
 2. port names -> clk/rst_n/start_i/we_i/addr_i/wdata_i/mask_i/done_o/rdata_o + 16 m_* AXI vs Bambu's clock/reset/start_port/done_port/_m_axi_gmem_*
 3. gpu_pkg import - addr_i/wdata_i/rdata_o are [N_LANES-1:0][31:0]; Bambu knows nothing of packages
 4. schedule sensitivity - test_empty_mask asserts done 'immediately', test_serial_4lane_load counts 4 transactions. Expect 1-2 tolerances to widen; APPLY THE LOOSENED TEST TO BOTH ARMS.

Verify arlen is driven to 0 (single-beat, C loop not burst-inferred).
close_reason:
DONE (commit d89b3c9). Both equivalence legs green.

LEG 1 (Bambu C/RTL cosim, validates the HLS step): PASS, 5/5 vectors (8-lane load, sparse load, 8-lane store, sparse store, empty mask), 119 cycles / 23 avg.
LEG 2 (the SAME unmodified cocotb suite as the hand-RTL arm): both arms 5/5. gpu_unit 9/9 suites exit 0; tb/tests 149 passed.

METHOD: C authored by a fresh agent given ONLY the NL spec (header comment of rtl/gpu/memory_coalescer.sv) + port list, explicitly barred from reading anything under rtl/. The session coordinator had already read the reference body and therefore could not author it. Verbatim prompt preserved; ASSUMPTIONS.md records 5 functional assumptions (A1-A6) + 5 HLS-abstraction gaps (B1-B5).

THE SPEC GAP DID NOT BITE. The spec never states that inactive lanes must read back 0, yet test_serial_4lane_load depends on it (it runs right after the 8-lane test; the reference only passes by clearing rdata_q on every start_i). Per the user's decision the spec went over as-written rather than pre-loading the answer. The author independently reasoned to the same behaviour, recorded it as A1, and flagged it as a coin-flip with 'low-medium' confidence of matching the reference. It matched. So on this block, NL->C spec drift did NOT materialise -- a result worth reporting as-is, since the eval doc treats it as a headline risk.

FIRST QUANTIFIED QoR RESULT: test_empty_mask initially FAILED on the HLS arm. Measured: hand-RTL asserts done_o after 1 rising edge (IDLE->DONE directly); Bambu after 6 (47 FSM states / 33 control steps, walking all eight lane predicates sequentially even when none fire). A 6x latency penalty on the empty-mask control path, missing the test's bound by exactly one cycle. This is the 'HLS is weaker on control logic' claim the eval doc argues from literature, now MEASURED on this project's own RTL.

Bound rebased 5 -> 16 rather than accepting the failure, because the spec sets NO cycle budget anywhere -- range(5) was a TB assumption calibrated to the reference's timing. The properties with teeth (done_o eventually asserts; NO AXI traffic) hold on both arms and their assertions are untouched. Change applies to both arms (one shared file) and the test now prints its own measured latency. Routed through chip-design-verification:verification-orchestrator per policy; it independently confirmed the reasoning before editing.

Also corrected two FALSE claims in that TB: it never counted 'exactly 4 AXI transactions issued' (no transaction counter exists; it infers the count from inactive lanes reading 0). Those claims were in the file header and the test docstring.

SHIM IS WIRE-ONLY: module memory_coalescer_hls, port list byte-identical to rtl/gpu/memory_coalescer.sv:17-68 apart from the name. Zero always/always_ff/always_comb/initial blocks, no registers; 0 Verilator warnings from the shim (the core contributes ~100 and is built with -Wno-lint -Wno-style). CONSEQUENCE FOR STAGE 2: Flow B's area is not inflated by the wrapper, so the arms compare without a separate shim line. Absorbs two extra Bambu ports: 'mem' (gmem base from offset=direct, tied 0 so the AXI byte address is exactly addr_i[i]) and 'cache_reset' (vestigial -- passed down to gmem_bambu_artificial_ParmMgr_modgen and never referenced in any always/assign there).

Shim is named memory_coalescer_hls, NOT memory_coalescer, because Bambu's generated core is itself called memory_coalescer. Renaming machine output on every build is one more thing to break silently; the TB never references a module name, only dut.<signal>.

INFRA: sim/Makefile gains gpu_coalescer_hls (distinct SIM_BUILD) + an EXTRA_VERILATOR_FLAGS hook. The hook is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: setting COMPILE_ARGS on a sub-make command line overrides every += in that block and silently drops -Wno-fatal, --public-flat-rw, --no-timing, --timescale and the include dirs.

GITIGNORE TRAP FIXED: the blanket '*.xml' (aimed at cocotb's generated results.xml) was silently swallowing memory_coalescer_tb.xml, which is an INPUT required to regenerate the artefact. It would have gone missing from the repo with no error. Added '!hls/**/*_tb.xml'.

FOR STAGE 2 / bead cge: pin verilog_sha256_normalized = 2cb8a8a2c8b146080a98039ae1a3a07b3a72c70b4a13efb5072cf85d4301a045. Bambu's own estimates (820 FF, area 352744) are NOT comparable to hand-RTL -- they cover the whole generated hierarchy including the AXI master adapter the hand-RTL has no equivalent of, and only 45 of those registers are datapath storage. Stage 2 must synthesise for real and decide the counting boundary first. Cycle counts for throughput normalisation (doc L133): empty-mask 1 (hand-RTL) vs 6 (HLS).

title: GH #119: hls/ tree + tools/hls/ install+run drivers + wrap-bambu.sh (dwp)
description:
Infrastructure. tools/hls/install_bambu.py follows the install-asap7-rcx-rules precedent (pnr/Makefile:839 -> tools/setup/install_asap7_rcx_rules.py): pins BAMBU_VERSION/URL/SHA256/SIZE=1405510848, verifies size AND sha256, HARD-REFUSES any target fs with <10 GB free (/ has only 6 GB), extracts, smoke-tests --version. --check-only gate for every hls/ target. Root Makefile: install-bambu / check-bambu.

tools/eda/wrap-bambu.sh + parse_bambu in tools/eda/summarize.py, dwp discipline, rule order:
 1. ERROR(2) if log lacks EVERY recognised Bambu terminal marker
 2. ERROR(2) if --simulate requested but no sim-result section, or expected .v missing/0 bytes
 3. FAIL(1) on ERROR:/THROW, non-zero cosim mismatch count, non-zero exit
 4. PASS(0) only on explicit success marker AND non-empty .v
Negative-control fixture (truncated log) required to prove the parser is not vacuous.

Generated .v is NOT committed to rtl/ - lives in /nobackup/hls/out/<block>/, only sha256 committed.
close_reason:
DONE (commit c1fc9f7). Delivered: hls/{Makefile,bambu.mk,README.md}, tools/eda/wrap-bambu.sh, parse_bambu in tools/eda/summarize.py, 7 new tests in tb/tests/test_eda_summarize.py, .gitignore + tools/eda/README.md + CLAUDE.md updates.

SCOPE CORRECTIONS vs this bead's original text:
- tools/hls/install_bambu.py NOT written: superseded by the nix flake (commit 8ce91ad). fetchurl enforces the sha256; 'nix develop .#hls --command bambu --version' is the check. No make install-bambu/check-bambu.
- run_bambu.py NOT written: flags live in hls/bambu.mk, and the aggregate hls/PROVENANCE.json is bead cge's deliverable. A second provenance mechanism here would leave two half-finished ones. Per-run provenance (top/device/clock/cycles/ff/area/sha256) is emitted as fields in the wrapper's JSON verdict.

PARSER DESIGN: parse_bambu reads Bambu's own echoed command line from log line 1 to learn whether --simulate was requested, instead of making the caller declare it. This is what distinguishes a generation-only run (legitimately has no cycle block -> PASS) from a --simulate run whose cosim silently died (-> ERROR). Ladder: FAIL on exit!=0 or any 'error ->'/'Returned error code'/MDPI line; ERROR if no 'Total number of flip-flops' (banner alone proves nothing, Bambu prints it before doing any work); ERROR if --simulate but no 'Total cycles'; ERROR if the .v is missing or 0 bytes; else PASS. Takes a 3rd arg (verilog path) so it stays OUT of PARSERS, exactly like parse_cocotb.

TWO FINDINGS worth carrying forward:
1. Bambu's -o does NOT relocate the emitted Verilog. It writes <top>.v and HLS_output/ into the CURRENT directory. wrap-bambu.sh cd's into the out-dir; callers MUST pass source/testbench paths as ABSOLUTE. (Cost one failed end-to-end run to discover.)
2. Bambu output is NOT byte-reproducible: it stamps the generation time into a header comment of every .v. Verified across 3 back-to-back runs of identical input -> 3 different sha256, byte-identical everywhere except the '- Date ...' line. The wrapper now emits BOTH verilog_sha256 (identity of the file on disk) and verilog_sha256_normalized (date blanked, stable across runs = b75de22c... for gate_b). ACTION FOR BEAD cge: pin the NORMALIZED digest; a committed raw sha256 would fail on every regeneration.

VERIFIED: 32 summarize tests pass (7 new bambu cases), 149 in tb/tests overall, ruff format/check + mypy clean. Ladder exercised against the REAL Gate A/B logs, not just inline fixtures: gb_xml.log+.v -> PASS(0); gateb.log generation-only -> PASS(0); gb_sim2.log 'error -> Co-simulation main aborted' -> FAIL(1); missing .v -> ERROR(2); head -20 truncated -> ERROR(2); --simulate stripped of error lines but no cycles -> ERROR(2). End-to-end 'nix develop .#hls --command make -C hls gate_b' -> exit 0 with full JSON provenance.

title: GH #119 Gate B: Bambu port-shape probe (B1-B4) - the real feasibility gate
description:
~30-line gate_b.cpp with the coalescer's SHAPE and none of its logic: one m_axi bundle; a0..a7/w0..w7/mask/we as INDIVIDUAL SCALARS (not arrays - arrays become BRAM-style _address0/_ce0/_we0/_d0/_q0 ports); r0..r7 as mode=none pointer-outs.

B1: one _m_axi_gmem_* master set, all of araddr/arvalid/arready/rdata/rvalid/rready/awaddr/awvalid/awready/wdata/wstrb/wvalid/wready/bvalid/bready present.
B2: a0..a7,w0..w7,mask,we plain scalar inputs; r0..r7 plain scalar outputs; NO BRAM-style ports. (shim-cost test)
B3: clock/reset/start_port/done_port present; FFs async active-low (--reset-type=async --reset-level=low; Bambu default is 'no' reset).
B4: --simulate succeeds AND verilator lints the .v clean.

B1-B4 pass -> wire-only shim, proceed. B2 alone fails -> shim gains registers; split Stage 2 table into core+shim BEFORE measuring. B1 fails -> kill the coalescer AXI arm.
close_reason:
PASSED (B1-B4), with one criterion restated. The coalescer arm is viable with a WIRE-ONLY shim.

Probe: /nobackup/hls/scratch/gateB/gate_b.c (44 lines, coalescer port SHAPE only, no real algorithm) -> coal_shape.v.

B1 PASS - full AXI4 master emitted as one m_axi_gmem_* bundle: araddr/arvalid/arready, rdata/rvalid/rready/rlast/rid/rresp/ruser, awaddr/awvalid/awready/awid/awlen/awsize/awburst/awlock/awcache/awprot/awqos/awregion/awuser, wdata/wstrb/wlast/wvalid/wready/wuser, bvalid/bready/bresp/bid/buser.

B2 PASS - THE decisive result. ZERO BRAM-style ports anywhere in the top module (no _address0/_ce0/_we0/_d0/_q0). All 18 inputs (a0..a7, w0..w7, mask, we) are plain 'input [31:0]' scalars and all 8 outputs (r0..r7) are plain 'output [31:0]' scalars. Declaring the lanes as INDIVIDUAL SCALAR ARGS (not arrays) is what achieves this - keep that constraint when authoring the real memory_coalescer.cpp. Consequence: the shim adapting Bambu's interface to memory_coalescer's port list is pure renaming/slicing, no registers, so Flow B's area is not inflated by the shim.

B3 PASS - clock, reset, start_port, done_port present (plus cache_reset). 11 'always @(posedge clock or negedge reset)' blocks = async active-low, matching repo convention.

B4 PASS (cosim) - exit 0, 2/2 vectors (full mask 0xFF and sparse mask 0x55), 58 cycles total / 29 average, verified against the C golden by Bambu's MDPI driver.

B4 CRITERION RESTATED (lint): 'Verilator lints the generated .v clean' is NOT achievable and should not be a gate for machine-generated HLS output. Under -Wall: 100 warnings (59 UNUSEDSIGNAL - mostly unused AXI sideband rid/rlast/bid, expected for a single-beat design; 10 WIDTHTRUNC, 10 WIDTHEXPAND, 9 GENUNNAMED, 8 UNDRIVEN, 2 UNUSEDPARAM, 1 PROCASSINIT, 1 DECLFILENAME). Even DEFAULT lint exits 1 (20 warnings; verilator errors out on warnings). ZERO errors in either case. The achievable, meaningful criterion - verified for BOTH gate_b/coal_shape.v and gateA/sum.v - is: elaborates cleanly (exit 0) under 'verilator --lint-only -Wno-lint -Wno-style'. Bambu's own cosim builds it with Verilator 5.048 successfully. ACTION for bead cfi: the cocotb target for the HLS arm must carry these suppressions; do NOT apply them to the hand-RTL arm.

Two reusable testbench gotchas found:
1. A C-driver testbench (--generate-tb=x.c) does NOT size m_axi memory spaces from a decayed pointer: 'unsigned* mem' got a 4-byte space, so any access past offset 0 failed with 'Interface N: Read to non-mapped address'. Passing 8 pointers into ONE array also collapses to a single 4-byte space ('Unknown data required: 4'). Use the XML testbench form (--generate-tb=x.xml) where mem="{v0,...,vN}" sizes the space explicitly, and give each pointer output its own r_i="{0}" entry. XML is the reliable route for m_axi designs.
2. --tb-param-size=<param>:<bytes> would fix the sizing but its own help says it 'will disable automated top-level function verification' - using it makes the equivalence leg VACUOUS. Do not use it.

title: GH #119 Gate A: Bambu 2024.10 AppImage install + ASAP7 device smoke test
description:
Feasibility gate A. Install to /nobackup/hls/bambu via --appimage-extract (no FUSE), record sha256+size+--version, capture full --help. Reproduce Bambu's own tutorial_hpca_2023/04-axi exercise with --device-name=asap7-TC from inside nix develop (Bambu locates verilator with a literal system("which verilator")).

GO/NO-GO: exit 0; generated .v has _m_axi_.*_(araddr|arvalid|rvalid|awvalid|wvalid|bvalid) ports; log shows an explicit cosim-success marker. Fail -> AppImage/ASAP7-device/Verilator triple broken, re-scope.
close_reason:
PASSED. Bambu 2024.10 (rev c2ba6936ca2ed63137095fea0b630a1c66e20e63-main) packaged as nix devShells.hls in flake.nix (commit 8ce91ad), AppImage pinned by sha256 e4f0214496a5d35de1932975b0f41cd95bc33a53a904fc565d6c2cb01df40773 (1405510848 B). Ad-hoc /nobackup/hls/bambu tree (5.7 GB) deleted; nix build has ZERO /nobackup references and reproduces the run identically.

Gate A criteria, all met:
- exit 0 on an m_axi array-sum kernel with --device-name=asap7-TC --clock-period=0.705
- generated .v carries a full AXI4 master: 44 m_axi_gmem_* ports incl. araddr/arvalid/arready/rdata/rvalid/rready/awaddr/awvalid/awready/wdata/wstrb/wvalid/wready/bvalid/bready
- clock/reset/start_port/done_port/return_port present
- 'always @(posedge clock or negedge reset)' = async active-low, matches repo convention
- Verilator 5.048 cosim ran 2/2 XML vectors, 62 cycles total / 31 average (Bambu aborts on mismatch, so this IS the equivalence pass)

Five env fixes were required; all documented inline in flake.nix. Root causes worth remembering:
1. nixpkgs appimage-exec.sh execs AppRun without ARGV0 -> tool_select.sh multi-call dispatch resolves to a bare directory. Fixed by exec'ing usr/bin/bambu directly.
2. APPDIR re-roots the binary's hardcoded /usr/share/panda and /usr/gcc_plugins.
3. libbdd.so.0 missing made clang16_plugin_dumpGimpleSSA.so silently fail to load, so its -panda-* options never registered and clang emitted the MISLEADING 'Did you mean --panda-TFN?'. pkgs.ncurses5 is NOT a valid source of libtinfo.so.5 (ldconfig indexes by SONAME; ncurses-abi5-compat libtinfo.so.5 -> libncursesw.so.5.9 has SONAME libncursesw.so.5, so no libtinfo.so.5 cache entry exists). LD_LIBRARY_PATH is also NOT viable: the MDPI cosim sub-make does not inherit it. Use the AppImage own libs symlinked into FHS /usr/lib64.
4. verilator must be INSIDE the FHS env (literal system(which verilator)).
5. MDPI harness is built -m32 (matches the design 32-bit pointers, true for our blocks too) -> needs glibc_multi.dev AND multiArch=true. multiPkgs alone leaves /usr/lib32 empty.

title: Beads off-machine sync is dead: refs/dolt/data 71 days stale, Dolt backup writes only to a gitignored local dir
description:
Found 2026-08-16 while implementing bead b1o's fix. CLAUDE.md states 'sync uses refs/dolt/data on your git remote; .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export'. Neither half is currently true in practice.

MEASURED:
 * git ls-remote origin 'refs/dolt/*' returns exactly one ref, refs/dolt/data -> e70ebde13d27ca896ac562fa1e2f2ab1b6c609cb.
 * git log -1 --format=%ad e70ebde -> Sat Jun 6 10:32:49 2026. That is 71 days stale as of today.
 * The ref did NOT advance across two real 'git push' operations this session, despite bead closures and a new bead being created between them.
 * 'bd backup status' reports enabled=true (auto: git remote detected), last backup 13m ago, interval 15m -- so backup IS running. But it writes Dolt archive (.darc) files into .beads/backup/, which is gitignored (.beads/.gitignore:54 'backup/'). Nothing in .beads/ records any remote URL. Note 'Database size: 0 B' in that same status output, which also looks wrong.

CONSEQUENCE: the only bead state that reaches the remote is the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl. The Dolt DB and its backups are local to this machine. The config comment calls the backup 'off-machine recovery'; it is not off-machine. A disk loss here loses all issue history beyond whatever the last committed jsonl held.

This is why fix (a) on b1o (untrack the jsonl) was attempted and REVERTED -- untracking would have left 123 issues with no shared copy at all.

ALSO RELEVANT (root cause of b1o itself, established while testing): git worktrees each get their own .beads/embeddeddolt, seeded from the tracked jsonl when the worktree is created. Agents working in separate worktrees therefore run independent Dolt DBs that diverge from the main one, and beads' pre-commit hook exports each worktree's own DB state into its branch. A branch cut before a closure carries that stale state and reinstates it on merge. b1o's merge driver fixes the merge side of this; the divergence itself is inherent to per-worktree DBs and is worth understanding before relying on multi-worktree agent workflows.

TO INVESTIGATE: why refs/dolt/data stopped updating in June (bd was upgraded? backup destination reconfigured to local?); whether 'bd backup init' should point at a real off-machine destination; whether 'Database size: 0 B' indicates a broken backup despite the success timestamp. If off-machine sync is restored, b1o fix (a) becomes available and is the cleanest answer.
notes:
2026-09-07 ROOT-CAUSED. The premise of this bead was half wrong; corrected in CLAUDE.md:391 this session.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (bd version 1.0.4, ce242a879):
 * bd 1.0.4 has NO refs/dolt/data mechanism. `bd backup --help` shows the whole model:
   `bd backup init <path>` -> a filesystem directory OR a DoltHub remote URL
   (https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/<user>/<repo>, DOLT_REMOTE_USER/DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD).
   There is no git-ref transport anywhere in it. The refs/dolt/data ref on origin
   (e70ebde, Sat Jun 6 10:32:49 2026) is a FOSSIL from a pre-1.0.4 bd. Nothing advances
   it because nothing in the installed bd knows it exists. "Why it stopped updating in
   June" = bd was upgraded past the mechanism. Not a regression to chase.
 * Backup is running and HEALTHY, not broken: 13 MB of .darc archives in .beads/backup/,
   newest 2026-09-07 20:44, 15-minute interval, backup_state.json current. The bead's
   "whether Database size: 0 B indicates a broken backup" question resolves to NO -- it
   is a cosmetic reporting bug in `bd backup status`. The real DB is 21 MB at
   .beads/embeddeddolt/.
 * The REAL defect is narrower than the bead states and worse in one respect. Auto-detection
   ("enabled=true (auto: git remote detected)") chose .beads/backup/ as the destination.
   That is gitignored (.beads/.gitignore "backup/") AND on the same physical disk as the DB
   (both under / on /dev/sdb2). So it is not off-machine and not even off-disk: a single
   sdb2 failure loses the DB and every backup of it simultaneously. Only the tracked
   issues.jsonl survives.

NOT A PROBLEM (checked while here): the merge driver is correctly registered --
merge.beads-export.driver -> tools/setup/beads_merge_driver.sh %A. b1o's protection is
intact. (An earlier grep for merge.beads-jsonl.* returned nothing; that was the wrong key
name, not a missing driver.)

REMAINING WORK = a destination decision that needs the user, since no off-machine target
exists on this host (df shows only / on sdb2 and /nobackup on sda1 -- no NAS, no Dropbox,
no network mount; DOLT_REMOTE_USER/PASSWORD unset):
 (a) DoltHub: `bd backup init https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/<user>/<repo>` + creds.
     Genuinely off-machine. Needs a DoltHub account -> user decision, not agent-actionable.
 (b) /nobackup/beads-backup: different physical device (sda1, 463 G free), so it survives an
     sdb2 failure but not a machine loss. Free, immediate, strictly better than today.
     Note the mount is named "nobackup" and is presumably not itself backed up.
 (c) Accept and document. Done either way -- CLAUDE.md:391 now describes the real
     mechanism, the real destination, the same-disk exposure, and the cosmetic 0 B bug.

Bead stays OPEN pending the (a)/(b)/(c) choice. The documentation half is landed.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-09 per user decision: backup destination moved to /nobackup/beads-backup.

DONE AND VERIFIED:
  bd backup init /nobackup/beads-backup
  bd backup sync              -> "Backup synced in 1.446s"
  du -sh /nobackup/beads-backup -> 9.7 MB (manifest, oldgen, LOCK, .darc archive present)
  bd backup status            -> "Destination: file:///nobackup/beads-backup"
  df                          -> /nobackup = /dev/sda1, repo/.beads = /dev/sdb2
Different physical device confirmed -- that was the whole point.

WHAT THIS FIXES: auto-detection had chosen .beads/backup/, which is gitignored AND on the same
physical disk as the Dolt DB. A single sdb2 failure would have destroyed the database and every
backup of it simultaneously, leaving only the tracked issues.jsonl.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated plainly so nobody over-reads it: this survives a DISK loss, not a
MACHINE loss. /nobackup is a local mount and is presumably not itself backed up (the name says
so). For machine-loss protection the option remains a DoltHub remote --
`bd backup init https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/<user>/<repo>` with DOLT_REMOTE_USER /
DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD -- which needs an account and was deliberately deferred.

CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL PREMISE, established during investigation and already
landed in CLAUDE.md:
 * bd 1.0.4 has NO refs/dolt/data mechanism at all. The stale ref on origin is a fossil from a
   pre-1.0.4 bd. It did not "stop working" -- bd was upgraded past the mechanism. Not a
   regression to chase.
 * Backup was never broken. It had been running healthily on a 15-minute interval the whole
   time; only its destination was wrong.
 * `bd backup status`'s "Database size: 0 B" is a cosmetic reporting bug, not evidence of a
   broken backup. The real DB is 21 MB at .beads/embeddeddolt/.
 * The merge driver (merge.beads-export -> tools/setup/beads_merge_driver.sh) was checked while
   here and is correctly registered, so bead b1o's protection is intact.

RESTORE PATH NOT EXERCISED: `bd backup restore` was deliberately not run, because it would
overwrite the live database. A backup whose restore has never been tested is a known residual
risk -- worth exercising once against a scratch copy if anyone wants full confidence.

title: Merging a PR branched before a bead closure resurrects that closed bead (stale .beads/issues.jsonl re-import)
description:
REPRODUCED TWICE on 2026-08-16, deterministically.

SYMPTOM: beads that were closed and whose fixes are merged silently return to status=open after a routine 'git pull' of main.

MEASURED: after the PR #159 merge sync, open beads went 8 -> 10; claude_verilog_test-0eh (fixed+merged PR #157) and claude_verilog_test-pzj (fixed+merged PR #158) were both back to open. Re-closed them. Then after the PR #160 merge sync, the IDENTICAL pair resurrected again, 8 -> 10. Not a one-off.

MECHANISM: .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export of the Dolt DB (per CLAUDE.md and the beads SYNC_CONCEPTS doc), but it is a tracked file. A PR branched BEFORE a bead was closed carries that bead's older open-state row. Merging that PR overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl in main with the stale content, and bd then re-imports the file into the DB, overwriting the newer closed state. The longer a branch lives, the more closures it silently reverts on merge. PRs #159 and #160 were both branched before the #157/#158 closures landed -- hence exactly that pair each time.

WHY IT MATTERS: this corrupts tracker state invisibly. Nothing errors; the bead just quietly reopens, and the close_reason (which carries the verification evidence) can be lost. Anyone reading 'bd ready' after a merge gets phantom work that is already done and shipped.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not yet evaluated, pick deliberately):
 (a) stop tracking .beads/issues.jsonl in git (add to .gitignore); the Dolt DB + refs/dolt/data is already the sync mechanism, so the jsonl is redundant as a tracked artifact and only exists as a convenience snapshot.
 (b) keep it tracked but add a merge driver / .gitattributes entry so it is never taken from the incoming branch verbatim.
 (c) make the DB authoritative on import: refuse to move an issue backwards (closed -> open) from a jsonl import without an explicit flag.
 (d) a post-merge hook that always re-exports from the DB, so the file is regenerated rather than consumed.

WORKAROUND IN USE: after every merge sync, run 'bd list --status open' and compare against the expected set; re-close anything that resurrected. Done manually twice already, which is exactly the kind of silent-corruption toil that should not be manual.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-16, after b1o was closed: the root-cause layer 1 recorded in the close reason and in PR #161 is WRONG. It claimed 'each git worktree gets its own .beads/embeddeddolt, so agents in separate worktrees ran independent, diverging Dolt DBs'. That is false.

MEASURED: only the primary worktree has a DB (.beads/embeddeddolt, 19 MB). The secondary worktree claude_verilog_test-q7n has NO embeddeddolt at all -- its .beads/ holds only config.yaml, hooks/, metadata.json, README.md and the two jsonl files. There is exactly one shared database.

ACTUAL MECHANISM (evidence-backed):
 * beads' commit-time export hook writes to the PRIMARY worktree's .beads/issues.jsonl regardless of which worktree the commit is made in (observed independently by the q7n agent, which saw its commit rewrite the main worktree's file).
 * A secondary worktree keeps its own checked-out copy of .beads/issues.jsonl, frozen at branch-creation time, and nothing ever refreshes it. Confirmed: claude_verilog_test-q7n/.beads/issues.jsonl still carries 0eh -> open (updated 2026-08-15T00:43:18Z) and pzj -> open (updated 2026-08-05T10:33:07Z), both pre-closure.
 * An agent in a secondary worktree that runs 'git add .beads/issues.jsonl' therefore commits that STALE snapshot onto its branch. Merging it to main reinstates the stale rows, which the post-merge import replays into the DB.
 * Corroboration: PR #162 (q7n) touched only the three tools/formal files and no .beads/ file at all -- that agent did not stage the stale copy, and no stale rows came from it. The earlier branches that DID commit beads exports are the ones that carried the regression.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: none. The merge driver landed in PR #161 regenerates issues.jsonl from the DB on merge, which neutralises this mechanism just as well as the one originally described, so b1o stays correctly CLOSED. Only the explanation needed fixing.

PRACTICAL RULE, now documented in CLAUDE.md: agents working in a secondary worktree must NOT 'git add' .beads/.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED in PR #161 (merge 2829c68).

Fix landed: option (b), a custom git merge driver. .gitattributes points .beads/issues.jsonl at merge=beads-export -> tools/setup/beads_merge_driver.sh, which REGENERATES the file from the authoritative Dolt DB rather than reconciling two texts, so the result is correct by construction and beads' post-merge import becomes a no-op. interactions.jsonl keeps merge=union, which is genuinely correct for an append-only audit log. Registered per clone by 'make setup-beads' (now a dependency of 'make setup') and CHECKED by 'make verify-tooling' -- an unregistered driver otherwise fails silently back into the old behaviour.

ROOT CAUSE, established during the fix and more precise than this bead's original description -- two layers:
 1. Each git worktree gets its OWN .beads/embeddeddolt, seeded from the tracked jsonl at worktree creation. Agents working in separate worktrees therefore ran independent, diverging Dolt DBs, and beads' pre-commit hook exported each worktree's own state into its branch. A branch cut before a closure carries the pre-closure state.
 2. merge=union kept it. Union is right for an append-only log and wrong for a per-record STATE file: it concatenates hunks, keeps a stale status:open row for an already-closed issue, and never reconciles two rows sharing an id.

VERIFIED, not assumed:
 * driver run against main's real post-#160 stale file: 0eh and pzj flip open -> closed, exit 0.
 * git check-attr merge: issues.jsonl -> beads-export, interactions.jsonl -> union.
 * bd absent from PATH: warns, keeps ours, exit 0 (a missing tool must not hard-fail a merge).
 * END-TO-END on the real #161 merge pull: open beads stayed 10 (previously went 8 -> 10 on each of the two prior merge syncs), 0eh and pzj both stayed CLOSED, and main's tracked jsonl now records them as closed. Caveat: that particular pull's incoming content already matched the DB, so it may not have exercised the driver's conflict path -- the direct stale-file test above is the stronger evidence.

FIX (a), untracking the jsonl, was attempted and REVERTED as unsafe: refs/dolt/data is 71 days stale and the Dolt backup writes only to the gitignored .beads/backup/, so the tracked jsonl is currently the only bead state reaching the remote. That is filed separately as claude_verilog_test-a7c and remains OPEN. If off-machine sync is repaired, (a) becomes available and is the cleaner answer.

Fixes (c) and (d) not implemented; unnecessary under (b), but recorded there if the file is ever tracked differently.

title: ASAP7 DRT-0073/0074 pin-access geometry root cause not yet solved (follow-up to xy6)
description:
Follow-up to claude_verilog_test-xy6, which root-caused the ZERO-WIRE symptom
(drt.tcl's catch{} around detailed_route aborts the whole routing call on the
first pin-access failure, before track assignment starts) and landed a
fail-loud gate (tools/verif/check_asap7_routing.py + pnr/Makefile
check-asap7-{routing,gpu-routing,soc-routing} targets).

NOT solved by xy6: WHY the individual DRT-0073 (macro boundary pins, e.g.
u_cpu/apb_paddr_i[5], u_gpu/m_axi_araddr[19] on SoC run 14) and DRT-0074
(top-level I/O pins, e.g. 325 on GPU standalone, 401 on CPU standalone)
pin-access points fail to resolve in the first place.

Partially characterized (see memory/pd/knowledge.md "DRT-0074: No Access
Point for PIN" and the 2026-08-16 UPDATE under the xy6 entry):
- Top-level I/O pins: ASAP7 M4/M5 WIDTHTABLE rejects narrow pin widths;
  FP_IO_HTHICKNESS_MULT mitigated (2->5->8) but did NOT eliminate all
  failures -- congestion/obstruction near specific die-edge locations is
  the untested remaining hypothesis.
- SoC macro-boundary pins: unexplained beyond "abstract LEF pin geometry
  vs. post-macro-placement track grid." Run 14's exact failing-pin geometry
  cannot be reconstructed (pin_order.cfg postdates it by GH #96; 393/401
  boundary pins reshuffle on every macro regeneration absent it).

Next steps (not started): load a failing run's post-placement ODB in the
eda-openroad MCP session and query the exact track/via geometry around a
known-failing pin (e.g. u_gpu/m_axi_araddr[19] in SoC run 14, if that ODB
checkpoint still exists) to determine whether it's a track-alignment,
obstruction, or via-rule issue. Will likely require a full P&R run to
reproduce on a current macro/config (host reboot risk, bead o1i -- run in
tmux/nohup, expect 4-8h for SoC).

Distinct from and cross-linked to (do not merge):
- claude_verilog_test-e69 (RCX rules) -- blocked behind real routing existing
- claude_verilog_test-gyx (PSM-0069 tap-cell artifact) -- considered as a
  related PDK-geometry mechanism, no evidence found linking the two
notes:
2026-09-09 ***ROUTING GATE PASSES.*** RUN_2026-09-09_14-56-03 is the FIRST ASAP7 run in this
project's history to produce a genuinely routed result. check_asap7_routing.py exits 0.

  routed_net_record_count  33,396
  route__wirelength        270,938
  route__wirelength__max   321.17     (previously 0 on every run ever)
  drt_error_count          0
  steps completed          52         (reached write_views; final DEF exists)

All three gate conditions met: >=1 ROUTED record in the final DEF, route__wirelength__max > 0,
and zero [ERROR DRT-*]. Run marked .signoff so prune_runs cannot evict it.

⚠️ THIS IS NOT PHYSICAL CLOSURE, AND THE GATE DOES NOT CLAIM IT IS. route__drc_errors = 2045.
The gate checks only that detailed routing committed wires and threw no errors; ordinary DRC
violations are deliberately NOT among its criteria. DRT_OPT_ITERS was bounded to 12 (default
64) specifically to obtain a final DEF within the available time and memory -- the unbounded
run reached 43 violations by iteration ~45 but never wrote views. So 2045 is a consequence of
the deliberate iteration cap, not a routing defect. DO NOT quote this run as DRC-clean, and do
not let the gate PASS be read as sign-off.

WHAT THIS DOES SETTLE:
 * The whole chain from bead ocm is confirmed end to end. edf00dff could not grant pin access
   on ASAP7 at all; dcf36133 can; the +10 DBU shift on gen_data_sram[1] clears the residual 16
   DRT-0255; and detailed routing then runs to completion and writes a real DEF.
 * The "0 DRC / 0 antenna" claims withdrawn under bead xy6 were withdrawn correctly -- those
   runs committed zero wires. This run committed 33,396 routed nets, so the project finally has
   a routing result that is not vacuous.

WHAT REMAINS BEFORE ANY ASAP7 SIGN-OFF CAN BE RE-CLAIMED:
 1. Re-run unbounded (or with a higher cap) to drive DRC violations down; the unbounded run
    plateaued at 43, whose layer/type is still untriaged.
 2. Memory: the unbounded DRT step peaked at 13 GiB on a 15.9 GB host and did not reach

 3. Timing/power from this run are NOT trustworthy -- the 3.0.14 shell resolves sta to OpenSTA

 4. The grid-alignment mechanism behind the point fix is still only correlational -- its
    positive control refuted it as a general rule (see the session-3 correction). The fix is a
