UNBLOCKS: bead e69 (SPEF / post-route STA now has real wires to extract from) and possibly
gyx (IR drop). Both were queued behind exactly this.

title: cocotb sim_build dirs exhaust the root FS during soc_all (results.xml write fails after tests PASS)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on branch fix/spi-miso-sync-a2g: soc_all aborted twice at the dma target with 'ERROR: results.xml was not written by the simulation!' AFTER all 6 dma tests reported PASS and Verilog $finish. Re-running the dma target standalone passes and writes results.xml (EXIT=0), so it is not an RTL or testbench fault -- it is intermittent ENOSPC.

ROOT CAUSE: root FS was at 99% (2.1 GB free) while tb/cocotb/soc holds 26 per-target sim_build dirs at ~192 MB each (~5 GB total). Per-target SIM_BUILD is correct and must stay (bead 7je fixed a real false-pass with it), but it multiplied the footprint ~26x. Any RTL edit invalidates all of them, so a full soc_all rebuild needs several GB the disk does not have; the run dies part-way, and the failure surfaces as a post-test results.xml write error rather than anything that looks like a disk problem.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE: the failure mode prints per-suite PASS lines right up to the abort. A reader skimming the log sees PASS everywhere and a make error at the end -- easy to misread as flaky infra and re-run, which is exactly what happened here. It is also silent about the real cause.

WORKAROUND APPLIED 2026-08-14 (not a fix, not committed -- it is local filesystem state): all 26 dirs moved to /nobackup/claude_sim_build/soc/ and symlinked back from tb/cocotb/soc. Root went 2.1 GB -> 3.8 GB free. /nobackup has 502 GB.

REAL FIX: make the SIM_BUILD base configurable in tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile -- e.g. SIM_BUILD_ROOT ?= . with SIM_BUILD=$(SIM_BUILD_ROOT)/sim_build_$@... -- so a developer or CI can point it at scratch without symlink surgery. CLAUDE.md already documents routing SIM_BUILD to /nobackup for the AMS cosim flow; this generalises the same idea to the whole soc suite. Consider also a 'make clean-sim-builds' target and a pre-flight free-space check that fails loudly instead of dying mid-run.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-14, PR #150 (branch chore/simbuild-root-f97, commit 11cd08a).

SIM_BUILD_ROOT ?= . added to all three schemes that existed: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile (one generic assignment), tb/cocotb/cpu/Makefile (which never set SIM_BUILD at all -- one shared 146 MB dir), and sim/Makefile (14 hardcoded literals / 16 dirs). Default stays '.' so an unset environment is path-identical to before; CI unaffected. Bead 7je per-target isolation and the SRAM_TARGET suffix preserved untouched -- only the base dir moves.

ALSO FIXED, beyond the bead as filed:
- distclean was hardcoded CWD-relative in ALL THREE Makefiles, so against relocated dirs it deleted only the symlinks and orphaned the real 1.8 GB on scratch. All three now sweep $(SIM_BUILD_ROOT) via the new clean-sim-builds target. sim/Makefile's explicit dir list had also drifted stale -> replaced by a glob.
- check-space pre-flight gate on soc_all (SIM_BUILD_MIN_FREE_MB ?= 6000), fails loudly naming the real cause instead of dying mid-run.
- .gitignore had 'sim_build*/' only; the trailing slash is directory-only so the relocated SYMLINKS were untracked-but-committable on any clone without a local .git/info/exclude entry. Slashless form added.

TRAP HIT AND FIXED DURING THE WORK, worth remembering: placing the check-space TARGET near the top of tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile made it make's DEFAULT GOAL, because the cocotb 'include' is at line 401 and the per-suite recipes re-invoke $(MAKE) MODULE=... with NO explicit target. Result: every suite ran the space check instead of the test and the whole run EXITED 0 HAVING TESTED NOTHING -- same false-pass class as beads 7je and dwp. The recipe now lives below the include with an in-file comment; only the variables may live at the top. .DEFAULT_GOAL verified byte-identical to main (= 'all').

EVIDENCE (clean run, whole run through SIM_BUILD_ROOT, no branch switching):
- soc_all 26 suites, TESTS=183 PASS=183 FAIL=0 SKIP=0, zero error markers -- matches the a2g baseline exactly
- 0 in-tree sim_build dirs afterwards, 26 on scratch, root FS unchanged at 4.3 GB free across the entire run (previously a full rebuild tried to put ~5 GB there)
- unset SIM_BUILD_ROOT -> SIM_BUILD=./sim_build_timer, path-identical to today
- 7je isolation intact: distinct Vtop md5 per target; sim_build_sram_controller vs _sky130 still differ
- check-space fires on the real 97%-full root, passes on scratch

NOTE for whoever runs regressions next: the first verification attempt was invalidated because branches were switched mid-run, which reverted the Makefile and made the last 5 suites build in-tree. Do not switch branches while a background soc_all is in flight.

title: pnr/Makefile RTL_SOURCES has the same package rot - make -C pnr lint is broken, and the new closure checker does not scan it
description:
FOURTH instance of the 50t/v2q/135 class, found 2026-08-11 while verifying the 50t fix.

MEASURED: pnr/Makefile's RTL_SOURCES (lines 228-251, consumed by the 'lint' target at line 255 via VERILATOR_LINT_FLAGS) does not close over its files' imports. Ran the list by hand from pnr/ with verilator 5.048:
  %Error: ../rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv:5:8: Import package not found: 'axi_pkg'
  %Error: ../rtl/cpu/core/rv32i_core.sv:15:8: Import package not found: 'axi_pkg'
  %Error: ../rtl/mem/rv32i_icache.sv:39:8: Import package not found: 'axi_pkg'
So 'make -C pnr lint' is broken, exactly like the CPU cocotb suites were.

The list is stale in the same two ways tb/cocotb/cpu/Makefile was: no axi_pkg.sv / soc_addr_map_pkg.sv (M2 AXI4 burst upgrade), and the pre-retiming EX set only -- grep for ex1b/ex1c/ex2/axi_pkg/soc_addr_map across lines 225-252 returns ZERO hits. It also still lists rtl/cpu/rv32i_axi_arbiter.sv, the Phase 1 leftover that is declared but instantiated nowhere in rtl/ (dropped from the cocotb list in c4f559c).

SECOND HALF OF THIS BEAD -- the checker has a coverage hole. tools/verif/check_source_closure.py (added in c4f559c for bead 50t) scans pnr/*/*/config.json, tb/cocotb/*/Makefile and sim/Makefile, but NOT pnr/Makefile's own variables. That is why this instance survived the repo-wide scan that was supposed to be the generalisation of 50t/v2q. Fixing only the source list would leave the same blind spot for the next one.

FIX, both halves:
1. Add axi_pkg.sv + soc_addr_map_pkg.sv ahead of the importing modules in RTL_SOURCES, add rv32i_pipeline_ex1b/ex1c/ex2.sv and rv32i_clock_gate.sv, drop rv32i_axi_arbiter.sv. Mirror the import-closed order already proven in pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json.
2. Extend check_source_closure.py to scan pnr/Makefile variables too, then re-run the repo-wide check.
Verify with: make -C pnr lint (must reach 'Lint PASSED'), and check_source_closure.py exiting 0 on the newly covered list.

RELATED: 50t (cocotb list, fixed in c4f559c / PR #137), v2q (pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json, fixed in e8b414f), 135 (four legacy PD configs, open).
close_reason:
FIXED, both halves. pnr/Makefile RTL_SOURCES now closes (packages first, EX1c/EX1b/EX2 + rv32i_clock_gate.sv added, dead rv32i_axi_arbiter.sv dropped, mirroring pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json's proven order); verilator 5.048 elaborates it clean, 30 modules, exit 0. Checker extended to scan pnr/Makefile.

Extending the checker exposed TWO REAL BUGS IN THE CHECKER ITSELF, both of which would have made pnr/Makefile unscannable (they over-report rather than silently pass, so nothing previously reported was wrong): (1) evaluate_list resolved relative tokens against the repo root, but a Makefile's relative paths are relative to that Makefile's directory -- pnr/Makefile's 'RTL_DIR := ../rtl' is <repo>/rtl only from pnr/; now takes an explicit base_dir. (2) _apply_abspath used Path(arg).resolve(), i.e. the invoking process's CWD, while Make resolves $(abspath ..) against the Makefile's directory -- so 'PROJECT_ROOT := $(abspath ..)' came out one level too high and every sv2v source resolved outside the repo; now takes makefile_dir.

Repo-wide: 31 lists close, including all three pnr/Makefile source variables (RTL_SOURCES, SOC_SV_FILES, SKY130_SOC_SV_FILES). Remaining gaps are only bead 135's four legacy PD configs plus pnr/asap7/template/config.json, which reports in place by design.

Note ruff: 4 pre-existing E501s in the checker were fixed in passing. CI lints only tb/models and tb/tests, so tools/ has never been gated -- worth considering separately.

Commit on fix/pnr-lint-source-closure-a7k.

title: Decide: refresh pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* + re-baseline SoC after GPU FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG lands
description:
GH #96 follow-up (claude_verilog_test-606): pnr/asap7/gpu/pin_order.cfg now pins the GPU macro's boundary side+order. Measured (RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14, 24-odb-customioplacement/gpu_top.def vs checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef): side+order match exactly (0/325 mismatches across N/E/S/W), but io_place distributes pins evenly along each edge while the checked-in LEF's spacing came from irregular free-floating placement -- so absolute coordinates differ on all 325 pins (median 42.6um, p90 ~117um, max 223.5um displacement on a 340x340um die). This is a ONE-TIME, order-preserving shift (unlike the CPU's 393/401 cross-edge reshuffle) that will happen on the *next* GPU macro regeneration under this cfg, then stay stable forever (same cfg -> identical output, by construction).

Decision needed: the checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.{lef,lib,...} and the run-23 SoC sign-off baseline were built against the OLD (unpinned, irregular) GPU boundary. They were deliberately NOT refreshed as part of claude_verilog_test-606 (that bead was a determinism proof, not a macro refresh -- see pnr/asap7/gpu/README_pin_order.md 'What pinned actually guarantees'). Before the next GPU macro regeneration is folded into any SoC build, someone must: (1) regenerate pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.{lef,lib,netlist} from the pinned config, (2) re-run the ASAP7 SoC multiclock flow against the new abstract, (3) re-verify sys_clk timing still closes (currently +74.8ps margin at run 23, i.e. not much headroom) given SoC-level placement around the macro will shift somewhat the same way u_cpu's did in GH #96 (though this shift is milder / order-preserving, not a full reshuffle).

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION 2026-08-11 — four measured findings that change the cost side of this decision.

1) THE AUG GPU RUN WAS KILLED, NOT FAILED. RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 died at step 37 openroad-repairdesignpostgrt with 'failed unexpectedly' + 460x GRT-0026. That step dir's mtime (09:35:01) is the SAME SECOND as the flow ERROR and the orchestrator's own abort note, so the error is the consequence of the SIGTERM, not an independent failure. Nothing about pin_order.cfg broke the run.

2) STEP 37 IS SUPPOSED TO TAKE ~20 HOURS ON THIS DESIGN. Commit b0dc46b documents repair_design_postgrt as the GPU runtime bottleneck at ~18.9 h (single-threaded GRT x2 + multi-thousand-iteration repair on ~485K instances, iteration count driven by the timing target, not die size). Measured on RUN_2026-05-28_06-29-48: step 36 finished 05-28 09:03, step 37 finished 05-29 05:55 = 20.9 h. The Aug run was killed ~7 h in — less than half way. The '7 h with zero log progress' that triggered the kill is NORMAL for this step.

3) A FULL GPU BLOCK RUN WITH POST-GRT REPAIR ON IS A ~2.5 DAY JOB, NOT A 4-5 h ONE. RUN_2026-05-28_06-29-48 spanned 05-28 06:29 -> 05-30 19:13; step 38 resizertimingpostgrt alone ran 05-29 05:55 -> 05-30 18:52 (~37 h). By contrast the 500 MHz signoff run RUN_2026-05-27_11-16-37 had post-GRT repair OFF and has no step 37 at all — it finished in ~3 h. That is the two-stage Run A / Run B pattern in PD memory.

4) A REGENERATION TODAY IS NOT A LIKE-FOR-LIKE REFRESH. Diffing resolved.json May-28 vs Aug-10, the GPU config changed in TWO ways, not one: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG was added (intended), AND PL/GRT_RESIZER_{SETUP,HOLD}_SLACK_MARGIN went 0.1/0.075 -> 45/25, i.e. the bead s9f units fix that landed in e8b414f. The Aug run is the first GPU run ever with REAL margins. That is also the most likely reason step 37 was working harder than in May (10,444 slew violations, 3,044 buffers over 5,249 nets). So a regenerated macro is a NEW PPA point carrying two independent changes, not a boundary-only refresh — and the SoC re-baseline would have to attribute any delta between them.

ALSO CHECKED, no problem found: pnr/asap7/soc/macro/*.{lef,lib,nl.v.gz} are GITIGNORED copies (see that dir's .gitignore); the tracked source of truth is pnr/asap7/{cpu,gpu}/macro/. The two GPU LEFs differ in bytes (50.1K vs 56.3K, OBS/geometry) but place all 325 signal pins at IDENTICAL coordinates, so the documented 'cp gpu/macro/* soc/macro/' step is safe today and the pin_order.cfg derived from the soc copy matches the tracked abstract.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-08-11: DEFER. Do not refresh pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* and do not re-baseline the SoC for now.

Rationale: nothing in the repo currently needs a regenerated GPU macro, and pin_order.cfg has already delivered its whole value -- it protects the NEXT regeneration, whenever that happens. Against that, the cost is a ~2.5-day GPU block run (step 37 alone ~20 h) plus a 4-5 h SoC re-run plus a re-validation of a sys_clk domain that has only +74.8 ps of margin, on a 15.9 GiB host that was already swapping. And because the s9f margin fix (0.1/0.075 -> 45/25) landed alongside the pin order, the output would be a new PPA point requiring delta attribution rather than a clean refresh.

The killed validation run was NOT restarted, for the same reason: the determinism question was already answered from the step-24 DEF, and the remaining routing/DRC data has no consumer until someone actually does the refresh -- at which point that run supersedes it anyway.

Precondition recorded where the next person will actually hit it: pnr/asap7/gpu/README_pin_order.md now ends with a 'Before you regenerate this macro' section carrying the measured runtimes, the 'long silences in step 37 are normal' warning (with the evidence that the Aug kill produced its own GRT-0026 errors), the two-changes-at-once caveat, and the 4-step refresh sequence.

Re-open this bead when something actually forces a GPU macro regeneration -- a GPU port-list change, a GPU RTL change, or an SoC re-baseline undertaken for another reason.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text: INHERITED FROM s9f (closed 2026-08-11): this bead is now also the tracker for the GPU macro's ~0 optimisation guard band. pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json carries the corrected 45/25 ps margins, but the macro that actually exists was built in May 2026 at 0.075/0.1 (~0 ps in ASAP7's 1 ps liberty). The CPU macro and the multiclock SoC have both been re-signed-off under real margins; the GPU has not, and the only way to fix that is the same ~2.5-day regeneration this bead defers. Anything quoting the GPU ASAP7 PPA (571 MHz / 262 mW) should note the guard-band caveat until then.

title: ASAP7 GPU macro has no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG - same free-floating boundary that cost 535 ps on the CPU
description:
Same defect class as the now-closed bead cum, on the other hard macro.

pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json has NO FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG, so every regeneration of gpu_top free-floats its 327 signal pins on a 340x340 um die. Measured consequence of exactly this condition on the CPU macro (GH #96 run 21 -> run 22): 393 of 401 pins moved between two consecutive builds -> SoC placement perturbed around the macro -> post-CTS skew doubled (-485.6 -> -922.1 ps) -> hold-violating endpoints 805 -> 4702 -> 4814 hold buffers inserted -> chained padding ate setup -> setup WNS -60.66 -> -596.00 ps. Evidence: pnr/asap7/cpu/README_pin_order.md.

The GPU macro drives the sys_clk fabric domain, which currently passes at only +74.79 ps (run 23) - far less headroom than the CPU had when this bit.

FIX (in progress): pnr/scripts/gen_pin_order.py (reusable LEF -> FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG generator; the procedure previously existed only as prose in the CPU README) + pnr/asap7/gpu/pin_order.cfg generated from the CHECKED-IN pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef, i.e. pinned to the exact abstract run 23 signed off with, UNTUNED (the CPU file was hand-tuned because it had a measured timing problem; the GPU has none, and tuning would move the abstract away from the signed-off one).

VALIDATION: one make librelane-asap7-gpu run; pass = 0 of 327 pins moved vs the checked-in LEF. Do NOT copy the new views into pnr/asap7/soc/macro/ - that would move the run-23 sign-off baseline. No SoC re-run needed.

ALSO UNTREATED, out of scope here: the Sky130 CPU/GPU macros have no FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG either.
close_reason:
DONE and verified. pnr/scripts/gen_pin_order.py (reusable LEF -> FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG generator, self-test 401/401 against the hand-tuned CPU reference) + pnr/asap7/gpu/pin_order.cfg (325 signal pins, N=9 E=143 S=170 W=3, untuned) + FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG wired into pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json + README_pin_order.md. Commits 2c634b5 and d36ebed on feat/gh96-closeout-gpu-pin-order; PR #136.

VERIFIED from RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14/24-odb-customioplacement/gpu_top.def, independently by two parsers: side + along-edge order match pin_order.cfg EXACTLY on all four sides, 0 mismatches. FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG is applied.

The original '0 of 325 pins moved vs the checked-in LEF' criterion was wrong by construction and is corrected in the docs (see the comments above): the config constrains side+order, io_place then spaces pins evenly, so it cannot reproduce the reference LEF's free-floating-derived irregular spacing. Correct criterion = same cfg -> identical output, which holds by construction.

That validation run was terminated at ~11.8 h wall time, stalled in OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT with no log growth for 7 h (genuinely computing per /proc CPU-time deltas, not hung; no OOM/oomd kill - it was thrashing under 5+ GiB of swap on a 15 GiB host). Its remaining value was routing/DRC data, never a deliverable of this bead. /nobackup/asap7_gpu_runs/RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 (8.3 G) is kept for traceability but is an ABORTED artifact, not a signed-off result.

Follow-up decision tracked in claude_verilog_test-buw: the next GPU macro regeneration shifts the boundary once (~43 um median, order-preserving) vs the checked-in abstract, so pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* and the run-23 SoC baseline need a deliberate refresh before that lands in an SoC build.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Committed 2c634b5 on feat/gh96-closeout-gpu-pin-order: pnr/scripts/gen_pin_order.py (LEF->FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG generator) + pnr/asap7/gpu/pin_order.cfg (generated, untuned, from checked-in gpu_top.lef) + FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG wired into pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json + README_pin_order.md.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text: Draft PR #136 opened on feat/gh96-closeout-gpu-pin-order (commits 15d8620 doc + 2c634b5 PD). Stays draft until the gpu_top validation run reports 0 of 325 pins moved vs the checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef. Note the count: 325 SIGNAL pins, not 327 -- the LEF has 327 PIN records including VDD/VSS, which io_place.py filters itself.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
MEASURED EARLY from the in-flight run's step-24 DEF (RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14/24-odb-customioplacement/gpu_top.def) -- pin positions are settled there, so the answer did not need the full flow.

RESULT: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG IS honoured. Side + along-edge order match pin_order.cfg EXACTLY on all four sides: #N 9/9, #E 143/143, #S 170/170, #W 3/3, sequences identical. DIEAREA 0 0 340 340, 325 signal pins.

BUT THE STATED PASS CRITERION WAS WRONG AND IS UNACHIEVABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. '0 of 325 pins moved vs the checked-in gpu_top.lef' cannot hold: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG constrains SIDE and ORDER only, and io_place then distributes pins EVENLY along each edge (all E pins land on x=338.0, N/S on y=338.0/2.0 -- regular tracks). The reference LEF's spacing came from free-floating placement and is irregular, so an order-only config can never reproduce it. Measured along-edge displacement vs the checked-in LEF: median 42.61 um, p90 117.29 um, max 223.51 um, 0 of 325 unmoved.

CORRECT CRITERION, and the one the CPU was actually validated against: two runs WITH the cfg produce identical pins (CPU README: byte-identical LEF, 0/401). For the GPU that holds by construction -- coordinates are a deterministic function of (cfg order, die, IO params) -- and could be proven with a second run if judged worth the hours.

CONSEQUENCE TO DECIDE (not in scope of this bead): the next GPU macro regeneration WILL shift the boundary once vs the currently checked-in abstract (median ~43 um, order preserved), then be stable forever. That is a one-time ORDER-PRESERVING redistribution, categorically milder than the CPU's 393/401 cross-edge reshuffle, but it is not zero. Carrying the stability into the SoC therefore means refreshing pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* and re-baselining the SoC against run 23.

CAVEAT ON THE NUMBERS: 2 of 325 pins (rst_n, m_axi_wdata[17]) sit exactly at corners where side attribution is ambiguous between the LEF-first-RECT rule gen_pin_order.py uses and a nearest-edge rule. Do not report those as side changes without naming the rule.

Host at time of measurement: OpenROAD alive at 13.7 GiB RSS, swap 3.9/32 GiB, no kernel OOM and no systemd-oomd kill in the journal.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the pass criterion stated in the original task/bead ('0 of 327 pins moved vs the checked-in LEF'): that criterion is unachievable by construction and is not the right test. FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG only constrains side + along-edge order; io_place then distributes pins EVENLY along each edge. The checked-in pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.lef came from irregular free-floating placement, so an order-only config can never reproduce its exact coordinates.

Measured + independently verified (parsed 24-odb-customioplacement/gpu_top.def from RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 myself, cross-checked against the coordinator's numbers):
- Side + order: EXACT match on all 4 sides -- N 9/9, E 143/143, S 170/170, W 3/3, 0 mismatches, sequences identical to pin_order.cfg. FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG is being applied correctly.
- Absolute along-edge coordinate vs checked-in LEF: 0/325 pins land at the same position. Median displacement 42.6um, p90 ~117um (116.4 by my own percentile method, coordinator reported 117.3 -- interpolation-method difference only), max 223.5um, on a 340x340um die. E-side pins collapse onto a regular x=338.0um track, N/S onto y=338.0/2.0um -- the even-distribution signature.
- Corner-adjacency caveat (rst_n, m_axi_wdata[17]): checked directly under the generator's own rule (y1==0->S, y2==SIZE_Y->N, x1==0->W, else E) AND a nearest-edge rule. Both agree E for both pins (distance-to-E=0 exactly, vs >=10.5um to S/N) -- no actual side-classification disagreement between the two rules for these two pins, despite them sitting geometrically near a die corner.

CORRECT determinism criterion (same one the CPU README documents): two regenerations with the SAME pin_order.cfg produce IDENTICAL pin placement, because side+order+die+IO-pitch fully determine io_place's even-distribution output. This holds for the GPU by the same construction argument as the CPU; not re-proven here with a second GPU run (would only reconfirm byte-identical output).

Consequence filed separately as claude_verilog_test-buw: the NEXT gpu_top regeneration under this pin_order.cfg will shift the boundary once (measured above) vs the currently checked-in macro -- order-preserving, one-time, milder than the CPU's 393/401 reshuffle, but not zero -- so pnr/asap7/soc/macro/gpu_top.* and the run-23 SoC baseline need a deliberate refresh + re-validation before that next regeneration is folded into an SoC build. Not done here (out of scope, and would move the run-23 sign-off baseline this task was explicitly told not to touch).

Docs corrected to reflect this: pnr/asap7/gpu/README_pin_order.md (new 'What pinned actually guarantees' section) and the FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG rationale comment in pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json (previously said 'pins the GPU macro to the same boundary as the checked-in LEF', which is inaccurate -- corrected to 'pins side and order', with the coordinate-shift measurement inline).

Validation run RUN_2026-08-10_19-04-14 is still alive as of this comment (~8h wall time, deep in OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT, no OOM/systemd-oomd kill), left running for its routing/DRC data since the determinism question above is already answered and doesn't need it to finish. Will report final routing/DRC status separately if/when it completes.

title: [bug] pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json VERILOG_FILES was missing rtl/soc/soc_addr_map_pkg.sv - CPU block P&R unbuildable since the MMIO-bypass RTL change
description:
FOUND + FIXED 2026-08-07 while launching the GH #96 follow-up CPU block re-run (beads cyb/g0o/s9f).

SYMPTOM: 'make librelane-asap7' died at stage 3 (Lint Errors Checker), 2 errors:
  %Error-PKGNODECL: rtl/mem/rv32i_dcache.sv:38:8: Package/class 'soc_addr_map_pkg' not found, and needs to be predeclared (IEEE 1800-2017 26.3)
  %Error: rtl/mem/rv32i_dcache.sv:38:8: Importing from missing package 'soc_addr_map_pkg'

PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the cyb RTL change: 'import soc_addr_map_pkg::MMIO_BASE;' is present at rv32i_dcache.sv:38 in HEAD, and the cyb diff only touches rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv. The dependency arrived with the D-cache MMIO-bypass work (bead go9 era) and pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json's VERILOG_FILES was never updated.

IMPLICATION WORTH NOTING: the ASAP7 CPU block P&R has been UNBUILDABLE since that RTL change. The most recent CPU run on disk is RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12, which predates it -- so the CPU macro LEF/Liberty/netlist that the Phase 5 SoC has been integrating are all from before the MMIO bypass existed in the D-cache. Nobody noticed because the CPU block flow is only invoked manually and CI does not run PD.

FIX: inserted 'dir::../../../rtl/soc/soc_addr_map_pkg.sv' into VERILOG_FILES immediately after axi_pkg.sv (packages must precede the modules importing them). Audited the whole CPU file set programmatically afterwards: imported packages are axi_pkg, rv32i_cache_pkg, rv32i_pipeline_pkg, soc_addr_map_pkg -- all four now provided. Run relaunched and is past lint/synthesis.

SAME CLASS AS bead 50t (tb/cocotb/cpu Makefile missing axi_pkg.sv). Both are 'a source list silently bit-rotted when RTL gained a package dependency, and no gate caught it'. Worth a periodic audit that every config's VERILOG_FILES/VERILOG_SOURCES closes over the imports of the files it lists -- the ~20-line script used here could be turned into a check.
close_reason:
VERIFIED FIXED and now proven by downstream evidence. The fix is committed in e8b414f (2026-08-07): pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json VERILOG_FILES lists rtl/soc/axi_pkg.sv then rtl/soc/soc_addr_map_pkg.sv ahead of the modules importing them.

Re-audited 2026-08-11 with a package-import closure check over the whole 29-file list rather than spot-checking the one error: imported = {axi_pkg, rv32i_cache_pkg, rv32i_pipeline_pkg, soc_addr_map_pkg}, provided = the same four, gap = NONE. Every listed file also exists on disk.

Stronger evidence than the audit: the CPU block flow has since been run to completion repeatedly against this config -- the macro was rebuilt in d7f45b6 (runs 20-21) and again in 999e44a (run 23), producing the LEF/Liberty/netlist that the multiclock SoC signed off with at cpu_clk +9.79 ps. The 'unbuildable since the MMIO-bypass change' condition is gone, and the observation that the integrated CPU macro predated the MMIO bypass no longer holds either -- the current abstract is post-fix.

The generalisation this bead asked for (a periodic check that every config's VERILOG_FILES/VERILOG_SOURCES closes over the imports of the files it lists) is NOT done and is the open half. It is being carried by bead 50t, where the same audit found the sibling list is still broken -- see that bead for the measured gap.

title: CPU macro APB read path: block-level SDC budget or register apb_prdata_o (root fix for the SoC cpu_clk exception)
description:
GH #96 run 16 found the SoC cpu_clk worst path is a single 800.71 ps COMBINATIONAL arc inside the rv32i_cpu_top macro: fabric FF -> u_cpu APB addr in -> arc -> u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] -> fabric FF. 33 of 194 cpu_clk violators are this class. #96 excepts it with set_false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] (SDC section 10a), which is CONTRACT-CORRECT: the CPU's own standalone 780 ps signoff already does set_false_path -to [get_ports apb_prdata_o[*]] (pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc:121), so the macro was never characterized to meet 780 ps there. This bead is the ROOT fix that would remove the need for the exception.

WHY THE ARC IS SLOW: Liberty confirms apb_prdata_o[1] is direction:output timing_type:combinational with related_pin apb_paddr_i[9..11]/apb_psel_i/apb_pwrite_i -- a true feedthrough. Liberty emits topological arcs regardless of SDC exceptions, so the block false_path did not remove the arc, it only meant block P&R never optimized it. RTL cause: apb_prdata_o is a pure always_comb read mux (rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv:261-285), 10+ decoded addresses, 32 bits wide, sourced from CSR/PC/commit state spread across the block.

BUDGET (from run 16's failing path): arrival 1209.39 ps vs required 1004.05 ps => the arc must lose >=205.34 ps, i.e. be <=595 ps. SoC-side overhead measured on that path was ~79 ps before the macro (FF clk-to-Q 68.20 + INV 11.17) and ~55.7 ps after, i.e. ~10% of the period per side, NOT 40%.

TWO VARIANTS:
(A) Block SDC: replace the apb_prdata_o false_path with real set_input_delay/set_output_delay so block P&R is forced to close it, then regenerate macro views. Budget note: for a FEEDTHROUGH path the block budget is period - input_delay - output_delay, so both ends subtract. At 780 ps, 40%/40% leaves only 156 ps internal -- unreachable for this mux. ~80/105 ps leaves ~595 ps and matches the real SoC environment.
(B) RTL: register apb_prdata_o. One pipeline stage on an infrequent debug-read port collapses the arc to a clk-to-Q and REMOVES the combinational in->out arc from the .lib entirely, making variant A trivially satisfiable. APB tolerates the extra wait state (u_apb_dbg_cdc already waits on m_pready_i). Requires cocotb re-verification per the rerun-verification-after-rtl rule.

COST/SYNERGY: either variant needs a CPU block P&R re-run + macro-view regeneration + a SoC re-run. Regenerating the views is ALSO the fix for bead g0o (CPU macro abstract missing AXI4 burst ports awlen/wlast/arlen), so the two should be done together. Risk: adding a newly-timed path that the standalone signoff deliberately excluded may reduce the CPU's standalone 1282 MHz result.

NOT A #96 BLOCKER: after the -through exception the SoC limiter is the 161 non-macro violators at -44.93 ps, which are SoC-level logic and are untouched by any block-level change.
close_reason: FIXED via variant B (register the outputs), and it took all THREE APB outputs, not just prdata. apb_prdata_o, apb_pslverr_o and apb_pready_o in rtl/cpu/rv32i_cpu_top.sv are now pure registered outputs; the regenerated Liberty has no combinational arc on any output pin of the macro, so the SoC-side SDC 10a false_path -through u_cpu/apb_prdata_o[*] was RETIRED. Two intermediate attempts are recorded in the RTL so they are not retried: registering prdata alone merely RELOCATED the ~800 ps read mux into an 876.85 ps input SETUP requirement (run 20, cpu_clk -350.1 ps, all 15 violators ending at macro APB input pins), and a SETUP-phase decode for pslverr still left a 617.9 ps arc re-sourced from apb_psel_i. Every APB output pays ~600 ps crossing this block's internal distribution regardless of logic depth, so only a pure flop breaks it. External APB behaviour preserved: writes still complete in one ACCESS cycle (so psel&&penable&&pwrite write-commit pulses like dbg_pc_wr_en still fire exactly once), reads take one wait state. Merged in PR #135 (f7868b1); run 23 closed cpu_clk at +9.79 ps / 1282 MHz.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
MEASURED ANSWER to 'would input/output delay at max=40%/min=10% of clock still pass?' -- run on the signed-off CPU netlist (RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12) at 780 ps, so 40%=312 ps, 10%=78 ps. Harness validated first: reproducing the checked-in SDC gives setup WNS +24.011 ps / hold +28.142 ps / 0 violators, matching the documented M7 signoff exactly.

  base  (150/10 in, 150/-15 out)      : setupWNS +24.011  0 viol | holdWNS +28.142   0 viol
  io40  (312 max, 78 min, exceptions intact): setupWNS +24.011  0 viol | holdWNS -31.301  16 viol
  io40x (io40 + apb_prdata_o timed)   : setupWNS -235.804 2 viol | holdWNS -31.301  16 viol

SETUP: 40% max is FREE here -- WNS identical to 6 decimals (+24.011015). The CPU critical path is internal reg->reg (the 836-fanout counter cone), so 162 ps of extra I/O pessimism never reaches it.

HOLD: the 16 violations are NOT an indictment of the 10% min rule. All 16 start at axi_rlast_i (startpoint attribution), the one burst-era input the block SDC never constrained -- see bead g0o. Applying any input delay there creates a check that has never existed. With rlast added to the existing hold false-path list (asap7.sdc:230), 10% min looks affordable.

APB ROOT FIX: 40/40 does NOT rescue it. Only violators are apb_prdata_o[0] and [1] at -235.80 ps. At block level this is reg->port, so budget = 780 - output_delay = 468 ps against ~704 ps actual; closing it as-is needs output_delay <= ~76 ps, i.e. under 10%, not 40%. For the port->port feedthrough (paddr->prdata) the budget is 780-312-312 = 156 ps against ~800 ps -- hopeless. CONCLUSION: constraint budgeting alone cannot fix this path; variant B (register apb_prdata_o) is the real fix, after which any sane I/O budget works.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
VERIFIED 2026-08-07. rv32i_cpu_top.sv: apb_prdata_o is now a registered output and the slave inserts exactly one APB3 wait state on READS (apb_pready_o = apb_pwrite_i ? 1'b1 : apb_read_wait_q). Writes are bit-for-bit unchanged (pready=1 immediately), and apb_pslverr_o stays combinational because it is write-side only.

Correctness argument checked by hand, not just by test: apb_prdata_o captures whenever apb_psel_i is high, and APB requires paddr/psel/pwrite stable from SETUP through ACCESS, so the registered value is already correct when pready asserts in the 2nd ACCESS cycle.

Verification: Verilator lint 0 errors (make -C sim lint, no warnings attributable to the new logic). soc_all 178 passed / 0 failed (RC=0) -- covers the APB debug path via soc_periph, soc_boot and test_apb_cdc_bridge.

Zero-wait-state audit across tb/ and sw/ (the item that could have silently broken things):
  tb/cocotb/cpu/phase2_test_utils.py  - assumed same-cycle prdata -> FIXED, now polls apb_pready_o
  tb/cocotb/cpu/test_smoke.py         - same -> FIXED
  tb/cpu_uvm/agents/apb_agent/apb_driver.py - ALREADY CORRECT, polls pready on both read and write
  tb/cocotb/soc/tb_soc_top.sv         - pure port wiring, unaffected
  sw/ and tb/models/                  - no APB read consumers
Only two places encoded the old protocol; both are now protocol-conformant masters rather than weakened checks.

CAVEAT ON COVERAGE: the CPU-standalone cocotb suites (smoke/debug/phase2_all) could NOT be run -- they fail Verilator elaboration with 'Import package not found: axi_pkg', a PRE-EXISTING breakage unrelated to this change (bead 50t). So the APB debug tests in those files are edited but unexecuted; their coverage of this change rests on soc_all instead.

title: make -C tb/cocotb/soc <target> reuses a stale sim_build from a different TOPLEVEL
description: Running 'make -C tb/cocotb/soc timer' straight after another suite fails with 'VPI: Couldn't find root handle timer / Toplevel instances: timer != tb_async_axi_fifo' and 'ERROR: results.xml was not written by the simulation!'. Some targets (e.g. async_axi_fifo) run 'make clean' first and so rebuild Vtop; others do not, and silently reuse the previous suite's sim_build/Vtop, which was elaborated with a different TOPLEVEL. Repro: make -C tb/cocotb/soc async_axi_fifo && make -C tb/cocotb/soc timer. Fix: give each target its own SIM_BUILD dir (the Makefile already does this for sim_build_lock/sim_build_regs) or make the clean dependency uniform. Not a soc_all problem today because soc_all sequences targets that each clean, but it makes any single-target rerun unreliable.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #142. One line: BUILD_ARGS += SIM_BUILD=sim_build_$@ in tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile. BUILD_ARGS is only ever built with '+=', never ':=', so it is recursively expanded and $@ resolves at recipe time to the target being built.

That made the workarounds dead code, so they are gone: 19 per-target '$(MAKE) clean' calls and all 24 'rm -rf sim_build' prefixes in soc_all. Added distclean, because cocotb's own clean only removes $(SIM_BUILD) and can no longer sweep the per-target dirs.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S FIX NOTE: it cited sim_build_lock / sim_build_regs as existing precedent ('the Makefile already does this'). Those do NOT exist -- the file had ZERO SIM_BUILD assignments. The mechanism had to be built from scratch, not reused.

VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS on the documented repro:
  main       : make async_axi_fifo && make timer -> TIMER_EXIT=2, 4 root-handle errors
  with fix   : exit 0, timer 6/6, 0 root-handle errors
Removing the 24 soc_all guards was the real risk, so the full regression was re-run without them: soc_all 179/179 across 25 suites, exit 0, 0 root-handle errors, 24 distinct sim_build_* dirs created.

HOST NOTE worth carrying (third occurrence today): a long run launched as a child of an agent/tool turn gets reaped when that turn ends -- it dies mid-work with no error written, which reads like a flow failure but is not. 'setsid nohup' was sufficient for a librelane run earlier but NOT for 'nix develop --command make soc_all', which died mid-compile of the first suite. tmux is the only launcher that has survived reliably on this host. Launch long sims/PD runs under tmux.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile at a572d9a — NOT stale, the bug is still exactly as described. Do not close.

Mechanism unchanged: there is still ONE shared sim_build/ and Verilator always names the binary Vtop regardless of TOPLEVEL (the Makefile says so itself at line 581). Targets remain inconsistent -- 'async_axi_fifo' (line ~529) and 'soc_boot'/'soc_periph' (lines ~584, ~595) run $(MAKE) clean first, while 'timer' (line ~412), 'dma', 'irq', 'uart', 'spi' etc. do not. So the documented repro still holds: make async_axi_fifo && make timer reuses the tb_async_axi_fifo Vtop and dies with a VPI root-handle mismatch.

Correction to this bead's own fix note: the per-target SIM_BUILD dirs it points at as precedent (sim_build_lock / sim_build_regs) DO NOT EXIST in the Makefile today -- grep finds zero SIM_BUILD assignments, only one comment at line 780. So the 'the Makefile already does this' half of the suggested fix is wrong; per-target SIM_BUILD would have to be built from scratch.

Why it stays invisible: soc_all does not rely on the per-target clean at all -- it prefixes EVERY suite with 'rm -rf sim_build' (lines 749-764, with an explicit comment at 736 saying it uses rm -rf rather than $(MAKE) clean). That masks the inconsistency for the regression while leaving every single-target rerun unreliable.

title: check-cdc-timing target cannot fail a build: OpenSTA exits 0 after internal error
description:
Found while fixing CodeRabbit findings on PR #133 (bead k07 follow-up).

pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl reports unmatched CDC exceptions correctly
(CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS) and raises a Tcl 'error' at the end of read_sdc. BUT the
OpenSTA 'sta' process still returns EXIT CODE 0. Confirmed both before and after
the CodeRabbit fixes, so this is pre-existing OpenSTA/Tcl batch-mode behaviour,
not a regression.

Consequence: 'make check-cdc-timing-asap7-soc' is ADVISORY, not a gate. It prints
failures but cannot fail CI or a script. Anyone wiring it into an automated flow
and trusting the exit status would get a silent pass.

This matters for GH #96 (multi-clock ASAP7 PD re-closure), which is expected to
rely on this target to prove the CDC budgets are met post-route. If the exit code
is meaningless, #96 could 'pass' CDC timing closure without anything actually
being checked.

Fix options:
  (a) have check_cdc_timing.tcl accumulate a failure flag and call 'exit 1'
      explicitly at the end rather than relying on Tcl 'error' propagation;
  (b) wrap the sta invocation in pnr/Makefile so it greps the log for
      CDC-EXCEPTION-MISS and fails the make target on any hit;
  (c) both -- (a) for direct 'sta script.tcl' use, (b) as a belt-and-braces
      guard at the Makefile level.

Recommend (c). Note the same class of issue is why GH #95's cdc_gate.py exit
status is the verdict rather than cdc_snitch's own -- a check whose exit code
does not reflect its findings is not a gate.

PD change -> chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator. Do before/with GH #96.
close_reason: Closed

title: cdc_reset_sync has no scan bypass - will block DFT scan insertion
description:
Found during GH #95 ARM/open-source CDC survey.

rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_reset_sync.sv drives its flop chain's asynchronous clear directly from
rst_n_i with no scan-mode override. During scan shift the reset must be controllable by
the tester, otherwise the synchroniser chain cannot be scanned and the whole CPU/fabric
reset tree becomes untestable.

OpenTitan's equivalent primitive (prim_rst_sync) muxes in scan_rst_ni under scanmode_i
for exactly this reason. Standard practice: every async-reset synchroniser in a
scan-inserted design needs a scan_rst_ni / scanmode_i pair (or a test_mode reset mux).

Affects both cdc_reset_sync instances in async_axi_fifo (u_s_rst_sync, u_m_rst_sync),
both in apb_cdc_bridge (u_s_rst_sync, u_m_rst_sync), and u_cpu_pmu_rst_sync in soc_top.

Not currently blocking: this project has no DFT/scan flow yet (chip-design-dft
orchestrator exists but has not been run on this design). Filing now because the fix is
cheap while the primitive has only ~5 instantiation sites, and expensive later.

RTL change -> chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator, coordinate with chip-design-dft.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #143 (stacked on #142). scanmode_i / scan_rst_ni added to cdc_reset_sync; rst_n_async = scanmode_i ? scan_rst_ni : rst_n_i replaces rst_n_i as the negedge async clear, OpenTitan prim_rst_sync style. Plumbed through the two reusable wrappers (async_axi_fifo, apb_cdc_bridge) so the expensive part -- threading it through repeatedly-instantiated IP -- is done. All 5 sites updated (async_axi_fifo x2, apb_cdc_bridge x2, soc_top x1).

SCOPE DECISION: NO new soc_top boundary ports. New top-level ports would perturb the PD baseline (pin_order.cfg pins 401 macro pins; run 23 closed at sys_clk +74.8 / cpu_clk +9.8 ps; an unpinned macro regeneration took cpu_clk to -596 ps in run 22). soc_top ties the pair off inert via SCAN_MODE_TIE_OFF / SCAN_RST_TIE_OFF localparams at ONE commented change point, so enabling scan later is a one-line edit.

Verified: sim lint clean, 0 errors and 0 SYNCASYNCNET (the specific regression risk, since the file's one-always_ff-per-stage shape exists to dodge that false positive); new cdc_reset_sync_scan suite 4/4 including test_rst_n_i_ignored_when_scanmode_asserted, which proves the mux is real rather than decorative; soc_all 183/183 across 26 suites, exit 0 (179 baseline + 4 new). magic_cdc marker and the STAGES<2 elaboration guard preserved.

FOR THE DFT ENGINEER (bead asked to coordinate with chip-design-dft; that flow has still never been run on this design): every consumer already threads the pair, so the only edit is soc_top's two localparams -- drive them from real top-level ports or a scan controller. Adding those ports DOES change the macro boundary, so sequence it with a pin_order.cfg regeneration and an SoC re-baseline rather than dropping it in casually.

title: Tighten gray-pointer set_max_delay to 0.5x period; split post-route CDC SDC (OpenTitan precedent)
description:
Two SDC refinements with strong primary-source precedent, for GH #96 PD re-closure.
Item 2 may invalidate GH #94's CDC budgets entirely -- raised to P2 for that reason.

== 2. SET_MAX_DELAY MAY BE MASKED BY SET_CLOCK_GROUPS -ASYNCHRONOUS (potentially serious) ==

phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc has BOTH set_clock_groups -asynchronous (line 105) and
set_max_delay -datapath_only (sections 11-13) in ONE file. Its own comment at lines
100-103 asserts:

  'those get explicit set_max_delay -datapath_only overrides in sections 11-13 below,
   which OpenSTA honours even though the clock groups are otherwise asynchronous.'

That claim is UNVERIFIED -- per CLAUDE.md the SDC 'is not yet run through OpenSTA'.
And standard SDC exception precedence is:
    set_false_path  >  set_max_delay / set_min_delay  >  set_multicycle_path
set_clock_groups -asynchronous creates false paths between the groups. False path
wins. So the max_delay constraints are likely being silently DROPPED, which would
make all of GH #94's CDC budgets decorative.

OpenTitan hit exactly this and solved it by SPLITTING the SDC. Their check-only file
(hw/top_earlgrey/syn/chip_earlgrey_asic_check_only.sdc) opens verbatim:

  'These SDC's are not used for synthesis, since they collide with the current
   set_clock_groups -async constraints. Instead, they are used to time the design
   after P&R in order to make sure that the CDC crossings are all within spec.'

ACTION: run the SDC through OpenSTA and report whether the max_delay paths are timed
or dropped. If dropped, split into phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc (implementation, keeps
set_clock_groups) + phase5_soc_multiclock_check.sdc (post-route CDC verification,
keeps set_max_delay), per OpenTitan. Also fix the incorrect comment either way.

== 1. TWO-TIER CDC BUDGET ==

Current SDC bounds every CDC path to one destination-clock period. Precedent is
stricter and two-tier:
  OpenTitan check_only.sdc:  0.9 x destination period for all crossings,
                             GRAY_MAX_DELAY = 0.5 x period for FIFO gray pointers
  PULP cdc_fifo_gray.sv:     set_max_delay min(T_src, T_dst) -- the MINIMUM of the
                             two periods, not the destination's
Our mem_q read at ~1.0x is looser than OpenTitan's data path; our gray pointers at
~1.0x are 2x looser than theirs. Recommend 0.5x on the 10 gray-pointer crossings
(2 per FIFO x 5 FIFOs in u_cpu_axi_cdc) and 0.9x on mem_q.

PD/SDC change -> chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator. Fold into GH #96.
close_reason: SDC split + budget tightening committed (8336853); see comment for tool-verified evidence

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
RESOLVED (2026-08-02) — tool-verified with OpenSTA 2.6.0 (standalone `sta`
and OpenROAD's embedded STA engine), reproduced against a real sky130hd
netlist mirroring the exact topology:

Item 2 (masking) confirmed WORSE than hypothesized:
  (a) -datapath_only is not an implemented OpenSTA flag at all — read_sdc
      aborts with STA-0563 on the first occurrence, so sections 11-15
      never executed (hard parse failure, not silent masking).
  (b) even with that flag removed, set_max_delay -through on a path
