title: Port OpenTitan prim_cdc_rand_delay metastability injection into cdc_2ff_sync
description:
Closes the 'metastability injection is not modelable in Verilator' residual gap
recorded in design_state.json:164 and CLAUDE.md.

OpenTitan does model it. hw/ip/prim_generic/rtl/prim_flop_2sync.sv wraps its first
synchroniser stage in:

    `ifdef SIMULATION
      prim_cdc_rand_delay #(.DataWidth(Width), .Enable(EnablePrimCdcRand))
      u_prim_cdc_rand_delay (.clk_i, .rst_ni, .src_data_i(d_i),
                             .prev_data_i(intq), .dst_data_o(d_o));
    `else
      always_comb d_o = d_i;
    `endif

prim_cdc_rand_delay.sv is 67 lines of plain RTL (randomised delay model, not #delay),
so it IS portable to a Verilator flow -- which contradicts our current claim that
metastability is unmodelable here. Defeatable per-instance via the Enable parameter.

Would give real coverage of the class of bug GH #93 found only by accident at a
divergent clock ratio. Apply to rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv (every synchroniser in
the design is an instance of it, so one edit covers all 13+ crossings).

Verilator lint waiver precedent also in OpenTitan: hw/ip/prim/lint/prim_cdc_rand_delay.vlt
lint_off UNUSED for the whole file.

RTL change -> chip-design-rtl:rtl-design-orchestrator. Needs async_axi_fifo +
apb_cdc_bridge + soc_all re-run after.
notes:
2026-09-07 THIRD MUTANT SPECIES TRIED. NEGATIVE RESULT, WITH A STRUCTURAL REASON. Tree
verified mutant-free afterwards (git diff clean on rtl/soc/cdc/ and tb/cocotb/soc/).

NEW AND DECISIVE -- reading the injector RTL closely: the hold decision ($urandom_range draw)
is made ONCE PER DESTINATION-CLOCK EDGE FOR THE WHOLE WIDTH-BIT WORD, not per bit. stage0_d is
therefore always either the full current d_i or the full previous sync_q[0], never a mixed or
torn value. That rules out the ENTIRE bit-tear / broken-gray-coding fault family (option (a) in
the acceptance criteria) BY CONSTRUCTION -- no mutant of that species can ever be reached by
this injector. Option (a) was correctly not built, for this reason, rather than tried and
failed.

OPTION (b), RE-CONVERGENT CROSSING, WAS BUILT AND DID REACH THE DESIGN. Duplicated a
cdc_2ff_sync in cdc_gray_fifo.sv (same source, different seed) and made empty_q/full_q require
the two copies to agree, forcing the flag wrong on disagreement. Tried on BOTH the empty (read)
and full (write) sides. The fault is real and lands: ~750-789 word-level divergences between
the two synced copies per run, 11 landing on a semantically-relevant "would-have-been-full"
cycle, and 6-7 CONFIRMED actual overflow writes (wr_valid_i=1 while full_q was wrongly clear)
on u_aw_fifo / u_ar_fifo / u_r_fifo / u_b_fifo.

AND THE SUITE STILL PASSED. OFF 26/26, ON 26/26, with those 7 real overflow-write events inside
the ON run's window. Two further attempts to build a check that would catch them:
 * targeted AR exact-depth check + 16-point clock-phase sweep -> 0/16 failed. Diagnosed: that
   scenario starts from cold reset with no read-side consumption, so the read-domain gray
   pointer never changes and the injector never draws on that crossing at all.
 * data-integrity check added to test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full (the scenario where the
   overflow writes were confirmed) -> first attempt was a FALSE POSITIVE: the same "missing
   writes" appeared on fully clean, unmutated RTL. See the separate bead filed for that
   pre-existing TB race. After fixing it with a settle delay and re-verifying clean-RTL PASS:
   OFF 26/26, ON 26/26. Still no discrimination.

STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION: the injector's fault model is a self-clearing, whole-word EXTRA LATENCY
on a synchroniser's registered output -- never a torn or fabricated value. A Cummings-style
dual-clock FIFO's registered, one-cycle-delayed full/empty comparison has exactly the margin it
is supposed to have to absorb arbitrary but eventually-consistent settling delay without data
loss. That absorption IS acceptance criterion 1's expectation for a CORRECT synchroniser. So
criteria 1 and 2 are in tension on this design: the same property that makes the design correct
makes the injector non-discriminating against it.

STATE OF THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) met, trivially and in the wrong direction -- correctness
holds under forced-ON. (2) NOT met, now across three independent mutant species (same-domain
reset gating; synchroniser bypass; re-convergent crossing x2 sides), with a construction-level
argument for why species (a) is unreachable. (3) not attempted -- correctly stopped before
wiring a dormant feature ON with nothing demonstrated.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE DECISION: this now looks like a bounded tool result rather than an
unfinished task. Three species tried; the fourth is provably unreachable; the design absorbs
the one that does land, by construction. The remaining honest options are (i) close with the
finding -- record that cycle-accurate Verilator injection of whole-word settling delay cannot
discriminate faults on THIS design, and that CDC lint (magic_cdc / check_cdc_timing.tcl) is the
tool that catches the unsynchronised-crossing species; or (ii) change the injector itself to
draw per-bit rather than per-word, which would make species (a) reachable -- but that is a new
fault model, not a continuation of this one, and should be scoped as such.

REGRESSION, mutant-free tree: test_async_axi_fifo 26/26, test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23 (suite has
GROWN from the 15/15 recorded baseline -- not a regression), soc_multiclock 4/4. soc_all was
NOT re-run this session (host load); the tree is byte-identical to baseline on both touched
files, so this is a gap in evidence rather than a known risk.
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-09 with the finding, per user decision. NOT closed as "done" -- closed because
the investigation reached a bounded, defensible negative result.

WHAT IS IN THE TREE AND STAYS: rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv carries a convergent,
simulation-only randomised settling-delay injector (RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN, default OFF, guarded by
`ifdef SIMULATION` which only tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile defines -- never lint_soc, tools/cdc, or
the pnr sv2v path). Commit a754ee9. It is correct and harmless; it simply has no demonstrated
discriminating power on this design.

THE DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FACT: the hold decision ($urandom_range draw) is made ONCE PER
DESTINATION-CLOCK EDGE FOR THE ENTIRE WIDTH-BIT WORD, not per bit. stage0_d is therefore always
either the full current d_i or the full previous sync_q[0] -- never a mixed or torn value. That
makes the ENTIRE bit-tear / broken-gray-coding fault family UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. It was
correctly never built, rather than built and failed.

THREE MUTANT SPECIES TRIED, all honest negatives:
 1. Reverting 7a9f9d4's wr_ready_o reset gating -- a SAME-DOMAIN reset bug, orthogonal to a
    settling-delay fault model. Caught with the injector OFF too, so it proves nothing.
 2. Bypassing u_rd_ptr_to_wr in cdc_gray_fifo (reading rd_gray_q instead of rd_gray_sync_w) --
    26/26 PASS both OFF and forced ON. Structurally expected: the bypass never reads the
    synchroniser output, so the injector's fault model has no path into the comparison.
 3. Re-convergent crossing (duplicated cdc_2ff_sync, differently seeded, downstream logic
    requiring the two copies to agree), tried on BOTH the empty and full sides. THE FAULT
    GENUINELY LANDED: ~750-789 word-level divergences per run, 11 on a semantically relevant
    "would-have-been-full" cycle, and 6-7 CONFIRMED actual overflow writes on
    u_aw_fifo/u_ar_fifo/u_r_fifo/u_b_fifo. The suite still passed 26/26.

WHY THAT LAST RESULT IS THE ANSWER, not a failure to try hard enough: the injector's fault
model is a self-clearing, whole-word EXTRA LATENCY on a synchroniser's registered output --
never a torn or fabricated value. A Cummings-style dual-clock FIFO's registered, one-cycle-
delayed full/empty comparison has exactly the margin it is designed to have to absorb arbitrary
but eventually-consistent settling delay without data loss. THAT ABSORPTION IS ACCEPTANCE
CRITERION 1's DEFINITION OF A CORRECT SYNCHRONISER. Criteria 1 and 2 are therefore in tension
on this design: the property that makes it correct is the same property that makes the injector
non-discriminating against it.

CONCLUSION RECORDED: cycle-accurate Verilator injection of whole-word settling delay cannot
discriminate faults on this design. The unsynchronised-crossing species is caught by CDC LINT
(magic_cdc / pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl), not by simulation -- that is the right tool for
it, and it is already in the flow.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, filed separately: the attempt surfaced a pre-existing settle-timing race in
test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full that produced false "missing write" failures on CLEAN RTL.
That became bead 5ej, and is now FIXED (commit 4890df3) with a handshake-count gate.

IF SOMEONE WANTS THIS CAPABILITY LATER: change the injector to draw PER BIT rather than per
word. That makes the bit-tear family reachable and would be a genuinely different fault model
-- scope it as NEW work, not as finishing this bead. Do not reopen this one for it.

title: apb_cdc_bridge 2-phase toggle is not one-sided-reset safe; PMU resets CPU domain alone
description:
Research finding (primary sources) + empirical result from GH #95 directed testing.

== STATUS: no counterexample found in simulation; class concern remains open ==

GH #95 added 3 directed one-sided-reset tests to test_apb_cdc_bridge.py
(test_reset_asym_s_held_m_free, test_reset_asym_staggered_s_then_m,
test_reset_asym_staggered_m_then_s), on top of pre-existing
test_reset_mid_transaction_m_side / test_availability_* coverage. Suite is 22/22 PASS.

Verified clean across stagger windows of 1x/3x/8x the slower period, both release
orders, at 7/13ns, 18/4ns and 10ns-equal ratios:
  - m_psel/m_penable never pulse while m_rst_n_i is genuinely low (no fabricated
    destination write)
  - s_pready always force-completes within bounded time (no hang)
  - post-recovery reads/writes land exactly once (no duplication)

IMPORTANT: this is empirical absence-of-failure in the constructed scenarios, NOT a
proof that the class is safe. cocotb cannot establish the general property. A formal
treatment would need chip-design-formal (2-phase toggle FSM reachability under
arbitrary one-sided reset timing). Leaving this bead OPEN on that basis.

== THE UNDERLYING CLASS CONCERN (unchanged) ==

Both PULP and OpenTitan independently conclude a 2-phase (NRZ) handshake CDC is
unsafe under one-sided asynchronous reset, and both ship a 4-phase (RZ) variant
specifically to fix it:

- PULP cdc_reset_ctrlr.sv: 'We use a 4-phase rather than a 2-phase CDC to avoid the
  issues of one-sided async reset that might trigger spurious transactions.'
- OpenTitan prim_sync_reqack.sv: the RZ four-phase option 'is safe to reset either
  domain in isolation, since the two FSMs cannot get out of sync due to persistent
  EVEN/ODD states.' Its NRZ default instead carries the contract 'When resetting one
  domain, also the other domain needs to be reset with both resets being active at
  the same time', machine-checked by SyncReqAckRstSrc/Dst assertions.

rtl/soc/apb_cdc_bridge.sv is 2-phase toggle -- the variant both projects call unsafe.
Today largely masked by cross-coupled resets, BUT the PMU can reset the CPU domain
alone (pmu_cpu_rst_n), which is exactly the one-sided case.

Note apb_cdc_bridge.sv:281-335 documents a separate reviewed exception for
m_rst_n_s availability-gating -- different concern, not this one.

Resolution options if a counterexample is ever found: RZ 4-phase conversion (halves
throughput, irrelevant on a config path), or a documented+asserted contract that PMU
CPU-domain reset must not overlap an in-flight APB_PLL2 transaction.
notes:
ARM/open-source survey (GH #95) found a NAMED UPSTREAM FIX and confirms we are the minority choice.

Three independent implementations of an async APB bridge all use 4-phase RZ, not our
2-phase NRZ toggle, and at least one states the reason in exactly our terms:

  - ARM cmsdk_ahb_to_apb_async.v -- 4-phase, per its own OVL assertion names
    ('Test 4 phase hande shaking - phase 1', 'Req rising edge should only take place
    when Ack is low'). Structure otherwise identical to ours: 2x 2-FF on the handshake
    only, payload passed unsynchronised and held stable by the handshake.
  - Hazard3 hazard3_apb_async_bridge -- 4-phase.
  - OpenDAP bridge -- 4-phase, stating: 'A NRZI toggle handshake ... can cause spurious
    bus accesses when only one side of the link is reset.'

That last sentence is this bead, verbatim, from an upstream project.

So: our bridge's STRUCTURE matches ARM's async APB bridge exactly; only the handshake
ENCODING differs, and ours is the one all three projects avoided. Conversion to 4-phase
RZ halves throughput, which is irrelevant on a config path (APB_PLL2).

Note ARM's STA guidance for its async bridge is the older set_false_path on the payload;
our GH #94 set_max_delay -datapath_only is the stronger choice.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #140 (merged, 10/10 CI checks). apb_cdc_bridge converted from 2-phase NRZ to 4-phase RZ, matching PULP/OpenTitan and all three surveyed async-APB bridges (ARM cmsdk, Hazard3, OpenDAP). The cheaper 'document a contract' option was rejected as unsound here: OpenTitan's NRZ contract requires the other domain to be reset too, overlapping, which PD_CPU power-down cannot honour, and the PMU has no drain/quiesce step.

Verified: sim lint clean; test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23 including a NEW test_rz_four_phase_structural_proof that discriminates the encodings (the pre-existing 22 pass on BOTH, which is why GH #95's directed one-sided-reset testing never found a counterexample); soc_all 179/179 across 25 suites; CDC-filter non-vacuity gate PASS with negative control.

Caught during integration and worth remembering: the rename silently broke check_cdc_timing.tcl's filters (still matching *req_toggle_q*), which would have made the post-route CDC check examine zero nets -- bead 7l5's failure mode, re-introduced and nearly shipped. Also two review-caught doc contradictions the conversion itself introduced (fd11176).

RESIDUE, filed separately: set_max_delay -datapath_only BUDGET compliance is still unverified -- binding is proven, budgets are not, and that needs post-route delays from a full SoC run.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
VERIFIED + PR #140 opened on fix/apb-cdc-4phase-rfz (commit da73ac6).

RESULT: sim lint clean (0 errors, no apb_cdc_bridge warnings); test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23; soc_all 179/179 across 25 suites, 0 failures. Note the baseline in this bead's history (159/159, 21 suites) is stale -- the suite count grew with the PMU/CDC/multiclock work. The divergent-ratio suites (soc_multiclock, soc_pll_multiclock at 7ns/3ns) are included and green.

NO testbench needed a latency update. Throughput on this path is intentionally halved by the RZ conversion, and nothing in the regression had hard-coded the old 2-phase cycle count, so the extra wait state passed through cleanly. axil_to_apb's tolerance of arbitrary pready wait states held in practice, not just on paper.

THE DISCRIMINATING TEST NOW EXISTS. test_rz_four_phase_structural_proof walks all four phases and asserts the RZ-defining ordering: req_q still 1 when ack_s asserts, ack_s still 1 when req_q falls, s_state_q visiting S_DROP. That sequence is impossible on the old NRZ encoding -- unlike the pre-existing 22 tests, which pass on BOTH encodings and therefore never proved anything about this bead. This is the artifact the bead was missing: the GH #95 one-sided-reset tests found no counterexample precisely because cocotb could not distinguish the encodings.

TWO DEFECTS CAUGHT DURING INTEGRATION, both worth recording:
1. The new test initially FAILED on correct RTL -- it compared s_state_q against 3 (S_DONE) while its own message said S_DROP (2); the enum is S_IDLE=0, S_REQ=1, S_DROP=2, S_DONE=3, and the TB documented that correctly elsewhere in the same file. Phases 1-3 (the real ordering proof) had passed. State ordinals are now named constants in the TB so a structural check cannot silently assert against the wrong one.
2. pnr/scripts/check_cdc_timing.tcl still filtered on *req_toggle_q* / *ack_toggle_q* for u_apb_pll2_cdc and u_apb_dbg_cdc. After the rename those match ZERO nets, so the post-route CDC budget check would have reported clean because it examined nothing -- bead 7l5's exact failure mode, re-introduced by this change and nearly shipped. Filters repointed at req_q/ack_q with a comment tying them to the rename.

CARRIED, NOT CLOSED BY THIS BEAD: the SDC edits are comment/line-number only (the set_max_delay exceptions target instance names u_req_sync/u_ack_sync/u_apb_pll2_cdc/u_apb_dbg_cdc, which did not change) and are Tcl-SYNTAX-validated only. Binding against a real netlist is unverified -- it needs a PD run, and the CDC budget check's non-vacuity on the new names has not been demonstrated by negative control the way 7l5's fix was.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
CDC-CHECKER NON-VACUITY GATE: PASS (2026-08-13), with negative control.

Measured on a flattened netlist built from pnr/asap7/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v (regenerated 21:43 from the post-rename RTL):
  NEW filters   u_apb_pll2_cdc req_q=1  ack_q=1   |  u_apb_dbg_cdc req_q=1  ack_q=1
  OLD filters   u_apb_pll2_cdc req_toggle_q=0  ack_toggle_q=0  |  u_apb_dbg_cdc  both 0
Exact names: \u_apb_pll2_cdc.req_q, \u_apb_pll2_cdc.ack_q, \u_apb_dbg_cdc.req_q, \u_apb_dbg_cdc.ack_q -- the dot-joined escaped NET form bead 7l5 documented. Over-match checked: the pattern *u_apb_pll2_cdc*req_q* matches exactly ONE net, not a family.

INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK that makes this more than a self-consistent result: run 23's signed-off netlist (/nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/RUN_2026-08-09_14-36-16/final/nl/soc_top.nl.v, built from the PRE-rename RTL) contains \u_apb_pll2_cdc.req_toggle_q, 6 hits. So the old filters were genuinely non-vacuous BEFORE this change and are genuinely dead AFTER it, with the rename as the only variable. That is the same negative-control standard 7l5 was closed under.

METHOD NOTE -- the full synth run was ABANDONED and is not needed for this question. 'make librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock --to OpenROAD.STAPrePNR' ran 7h21m stuck in ABC at 10.2 GB RSS on a 15.9 GB host (2 GB available), against a 74-minute budget from run 23's step-04 timing, and had produced no netlist. Killed it. The gate was then answered in minutes with yosys 'read_verilog -sv; hierarchy -top soc_top; proc; flatten; opt_clean; write_verilog' and NO ABC, because flattened register net names come from the flatten pass, not from technology mapping. Anyone re-running this class of name-binding check should skip ABC deliberately rather than budget for a full synthesis.

Two earlier attempts died for an unrelated reason worth recording: a run launched from inside an agent turn was reaped when that turn ended (93 s in, mid-ABC, error.log 0 bytes, no OOM). Long PD runs must be launched detached -- setsid/nohup or tmux -- not as a child of an agent turn.

STILL OPEN, unchanged: this proves BINDING only. Actual set_max_delay -datapath_only budget compliance needs post-route delays from a full ~6 h SoC run, deliberately deferred to the next run done for another reason. Also, the flatten is not technology-mapped, so post-ABC names could in principle differ; run 23's identical naming form for the old name is what makes that low-risk rather than an assumption.

title: Test live PMU power-cycle at a divergent cpu_clk/clk ratio (GH #90 residual)
description: Residual coverage gap identified while fixing bead 542. No suite exercises a LIVE, firmware-driven PMU power-cycle (runtime write to PMU CTRL, CPU domain off then on) while cpu_clk_i and clk_i run at different rates - which is exactly the scenario bead 542's bug lived in. Existing coverage validates the two halves separately: cold boot at a divergent ratio (soc_multiclock 4/4) and PMU sequencing at 1:1 (test_pmu 10/10, tb_pmu instantiates pmu.sv standalone with no CDC at all). The 542 fix (soc_top.sv commit 30beab3: cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync) is justified structurally with unbounded skew tolerance, but is not directly tested. Suggested test: extend the soc_multiclock suite with a firmware sequence that powers the CPU domain down and back up via the PMU, asserting the CPU resumes with architectural state intact (PC/MSTATUS/MTVEC preserved - see docs/POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md:25, retention-by-construction because the behavioral model clock-gates rather than removing supply). Owner: verification-orchestrator.
close_reason: Already delivered and never closed. Test landed as tb/cocotb/soc/test_soc_pmu_multiclock.py (GH #95 Group C, 26.9K) with new firmware pmu_cycle_fw/pmu_cycle.hex and Makefile target soc_pmu_multiclock (tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile:742-753, in the .PHONY suite list). CPU=3ns/fabric=7ns coprime ratio; DMA writes MODE_CPU_OFF to PMU CTRL on the CPU's behalf, TB backdoor supplies the power-up trigger. It did its job: found a P1 (post-power-cycle CPU deadlock) fixed in be37959 -- u_cpu_axi_cdc.s_rst_n_i re-sourced to cpu_core_rst_n so the bridge retains like the CPU it serves, instead of async-flushing while the CPU retained by clock-gating. Also gives the first live exercise of the 30beab3 power-up ordering fix.

title: PD port stubs missing cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i (blocks GH #96 multi-clock PD re-closure)
description: GH #92 added top-level ports cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i to soc_top and GH #93 made them load-bearing (u_cpu_cg is sourced from cpu_core_clk). The PD port stubs were never updated: pnr/asap7/soc/soc_top_ports.v, pnr/sky130/soc/soc_top_ports.v and pnr/sky130/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v all have ZERO occurrences of cpu_clk_i - they still declare only clk_i/rst_n_i. Any PD run against these stubs would synthesise a single-clock SoC and silently lose the CDC boundary. Must be regenerated before GH #96 (multi-clock PD re-closure), and before any SoC LibreLane run on this branch. Also note phase5_soc.sdc is still single-clock (one create_clock, no set_clock_groups -asynchronous) - that is GH #94's job, but #96 depends on both.
close_reason: Both soc_top_ports.v stubs synced with cpu_clk_i/cpu_rst_n_i/cpu_pll_locked_o; 24/24 ports verified against rtl/soc/soc_top.sv, Verilator clean. soc_top_sv2v.v files are generated/untracked and regenerate from soc_top.sv. Remaining PD work for GH #94/#96: create_clock on cpu_clk_i + set_clock_groups -asynchronous.

title: GH #94 SDC must cover apb_cdc_bridge cross-domain paths
description: GH #93 added rtl/soc/apb_cdc_bridge.sv. Its 4 cross-domain combinational payload reads (cmd_*/resp_*) plus both toggle-bit cdc_2ff_sync crossings need set_max_delay -datapath_only in the multi-clock SDC, alongside the already-known async_axi_fifo mem_q read and the two gray-pointer crossings. Do not close #94 without covering both modules.
close_reason: GH #94 done: pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc covers both CDC modules -- async_axi_fifo (5 instances: mem_q read + 2 gray-pointer crossings each, set_max_delay -datapath_only bounded per-instance to source/destination period) and apb_cdc_bridge (2 toggle-bit crossings + 4-signal cmd_* bus + 2-signal resp_* bus, same treatment). Also fixed pnr/Makefile's stale SKY130_SOC_SV_FILES/SOC_SV_FILES sv2v lists (missing rv32i_clock_gate.sv + all 5 CDC files), verified via a clean make sky130-soc-sv2v + make asap7-soc-sv2v (all new modules present, zero undefined-module warnings). Constraint-authoring only, no P&R run launched -- GH #96 owns wiring the SDC into config.json and re-closure.

title: pmu.sv power-up ordering unsafe across async CPU domain (GH #90 follow-up)
description: Found during GH #93. pmu.sv's per-domain sequencer asserts rst_n_w=1 (DOM_PU_RST) one full core_clk cycle BEFORE it asserts clk_en_w=1 (DOM_PU_CLK) on the power-up path. Since GH #93, pmu_cpu_rst_n and pmu_cpu_clk_en cross into the independently-clocked cpu_core_clk domain through two SEPARATE 2-stage synchronisers, so the 1-cycle offset is not structurally preserved downstream. A live firmware-driven CPU power-down/up cycle could see cpu_domain_rst_n release before the clock ungates - the same bug class as 4398c2e, narrower window. Cold boot is unaffected (verified: soc_all 159/159). Fix likely in pmu.sv: merge DOM_PU_RST/DOM_PU_CLK, or ungate the clock before releasing reset. Note the UPF fixes the sequencing order, so check phase5_soc.upf compliance before changing it. Untested area: no suite exercises PMU-driven live power-cycling across domains.
notes: Fixed in rtl/soc/soc_top.sv (not pmu.sv -- UPF-mandated ordering preserved). Gated u_cpu_cg enable with pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync: cpu_gated_clk_en = ~pmu_cpu_clk_dis_sync & pmu_cpu_rst_n_cpu_sync. Verified lint_soc 0 errors, make pmu 10/10, soc_boot 3/3 (100/100 stability), soc_multiclock 4/4. Commit on feat/cpu-domain-cdc-gh93.

title: Sky130 SoC Stage-2: setup fails at ss corner (WNS -8.9ns); sign-off gated to tt only
description:
Found 2026-07-28 auditing run RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57. At 65 MHz (CLOCK_PERIOD 15.385 ns) the SoC closes setup at tt and ff but FAILS at all three ss corners: max_ss_100C_1v60 WNS -8.902 ns / TNS -118.16 ns; nom_ss -7.767; min_ss -6.386. Checker.SetupViolations reports 'No setup violations found' ONLY because pnr/sky130/soc/config.json sets TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS=['*tt*'] — STA_CORNERS runs all 9, but the gate ignores ss and ff. So the 'Stage-2 signed off at 65 MHz' claim is tt-only and should be stated that way.

ROOT CAUSE: the CPU hard macro's characterized clk->Q. Worst ss path is u_cpu/clk_i -> u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[15] = 8.155 ns, i.e. 53% of the 15.385 ns period consumed inside the macro before any SoC logic runs. The 12 worst ss paths are all u_cpu -> u_cpu or *_ -> u_cpu. This is bead 1ls (GH #123) resurfacing at the slow corner: 4.55 ns clk->Q at nom_tt, 7.54 at nom_ss, 8.12 at max_ss, against a 2.0 ns set_output_delay budget in pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc that gives the optimizer no pressure.

CONTEXT: 1ls was closed 2026-07-25 with 'Accepted 65 MHz (user decision)' after proving budget tightening is a dead end (8.0 ns budget failed to close Stage-1: WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints). That decision was about not reaching 75 MHz — it did NOT establish that ss fails outright at 65 MHz. This bead records that distinct fact so it is not lost.

OPTIONS: (a) document the tt-only position explicitly and keep 65 MHz — cheapest, but then Sky130 Stage-2 is not a true multi-corner sign-off; (b) drop the SoC clock to ~41 MHz (1/(15.385+8.902)) so ss closes honestly; (c) re-harden the Stage-1 CPU macro against an ss-aware budget — 1ls suggests this is very hard for this topology. NOTE the ss numbers are honest for the CPU macro (9 per-corner CPU libs staged 2026-07-25, commit 86e89c1) but the SRAM macro is still TT-only analytical (bead o1i / GH #120), so the ss result carries some SRAM-model error. DECISION NEEDED — not PD tuning.
notes:
2026-07-29 RESULT — the 40 MHz relaxation did NOT close ss. RUN_2026-07-29_18-40-38 post-PnR STA at CLOCK_PERIOD 25.0 ns: max_ss setup WNS -4.328 ns (was -8.902 @15.385), nom_ss -2.885, min_ss -1.120. tt and ff clean.

WHY THE 41 MHz ESTIMATE WAS WRONG: it assumed path delay is invariant under relaxation. It is not. Effective path was 24.287 ns at T=15.385 and 29.328 ns at T=25.0 — 5.041 ns slower for 9.615 ns of relaxation, i.e. dpath/dT = 0.524. Each ns of period buys only ~0.48 ns of slack because the optimizer hands speed back (downsizes cells) as soon as it has margin. Linear two-point fit: slack = 0.476*T - 16.222, zero at T = 34.08 ns = 29.3 MHz. Crude extrapolation from two points — the same give-back effect may recur, so 29 MHz is a lower bound on the answer, not a guarantee.

PARKED. User decision 2026-07-29: fix the hold regression first (see 9t6/58q), then re-judge frequency against a clean baseline. CLOCK_PERIOD stays at 25.0 ns meanwhile. Do not chase ss further until hold is green at all 9 corners.
2026-08-13 DEFERRED (host-blocked). Already PARKED by user decision 2026-07-29 pending the hold regression; independently cannot be honestly closed before bead o1i (per-corner SRAM SPICE characterization, ~80-95 h), which is itself host-blocked. Removing from bd ready so the backlog stops offering unschedulable work; analysis retained verbatim.

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR is false — same unrepaired over-cap nets as the SoC had
description: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json:102 has RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR: false, the same setting that on the SoC (pnr/sky130/soc/config.json) left a 0.626 pF / 1.687 ns-slew net unrepaired and cost 1.03 ns on a macro clk->Q arc. Enabling it on the SoC (bead y7v, commit 1ef3426) recovered setup from -1.4304 to +1.3873 -- +1.15 ns better than the pre-existing baseline -- because it also repaired other over-cap/over-slew nets that had gone unrepaired for the whole Stage-2 history. The Stage-1 CPU hardening run has never had this step enabled, so rv32i_cpu_top's internal nets likely carry the same unrepaired slew/cap violations. Its .lib is not WRONG (arcs are characterized from the actual netlist) but is probably pessimistic, and the SoC consumes that .lib as a hard macro whose output drive cannot be resized. NOTE enabling it will likely hit the same RSZ-0090 abort if any macro .lib in the CPU flow declares an unachievable max_transition -- the SRAM fix was 8b11092. Also note the SoC antenna cost: pin violations went 144 -> 164 when this was enabled (bead 58q). Precedent: all ASAP7 configs run with this true.
notes: 2026-07-27 FINAL — RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57 COMPLETE, adoption fully validated on every axis vs the previously published closure RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43. TIMING, all three gated *tt* corners improved on BOTH setup and hold: setup nom_tt +1.3873->+1.8585 (+0.471), min_tt +2.5656->+2.8940 (+0.328), max_tt +0.3391->+0.8662 (+0.527); hold nom_tt +0.1444->+0.2932 (+0.149), min_tt +0.2489->+0.2919 (+0.043), max_tt +0.0923->+0.2706 (+0.178). Violator list EMPTY, and both Checker.SetupViolations and Checker.HoldViolations were LIVE GATES for this run. LVS 'Circuits match uniquely'. KLayout DRC 4 and Magic DRC 9081, both identical to baseline. ANTENNA IMPROVED 164->147 pin and 134->127 net -- I had predicted a regression there (design repair cost +20 pin at SoC and +4 at CPU previously); the better-repaired macro actually reduced it. max_tt, the tightest corner and the one where the CPU macro STILL violates setup internally at -0.12078, gained the most setup and nearly tripled hold margin, so that residual macro violation does not propagate to the SoC. CONCLUSION: the 0ro premise is confirmed end-to-end -- unrepaired over-cap/over-slew nets in the Stage-1 CPU made its .lib arcs pessimistic, and repairing them improves everything downstream. Macro views staged in commit 995c487, merged to main via PR #125.
close_reason: Validated by RUN_2026-07-27_17-15-57: staging the re-hardened CPU macro improved all three gated corners on both setup and hold (max_tt +0.527 setup / +0.178 hold), LVS match uniquely, DRC unchanged (KLayout 4 / Magic 9081), antenna improved 164->147 pin. Macro merged to main in PR #125.

title: Sky130 Stage-2: nom_tt hold violation -0.0923 ns at the sign-off corner
description: RUN_2026-07-25_13-29-40 shows nom_tt_025C_1v80 hold WNS -0.0923 ns / TNS -0.0923 (1 violating endpoint). The baseline (RUN_2026-07-24_21-36-12, nom_tt-wildcarded macro libs) reported nom_tt hold +0.1807 ns MET. The violation surfaced when the CPU macro moved to genuine per-corner Liberty views AND the antenna repair flow was enabled (2018 diodes, perturbing routing) -- the two changed together so the cause is not cleanly attributed. This is a violation at the ACTUAL SIGN-OFF CORNER, so it matters more than the ss-corner residuals. Note pnr/Makefile's librelane-sky130-soc recipe has --skip Checker.HoldViolations, so the flow does not gate on this. Investigate: identify the violating endpoint, confirm whether post-CTS/post-route hold repair ran and why it left this path, and whether it is diode-induced or lib-induced (a libs-only run would separate them).
notes: RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43 CLOSES BOTH at nom_tt_025C_1v80: SETUP +1.38729 MET (was -1.4304), HOLD +0.14439 MET (was -0.0923 at baseline). Violator list EMPTY. Cleared OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT with no RSZ-0090 recurrence. Step-40 setup recovered 3.0776 -> 4.0130 (baseline 4.0600). DIRECT PROOF the repair hit the real defect, not luck: u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[18] restored to fanout 1, cap 0.019504, clk->Q 4.544736 -- vs broken 2/0.625885/5.572786 and baseline 1/0.019349/4.544564. Setup is also +1.15 ns BETTER than baseline (+1.387 vs +0.2413) because post-GRT design repair fixed other over-cap/over-slew nets too. TWO fixes required, both committed: (1) clk_i excluded from set_driving_cell [all_inputs] and given its own clkbuf_16, worth +362 ps hold, setup-neutral, clock port 886->371 ps [e946350]; (2) RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR true [1ef3426] + SRAM lib max_transition 0.04->0.5 [8b11092] to unblock the RSZ-0090 hard abort (40 ps unachievable in sky130_fd_sc_hd, PDK floor 43 ps; 0.04 was OpenRAM's characterization-range ceiling). GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN was investigated and EXONERATED (step-40 hold bit-identical at 0.15 and 0.05); left at default 0.05. DRC/LVS/antenna still pending -- run at step 52 of ~63. Do not close until those confirm.
close_reason: RESOLVED by RUN_2026-07-26_16-05-43: nom_tt_025C_1v80 setup +1.38729 (TNS 0.0) and hold +0.14439, both MET, violator list empty, LVS circuits match uniquely. Required two fixes: clk_i own clkbuf_16 driving cell (e946350) for hold, and RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR true (1ef3426) + SRAM lib max_transition 0.04->0.5 (8b11092) for setup. Defect net u_cpu/axi_araddr_o[18] verified restored to baseline cap/clk->Q. Antenna regression 144->164 pin recorded on bead 58q.

title: SRAM_SKY130 hard-macro branch not covered by default regression
description:
tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile defaults SRAM_TARGET=freepdk45, and the soc_all target invokes sram_controller without SRAM_TARGET=sky130. So the OpenRAM hard-macro read path in rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv (rd_pend_q pipeline + 2-entry skid buffer handling the macro's 1-cycle registered read latency) is only exercised by a separate manual invocation.

Evidence: Stage-2 sign-off reported soc_all 99/99 AND sky130-branch 11/11 as two distinct runs, not one.

Risk: the SRAM_SKY130 branch can silently bit-rot on future unrelated RTL changes, since nothing in routine regression touches it. This is the branch that carried a P0 data-corruption bug (rvalid asserted one cycle before the macro's negedge-launched dout1 latched) found on 2026-07-24 - exactly the class of defect that must not regress unnoticed.

Fix options: add a soc_all_sky130 target, or make soc_all run the sram_controller suite twice (both SRAM_TARGET values), or add a CI job.
close_reason: Verified: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile soc_all now runs sram_controller twice (default flat freepdk45 + SRAM_TARGET=sky130 OpenRAM macro branch). Full soc_all re-run: 18 suite invocations, 110/110 tests PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0. sky130 sram_controller pass = 11/11, confirmed built with +define+SRAM_SKY130 -GMEM_WORDS=1024 and sim/sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8.sv (not a silent flat-array fallback). No ordering/stale-sim_build issue running sram_controller twice back-to-back. Log: /nobackup/soc_all_gh104/soc_all_68m_run1.log. design_state.json history[] + memory/verification/experiences.jsonl updated.

title: GH #104: sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 has 4 KLayout DRC violations (upstream OpenRAM generator)
description:
Full-deck KLayout DRC (sky130A_mr.drc) on the Stage-2 SoC sign-off GDS (RUN_2026-07-24_09-58-19) found 4 real violations, all inside the OpenRAM-compiled sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 macro's own internal cells. Confirmed via an isolation test (full KLayout deck on the macro's raw standalone GDS, no SoC context): identical violations, identical coordinates -- proving these are baked into the OpenRAM compile itself, not caused by or fixable via SoC-level PDN/floorplan/routing work.

Violations:
- m2.2 (met2 spacing <0.14um) x1, cell ..._wmask_dff, measured 0.055um (~60% short of spec)
- via2.2 (via2 spacing <0.2um) x2, cells macro-top + ..._bank, measured 0.125um (~37.5% short)
- m3.2 (met3 spacing <0.3um) x1, cell ..._bank, measured 0.29um (~3% short, ~1nm, plausibly grid-rounding but still non-conformant)

Root cause: the macro was compiled views-first with check_lvsdrc=False (OpenRAM's own DRC/LVS never ran), a deliberate choice made after the check_lvsdrc=True extraction died to a host reboot at ~7h. Confirmed these are in OpenRAM's generated assembly layer (compiler/modules/bank.py + the generic dff_array factory type used as wmask_dff), not a foundry-drawn primitive -- searched the installed sky130_fd_bd_sram primitive library, zero matches for these cell names.

USER DECISION (2026-07-24): accept + document for now, do not patch the GDS, do not retry OpenRAM config, do not attempt a DRC-clean regenerate at this time. Full record: pnr/sky130/soc/pdn.tcl (header comment) and memory/pd/run_state.md.

Follow-up: a future DRC-clean macro regeneration (options considered: (a) check_lvsdrc=True regen -- high non-completion risk given reboot cadence, and wouldn't fix anything by itself since OpenRAM geometry is deterministic, only reports; (b) OpenRAM config tweak, e.g. different words_per_row/column-mux, that might shift the bank/wmask_dff floorplan to avoid these spots -- speculative, ~190min+ per rebuild attempt; (c) targeted GDS patch of the 4 exact coordinates -- fast but fragile/non-reproducible from config).

Full-chip DRC signoff for GH #104 is NOT complete until this is resolved or explicitly re-accepted at tape-out-readiness review.
notes: Tracked on GitHub: https://github.com/chuanseng-ng/claude_verilog_test/issues/121
close_reason: Won't-fix, accepted with evidence (GH #121). efabless prebuilt sky130_sram_2kbyte_1rw1r_32x512_8 -- used in real MPW silicon -- ships 32 magic DRC errors in its own OpenRAM build log and is likewise analytical + nominal-corner-only; repo has no 4KB 32x1024_8 variant to swap to. Our 4 violations (one ~1nm) are OpenRAM generator norm, not a consequence of check_lvsdrc=False (geometry is deterministic; the checker only reports). All fix options cost 190min+/attempt on a host rebooting every 2-8h for no correctness gain. Re-open trigger: genuine tape-out-readiness review.

title: Sky130 Stage 2: CPU-macro + peripherals SoC, real DRC/LVS (GH #104)
design:
GH #104, part of epic #102 (bead n0i). Stage 2: pnr/sky130/soc/ — CPU as hard macro (Stage-1 native Sky130 views) + flat peripherals, NO GPU, real Magic DRC + KLayout DRC + Netgen LVS. Template = pnr/asap7/soc/ (adapt ASAP7->Sky130, drop GPU, flip DRC/LVS true).

APPROACH (PD-only; no functional RTL change):
- GPU exclusion = TIE-OFF STUB (not RTL surgery). Swap rtl/gpu/gpu_top.sv for a synthesizable stub driving all AXI master + irq outputs idle/0; soc_top.sv UNCHANGED. GPU optimizes away; crossbar keeps idle GPU master ports. Zero RTL re-verification (preserves soc_all 82/82). Drop rtl/gpu/* + gpu_pkg from the sv2v file list, add the tie-off stub.
- CPU = hard macro: blackbox stub at synth (rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv) + Stage-1 native Sky130 views at P&R (pnr/sky130/cpu/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.{lef,lib,nl.v.gz}). CPU macro = VPWR/VGND PG pins, 3600x1800um.
- SoC SRAM (sram_controller, 4KB) + boot_rom (4KB): keep BEHAVIORAL (flat flops ~32K each -> ~25-30K cells total). 'flat peripherals' per issue; avoids a 2nd SRAM-macro Magic artifact. Note added die area.
- sv2v frontend (soc-synth-needs-sv2v): new make sky130-soc-sv2v target, SV file list = ASAP7 list minus GPU + the tie-off stub; json_header_soc.py workaround for soc_top port stub.

FILES TO CREATE (pnr/sky130/soc/): config.json, constraints/sky130_soc.sdc, pdn.tcl, macro_placement.cfg, gpu_top_tieoff.sv, rv32i_cpu_top_stub.sv, soc_top_ports.v, json_header_soc.py, gen scripts; pnr/Makefile targets sky130-soc-sv2v + librelane-sky130-soc.

KEY CONFIG:
- Clock ~75 MHz (Sky130 CPU ceiling; no GPU governing). Apply set_driving_cell on inputs (Stage-1/CodeRabbit lesson) for honest timing.
- Die: must exceed CPU macro 3600x1800 + flat logic; est ~5000x2400um, util ~40-50%. PD agent to size.
- PDN: sky130 met1-5 grid + CPU macro M4/M5 ring; PDN_MACRO_CONNECTIONS=".*u_cpu.* VPWR VGND vccd1 vssd1"; PDN_CONNECT_MACROS_TO_GRID=true.
- RUN_MAGIC_DRC=true, RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC=true, RUN_LVS=true.
- CPU macro in MACROS object (Stage-1 lesson) so Magic DRC blackboxes it (avoid flattening macro GDS -> phantom li.3). EXTRA_SPICE_MODELS = CPU macro spice + any SRAM spice for Netgen LVS.
- Portable pdk_dir:: paths (CodeRabbit lesson). GPL/DPL_CELL_PADDING=4 (Stage-1 lesson).

RISKS: (1) CPU-macro Magic DRC artifact (same class as Stage-1 SRAM; KLayout authoritative). (2) Behavioral SoC SRAM/ROM flop area bloats die. (3) LVS needs CPU macro spice/netlist + correct PG. (4) sv2v file-list drift. (5) CPU macro PG (VPWR/VGND) -> SoC PDN connection correctness (floating-domain risk).

GATE: KLayout DRC=0, Netgen LVS=MATCH, Magic DRC (expect macro artifact -> documented, KLayout authoritative), timing met @~75MHz honest (with set_driving_cell), PDN connected (CPU macro powered). Record fmax/power/area + DRC/LVS logs.

EXECUTION: chip-design-pd:physical-design-orchestrator (read PD memories + knowledge.md first). PD-only -> no functional re-verification.
notes: 2026-08-01 SUPERSEDES the earlier 'STAGE 2 STATUS: NOT fully closed / ujv OPEN / 44.1 mW' text in this bead's notes -- that wording is HISTORICAL. Current state: Stage 2 is CLOSED as a typical-corner (nom_tt) timing sign-off. ujv is DEFERRED host-blocked (not open); 58q is CLOSED as a quantified accepted antenna/hold trade-off (not an open gate). Power is recorded per corner, not as one scalar: nom_tt 37.63 mW, worst corner max_ff 44.13 mW -- the 44.1 mW figure in the older note was the max_ff corner mislabeled as the headline. Corner accounting also corrected: max_tt_025C_1v80 (+6.959 ns setup, clean) had been omitted from both the clean and failing lists, so only 8 of 9 corners were classified; the adopted run is 6 clean (nom/max/min tt, nom/min/max ff) and 3 failing (ss only).

Residuals are tracked separately and are NOT open gates on this bead: ujv (ss setup, deferred host-blocked behind o1i's per-corner SRAM characterization) and 58q (antenna 140/120, closed as an accepted trade-off against hold). title: apb4_register_bank: range check truncates N_REGS at max bank size (GH #87)
description: CodeRabbit follow-up PR #84, pre-existing latent edge. WORDW'(N_REGS) cast wraps to 0 when N_REGS==2**WORDW exactly -> write/read guards reject every access at max bank size. Latent today: all banks N_REGS<2**WORDW. Phase 6 adds ~6 new peripheral banks that could hit max. FIX: compare addr_word against integer-sized N_REGS first, then slice for indexing (write+read paths). RTL->rtl-design-orchestrator, verify apb4_register_bank unit suite + soc_all.
close_reason: Fixed — rtl/soc/apb4_register_bank.sv:102,117 zero-extend addr_word to 32b before comparing against N_REGS ({{(32-WORDW){1'b0}}, addr_word} < N_REGS), so N_REGS==2**WORDW no longer wraps to 0. Comment at :100 documents the truncating-cast bug. GH #87.

title: axil_to_apb: gate ARREADY against concurrent AW/W in S_IDLE (GH #85)
description: CodeRabbit follow-up PR #84, pre-existing latent. In S_IDLE with AWVALID+WVALID+ARVALID all asserted, write wins state_d but AR capture overwrites addr_q/is_write_q -> accepted write lost or wrong-channel response. Latent today: CPU D-cache never issues concurrent R+W. Phase 6 adds AES/NPU/DMA masters that can. FIX: gate s_axil_arready with && !s_axil_awvalid && !s_axil_wvalid (axil_to_apb.sv:133) + directed AR+AW+W concurrent test. RTL->rtl-design-orchestrator, verify axil_to_apb unit suite + soc_all.
close_reason: Fixed — rtl/soc/axil_to_apb.sv:138 gates s_axil_arready with && !s_axil_awvalid && !s_axil_wvalid, so a concurrent AR+AW+W in S_IDLE cannot overwrite addr_q/is_write_q. GH #85 rationale documented in-line at :133-137.

title: PLL safety: clearing pll_enable (CONTROL[0]) self-bricks the SoC
description: CodeRabbit (PR #88) MAJOR, pre-existing (not introduced by the pll_subsystem refactor; same gating in old pll_axil_regs). pll_enable=CONTROL[0] in pll_apb_regs (clk_i domain, reset default=1). If firmware clears it: pll_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_enable->0 -> PLL held in reset -> pll_locked->0 -> core_rst_n=rst_n_i&pll_locked->0 -> resets CPU+soc_bus. pll_apb_regs is NOT reset by core_rst_n (clk_i domain) so pll_enable stays 0 -> permanent deadlock; the APB master that wrote 0 is gone before it can write 1 back. FIX OPTIONS: (a) make CONTROL[0] set-only / non-clearable in SoC integration (firmware can enable, not disable); or (b) gate PLL reconfig so it doesn't drop core_rst_n in a non-recoverable way; or (c) add a startup/watchdog recovery. Functional design change -> own PR + soc_all re-verify. Natural to fold into #4 (3-PLL/CDC) where PLL control is reworked. NOT fixed in the refactor PR #88 (which preserved existing behavior).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #108 — CONTROL[0] non-clearable (WMASK 03F1->03F0)

title: Evaluate per-IP power domains + power on/off sequencing (CPU/GPU/periph)
description: OWN TRACK (NOT gating Phase 6) — evaluate, schedule deliberately. phase5_soc.upf already declares PD_CPU/PD_GPU/PD_SRAM/PD_PERIPH but gating is NOT implemented/validated (M11 PDN was single-VDD). Real per-IP power domains for on/off sequencing testing need: isolation cells, level shifters, retention FFs, power switches, UPF-driven gating, a power-sequencing controller, and power-aware verification (UPF sim) + multi-rail PDN in PD. Substantial low-power track. Deliver: feasibility/architecture eval -> if pursued, a low-power feature epic. physical-design + verification (UPF/power-aware).
notes: 2026-08-01 DELIVERED via GH epic #98 (#99 RTL, #100 soc_top integration, #101 cocotb verification), PR #129 on branch feat/pmu-power-mode-sequencer-gh98. rtl/soc/pmu.sv = APB4 slave (reusing apb4_register_bank) + per-domain 9-state sequencer FSM encoding the 4 PST states from phase5_soc.upf. UPF-mandated order walked one action per cycle, structurally guaranteed: down = ret_save -> iso_en -> gate clk -> assert reset; up = release reset -> ungate clk -> ret_restore -> de-assert iso_en. Scope held to the 2026-06-27 decision: sequencing ONLY -- retention save/restore emitted in order for assertion but a functional no-op (phase5_soc.upf:23, no retention registers in Phase 5); no supply removal, no power switches, pg_ctrl deliberately not emitted. PMU at 0x2000_8000-8FFF; no free APB slot existed so PERIPH_LIMIT and AXIL_APB_LIMIT both extended to 0x2000_8FFF. First SoC-level clock gates (2x rv32i_clock_gate on core_clk into u_cpu/u_gpu). Reset style synchronous, matching the APB peripheral ring rather than introducing the project's first reset synchronizer -- reasoning in the file header. Verification: soc_all 120/120, test_pmu 10/10 with per-cycle ordering assertions both directions. One pre-existing test fixed: test_decerr_unmapped hardcoded BAD_HIGH=0x2000_8000, now legitimately mapped -> bumped to 0x2000_9000 (stale constant, not an RTL defect).
close_reason: Evaluation done — docs/POWER_DOMAIN_EVALUATION.md delivered. Implementation re-homed to GitHub epic #98 Behavioral PMU power-mode sequencer (children #99 pmu.sv, #100 soc_top wiring, #101 cocotb test_pmu.py). Bead scope (evaluate) is complete.

The CPU macro views were regenerated during GH #96 and all three stale artifacts are now current: (1) LEF pnr/asap7/soc/macro/rv32i_cpu_top.lef has 403 PINs including axi_rlast_i and axi_wlast_o; (2) Liberty rv32i_cpu_top__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib carries pin(axi_rlast_i), pin(axi_wlast_o) and bus(axi_awlen_o); (3) the block SDC pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc now constrains the burst ports -- set_input_delay 150/10 on axi_rlast_i (lines 57-61), set_output_delay 150/-15 on axi_awlen_o[*] and the other AW/AR burst outputs (lines 96-100), and axi_rlast_i added to the R-channel hold false-path list (lines 259-264), which closes the 16 hold violations at -31.30 ps that the constraint-side twin comment predicted would appear the moment the port got an input delay. comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
CONSTRAINT-SIDE TWIN OF THIS BEAD (found 2026-08-06 while evaluating 40%/10% IO budgets for GH #96): pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc has ZERO references to the AXI4 burst-era ports. Measured: axi_rlast_i, axi_awlen_o, axi_wlast_o, axi_arlen_o, axi_awsize_o, axi_arsize_o all appear 0 times in that SDC. So it is not only the LEF abstract and Liberty that predate the M2 burst upgrade -- the block SDC does too. Three stale artifacts, one root cause.

Concrete consequence, measured on the signed-off CPU netlist (RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12): axi_rlast_i is entirely unconstrained, so it gets NO timing check at all today. Lines 230-231 of that SDC explicitly hold-false-path the other AXI inputs (axi_rvalid_i/rdata/rresp and axi_awready_i/wready/bvalid/bresp) but axi_rlast_i is missing from those lists because it did not exist when they were written. The moment any input delay is applied to it, 16 hold violations appear at -31.30 ps, ALL 16 starting at axi_rlast_i (verified by startpoint attribution). They are invisible today only because the port is unconstrained.

Fix alongside the LEF/LIB regeneration: add the burst ports to the block SDC -- input delay on axi_rlast_i plus adding it to the existing hold false-path list at line 230, and output delays on axi_awlen_o/wlast_o/arlen_o/awsize_o/arsize_o.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
BLOCK SDC HALF FIXED 2026-08-07 (LEF/Liberty regeneration still outstanding). Added to pnr/asap7/cpu/constraints/asap7.sdc: set_input_delay/set_output_delay for axi_rlast_i, axi_awlen_o[*], axi_awsize_o[*], axi_wlast_o, axi_arlen_o[*], axi_arsize_o[*], matching the neighbouring AXI ports (in -max 150/-min 10, out -max 150/-min -15); widths taken from rtl/soc/axi_pkg.sv (AXI_LEN_WIDTH=8, AXI_SIZE_WIDTH=3). axi_rlast_i added to the section-13 hold false-path list alongside its R-channel siblings.

Validated on /nobackup/asap7_runs/RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12 with the flow's own ASAP7 layer-RC injection + GRT-estimated parasitics. Harness proven first by reproducing the run's recorded numbers EXACTLY from its frozen historical SDC: setup WS 24.011015 ps, hold WS 28.141697 ps, 0 violators. After the edit: setup +33.36 ps, hold +37.18 ps, 0 violators -- unchanged vs the same netlist under the repo's current pre-edit SDC, i.e. NO new violations introduced.

BASELINE CORRECTION worth recording: the repo's CURRENT SDC gives +33.36/+37.18 on that netlist, not the +24.011/+28.142 quoted from the run's frozen SDC. The gap is later relaxations (Run 30 AXI hold false-paths, Run 37 ICG fix) that postdate the frozen signoff SDC. Quote the two numbers with their SDC, never interchangeably.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED: isolating the hold exemption (setup constraint added, hold false-path withheld) drops hold WS to +28.62 ps and report_checks shows axi_rlast_i becoming the design's worst hold path, 3 of the top-10 hold paths originating there. That is the same effect as the earlier -31.30 ps / 16-violation measurement, which used a 78 ps min input delay (the 40%/10% experiment) rather than the 10 ps neighbour value -- the two results agree once the different input delay is accounted for, they do not conflict.

STILL OPEN on this bead: the CPU macro LEF and Liberty abstracts still lack the burst pins. That needs a CPU block P&R re-run + macro-view regeneration, which is also what bead cyb requires.

title: CPU CSR read-mux retiming: restore 1418 MHz after M7 perf counters
description: M7 perf-counter CSRs (mcycle/minstret 64b, mhpmcounter3-5, mcountinhibit) widened the CSR read decode/rdata mux in rv32i_csr_file.sv, regressing ASAP7 CPU setup timing from Run 43 (1418 MHz, WNS +5.97 ps) to WNS -56.16 ps / TNS -173.4 ps at 705 ps (~1313 MHz) in run RUN_2026-06-02_17-49-55. Critical path = wide OR4/OR5/NOR5/NAND5 reduction tree, Path Group PIPELINE, in the CSR address-match -> rdata mux (NOT the 64-bit adder). Hold/DRC/antenna clean. Fix: retime/restructure CSR read decode (balanced one-hot mux tree, pre-decoded csr_addr select, and/or register rdata if pipeline-safe) to restore WNS>=0 at 705 ps. Must preserve test_perf_counters 7/7 + full CPU regression + CSR functional semantics. Execute via rtl-design-orchestrator for RTL; verification-orchestrator for re-verify; physical-design-orchestrator for confirming resynth. Blocks M11.
notes: Attempt 1 (read-mux 2-level restructure, commit 9d8f64a) verified 192/192 but timing-INEFFECTIVE: ASAP7 re-run RUN_2026-06-02_18-52-22 gave WNS -89.4ps/TNS -7646ps/259 endpoints (worse than pre-fix -56/-173). Diagnosis: worst-path depth unchanged (56->58 gates), violations dominated by 2 high-fanout startpoint regs (_53435_ 468 paths, _57540_ 350 paths) = counter/control cone, NOT read mux. Real limiter likely 64b mcycle/minstret increment adders + mcountinhibit/csr_write high-fanout write-wins mux across ~224 counter flops. PD-orchestrator producing concrete fix spec. SoC clock GPU-governed ~571MHz, so reduced standalone fmax is an acceptable fallback.
close_reason: Resolved by relaxing CPU ASAP7 clock to 780 ps. Flat-case M7 RTL (read-mux restructure reverted as ineffective) re-signs-off clean at run RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12: setup WNS +24.01ps/TNS 0, hold +28.14ps/0, slew/cap/antenna 0, 24.38mW, 4058um2 stdcell, achievable ~1323MHz. 1418MHz does not hold with M7 (limiter=836-fanout counter-write-enable cone, not read mux); moot for SoC (GPU-governed ~571MHz, >2x margin). config.json+asap7.sdc at 780ps. Counter-enable RTL restructure left as future option. Docs updated.

title: Re-run CPU synthesis + STA after M7 perf-counter RTL

This invalidates the Phase 2+3 ASAP7 CPU timing sign-off (Run 43, 1418 MHz / 27.27 mW / 3844 um2). Re-run synthesis + STA on ASAP7 (make librelane-asap7) to confirm WNS>=0 / TNS=0 hold; 64-bit increment adder is the likely new critical path. Watch mcycle carry chain + CSR rdata mux. Execute via physical-design-orchestrator. Deps: M7 (done, PR #62). Roll result into M11 SoC PD.

title: GH #119 egt follow-up: comb candidate synth drops rs2_i to 1 bit/lane after SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES fix
description: Physical-design orchestrator investigation (2026-09-15) of the sdc_longclk vector_alu HLS combinational candidate's anomalous ASAP7 OpenROAD.STAPrePNR result (1587 instances / 138.7 um^2 / 0.085 mW / WS +449 ps for pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/) found and fixed one real bug (yosys SHARE pass incorrectly deleting 'never active' per-lane $shl cells -- fixed via SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES:false, mirroring pnr/asap7/gpu/config.json's established fix for the same 8-lane vector_alu SAT-sharing hazard) but the fix made NO measurable difference to the final metrics (byte-identical before/after), proving a second, deeper, still-open bug: the final synthesized netlist (05-yosys-synthesis/vector_alu_hls.nl.v in RUN_2026-09-15_14-25-30) uses only 8 total bits of the 256-bit rs2_i port (bit 0 of each lane; bits [31:1] of every lane's second ALU operand are read by nothing), has only 22 XOR/XNOR-family cells total (structurally too few for even one correct 32-bit adder), and ALUMACC converts only 1 of 8 $mul cells (verified: a standalone yosys -sv + opt -full pass on the bare candidate module reproduces all 8 real 32x32 $mul cells at the RTLIL level, so they exist pre-synthesis and are lost somewhere in the real LibreLane/Synlig flow before final techmap -- no $mul/$macc/$alu-for-multiply template is invoked in the final techmap log at all). Bambu's own pre-synthesis area ESTIMATE for this candidate (11067363 units) is 8.5x the registered FSM baseline's own estimate (1298853), i.e. Bambu expects the unrolled combinational form to be LARGER, contradicting the 30-50x SMALLER final mapped netlist. Working hypothesis, NOT verified: three read_verilog frontend warnings in the candidate's generic Bambu shifter/comparator FU templates (Range [0:-1] select out of bounds on signal 'in2': Setting 1 LSB bits to undef, from an unparameterized-module-body BITSIZE_in2 vs computed-bitsize mismatch) inject spurious X-constants that cascade unchecked through this register-free, fully-combinational netlist during opt/OPT_MUXTREE (no clock-edge boundary contains the damage the way it does in the rtl/hls FSM arms). Needs: formal LEC (yosys equiv_make/equiv_induct with functional liberty models) or gate-level cosim between the pre-synthesis candidate .v (already verified 14/14 against reference) and the post-synthesis netlist to confirm/refute the X-propagation hypothesis, then a targeted fix (netlist pre-processing to neutralize the malformed generate-if constructs, or a Synlig/yosys-native-frontend A/B, or USE_SYNLIG:false with a comb-specific shim rewritten to avoid 'import ... ::*;' in the module header). Full writeup: docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md section 'GH #119 egt follow-up -- the combinational-candidate PPA attempt is INVALID (2026-09-15)'. DO NOT quote pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/ PPA numbers as valid until this is resolved.
notes:
2026-09-15 RESOLVED. Root cause: Synlig/UHDM frontend (USE_SYNLIG:true, LibreLane's default),
NOT LibreLane's opt passes. Two hypotheses tested and disproved first: (1) opt_expr -undriven
gated by SYNTH_TIE_UNDEFINED (default "low") -- setting it null reproduced the byte-identical
broken 1587-instance netlist; the offending OPT_MUXTREE call is inside librelane_synth()'s very
first librelane_opt(d, nodffe=True, nosdff=True) call, which never receives undriven= regardless
of config (confirmed by reading librelane/scripts/pyosys/synthesize.py). (2) SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES
alone (already a real, documented hazard for this design shape) -- real but not dominant, re-run
after that fix alone reproduced byte-identical broken metrics.

PROOF: SAT miter (yosys 0.46, real ASAP7 functional cell models via read_liberty -ignore_miss_func
on the same libs LibreLane loads) between the pristine RTL candidate and the real broken netlist
(RUN_2026-09-15_14-25-30), constrained to the valid handshake window (rst_n=1, start_i=1 fixed):
SAT (not equivalent). Counterexample: opcode_i=VMUL, active_mask_i=8'b00000001 (lane0 only active),
rs1_i/rs2_i nonzero only in INACTIVE lanes 2/7. RTL gives result_o=0 (correct, matches
test_partial_mask spec); broken netlist gives result_o[lane2]=rs1_i[lane2] (0x40000000) leaked
through unmasked. done_o/branch_taken_o match on both sides -- corruption isolated to inactive-lane
result_o masking via the ui_cond_expr_FU select mux (vector_alu_synth.v:330-347), whose $ternary$
cells lose 271 mux ports to OPT_MUXTREE in the broken run (only 10, legitimately dead, once fixed).

FIX: pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/config.json -- USE_SYNLIG:false, VERILOG_FILES points at an
sv2v-preprocessed shim (gpu_pkg.sv + hls/gpu/vector_alu/shim/vector_alu_hls.sv run through sv2v,
the project's existing Synlig fallback) instead of the raw .sv + USE_SYNLIG:true. Made
reproducible via new pnr/Makefile target egt-valu-hls-comb-sv2v (auto-run by
librelane-asap7-valu-hls-comb). Re-run (RUN_2026-09-15_15-06-29): 47791 instances / 4139.77 um^2 /
14.060 mW, only 10 (legit) mux ports removed vs 271.

FIX VERIFICATION: full-width SAT re-proof (fixed netlist vs RTL) did not converge in 3G/~10min
(238K cells/1.1M vars post-flatten -- 32x32 multiplier equivalence is SAT-hard at full width). Full
14-vector Verilator/cocotb regression also blocked: flatten exploded the 47791-cell netlist to
~238K primitive gates pre-write_verilog, Verilator build did not finish in 50+ min wall-clock
(egt-ppa-gcd-18, killed). Verified instead via direct eval (yosys, real ASAP7 functional models,
no SAT) on 5 discriminating vectors: the original counterexample plus VADD/VSLL/VAND with garbage
in inactive lanes and VMUL with all 8 lanes active + distinct operands -- ALL 5 match the RTL
candidate exactly, byte-for-byte, on done_o/result_o/branch_taken_o.

SCOPE NOT COVERED (tracked on new bead claude_verilog_test-b0t, filed by coordinator): (1) baseline
FSM arm (valu_hls, USE_SYNLIG:true) -- A/B synthesis (temp config /nobackup/pnr_ab_valu_hls/,
tracked config untouched) shows a ~25-40% instance/area/power gap under USE_SYNLIG:false too
(89224/9188.40um^2/52.7mW vs tracked 71480/7254.37um^2/37.667mW), present proportionally from the
first synthesis-log checkpoint -- but this was NOT functionally resolved (yosys sim -set is
non-functional in this yosys 0.46 build despite being documented; Verilator cosim OOMs at 3G even
without flatten). Verdict: INCONCLUSIVE, do not assume the baseline is also fixed by the same
change. (2) CPU/GPU macros (USE_SYNLIG:true) -- confirmed structurally NOT exposed to this specific
construct (grep -rl "ui_cond_expr_FU|_bambu_artificial_|BAMBU/PANDA" rtl/ = 0 matches; hand-RTL
masks via a plain if(active_mask_i[lane]) generate construct, not Bambu's per-instance-parameterized
generic FU template pattern) -- but not functionally re-verified per explicit instruction not to
re-run those flows.

Doc updated: docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md "GH #119 gcd follow-up" section (root cause, proof,
fix, corrected comb metrics + worst-arc decomposition, baseline verdict, CPU/GPU exposure verdict).
Closing this bead -- the comb candidate corruption it was filed for is root-caused, fixed, and
verified. Follow-up work (baseline arm, CPU/GPU audit) continues on claude_verilog_test-b0t.

title: GH #119: regenerated Bambu .v normalized digests no longer match hls/PROVENANCE.json pins
description: After the 2026-09-15 /nobackup wipe (bead alq) the HLS outputs were regenerated with the unchanged flake-pinned Bambu (same /nix/store/rih6b619 bambu-2024.10 as the Sep 6-7 pin-era logs) and unchanged C/tb inputs (last touched d89b3c9, before the pins). verilog_sha256_normalized: memory_coalescer d1370dbf... (pin 376e64ea...), rv32i_hazard_unit d341099b... (pin 72dde9f0...), vector_alu 8605c834... (no pin). Regeneration is deterministic here: a second memory_coalescer run into a separate HLS_OUT gave the identical normalized digest. Bambu-reported metrics are identical to the pin-era logs for all three (coalescer 820 FF/352744 area/119 cycles; hazard 50/1791535/203; vector_alu 6014/1298853/244), and strip_translate_off removes the same 243 bytes from the coalescer as the surviving Sep-7 Surelog copy implies. The old raw .v files are gone; the only surviving copies (librelane/slpp_all/lib/work, Sep 7 19:29-19:33) are Surelog-preprocessed (comments blanked, ifdefs expanded) so they cannot be byte-compared. Cause of the digest drift unknown. Decide whether to re-pin the normalized digests or investigate further; do not trust a PPA comparison against the Stage-2 table until resolved.
notes:
RESOLVED. Cause: Bambu stamps a THIRD volatile thing beyond the two summarize.py already
stripped (date, full command line) -- every auto-generated net/instance name carries a
decimal ID-pair from Bambu's own internal node-numbering counter, e.g.
`selector_IN_UNBOUNDED_memory_coalescer_428528_428695`. Evidence: diffed the 2026-09-15
regeneration against the 2026-09-07 Surelog-preprocessed survivors in
~/Downloads/Github/librelane/slpp_all/lib/work/ (comment-stripped, ifdefs resolved the
same way on both sides). The ID-pair's first number was IDENTICAL across two unrelated
designs (memory_coalescer, rv32i_hazard_unit): 428532 in both 2026-09-07 survivors,
428528 in both 2026-09-15 regenerations -- a constant -4 shift independent of the C
source, so it tracks Bambu's own startup/env state, not our inputs or flags. Grepped the
whole .v for any other absolute-path/timestamp/hostname leak beyond the two known header
lines: none found.

Proven non-semantic for memory_coalescer: with the ID-pair blanked, a full line-level
diff between the 2026-09-07 survivor and the 2026-09-15 regeneration is EMPTY except one
artifact of my own comparison script (unexpanded `CLOG2` macro -- Surelog expands it, my
ad hoc script didn't; confirmed not a Bambu difference). For rv32i_hazard_unit a second,
additional effect exists: emission order of functionally-interchangeable resource-shared
FU instances (truth_not_expr_FU/UUdata_converter_FU pools) also permutes across
environments -- same instance count/type distribution, different order, not capturable
by regex. Bambu's own reported flip-flops/area/cycles and cosim PASS were byte-identical
to the pin era for all three blocks throughout (already true before this investigation
started, per the bead description) -- Stage 2/3 PPA tables were never invalidated by a
logic change, only the digest tracking needed repair.

Both effects are stable WITHIN one environment/session: reconfirmed 2026-09-15 with
THREE separate `nix develop .#hls --command make -C hls <target>` invocations under
`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=3G -p MemorySwapMax=0` (wke-1/2/3), each design
regenerated twice into independent HLS_OUT dirs, all reproducing the same post-fix
normalized digest -- including a final foreground confirmation run (wke-3, this session)
using the real wrap-bambu.sh/summarize.py pipeline, which reproduced the newly-pinned
memory_coalescer digest exactly.

Fix: tools/eda/summarize.py now also blanks `_<5+ digits>_<5+ digits>` pairs before
hashing (checked exhaustively: the only place a bare run of 5+ decimal digits appears in
the emitted .v outside a 'b/'h literal). Two new regression tests in
tb/tests/test_eda_summarize.py (35/35 pass): ID-counter-only diff normalizes equal; a
real content change still normalizes different, so the fix cannot mask a genuine logic
change.

Resolution: the r8r-era memory_coalescer and rv32i_hazard_unit pins are RETIRED (not
trusted) -- same precedent r8r itself used for an unreproducible Stage-1 pin -- and all
three blocks re-pinned at their 2026-09-15 post-fix normalized digests, including a
first-ever pin for vector_alu (previously unpinned). New digests:
  memory_coalescer  9def6afd4ecb0052687d6a4225c2d4120700500e3ab04b31799c3d8ad9aea8be
  rv32i_hazard_unit 4299bf6112a338c575f451f4752eaff0f1faf406786e95d6c76e2deac3745b3f
  vector_alu        052227f9d9ae4a5f37be3a7125eb4646df978b30926faa4cbb209880e153d5d4
Full writeup in hls/PROVENANCE.json's digest_note; per-block notes in
hls/gpu/memory_coalescer/NOTES.md, hls/cpu/rv32i_hazard_unit/NOTES.md,
hls/gpu/vector_alu/NOTES.md. Stage-2/3 PPA table comparisons do NOT need
re-validation -- Bambu's metrics never changed, only the provenance digest.
close_reason: Resolved: cause identified (Bambu internal net/instance ID-counter is environment-sensitive, not source-sensitive), proven non-semantic, normalizer fixed, all three digests re-pinned. See notes.
