title: async_axi_fifo permanently stalls when the CPU domain is SLOWER than the fabric (reversed clock ratio)
description:
Found 2026-09-09 while fixing bead 5ej. NOT investigated, NOT root-caused, no fix attempted --
filed so it is not lost.

SYMPTOM: sweeping test_async_axi_fifo across clock ratios turned up an apparent PERMANENT STALL
when the ratio is reversed -- i.e. the CPU-side (s_clk) domain running SLOWER than the fabric
side. All the ratios in the realistic direction pass cleanly (10/10, 4/9, 4/20 with multiple
seeds -> 14 pass observations, 0 failures); only the reversed direction stalls.

WHY IT IS P3 AND NOT BLOCKING: this SoC's real relationship is CPU FASTER than fabric --
CPU domain ~1282 MHz (780 ps) against the GPU/bus/periph fabric at 571 MHz (1750 ps), per
GH #90/#96 and pnr/constraints/phase5_soc_multiclock.sdc. The reversed direction is
physically unrealistic for the current design, so nothing shipped is exposed to it today.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: async_axi_fifo is written and documented as a GENERAL dual-clock AXI4
bridge (rtl/soc/async_axi_fifo.sv, Cummings style-1 gray-code pointers, reusable primitives in
rtl/soc/cdc/). A general CDC bridge that deadlocks in one direction of the ratio space is a
latent trap for any future reuse -- e.g. a slow always-on domain talking to a fast fabric, or a
future Phase 6+ block clocked below the fabric. It is also a plausible sign of an asymmetry in
the design that could matter at extreme-but-realistic ratios in the current direction.

TO INVESTIGATE:
 1. Reproduce deliberately: drive s_clk slower than m_clk (e.g. 20 ns / 4 ns) and confirm the
    stall is permanent rather than a very long latency or a testbench timeout artifact. Rule
    the testbench out first -- bead 5ej was exactly that kind of false positive.
 2. If real, determine which channel wedges (AW/W/B/AR/R) and whether it is a full/empty flag
    computed in the wrong domain, a gray-pointer crossing that needs more settling at that
    ratio, or the reset cross-coupling.
 3. Note the class of bug this design has already produced twice, both found only at divergent
    ratios and both with the same signature -- A RESET VALUE THAT ADVERTISES AVAILABILITY
    (commits 4398c2e and 7a9f9d4, see CLAUDE.md GH #93). Check for a third instance of that
    pattern before looking anywhere else.

RELATED: 5ej (where this was found), GH #90/#91/#93 (the multi-clock CDC epic).
close_reason:
Closed 2026-09-09 as NOT A DUT DEFECT. The reversed-ratio "permanent stall" is a TESTBENCH
artifact -- and, pointedly, an artifact of the bead-5ej fix's own completion gate.

ROOT CAUSE: a test that releases backpressure (`dut.s_bready.value = 1`) from a point
ASYNCHRONOUS to the counting domain's clock -- typically just after an edge of the OTHER
domain's clock -- can land nanoseconds before the next s_clk edge while s_bvalid is already
high. cocotb's RisingEdge+ReadOnly sampling of that first post-release edge then sits one edge
out of phase with what cdc_gray_fifo's own always_ff used for rd_en at that same edge. The
software counter (_count_handshakes_bg) permanently UNDERCOUNTS by exactly one real,
already-delivered completion. The FIFO then drains legitimately with no further supply, so a
`count == expected` gate can never be satisfied. A software stall, not a deadlock.

WHY ONLY THE REVERSED DIRECTION -- this is the part that settles it: at the REALISTIC direction
(s_clk fast, m_clk slow) the same unsynchronised-release methodology does NOT stall, because
the fast s_clk's rapid follow-up edges recover the single miscount before the target is
exhausted. It becomes a hard stall only when the counting domain's clock is SLOW and the
workload has zero slack (exact saturation). So the direction-dependence is a property of the
TEST, not of the RTL's direction handling. No RTL asymmetry is implicated.

FOUR INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS:
 1. Internal FIFO pointer trace (u_b_fifo.wr_bin_q / rd_bin_q against a confirmed pre-release
    baseline of 0): exactly 9 writes = 9 reads for a 9-write saturation workload. Fully
    self-consistent, no overflow.
 2. Controlled fix: synchronising the release write to a clean s_clk RisingEdge makes the
    identical 9/4 workload pass immediately and exactly (b=9/9, r=13/13, ~180 ns after release).
 3. Direction check as above.
 4. Reproduced at two reversed ratios (9/4 and 20/4 ns), identical signature both times.

EXPLICITLY CHECKED AND ABSENT: the "reset value that advertises availability" signature behind
this design's two prior real CDC bugs (4398c2e, 7a9f9d4). Not present here.

WHY THE COMMITTED SUITE NEVER SAW IT: no shipped test combines saturation with a reversed
ratio. The reversed-ratio tests (test_clock_ratio_slow_to_fast, test_burst_integrity,
test_no_valid_withdrawal_stress) all use light round-trip workloads, and the saturation test
(test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full) runs at 10/10. Latent, not active. Suite reconfirmed 26/26.

HARDENING APPLIED (this is the durable part): the limitation is now documented in
_count_handshakes_bg's own docstring in tb/cocotb/soc/test_async_axi_fifo.py, including the
rule -- if a test releases backpressure and then waits on this counter, synchronise the release
to a RisingEdge of the counting clock FIRST. Documented rather than restructured because the
committed suite does not exercise the path and a restructure would risk the 26/26 baseline for
no active benefit.

NOTE FOR REUSE: async_axi_fifo remains a general dual-clock bridge and this finding does NOT
show a direction-dependent RTL weakness. The earlier concern on this bead -- that a slow
always-on domain or a sub-fabric-clocked Phase 6+ block would hit a bridge deadlock -- is not
supported. Any future reversed-ratio test should still synchronise its release writes.

title: ASAP7 SRAM macro LEF obstructs its own pin layer (M4 OBS covers all 77 M4 pins)
description:
Found 2026-09-08 during bead ocm's end-to-end routing bring-up. INDEPENDENT of the OpenROAD
build defect -- this would have blocked ASAP7 detailed routing under ANY OpenROAD version.

THE DEFECT: pnr/asap7/sram_1rw_256x32_asap7.lef declares all 77 signal pins on M4 --
  PIN dout0[0] ... LAYER M4 ; RECT 0.000 0.048 0.024 0.072 ;
i.e. 24 x 24 nm rects along x=0.000, the macro's left edge -- and then its OBS block
obstructs M4 across the ENTIRE 8.360 x 42.000 um footprint:
  OBS
    LAYER M1 ; RECT 0 0 8.360 42.000 ;
    LAYER M2 ; RECT 0 0 8.360 42.000 ;
    LAYER M3 ; RECT 0 0 8.360 42.000 ;
    LAYER M4 ; RECT 0 0 8.360 42.000 ;   <-- covers every pin on the macro
The abstract blocks the only layer its own pins live on. Pin layer distribution confirms it:
78 pin shapes on M4, one each on M1/M2/M3.

HOW IT SURFACED: first ASAP7 run in this project's history to reach detailed routing
(RUN_2026-09-08_22-12-30, LibreLane 3.0.14 + OpenROAD dcf36133). Pin access succeeded --
0 DRT-0073, 0 DRT-0074 -- track assignment succeeded, 33905 nets routed, and then routing
failed with exactly 16 [ERROR DRT-0255] "Maze Route cannot find path" errors. The failing
nets are precisely the SRAM macro pins:
  u_core.u_dcache.data_din0[71], data_din0[81]
  u_core.u_dcache.data_dout0[70], [84], [91]
  u_core.u_dcache.gen_data_sram[1].data_gclk
  u_core.u_icache.data_dout0[67], [77], [89]
  + 7 unnamed nets (net4824, net6161, net7166, net7176, net7187, net7436, net7465)

WHY IT WAS NEVER SEEN: every prior ASAP7 run aborted at pin access (bead ocm / xy6) before
track assignment, so no run ever attempted to reach these pins. The macro has been wrong
since it was created (file dated 2026-05-20) and every ASAP7 PPA number in this project was
produced without ever routing to it.

RULED OUT as the cause before finding this: GRT_ALLOW_CONGESTION (set false, identical 16
failures, same nets); PL_MACRO_HALO removal (defaults "0 0" and drives the AUTOMATIC macro
placer, which this design does not use -- it has a fixed macro_placement.cfg).

FIX APPLIED: dropped LAYER M4 from the OBS block; M1-M3 remain obstructed. Documented inline
in the LEF. This is a hand-written stub abstract, NOT memory-compiler output, so there is no
real internal M4 routing for a router to collide with. IF THIS MACRO IS EVER REPLACED BY A
REAL COMPILED SRAM, its true M4 blockages must be re-derived from the actual layout rather
than copied from this stub -- allowing free M4 routing over a real SRAM array would be wrong.

STILL TO VERIFY: that the fix actually clears the 16 DRT-0255 errors (run in progress).
Also unassessed: the 24 nm pin width against the ASAP7 M4 WIDTHTABLE. 24 nm is the M4 base
width so it is probably legal, but the top-level IO pins needed FP_IO_HTHICKNESS_MULT=8
(192 nm) for their own reasons -- if DRT-0255 persists at these pins, pin width is the next
thing to check.

RELATED: claude_verilog_test-ocm (OpenROAD build defect, the reason this was never exposed),
claude_verilog_test-xy6 (zero-wire symptom + fail-loud gate).
notes:
2026-09-09 CORRECTION -- THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Filed at P1 claiming the
M4 OBS covering the M4 pins was the cause of the 16 DRT-0255 failures. It is not. Demoted to
P3 and rescoped: the M4-OBS-over-M4-pins condition is REAL and worth recording as a latent
oddity in the abstract, but it is NOT what blocks routing.

DISPROVED BY DIRECT EXPERIMENT: removing LAYER M4 from the OBS block made routing WORSE, not
better -- DRT-0255 went 16 -> 79, and the failures spread from one worker column to five
(run RUN_2026-09-08_23-59-44). The LEF edit has been REVERTED; the file is back to its
committed state. Retrospectively obvious: pin access had ALREADY succeeded with the OBS in
place (0 DRT-0073, 0 DRT-0074 in RUN_2026-09-08_22-12-30), so the obstruction was never
blocking access -- it was keeping M4 clear of over-macro routing, and dropping it just added
congestion.

ALSO DISPROVED (do not re-try):
 * 24 nm M4 pin width being illegal -- it is LEGAL. ASAP7's M4 LEF58_WIDTHTABLE is
   "0.024 0.12 0.216 0.312 0.408", so 0.024 is an explicit table entry, and M4's own
   WIDTH is 0.024.
 * GRT_ALLOW_CONGESTION=false -- identical 16 failures on identical nets.
 * Routing-channel congestion -- widening the inter-macro channel 3x (2.00 um -> 6.00 um,
   stride 10.36 -> 14.36) gave EXACTLY 16 failures again (RUN_2026-09-09_01-02-44).
   Same count, same structural mix (2x data_din0, 3x dcache data_dout0, 1x data_gclk,
   3x icache data_dout0, 7 unnamed), only the bit indices moved. A fixed count whose
   identity tracks placement is not a congestion signature.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY POINTS AT (now tracked under bead ocm, not here): every failure in
a given run falls in ONE DRT worker routeBox column, and the reported source access points sit
exactly on that worker's boundary. Attempt 7: pin
gen_data_sram[3].u_data_sram/dout0[4] access point at x=62790 DBU, routeBox
(60060 5460)(62790 8190) -- the ap is ON the worker's right edge. The worker grid is 2730 DBU
(2.73 um) and that macro's left edge (62440) sat only 350 DBU from the boundary. Attempt 4
showed the same shape at a different column (x=24570 box, macro edge 25720). Currently under
test: shifting every macro +1.365 um (half a worker) to move pin columns to mid-worker.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING FROM THE ORIGINAL REPORT: the abstract does declare all 77
signal pins on M4 while obstructing M4 across its whole footprint, all pins sit on the single
left edge as 24x24 nm squares, and M1-M4 are blocked so only M5-M7 may cross the macro. That
is a genuinely awkward abstract for a router and is worth revisiting if this stub is ever
replaced by a real compiled SRAM -- but it is a latent characteristic, not the active defect.

LESSON: I asserted a root cause from a static file inspection before testing it, and filed it
P1. The A/B test is what settled it. Do not promote a geometry theory to root cause without
the negative control.
2026-09-15 RESOLUTION -- confirmed latent, not defective. Closing.

Tracked-LEF check: pnr/asap7/sram_1rw_256x32_asap7.lef is unmodified since its introduction
(git log: only the two original commits, `git status` clean, OBS block still lists M1/M2/M3/M4
across the full 8.360x42.000 footprint). The "drop M4 from OBS" experiment mentioned in this
bead's own notes was reverted and never committed -- confirmed directly, not just by reading
the prior note.

pin_access test on a real post-placement ASAP7 CPU block ODB with the SRAM macros, under
OpenROAD 26Q2 (the same 26Q2 binary bead ocm's fix relies on for pin access generally): used
the bpp validation's RUN_2026-09-15_21-27-12 CPU run (rv32i_cpu_top, 10 SRAM macro instances,
tracked LEF as-is), specifically the 34-openroad-detailedplacement/rv32i_cpu_top.odb checkpoint
(post-DetailedPlacement, pre-CTS -- macros are placed and fixed at this point same as at
detailed-routing time). Standalone script: `openroad -db <odb> -exit` running
`set_routing_layers -signal M2-M7` then `pin_access -min_access_points 1` (no full detailed
routing attempted).

RESULT: all ~750 SRAM macro pin terms (10 instances x ~75 signal pins) got DRT-0418/DRT-0419
WARNINGS ("no pins on routing grid" / "no routing tracks pass through the center of Term") --
expected given the pins are all on the macro's single left edge as 24x24nm squares, already
documented as an awkward-but-legal abstract in this bead's notes -- but ZERO of them appear
among the 56 actual DRT-0085 ("Valid access pattern combination not found") ERRORS. Checked by
extracting every DRT-0085 failure's target identifier (56 total, `awk` capture of the line
following each ERROR) and grepping for "sram": no matches. All 56 real failures are anonymous
synthesis net names (_NNNNN_ style) and placement-tool identifiers (place9779 etc.) -- ordinary
standard-cell nets, unrelated to the SRAM macro LEF.

CONCLUSION: the M4-OBS-over-M4-pins condition in the tracked LEF is confirmed LATENT, not
defective, consistent with this bead's 2026-09-09 correction (which reached the same conclusion
by a different route -- the A/B "drop M4" experiment). Pin access succeeds (with cosmetic
warnings) on the LEF as tracked; the 56 real access failures on this checkpoint are a separate,
unexamined issue (likely ordinary pre-CTS placement congestion) outside this bead's scope.
Keeping the inline LEF note about re-deriving M4 blockages if a real compiled SRAM ever replaces
this stub, per this bead's original resolution guidance. No LEF change made.
close_reason: Confirmed latent via pin_access on a real post-placement CPU ODB under OpenROAD 26Q2: all SRAM macro pins get access (warnings only, 0 DRT-0085 failures attributable to SRAM); tracked LEF unmodified, no fix needed.

title: Pre-existing settle-timing race in test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full gives false 'missing write' failures
description:
Found 2026-09-07 while working bead rvs (CDC settling-delay injector). Incidental to that
work, but it is a real testbench defect and outlives it.

WHAT HAPPENED: a data-integrity check was added to
tb/cocotb/soc/test_async_axi_fifo.py's test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full to try to catch
injector-induced overflow writes. It reported "missing writes" -- and then reported the SAME
missing writes against the FULLY CLEAN, UNMUTATED RTL with the injector off. So the check was
measuring a testbench settle-timing race, not a design fault.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is a false-positive generator sitting in a suite that is otherwise used
as a trusted green baseline (26/26). Any future attempt to add per-beat data or count
verification to this test will hit the same race and will look like an RTL bug. Somebody will
eventually spend real time chasing it -- this session nearly did, and only caught it because
the clean-RTL control was run.

MITIGATION USED (and then reverted with the rest of the rvs mutant work -- NOTHING IS IN THE
TREE): inserting a settle delay before sampling made the clean-RTL check pass, after which
OFF and ON both gave 26/26. So the race is in when the check samples relative to the DUT
settling, not in the DUT.

WHY IT IS NOT VISIBLE TODAY: the shipped 26 tests do no exact per-beat data/count verification
on the channel and cycle where this lands, so nothing currently samples in the racy window.
The bug is latent, not active -- the suite's green status is not in question.

TO FIX: add the settle delay (or an explicit handshake-based sample point) to
test_no_deadlock_all_fifos_full permanently, so the racy sampling window is closed before
anyone adds a check that would trip it. Verify by adding a deliberate per-beat data check on
clean RTL and confirming it passes reproducibly across seeds and clock phases -- a single
green run is not enough for a timing race.

RELATED: bead rvs (where this surfaced). Not a blocker for it -- rvs's conclusion is a
structural negative result independent of this race.
close_reason: Fixed in 4890df3. Reproduced on CLEAN unmutated RTL (5/5 identical failures, writes #7-#8 of 9 reading back None at the old drain condition's success point) -- confirmed a testbench defect, not a DUT bug. Fix replaces the one-shot idle-signal snapshot with an explicit handshake-count gate (_count_handshakes_bg samples at ReadOnly each rising edge and counts real VALID&&READY completions), structurally immune to idle gaps rather than a settle delay. Per-beat check kept permanently and proven able to fail (the reproduction is its negative control); failure-direction coverage confirmed for under-delivery (poll >= gate + timeout), over-delivery (== asserts) and wrong data (mem check). 14 pass observations / 0 failures across realistic clock ratios 10/10, 4/9, 4/20 with multiple seeds. Regression at baseline: test_async_axi_fifo 26/26, test_apb_cdc_bridge 23/23, soc_multiclock 4/4, soc_all 183/183.

title: core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks silently disables .git/hooks — code-review-graph pre-commit is dead
description:
Found 2026-09-07 while investigating bead a7c (unrelated to it).

MEASURED:
 * git config core.hooksPath -> /home/neuromorphic/Downloads/Github/claude_verilog_test/.beads/hooks
 * git honours core.hooksPath EXCLUSIVELY: when it is set, .git/hooks/ is not consulted at all.
 * .git/hooks/ still contains one real, non-sample hook: pre-commit (244 B, dated Mei 8),
   installed by code-review-graph. Its body runs `code-review-graph update` and
   `code-review-graph detect-changes --brief`.
 * grep "BEADS INTEGRATION" .git/hooks/* -> no match, confirming beads never wrote there;
   it set hooksPath instead and left the pre-existing hook stranded.

CONSEQUENCE: code-review-graph's incremental graph update has not run on any commit since
beads set core.hooksPath. The graph is only current because something else refreshes it
(the SessionStart hook reports node/edge counts and a build commit). No error is ever
emitted -- the hook file is simply never executed, which is why this went unnoticed.

This is a general trap, not a beads bug: ANY tool that installs into .git/hooks/ on this
repo is inert, and the next one to try will also fail silently.

FIX OPTIONS:
 (a) Chain it: append the code-review-graph pre-commit body into .beads/hooks/pre-commit
     OUTSIDE the "--- BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION ---" markers (beads regenerates only the
     marked block, same convention CLAUDE.md already documents for the rtk warning block).
     Preserves both. Recommended.
 (b) Delete .git/hooks/pre-commit if code-review-graph updates are genuinely not wanted at
     commit time, so nothing looks installed-but-dead.
 (c) Add a check to `make verify-tooling`: fail if any non-sample hook exists in .git/hooks/
     while core.hooksPath points elsewhere. Catches the next occurrence rather than this one.

Prefer (a) + (c). Verify by making a trivial commit and confirming code-review-graph
actually runs.
close_reason: Fixed in a3558c8. code-review-graph's pre-commit body chained into .beads/hooks/pre-commit outside the beads markers (with timeout guards so it can never hang a commit); dead .git/hooks/pre-commit removed; make verify-tooling now fails if any non-sample hook reappears in .git/hooks while core.hooksPath points elsewhere. Guard proven non-vacuous by planting a dummy post-commit hook. Chaining confirmed live: the commit itself triggered code-review-graph (4 files analysed).

title: GH #119 follow-up: can Bambu emit a single-control-step (combinational) datapath at all?
description: Stage 3 (bead gg8) measured rtl/gpu/vector_alu.sv and found Bambu schedules the lane loop into a multi-cycle FSM over a shared functional unit: mean 14.35 cycles/op, 9412 sequential cells, +55.4% area, +163.5% power vs a hand-RTL block with ZERO registers. Two ablations showed this is structural, not an authoring or clock artifact -- relaxing the clock to 1.75 ns gave identical area, and the 'HLS-friendly' ternary-select rewrite gave 3.3x area and was still sequential. Open question: does Bambu have ANY mode (pragma, scheduling option, --clock-period interaction, full unroll + bind directives) that emits 8 parallel combinational slices with no control FSM? If not, that is a hard boundary of the tool worth recording as such. If yes, the Stage 3 verdict should be re-measured against it.
notes:
2026-09-14 sweep (/nobackup/hls/egt_sweep.sh, out /nobackup/hls/out/egt). Bambu 2024.10, baseline flags + variants:
- sdc (--speculative-sdc-scheduling, 0.705 ns): 8375 FF (bambu) / 8595 seq cells (yosys) -> sequential.
- longclk (--clock-period=100, default sched): 64 control steps, 62 states, 6012 FF -> sequential (matches earlier 1.75 ns ablation).
- sdc_longclk (SDC + --clock-period=100): 3 control steps chained into 1 state, 0 registers, yosys generic synth 0 seq cells / 55494 cells, est 401 MHz -> COMBINATIONAL. Positive answer candidate: the lever is SDC scheduling + clock loose enough to chain the whole datapath; neither alone suffices.
- noreg_in (+ --registered-inputs=no): bambu 0 FF, 1 state.
- pipe_ii1 (--pipelining=vector_alu=1 @0.705): bambu error 'Timing of Vertex vector_alu_428532_428768 is not compatible with II=1' (mult FU 1.19 ns > period).
Sweep-script bugs fixed in re-count: yosys absent from the hls devshell (used nix-store yosys 0.62); stat regex assumed name-first but 0.62 prints count-first (initially reported false 0).

2026-09-14 final counts (yosys 0.62 generic synth): sdc 8595 seq/64405; sdc_longclk 0 seq/55494; longclk 5985 seq/54059; noreg_in 0 seq/55494 (identical to sdc_longclk -> --registered-inputs=no has no effect); pipe_ii1 bambu error. Table: /nobackup/hls/out/egt/results.tsv. Combinational netlist = sdc_longclk; cosim vs test_vector_alu HLS arm in progress.

2026-09-14 cosim #1 of sdc_longclk vs test_vector_alu HLS arm: 0/14, all 'TimeoutError: HLS arm: done_o never asserted within 50 cycles'. Harness artifact, not netlist: controller_vector_alu has one state S_0 with done_port=1 combinationally when start_port=1 (zero-latency; the 1-bit state reg is constant S_0->S_0, hence yosys 0 seq cells). VectorAluDriver.settle() drops start_i before sampling done_o. Driver being made latency-agnostic (verification-orchestrator), then rerun on candidate + baseline HLS arm + hand-RTL arm.
2026-09-14 cosim #2 (latency-agnostic driver, untracked confirm copy /nobackup/verif_egt/confirm): sdc_longclk vs test_vector_alu HLS arm 14/14 PASS, 'HLS-arm latency: 0 cycle(s) from start_i to done_o' on every op (baseline gg8 arm: mean 14.35 cycles/op). Bambu 2024.10 CAN emit a functionally correct zero-register, zero-latency vector_alu: --speculative-sdc-scheduling + --clock-period=100. Pending: tracked driver change + baseline HLS arm + hand-RTL arm regressions; then Stage-3 PPA re-measure vs hand RTL per bead.
2026-09-14: independent verification-orchestrator re-check agrees. controller_vector_alu single state S_0, done_port combinational on start_port; ParmMgr_Write output modules are pure assigns. sdc_longclk and noreg_in netlists are byte-identical apart from the header comment. Unmodified tracked suite: 0/14, a harness artifact; the latency-agnostic copy gets 14/14. Tracked driver change is being landed with gates on candidate + baseline HLS arm + hand-RTL arm.
2026-09-14 LANDED 66db8e5: tracked VectorAluDriver.settle() now latency-agnostic. It samples done_o in the ReadOnly phase of the start cycle, then on each edge up to 50. Gates were fresh builds, results in /nobackup/verif_egt/results_{a_candidate_clean,b_baseline,c_handrtl}.xml:
- (a) sdc_longclk candidate: 14/14, 0 cycles on every test.
- (b) baseline HLS arm: 14/14, per-test latency 3-18 cycles (mean ~6.6 over this 14-test mix; not comparable to Stage-3's 14.35 benchmark mean).
- (c) hand-RTL: 14/14.
Question answered YES. Remaining per bead: re-measure the Stage-3 PPA verdict vs hand RTL using sdc_longclk (deferred until the ASAP7 SoC run 6 synthesis frees RAM).
2026-09-15 (PD orchestrator, Stage-2/3 PPA re-measure of the sdc_longclk candidate): Three ASAP7 OpenROAD.STAPrePNR-only runs (pnr/asap7/valu_{rtl,hls,hls_comb}/, driver /nobackup/egt_ppa/run_all.sh) -- rtl and hls reproduce the r8r Stage 2 baseline (rtl: 54634 instances/4655.15 um^2/14.147 mW, exact match; hls: 71480 instances/7254.4 um^2/37.667 mW, <=1.1% drift). The comb arm (pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/, candidate netlist regenerated after the 2026-09-15 /nobackup wipe, sha256 777672bf...) came back invalid: 1587 instances/138.7 um^2/0.085 mW/WS +449 ps -- 30-50x smaller than either baseline for supposedly the same function. Root-caused to TWO bugs: (1) FIXED -- SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES was left enabled in valu_hls_comb/config.json (also valu_rtl/valu_hls, though those weren't visibly affected); yosys's SAT share pass declared 6 per-lane $shl cells "never active" and deleted them, wrong for a fully-parallel zero-register datapath. Fixed by adding SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES:false, mirroring the established GPU config fix for the same 8-lane vector_alu SAT-sharing hazard (project_yosys_share_pass_hang memory). (2) NOT FIXED -- re-running after fix (1) gave byte-identical metrics, proving SHARE wasn't the dominant cause. The final netlist uses only 8 of rs2_i's 256 bits (1 bit/lane), has only 22 XOR-family cells (too few for even one correct 32-bit adder), and only 1 of 8 $mul cells reaches ALUMACC (verified 8 real $mul survive at RTLIL level in a standalone yosys opt -full pass on the bare candidate module, so this is lost during the real LibreLane/Synlig flow, not absent pre-synthesis). Bambu's own pre-synthesis area ESTIMATE for the candidate (11067363 units) is 8.5x the FSM baseline's estimate -- Bambu itself expects combinational to be BIGGER, not 30-50x smaller. Working hypothesis (unverified): spurious X-constants from a malformed generate-if width mismatch in Bambu's generic shifter/comparator FU templates (3 "Range [0:-1] select... Setting 1 LSB bits to undef" warnings at read_verilog time) cascade unchecked through this register-free combinational netlist during opt/OPT_MUXTREE, since no clock-edge boundary contains the damage the way it does in rtl/hls. Comb PPA numbers are NOT valid and must not be quoted. Follow-up tracked as claude_verilog_test-gcd (discovered-from: egt). Full writeup + rtl/hls comparison table (with mandatory worst-arc decomposition per the asap7-to-openroad-staprepnr-comparisons-stopping-before-the memory: rtl worst arc 8.0%/fanout 6, hls worst arc 58.8%/fanout 469) in docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md, new section "GH #119 egt follow-up -- the combinational-candidate PPA attempt is INVALID (2026-09-15)". Bead egt itself stays OPEN pending gcd.
2026-09-15 (gcd resume): Bug 2 (comb candidate PPA corruption) root-caused and fixed -- see bd
show claude_verilog_test-gcd and docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md "GH #119 gcd follow-up" section.
Root cause: Synlig/UHDM frontend (USE_SYNLIG:true), not LibreLane's opt passes (two other
hypotheses -- SYNTH_TIE_UNDEFINED/opt_expr -undriven, and SYNTH_SHARE_RESOURCES alone -- were
tested and disproved). Fix: USE_SYNLIG:false + sv2v-preprocessed shim (pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/config.json,
make -C pnr egt-valu-hls-comb-sv2v). Corrected comb metrics: 47791 instances / 4139.77 um^2 / 14.060 mW --
SMALLER and lower-power than hand-RTL rtl arm (54634/4655.15/14.147), and far smaller/lower-power
than the registered hls arm (71480/7254.37/37.667). Verified via SAT-miter proof of the original
divergence (constrained to rst_n=1/start_i=1) plus direct eval on 5 discriminating vectors matching
the RTL candidate exactly (full SAT re-proof and full cocotb regression were computationally
infeasible under the 3G/session time budget -- documented in the doc). Baseline FSM arm (valu_hls)
status: INCONCLUSIVE -- an A/B synthesis shows a ~25-40% instance/area/power gap under
USE_SYNLIG:false too, but this was NOT functionally resolved (tool walls: yosys sim -set broken,
Verilator cosim OOMs at 3G) -- do not assume it is also fixed by the same change. New bead
claude_verilog_test-b0t tracks the general USE_SYNLIG:true audit; CPU/GPU hand-RTL confirmed
structurally not exposed to the specific corrupted construct (ui_cond_expr_FU, a Bambu-generated
generic FU template pattern absent from rtl/).
2026-09-15 (verification-orchestrator, GLS cross-check per coordinator directive):
COMB-FIXED gate netlist verdict: PASS, 252/252. Method: full Verilator/cocotb
GLS was abandoned mid-session (coordinator call -- Verilator front-end elaboration
of the ~48-90K-instance netlists is workable with -O0 --output-split 200 on a
6G-capped scope, confirmed by getting the comb-fixed arm's front end through to
g++ object compilation, but the g++ build phase alone ran 1h26m without finishing
and was killed by a low-memory guard while a concurrent SoC P&R job (je8-hier-r8 +
je8-grt-r9) was also running -- too slow for this session's remaining time).
Switched to a lighter, still-functional method: yosys 0.62 `eval` (not `sim` --
`sim` in 0.62 has no `-set` option at all, confirmed via `help sim`; the earlier
"sim -set is broken" note undersold it, the option simply does not exist for
`sim` in any yosys version checked here). 252 vectors generated independently
from the Python golden formulas embedded in tb/cocotb/gpu/test_vector_alu.py
(NOT from RTL) -- random + corners across all 9 non-branch opcodes the suite
exercises (VADD/VSUB/VMUL/VAND/VOR/VXOR/VSLL/VSRL/VSRA), VADDI/VANDI immediate
sweeps, VBEQ/VBLT branch corners+random, and a dedicated partial-active-mask
sweep (12 mask patterns x 8 ops, garbage data forced into inactive lanes) --
exactly the corruption class this investigation is about. Ran against the
TRACKED fixed netlist (pnr/asap7/valu_hls_comb/config.json's actual candidate,
run RUN_2026-09-15_15-06-29, USE_SYNLIG:false+sv2v, 47791 instances -- NOT the
newer RUN_2026-09-15_16-29-18, which is a leftover USE_SYNLIG:true diagnostic
re-run of the KNOWN-BROKEN 1587-instance netlist from bead gcd; using that one
by mistake would have re-tested the bug, not the fix) via `read_liberty
-ignore_miss_func <5 ASAP7 SIMPLE libs>; read_verilog; hierarchy; proc; flatten;
opt -full; eval -set ... -show done_o -show result_o -show branch_taken_o`,
one eval per vector, batched into a single yosys invocation (252 evals, ~6 min
wall, 1 GB peak, 3G systemd-run cap, no OOM). Parser:
tools/verif/gls/parse_eval_log.py. Result: 252/252 PASS, 0 mismatches, 0 X in
any output -- done_o=1, result_o and branch_taken_o exactly match the golden
model on every vector, including every partial-mask/garbage-inactive-lane
vector (the exact class the original SAT-miter counterexample exposed).
RTL-candidate cross-check (pre-synthesis Bambu vector_alu_synth.v + the
port-adapting shim) with the SAME 252-vector set was attempted but blocked:
yosys's own (non-Synlig) Verilog frontend does not accept the shim's
`module vector_alu_hls import gpu_pkg::*; (...)` import-in-header SV syntax
("ERROR: syntax error, unexpected TOK_IMPORT"). Not fixed this session (time).
Falls back on the already-recorded evidence for the RTL candidate: 14/14
Verilator/cocotb PASS (66db8e5 gate) plus the original SAT-miter counterexample
proof. Net effect: COMB-FIXED is now verified correct by 252 independent
functional vectors on the actual gate netlist, not just the original 5.
See tools/verif/gls/{gen_vector_alu_vectors.py,make_eval_ys.py,parse_eval_log.py}
(committed fdf166b) to reproduce or extend.
close_reason: Answered (2026-09-15). Bambu 2024.10 emits a zero-register, zero-latency vector_alu with --speculative-sdc-scheduling --clock-period=100. Stage-3 PPA re-measured: 47791 instances / 4139.77 um^2 / 14.060 mW, vs hand RTL 54634 / 4655.15 / 14.147 and the FSM baseline 71480 / 7254.37 / 37.667. That required the Synlig frontend fix (gcd, closed): USE_SYNLIG:false plus an sv2v shim. The comb netlist is verified 252/252 vectors against the Python golden model. Area and power are quotable; timing carries the no-resizer worst-arc caveat. Whether the FSM baseline is functionally correct under Synlig vs sv2v, and the CPU/GPU Synlig exposure, continue on b0t.

title: GH #119 follow-up: the datapath half of the HLS recommendation is UNTESTED
description:
Stage 1 correction, recorded in docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md and on GH #119.

docs/CPP_TO_RTL_HLS_EVALUATION.md recommends reserving NL->C++->HLS for 'future, datapath-dominant accelerators' (Phase 6 INT8 NPU, DSP/FFT, crypto). Stage 1 did NOT test that half.

WHY: the issue named rtl/gpu/memory_coalescer.sv as the 'datapath-ish -> HLS-favorable' pole. It is not a datapath block -- 214 lines of lane-walking FSM plus AXI handshakes with ZERO arithmetic, and GPU_ENABLE_COALESCE=0 means nothing is actually coalesced (it serialises one single-beat transaction per active lane). It was kept in Stage 1 because it is the block that exercises Bambu's m_axi path and carries the real interface risk, but it never tested the datapath hypothesis.

So the datapath recommendation is EXACTLY as evidenced as it was before the pilot ran: on literature alone. Stage 1 neither supports nor undermines it.

WHAT WOULD TEST IT: rtl/gpu/vector_alu.sv -- 81 lines, 8-lane SIMD, 8x 32-bit multiply plus shift/logic, purely combinational, no protocol at all. All-scalar C (no m_axi), so the shim is a pure rename plus start/done tie-off, and there is no interface risk to gate on. It is the genuine datapath pole.

EXPECTED CAVEAT, same as the hazard unit: Bambu cannot emit combinational logic, so a 1-cycle multiply array becomes a start/done FSM. Normalise on throughput at matched fmax and report Bambu's cycle count against the hand-RTL's 1. Note the hazard unit already established that this wrapping is structural rather than an authoring artefact, so the interesting question here is AREA and fmax on an arithmetic-dominated block, not latency.

PRECEDENT TO REUSE: the whole Stage 1 harness works -- hls/bambu.mk flags, tools/eda/wrap-bambu.sh, the withheld-RTL authoring protocol, the wire-only shim pattern, and the two-leg equivalence method (Bambu cosim + the same cocotb suite on both arms). vector_alu has an existing suite at tb/cocotb/gpu/ to reuse as the shared oracle -- check gpu_alu in sim/Makefile.

PRIORITY P3: only worth doing if the datapath recommendation is about to be ACTED on (e.g. before committing HLS to the Phase 6 INT8 NPU). If nobody is about to build a datapath accelerator, the untested status is fine as long as it is not mistaken for a tested one -- which is why it is written down.
close_reason: Datapath pole measured. HLS regresses on every axis (area +55.4%, power +163.5%, path x5.5, cycles x14-38). Datapath half of the recommendation does not hold; doc + PROVENANCE updated, both arms 14/14.

title: LibreLane nix-shell pins Verilator 5.018, rejects RTL that lints clean under project's 5.048
description:
Reproduced and FIXED 2026-09-07. The bead had no description; this is the write-up plus the fix.

THREE VERILATORS ARE IN PLAY ON THIS HOST:
  librelane nix-shell (~/Downloads/Github/librelane, `nix-shell --run`)  -> 5.018, 2023-10-30, rev UNKNOWN.REV
  project flake        (repo root, `nix develop`)                        -> 5.048, 2026-04-26
  ambient `nix-shell -p verilator`                                       -> 5.050, 2026-07-01
Every `make librelane-*` target runs inside the FIRST one, so librelane's step
`01-verilator-lint` (gated by `02-checker-linterrors`) uses 5.018. All sim/lint targets
run under the project flake's 5.048. The bead title's "pins 5.018" is correct.

THE REJECTED CONSTRUCT: non-blocking assignment to an unpacked array inside a for loop.
  %Error-BLKLOOPINIT: rtl/mem/rv32i_icache.sv:605:32: Unsupported: Delayed assignment to
    array inside for loops (non-delayed is ok - see docs)
  %Error-BLKLOOPINIT: rtl/mem/rv32i_dcache.sv:952:32: (same)
  %Error-BLKLOOPINIT: rtl/mem/rv32i_dcache.sv:953:32: (same)
  %Error: Exiting due to 3 error(s)
These are the valid_array/dirty_array bulk-clear loops in the reset branch of each cache's
always_ff (N_SETS = 256). 5.048 and 5.050 accept them; 5.018 does not.

HOW IT GOT IN, AND WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: commit f814b21 (2026-08-14 21:31 +0700, "[RTL]
Non-blocking assignment in i/d-cache valid/dirty reset loops (Spyglass SM_BNP/W336, GH #116
item B)") flipped these three lines from `=` to `<=`. That silenced Spyglass and broke
Verilator 5.018. Two lint rules in direct conflict.
  Proof it was never exercised: the newest P&R run on disk is 2026-08-13 (pnr/asap7/soc/runs/
  RUN_2026-08-13_05-09-56), i.e. all of them predate f814b21. The archived lint log of
  pnr/asap7/cpu/runs/RUN_2026-08-09_14-05-02/01-verilator-lint/verilator-lint.log shows those
  exact lines as `valid_array[j] = 1'b0;` with only %Warning-BLKSEQ, 0 errors -- the
  pre-f814b21 blocking form. Replaying that run's byte-exact recorded COMMANDS under the
  librelane shell today gives 3 errors / EXIT=1. So the NEXT CPU-block run started on this
  tree would have died at step 01, and nothing in the repo would have predicted it.

SCOPE: only configs that list the cache .sv files as VERILOG_FILES --
  pnr/asap7/cpu/config.json, pnr/asap7/template/config.json, pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json.
SoC configs are NOT affected: the CPU is a hard macro there and the caches never enter the
SoC's VERILOG_FILES (verified: soc_top_sv2v.v, regenerated 2026-08-15 07:15 i.e. AFTER
f814b21, contains 28 modules and no icache/valid_array).

FIX APPLIED: `/* verilator lint_off BLKLOOPINIT */` ... `lint_on` around both reset loops.
Comment-only, zero logic change, keeps the `<=` that Spyglass wants, and needs no librelane
version bump. Rejected alternatives: reverting f814b21 (re-breaks Spyglass SM_BNP/W336);
converting the arrays to packed `logic [N_SETS-1:0]` + `<= '0` (works for both linters but is
a real RTL change affecting synthesis inference, disproportionate for a lint conflict);
bumping librelane's Verilator (touches a vendored tool outside this repo).

VERIFIED, non-vacuously:
 * pragma on icache only -> BLKLOOPINIT 3 -> 2 under 5.018 (proves the pragma bound to that
   site rather than the errors vanishing for some other reason). An earlier minimal 8-entry
   testcase did NOT reproduce BLKLOOPINIT at all, so it could not have validated the pragma
   -- the rule appears to need the larger loop; the real files are the only valid harness.
 * both pragmas -> librelane 5.018: replayed CPU lint command EXIT=0, 0 BLKLOOPINIT;
   `make -C sim lint_soc` EXIT=0.
 * project 5.048: `make -C sim lint` EXIT=0, 0 errors; `make -C sim lint_soc` EXIT=0.
 * functional: `make -C sim phase3_all` -> ALL PHASE 3 TESTS PASSED (7/7, 8/8, 5/5).

FOLLOW-UP WORTH DOING (not this bead): nothing gates the version skew, so the next construct
that 5.018 rejects will again only surface when a PD run dies at step 01. A cheap guard is a
`make verify-tooling` check that runs the librelane-shell Verilator over the CPU source list,
or at minimum records the three versions.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #168 (commit d03f320). Root cause: commit f814b21's Spyglass SM_BNP/W336 fix flipped the i/d-cache valid/dirty bulk-clear loops to non-blocking, which librelane's Verilator 5.018 rejects as %Error-BLKLOOPINIT. Invisible because no sim/lint target uses 5.018 and every P&R run on disk predates f814b21 -- the next CPU-block run would have died at step 01-verilator-lint. Fixed with a lint_off BLKLOOPINIT pragma (comment-only, keeps the <= Spyglass wants). Added tools/setup/check_librelane_verilator.py, wired into make verify-tooling, so the next 5.018-rejected construct fails in seconds instead of at step 1 of a 6h run; proven non-vacuous by negative control. Full write-up in the bead description.

title: ASAP7 macro power characterization: write_timing_model omits power tables, macro Liberty carries none
description: Root-caused while resolving bead ew3: OpenROAD/OpenSTA's write_timing_model (used in pnr/scripts/asap7_macro_views.tcl to generate the abstracted macro Liberty for rv32i_cpu_top and gpu_top) has no power-characterization code path (verified: zero 'power' hits in vendored OpenSTA MakeTimingModel.cc). The resulting macro .lib files declare leakage_power_unit but never emit cell_leakage_power or internal_power groups, so report_power attributes 0.00 W to both hard macros in every ASAP7 SoC run (docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md, all figures fabric-only).
design: Add a real macro power-characterization step (distinct from write_timing_model) to asap7_macro_views.tcl or a sibling script: run report_power on each macro's own signed-off block netlist under representative activity (CPU pnr/asap7/cpu/, GPU pnr/asap7/gpu/) and inject the resulting lumped cell_leakage_power / per-pin internal_power values into the abstracted macro .lib by hand or script. Re-run SoC report_power afterward and confirm Macro row is nonzero and the fabric-only caveat in docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md can be removed.
notes:
2026-09-09 IMPLEMENTED in 7b7dbae. Two sibling scripts added (asap7_macro_power.tcl +
asap7_macro_power_inject.py); asap7_macro_views.tcl deliberately untouched so view generation
and power characterization stay separable.

Injection applied to the git-TRACKED canonical libs pnr/asap7/{cpu,gpu}/macro/*.lib -- the
soc/macro copies are gitignored, so patching only those would not have persisted. Verified
purely additive (0 lines removed / 62 added per file) and parsing with 0 errors under the
repo's OpenSTA 2.6.0.

RESULT, SoC round-trip against the run-23 signed-off flat netlist: Macro row 0.00 W ->
222.545 mW (internal 217.089 + leakage 5.456); whole-SoC 306.264 mW at a uniform 0.2/0.5
activity. Macro internal and leakage each equal the sum of the two standalone
characterizations exactly, so the injection round-trips.

ASSUMPTIONS, both disclosed in the injected .lib comment because the numbers are meaningless
without them:
 1. Flat vectorless activity (set_power_activity -global -activity 0.20 -duty 0.5). Not
    invented for this task -- it is this repo's own existing convention from
    pnr/scripts/08_power.tcl. No VCD or SAIF exists for either macro.
 2. No post-route SPEF/DEF was available (run dirs pruned -- see the prune bead), so this is
    Liberty-table power from gate input-pin capacitance only, with NO wire RC.

Liberty internal_power scalar units are declared nowhere in these files, so they were derived
EMPIRICALLY -- a single-cell test lib/netlist fed a known rise_power value, with real
report_power output confirming the implicit unit is capacitive_load_unit x voltage_unit^2
(= 1 fJ here), not 1 pJ or 1 nJ. The injector re-derives per file rather than hardcoding.

MAGNITUDE SANITY (bead 7l5 discipline): CPU macro leakage matches 10 x 128.9 uW vendor SRAM
Liberty leakage to 5 digits. Per-instance stdcell leakage ~37 fW (CPU) vs ~48 fW (GPU) -- same
order at one PDK/corner. Versus prior official standalone figures: GPU 166.0 mW here vs 262 mW
(0.63x), CPU 56.5 mW here vs 24.38 mW (2.3x) -- same order, spread explained by differing
activity and parasitic assumptions, not a unit error.

NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR ANY EXISTING FIGURE. 62.9 mW (run 14) and 51.9 mW (run 23) are correctly
reported fabric-only numbers and are NOT retro-edited. 51.9 + 222.5 = 274.4 mW MIXES
methodologies (real parasitics on the fabric, flat activity and no wire RC on the macros) and
must carry that caveat; 306.264 mW is the cleaner single-methodology figure.

REMAINING BEFORE THIS BEAD CLOSES:
 * Re-run SoC report_power inside a real flow rather than the standalone round-trip.
 * Update docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md's "fabric-only" caveat to point at the macro-inclusive
   figures, with the assumptions attached.
 * Do NOT use the LibreLane 3.0.14 shell for that -- its `sta` is OpenSTA 2.7.0, which
   corrupts report_power (bead zwc).
2026-09-13 SoC IN-FLOW POWER RUN ATTEMPT 1: OOM-KILLED IN SYNTHESIS. make librelane-asap7-soc-multiclock (config_multiclock.json, LibreLane 2.4.13, OpenSTA 2.6.0 shim) under systemd-run --scope MemoryMax=12G. Run /nobackup/asap7_soc_runs/RUN_2026-09-13_21-18-41 died at 22:25:36 in step 04-yosys-synthesis, ~65 min in: ABC (SYNTH_STRATEGY DELAY 2, SYNTH_ABC_BUFFERING true) plateaued near 11.25 GB RSS then crossed the cap. The cgroup cap worked as designed -- only the flow died, not the session. Not a netlist regression: the regenerated soc_top_sv2v.v has 28 fabric modules and does NOT define rv32i_cpu_top or gpu_top (both arrive as hard macros through MACROS LEF/LIB). Baseline: run 23 finished the same synthesis on this host UNCAPPED in ~74 min (14:36:25 -> 15:50:25), 220524 cells / 44412 DFFHQNx1; its logs record no memory peak, which is why a >12 GB synthesis requirement was never noticed. Useful finding for any future SoC run on this 15.9 GB host: synthesis alone needs somewhat more than a 12 GB cgroup. Retry strategy delegated to the PD orchestrator (options: reuse run 23's synthesized netlist via explicit --with-initial-state, or a ~13.5 GB cap). Separately noted for this bead: config_multiclock.json EXTRA_LIBS already point at pnr/asap7/soc/macro/*__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib, which carry the 2026-09-08 power injection, so LibreLane's own report_power should include macro power once an STA step completes -- to be confirmed against power.rpt.
2026-09-13 RETRY 2 (RUN_2026-09-13_22-28-40, seeded from run 23's synthesized netlist, 13G) died at 13-openroad-generatepdn -- NOT a design or memory problem. LibreLane 2.4.13's get_psm_error_count() parses *-grid-errors.rpt as YAML and cannot read OpenROAD 26Q2's tab-indented format (ScannerError line 2 col 1). Latent until now: the pdn.tcl partial-grid patch made check_power_grid write its first real error report. Patched the parser to count source entries line by line; verified empty->0, fallback->1 (both unchanged), real VSS/VDD reports crash->10692/11001. Patch: memory/pd/patches/librelane2413_psm_report_parser_26q2_format.diff. ERROR_ON_PDN_VIOLATIONS is false in config_multiclock.json, so the ~21.7k count is non-fatal. Also recorded before the crash: in-flow STAPrePNR power.rpt already shows Macro 167.33 mW (84.5%) of 197.998 mW, confirming macro power flows in-flow, but that is ~the GPU alone vs the bead's standalone 222.5 mW -- per-instance reconciliation requested at post-route.
2026-09-13 IN-FLOW MACRO POWER DEPENDS ON AN UNSTATED ACTIVITY ASSUMPTION (PD orchestrator per-instance probe, standalone OpenSTA 26Q2 on RUN_2026-09-13_22-28-40/11-openroad-tapendcapinsertion ODB with the flow's own libs + SDC). Per instance: u_cpu 10.1 mW internal + 1.29 mW leakage = 11.4 mW; u_gpu 162 + 4.16 = 166 mW. Reconciles with STAPrePNR's Macro group 167.33 mW = GPU 166.04 + CPU leakage 1.29, i.e. CPU dynamic ~0 at that step. Leakage matches the standalone characterisation exactly on both macros; the whole 167 vs 222.5 mW gap is CPU dynamic power. MECHANISM: the injected Liberty puts each macro's dynamic power on its clock pin (correct -- GPU reproduces its standalone 166.04 mW exactly). Clock reaches each macro through a structurally identical rv32i_clock_gate ICG. Under OpenSTA's default vectorless activity, u_gpu_cg.u_icg/ENA resolves to a constant (activity 0, duty 1.0), so GCLK runs at full rate (1.143e9, duty 0.5 = CLK). u_cpu_cg.u_icg/ENA is real logic (PMU -> CDC 2-FF synchroniser chain), so it gets activity 1.282e8 / duty 0.5 and GCLK is derated to 4.687e8 / duty 0.25 -- ~18% of ideal -- and ~80% of the CPU macro's dynamic power vanishes. The figure also drifted between STAPrePNR (CPU dynamic ~0) and step 11 (10.1 mW) as resizer passes changed the enable path. CONCLUSION: an in-flow macro-inclusive SoC total under default activity is NOT a physical number; it silently assumes the CPU domain is gated ~82% of the time and the GPU never. Report at declared operating points instead: (1) all-domains-on (both ICG enables forced active -- the point the macros were characterised at), (2) default vectorless, explicitly labelled as an artefact, (3) optionally CPU-gated as a lower bound. Requested from the orchestrator for the final checkpoint.
2026-09-13 PARSER FIX VALIDATED IN-FLOW. Run 3 (RUN_2026-09-13_22-43-29, fresh, seeded from run 23's synthesized netlist, 13G) passed 13-openroad-generatepdn and continued to global placement. state_out.json: design__power_grid_violation__count__net:VSS=10692, net:VDD=11001, total 21693 -- identical to the offline test and to the grid-errors reports' entry counts; no ScannerError/traceback in the driver log. The ~21.7k count is the known-failing old SoC PDN topology (not a regression) and is non-fatal with ERROR_ON_PDN_VIOLATIONS false.
2026-09-13 RUN 3 (RUN_2026-09-13_22-43-29) died at 20-openroad-globalplacement: [ERROR GPL-0326] apb_paddr_i[0] toplevel port is not placed. Root cause: second LibreLane-2.4.13-vs-OpenROAD-26Q2 incompatibility. 2.4.13 ioplacer.tcl passes -random_seed 42 unconditionally (FP_PPL_MODE was 'matching'); 26Q2 place_pins treats -random/-random_seed as obsolete ([WARNING PPL-0113] ... Skipping random pin placement) and places nothing -- 2 of 161 ports placed before AND after step 17. Run 23 predates the 26Q2 shim (added 2026-09-08) and placed 159 I/O. Patched ioplacer.tcl to drop the flag (diff memory/pd/patches/librelane2413_ioplacer_26q2_random_seed.diff). Verified standalone on run 3's own step-16 ODB: 2/161 -> 161/161 placed, PPL-0002 Number of I/O 159 (= run 23), apb_paddr_i[0] PLACED, no PPL-0113. A sweep of runs 2-3 found no other obsolete/skipped-option warnings through step 20; later steps on this tool combination remain unexercised.
2026-09-13 OPERATING-POINT POWER SCENARIOS (standalone OpenSTA 26Q2 on RUN_2026-09-13_22-28-40/11-openroad-tapendcapinsertion ODB, the flow's own libs + SDC):
 S0 default vectorless: u_cpu 11.4 mW (10.1 internal + 1.29 leakage), u_gpu 166 mW -> macros 177.4 mW.
 S2 CPU domain gated: set_power_activity -pins [get_pins u_cpu_cg.u_icg/ENA] -activity 0 -duty 0 -> u_cpu 1.29 mW (pure leakage), u_gpu 166 mW -> macros 167.3 mW. Clean lower bound.
 S1 all domains on: COULD NOT BE PRODUCED IN-FLOW. set_case_analysis 1 on u_cpu_cg.u_icg/ENA had zero effect on power; set_power_activity on ENA -activity 0 -duty 1 changed only GCLK duty (0.25 -> 0.5), not its rate; set_power_activity on u_cpu/clk_i (0-2 transitions/cycle units) had no effect, reproduced twice.
RESULT FOR THIS BEAD: macro power is a BOUNDED RANGE, not one number: 167.3 mW (CPU gated) .. 177.4 mW (default activity) .. 222.5 mW (all on, using the standalone CPU-block 56.5 mW as the only available full-activity CPU figure). SoC total = post-route fabric + that range, with the dependence on CPU-domain activity stated.
OPEN QUESTION, not a conclusion: the CPU gated clock's activity is 4.687e8 transitions/s in every attempt. That is NOT cpu_clk's rate (2 / 0.780 ns = 2.564e9) and not an obvious CLK x ENA product, whereas the GPU gated clock is 1.143e9 = exactly sys_clk (2 / 1.750 ns). So cpu_clk may not be propagating to u_cpu_cg.u_icg/CLK as a clock in the power engine. The orchestrator's broader explanation ('OpenSTA refuses power overrides on clock pins') is NOT established by this evidence. Requested a per-pin clock dump of u_cpu_cg.u_icg/CLK in the final report to settle it. Timing is a separate engine and run 23's cpu_clk closure (+9.8 ps) is not called into question by this alone.
2026-09-13 IOPLACER FIX VALIDATED IN-FLOW. Run 4 (RUN_2026-09-13_23-04-18, fresh, run-23 netlist seed, 13G, started 23:04 after the 23:01:30 ioplacer.tcl patch): step 17 OpenROAD.IOPlacement logged PPL-0001 slots 2024, PPL-0002 I/O 159, PPL-0003 I/O w/sink 159, no PPL-0113, no errors -- identical to run 23. Step 20 OpenROAD.GlobalPlacement then ran initial-placement iterations with no GPL-0326 (the run-3 failure). Both 2.4.13-vs-26Q2 fixes (PSM parser at GeneratePDN, ioplacer -random_seed) are now confirmed in-flow. Note: a wrong intermediate conclusion that 'the patch does not fix it' came from reading run 3 (which predated the patch) and from the args echo, which omits the hard-coded -random_seed; recorded in knowledge.md as a trap.
2026-09-13 RUN 4 (RUN_2026-09-13_23-04-18) passed GeneratePDN (checker cleanly reported 21693 PDN violations), IOPlacement (159 I/O, no PPL-0113) and GlobalPlacement, then died at 23-openroad-stamidpnr: 'invalid command name rsz::check_corner_wire_cap' in 2.4.13 sta/corner.tcl. Not a one-line fix: a sweep of all 28 namespaced internal calls in the 2.4.13 scripts against OpenROAD 26Q2 found four missing (rsz::check_corner_wire_cap, sta::corners, sta::set_cmd_corner, utl::metric_int) -- 26Q2 renamed corners to scenes -- so every in-flow STA step on 26Q2 would fail. Filed claude_verilog_test-bpp for the port. DECISION for this run: switch back to LibreLane 2.4.13's bundled toolchain (OpenROAD edf00dff + OpenSTA 2.6.0), exactly what run 23 used, via make OR_PATH_PREFIX= (bypasses only the PATH shim). Rationale: the 26Q2 shim exists for DRT pin access, which this host cannot reach (CPU-block DRT already OOMs); a 26Q2 run would most likely end post-GRT or OOM after more porting risk. Consequence to state in the final report: like run 23, detailed routing will commit no wires (bead xy6), so 'post-route' STA/power/CDC numbers are on GRT parasitics -- the same basis as the run-23 figures this bead and je8 compare against. The two 2.4.13 patches are format-agnostic and remain safe on edf00dff.
2026-09-14 RUN 5 (RUN_2026-09-13_23-34-16, bundled toolchain OpenROAD edf00dff + OpenSTA 2.6.0, no 26Q2 shim -- confirmed from the scope process PATH) PASSED 23-openroad-stamidpnr at 23:59 with zero invalid-command errors, i.e. past where run 4 died. It tracks run 23 step for step through mid-PnR: STAPrePNR setup WS -45.0 ns / hold 0.0 in both; pre-repair STAMidPNR setup WS -122.8 ns in both (hold -29.8 vs -25.4 ns, TNS -2.52e9 vs -2.49e9, power 1871.3 vs 1794.3 mW -- unbuffered post-GPL slews, not representative; run 23 recovered to -0.8 ns / 54.8 mW once repair ran). The one intended difference is STAPrePNR power: 198.0 mW (run 5) vs 30.7 mW (run 23); the 167.3 mW delta is exactly the macro power added by the 2026-09-08 injection, which is the in-flow evidence that macro power is now included. Also confirmed: the patched ioplacer.tcl on edf00dff placed all 159 I/O (2024 slots, no PPL-0113, no GPL-0326).
2026-09-14 RUN 5 FIRST REPRESENTATIVE CHECKPOINT -- STAMidPNR-1 (post-repair + CTS), vs run 23's same step (32-openroad-stamidpnr-1):
  setup WS   run23 -0.77 ns   run5 -0.71 ns   (+0.07)
  hold WS    run23 -0.37 ns   run5 -0.43 ns   (-0.05)
  setup TNS  run23 -4626.8 ns run5 -5844.5 ns (-1217.7, ~26% worse; cause not established -- partial PDN occupying resources is plausible, not proven)
  power      run23 54.82 mW   run5 222.26 mW  (+167.44)
    internal 43.48 -> 205.37 (+161.89) | switching 11.30 -> 11.40 (+0.10) | leakage 0.03 -> 5.49 (+5.46)
Reconciliation: fabric switching unchanged; leakage delta 5.46 mW = u_cpu 1.29 + u_gpu 4.16 macro leakage exactly; internal delta ~GPU macro dynamic power with CPU macro dynamic still ~0 (vectorless ICG-enable derating persists post-CTS). Total delta +167.44 mW matches the independently measured 167.3 mW. So in-flow macro power is real and fully accounted for, and at this checkpoint it sits at the CPU-gated end of the 167.3 / 177.4 / 222.5 mW range. Timing worst slack matches run 23 within ~0.07 ns.
2026-09-14 POST-CTS TIMING REPAIR, run 5 (29-openroad-resizertimingpostcts) vs run 23 (33-openroad-resizertimingpostcts), from each step's repair_timing iteration table (state_out.json metrics are carried over from the prior checkpoint, not updated by this step):
  setup START   run23 WNS -773.354 ps  TNS -4626796.5 ps  viol 11813   | run5 WNS -706.873 ps  TNS -5844515.0 ps  viol 34122
  setup FINAL   run23 WNS -384.273 ps  TNS -1771770.0 ps  viol 11727   | run5 WNS -389.816 ps  TNS -3310781.2 ps  viol 34085
  actions       run23 resized 194 inserted 602 cloned 142              | run5 resized 304 inserted 54 cloned 191
  hold FINAL    run23 slack +25.000 ps TNS 0 (4232 endpoints found)    | run5 slack +25.000 ps TNS 0 (4735 endpoints found)
READING: worst-case timing matches (setup WNS within 5.5 ps; hold clean in both). The violation SPREAD does not: after repair run 5 has 1.87x the setup TNS and 2.9x the violating endpoints, and repair barely reduces the count in either run, so the gap carries forward. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED. The partial PDN now committed by the 2.4.13 pdn.tcl patch is the main physical difference from run 23 (same netlist seed, SDC, config and toolchain), so it is the leading hypothesis -- not a finding. Relevance to je8: if the extra ~22k violators sit on the CPU/fabric CDC paths, run 5's CDC budget check is not comparable to run 23's. Asked the PD orchestrator for a per-domain / CDC-path attribution and a GRT congestion + placement density comparison vs run 23.
2026-09-14 PDN-CONGESTION HYPOTHESIS TESTED (PD orchestrator, run 5 vs run 23 at matching steps) -- the congestion pathway is RULED OUT, mechanism of the extra violators remains open:
  GRT final overflow     run23 0/0/0 every layer        | run5 0/0/0 every layer
  GRT blockages          137,270                        | 137,270 (identical)

title: apb_cdc_bridge: post-reset recovery margin (3 m_clk cycles) tight against CDC settling-delay class
description: Found while re-doing bead rvs (CDC delay injector, port 2) on branch feat/cdc-delay-injection-rvs: with rtl/soc/cdc/cdc_2ff_sync.sv's RAND_CDC_DELAY_EN forced ON at every instance (default stays OFF; not shipped), test_apb_cdc_bridge.py::test_availability_never_forwarded (tb/cocotb/soc/test_apb_cdc_bridge.py:881) fails deterministically with 'AssertionError: post-recovery write reported pslverr'. Root cause: after dut.m_rst_n releases, the test waits only ClockCycles(dut.m_clk, 3) before issuing a new write and asserting it succeeds. That margin assumes the m_rst_n_i-status synchroniser into the s domain (a cdc_2ff_sync instance, STAGES=2) always resolves in exactly its nominal 2-cycle latency. Once the settling-delay injector's one-extra-cycle fault model is active, that path can legitimately take 3 cycles instead of 2, so the write issued at cycle 3 still observes m_rst_n_s=0 (destination still reads not-yet-released) and is short-circuited with pslverr=1 -- not data corruption, a timing-margin miss. Confirmed as a genuine perturbation (not a suite-order artifact): isolated re-run of just this testcase with a fresh RNG position passes; it only fails at this specific point within the fixed apb_cdc_bridge suite ordering, reproducibly across repeated full-suite runs. NOT a functional RTL defect -- the design's data-correctness is intact; this is a test-authored recovery-margin assumption that is only exactly-tight, not generously-tight, against a synchroniser's own worst-case (not just nominal) latency. Two independent fixes possible: (a) widen the post-reset recovery wait in test_availability_never_forwarded from 3 to 4+ m_clk cycles, or (b) tie the wait to STAGES+1 explicitly so it self-documents the margin it relies on. Also worth asking whether any REAL firmware/integration code elsewhere in this repo assumes a similarly tight N-cycle (not N+1) reset-release-to-usable contract across this same crossing -- if so that is a latent integration risk independent of this injector work. Only reproduces with the injector forced on (not part of default soc_all); does not block bead rvs's signoff, filed as a residual finding per its acceptance-criteria instructions to distinguish real findings from model artifacts.

title: __pnr__ VERILOG_DEFINE is passed for the Sky130 SoC but not the ASAP7 SoC - the two flows elaborate different RTL
description:
Found during GH #96 Gate B while fixing the USE_ICG_CELL sv2v gap.

MEASURED: pnr/Makefile's sky130-soc-sv2v recipe passes __pnr__; the asap7-soc-sv2v recipe does not. rtl/soc/boot_rom.sv branches on `ifndef __pnr__, so the two PDK flows synthesise DIFFERENT boot ROM RTL from the same source tree.

LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE during #96: run 14 (the accepted single-clock M11 ASAP7 signoff) was built WITHOUT __pnr__, and adding it would have changed the boot ROM contents and therefore the PPA baseline mid-campaign. That reasoning expires once a new ASAP7 SoC baseline is accepted.

RELATED GOTCHA worth keeping with this bead: sv2v resolves `ifdef ITSELF, before Yosys runs, so config.json VERILOG_DEFINES arrives too late for anything sv2v already decided. Defines that must reach the sv2v layer belong in SOC_SV2V_DEFINES in pnr/Makefile. That is what bit GH #96 Gate B - USE_ICG_CELL was in VERILOG_DEFINES only, so rv32i_clock_gate.sv was frozen into its behavioural always_latch branch and Yosys could not map the resulting \$_DLATCH_N_ (2 unmapped instances, exit 2). Note the converse: sky130 must NOT get USE_ICG_CELL - ICGx1_ASAP7_75t_R is ASAP7-only.

DECIDE: either pass __pnr__ on ASAP7 too (and re-baseline), or document why the ASAP7 flow deliberately elaborates the behavioural boot ROM.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #153 (merged 2026-08-15, b2453f5). Decision: ADOPT __pnr__ on the ASAP7 SoC sv2v path. SOC_SV2V_DEFINES := --define=USE_ICG_CELL --define=__pnr__ (pnr/Makefile:1070), with the obsolete 'deliberately NOT passed here' block replaced by a dated rationale. The withholding reason expired: GH #96 run 23 is the accepted ASAP7 SoC baseline and is driven by config_multiclock.json, so run 14 / config.json stay byte-reproducible. Measured: $readmemh in pnr/asap7/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v 1 -> 0; netlist delta 43 lines; make sky130-soc-sv2v regenerates byte-identical; sim lint byte-identical to baseline. NOTE recorded in the Makefile: the delta is NOT boot_rom alone -- PR #152 (GH #116 item C) wired the same macro into the param-check initial/$fatal blocks in axi_lite_register_bank.sv, apb4_register_bank.sv, axil_to_apb.sv, so those drop too.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text:
Cross-link + new evidence 2026-08-14, measured while resolving GH #116's 'exact synth macro name' open question.

GH #116 plans to guard non-synthesizable initial/$fatal/$readmemh with `ifndef SYNTHESIS. Investigation shows that collides directly with THIS bead:

1. SYNTHESIS is defined by NOTHING in this toolchain. Only hit is pnr/freepdk45/config.json:71 LINTER_DEFINES, which feeds the Verilator lint step alone. Neither sv2v nor Yosys auto-defines it (librelane/scripts/pyosys/ys_common.py:58 builds -D purely from the config list; sv2v honours only explicit --define=). So the #116 guards as specified would be a silent no-op on every path.

2. __pnr__ ALREADY has exactly the semantics #116 wants (`ifndef __pnr__ == simulation-only) and is already plumbed through BOTH layers on sky130. Recommendation filed on #116: reuse __pnr__ or make SYNTHESIS a synonym, rather than add a second switch.

3. THE DECISION THIS BEAD OWNS IS NOW ON #116's CRITICAL PATH. Confirmed measured:
   - sky130 SoC passes __pnr__ at both layers (pnr/Makefile:693 sv2v + pnr/sky130/soc/config.json:47) -> grep -c '$readmemh' pnr/sky130/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v = 0
   - asap7 SoC withholds it -> pnr/asap7/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v:3571 still carries 'initial if (MEM_INIT_FILE != "") $readmemh(MEM_INIT_FILE, mem);' AND the parameter string
   If #116 guards boot_rom on the asap7 path it removes $readmemh from a netlist whose run-14 baseline contained it -- i.e. it silently makes this bead's decision. Must be decided here first, explicitly.

4. NEW HAZARD for whoever resolves this: a `ifndef SYNTHESIS wrapper does NOT subsume the __pnr__ branch in boot_rom.sv. The `else arm exists because MEM_INIT_FILE becomes an int under __pnr__ (Synlig UHDM asserts on parameter string, boot_rom.sv:33-41). Deleting the initial under SYNTHESIS while __pnr__ is unset leaves the parameter string in the netlist -- exactly what __pnr__ exists to prevent. The two macros would have to be set in lockstep = aliasing hazard. It would also drop the ROM zero-fill that the `else arm currently provides on sky130.

5. Also found: rtl/soc/pll/pll_rnm.sv guards its initial with '// synthesis translate_off', and SV2V STRIPS COMMENTS (grep -c translate_off pnr/asap7/soc/soc_top_sv2v.v = 0). Pragma-based guarding is unsafe on any sv2v path in this repo; only `ifdef survives. pll_rnm.sv is not in any P&R filelist so it is not currently exposed, but the pattern must not be copied.

Full write-up posted as a comment on GH #116.

title: analyze_power_grid is blocked on ASAP7 - PSM-0069 connectivity failure from the M1-only tap-cell artifact
description:
IR drop was an explicit GH #96 deliverable and could not be produced. Root cause is NOT the RCX/SPEF gap originally assumed.

MEASURED: analyze_power_grid fails with PSM-0069 'Check connectivity failed' on BOTH VDD and VSS, reporting 32,862 'Unconnected shape ... on Layer M1' errors. -source_type STRAPS fails identically. There is no bypass flag on the command. pnr/config/vsrc.tcl is in place and correct - it is the connectivity precheck that refuses, before any solve.

This is the SAME M1-only PSM connectivity model that produces the ~7-8 M benign tap-cell PDN 'violations' documented in memory/pd/knowledge.md:857-872 and accepted on the CPU, GPU and SoC signoffs. So the tap artifact does not merely inflate a violation counter - it blocks PSM IR analysis outright, on every ASAP7 design in this repo.

DISTINCT FROM bead e69 (ASAP7 rcx_rules.pex is 0 bytes, blocking SPEF and post-route STA). Both must be resolved to get real in-flow IR drop, but they are separate failures at separate stages - do not merge them. Cross-linked.

Consequence: no ASAP7 signoff in this project has an IR-drop number, and none can until either the PDN tap-cell connectivity is modelled properly or a standalone IR path is built.
notes:
2026-09-09 NOT RESOLVED. PSM-0069 persists on the routed run. The hopeful lead in the previous
note does NOT hold up -- recording that explicitly so it is not re-chased.

THE "2 VIOLATIONS" LEAD IS DEAD as evidence. That reading came from a DIFFERENT, coarser
in-flow PDN check that does not test the same thing as analyze_power_grid's connectivity
precheck. It reproduces, but it is not equivalent evidence and must not be read as PSM-0069
being gone.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY FOUND, working directly against the routed run with the pinned 26Q2 openroad
(the eda-openroad MCP session could not load the ODB -- schema mismatch):
 1. analyze_power_grid's API renamed -outfile to -voltage_file. Anyone reusing old scripts
    will hit this first.
 2. A NEW BLOCKER AHEAD OF PSM-0069: PSM-0021, M1/M4 zero resistance, traced to the ASAP7 tech
    LEF carrying NO RESISTANCE field for either layer.
 3. ⚠️ AN EARLY "LOOKS CLEAN" READING WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE. The run had aborted earlier at
    PSM-0021 and never reached the connectivity check at all; the absence of PSM-0069 in that
    log meant "not tested", not "passed". Exactly the bead-dwp failure mode. After working
    around PSM-0021 the run proceeds and hits PSM-0069 on the same M1-only tap-cell/filler
    artifact as before.

SO THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS STANDS: the M1-only tap-cell connectivity artifact blocks PSM IR
analysis, and routing closure did not change that. The two real paths remain (a) fix the
tap-cell PDN connectivity so PSM's model sees connected shapes -- which would also retire the
benign ~7-8 M PDN "violations" carried on the CPU/GPU/SoC sign-offs -- or (b) build a
standalone IR path. pnr/config/vsrc.tcl is correct; do not chase it.
NEW SUB-PROBLEM to solve first either way: the missing M1/M4 RESISTANCE in the tech LEF
(PSM-0021). Without resistance values an IR solve is meaningless even if connectivity passes.
close_reason: Resolved (2026-09-12, PR #171 merged). IR drop was blocked not by a tap-cell artifact but by the absence of any power grid (see 4l8). With the fixed grid plus VIAS_R (ASAP7 shipped no via resistances -> PSM-0021), analyze_power_grid reports 'All shapes on net VDD/VSS are connected' and produces IR drop: 0.18%/0.19% worst case at ORFS strap density, 1.33%/1.37% at the sparsest density now committed. That figure came from a floorplan-stage harness; a sign-off IR number must come from a fully routed run, which is host-gated on claude_verilog_test-2kn.

comments.author: RD-Chuanseng.Ng
comments.text: Cross-link: bead claude_verilog_test-e69 (ASAP7 rcx_rules.pex is 0 bytes) is the OTHER half of the missing in-flow IR path. e69 blocks SPEF/parasitics; this bead blocks the PSM solve itself. Both must clear for a real IR number; neither is a duplicate of the other.

title: ASAP7 SoC power numbers are not comparable across runs - report_power attributes 0.00 W to both hard macros
description:
Found while closing GH #96 (run 23 vs the run-14 single-clock signoff).

MEASURED: report_power on the multi-clock SoC gives total 51.9 mW (run 23) vs 62.9 mW (run 14), but Macro = 0.00 W in both. The CPU and GPU hard macros - which are the bulk of the design - contribute NOTHING to the reported number in this flow. So the SoC power figure is really 'fabric + glue power', not SoC power.

Two consequences:
1. The 62.9 -> 51.9 mW drop must NOT be quoted as a multi-clock efficiency win. It coincides with the first-ever insertion of real ICG clock gates (USE_ICG_CELL was added to SOC_SV2V_DEFINES during GH #96 Gate B), not with the domain split. Attribution is unverified either way.
2. Every ASAP7 SoC power number in docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md carries the same omission, including the 62.9 mW M11 signoff figure.

Per-hierarchy split measured on run 18 for reference: Sequential 29.9 mW (69.0%), Clock 13.0 mW (30.0%), Combinational 0.44 mW (1.0%), Macro 0.00 mW.

TO INVESTIGATE: whether the macro Liberty files carry power tables at all (rv32i_cpu_top__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib / gpu_top__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib), and whether OpenROAD needs them registered differently. Compare with the standalone CPU (24.38 mW) and GPU (262 mW) block signoffs, which DO include their own internals - naively summing those against the SoC number is the wrong arithmetic but bounds the gap.

Caveat already documented in docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md 'Caveats' section.
close_reason:
Investigated (no new P&R run, per task scope). Root cause confirmed: the macro
Liberty files (pnr/asap7/{cpu,gpu}/macro/*__nom_tt_025C_0p7V.lib) carry zero
cell_leakage_power/internal_power groups -- only leakage_power_unit (a unit
declaration, unused). They're generated by pnr/scripts/asap7_macro_views.tcl
via OpenSTA's write_timing_model, which has no power-characterization code
path at all (verified against vendored MakeTimingModel.cc source -- zero
power-related code). Macro-lib registration in config.json (EXTRA_LIBS,
nom_tt_025C_0p7V corner) is correct -- not a load/corner-mapping bug.

Independently re-measured via eda-openroad MCP session: loaded run 23's final
ODB with all stdcell/SRAM/macro liberty files, re-ran report_power --
reproduced the archived 51.9134 mW / Macro=0.00W split exactly.

Cannot be fixed inside OpenROAD or this repo's SoC PD flow as-is -- the fix
belongs in a real macro power-characterization step that doesn't exist today.
Filed follow-up bead claude_verilog_test-86a for that.

Docs corrected in PR #156 (branch fix/soc-power-attribution-ew3):
CLAUDE.md + docs/PHASE5_RUN_HISTORY.md now annotate every ASAP7 SoC power
figure as fabric-only, explicitly disclaim the 62.9->51.9 mW run14->run23
drop as a multi-clock efficiency claim (coincides with unrelated USE_ICG_CELL
insertion), and bound the gap against standalone CPU (24.38 mW) / GPU
(262 mW) block sign-offs with an explanation of why summing is wrong
arithmetic.
