title: SPI MISO sampled without 2-FF synchroniser (CDC hygiene)
description:
cdc_snitch (GH #95 gate) reports u_spi.rx_shift_q / u_spi.rx_push_data sampling the board-level asynchronous pin spi_miso_i directly into the fabric domain with no 2-FF synchroniser.

Benign in SPI *master* mode: the SoC generates SCLK, so MISO is sampled a known number of fabric cycles after the driving edge and is stable by construction. It is NOT clean by inspection though, and becomes a real metastability hazard in any future slave-mode or divided-SCLK use.

First reported by the 2026-06-09 cdc_snitch POC (docs/verification/CDC_SNITCH_POC.md:68-76), which recommended filing it. Carried in the GH #95 gate as an explicit kind:accepted-risk waiver (tools/cdc/cdc_config.yml, id spi-miso-unsynchronised-sample) rather than being silently canonicalized away.

Fix: instantiate cdc_2ff_sync on spi_miso_i in rtl/periph/spi_controller.sv, then drop the waiver. spi_controller.sv is Phase-5-verified RTL, so this needs a re-run of the spi suite (13 tests) + soc_all.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-14 (PR pending). rtl/periph/spi_controller.sv now routes spi_miso_i through cdc_2ff_sync #(.WIDTH(1),.STAGES(2)) u_spi_miso_sync; the miso_in mux selects the synchronised bit in non-loopback mode (loopback path untouched). The kind:accepted-risk waiver spi-miso-unsynchronised-sample was DELETED from tools/cdc/cdc_config.yml, so the gate proves the fix rather than tolerating it.

EVIDENCE: CDC gate PASS with 0 unwaived / 71 waived and non-vacuous counts (OK1 17854 / CDC 40 / OKX 330 / BAD 16124 vs the pre-change baseline 17791/39/330/16088 -- the deltas are exactly the new synchroniser's registers). soc_all 183/183 across 26 suites, EXIT=0. Verilator lint 0 errors, warning set byte-identical to baseline.

test_real_miso_mode0 (the only non-loopback MISO test, CLK_DIV_EXT=7) PASSes with rx=0xC3 -- it compares the whole received byte, so an off-by-one bit shift from the 2-cycle sync latency would have corrupted it. Not a pass-for-the-wrong-reason.

KNOWN GAP recorded in the RTL comment, NOT silently retimed: with a REAL external slave, SPI_CLK_DIV==0 (half-period 1 clock) and ==1 (half-period 2 clocks) are no longer safe -- the 2-cycle sync latency meets or exceeds the half-period, so the sampled bit can be stale by a full bit position. No existing test drives a non-loopback slave at those dividers (loopback bypasses the synchroniser entirely at any divider), and the module's own guidance already recommends SPI_CLK_DIV>=7 for external slaves.

ALSO: tb/cocotb/soc/Makefile needed cdc_2ff_sync.sv added to SPI_SOURCES, and -Wno-SYNCASYNCNET on the spi/spi_lint targets -- spi_controller uses synchronous reset while cdc_2ff_sync asserts reset asynchronously, and with spi_controller as the lint ROOT Verilator flags the mix. ~20 SoC-level targets in the same Makefile already carry that flag for the identical pattern; at soc_top scope it raises nothing.

title: sky130A Magic techfile missing layer/datatype maps for OpenRAM SRAM cells (blocks MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true)
description: Found while root-causing 45a. sky130A.tech maps GDS layer 235 only at datatype 4 (-> CELLBOUND), but sky130_fd_bd_sram__openram_dp_cell / _dummy / _replica / _cap_row draw their cell-boundary marker at 235/0. Layers 33 (types 42/43) and 22 (types 21/22) are unmapped entirely. Consequence: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true aborts the whole LibreLane flow with fatal 'Unknown layer/datatype in boundary' (18 errors, 4 distinct cell definitions). Mechanistically relevant beyond the abort: sky130A.tech has a two-tier li1 rule (strict li.3 0.17um for generic locali vs relaxed li.c2 0.14um for coreli), and coreli classification derives from COREID, which is bloated off the same CELLBOUND geometry Magic cannot read at 235/0. NOT the cause of the 27.7M flood (45a proved that: DEF+LEF mode never touches this GDS path and gives an identical count) — this only blocks GDS-mode Magic DRC. LOW PRIORITY: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS is false and staying false; KLayout+Netgen are authoritative for Sky130 sign-off. Only worth fixing if GDS-mode Magic DRC is ever wanted. Fix direction: add 235/0, 33/42, 33/43, 22/21, 22/22 to the cifinput/calma section of sky130A.tech, or source a techfile version matching the PDK SRAM GDS vintage. PDK path: ~/.ciel/ciel/sky130/versions/0fe599b2afb6708d281543108caf8310912f54af/sky130A/libs.tech/magic/sky130A.tech
close_reason: wontfix: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS stays false; KLayout+Netgen authoritative for Sky130 sign-off. Fix direction preserved in the description if GDS-mode Magic DRC is ever wanted.

title: Sky130 CPU Stage-1: Magic DRC reports 27.7M li.3 violations — never passed, likely LEF-abstract artifact
description: Every Sky130 Stage-1 CPU run reports Magic DRC errors: 27733913 — BIT-IDENTICAL between RUN_2026-07-21_18-02-11 and RUN_2026-07-27_05-52-19, so it is systematic and deterministic, not caused by any recent change. KLayout DRC on the same runs is 0 and Netgen LVS says 'Circuits match uniquely', which makes the Magic result the odd one out. The report (*-magic-drc/reports/drc_violations.magic.rpt, 27.7M lines) is dominated by 'Local interconnect spacing < 0.17um (li.3)' with roughly a dozen other rule types present (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b, nwell.4). PRIME SUSPECT: pnr/sky130/cpu/config.json sets MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: false, so Magic runs DRC on the LEF/DEF-derived view where the sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 macro is an abstract black box rather than real GDS geometry — a classic source of spurious li spacing errors at macro boundaries. Worth testing MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS: true on one run to confirm before treating any of these as real. CONSEQUENCE: Stage-1 CPU has never had a genuine Magic DRC sign-off, and that gap is inherited by everything consuming the rv32i_cpu_top macro.
notes: 2026-07-27 HYPOTHESIS REFUTED — RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10 with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true. Magic DRC COUNT = 27,730,498 with REAL GDS vs 27,733,913 with the LEF abstract. Difference 3,415, about 0.01 percent — essentially IDENTICAL. The li.3 violations are NOT a macro-boundary/LEF-abstract artifact; they persist when Magic reads actual geometry. Same rule families in both reports (licon.1, licon.5a, licon.8a, poly.2/4/7/8, psd.10b). So Stage-1 CPU has a real, large, systematic DRC condition that needs its own root-cause, not a reporting artifact. IMPORTANT SCALE CORRECTION from the magic log: '[INFO] COUNT: 27730498' is followed by '[INFO] Should be divided by 3 or 4' — Magic counts each violation 3-4x, so distinct violations are roughly 6.9M-9.2M, still enormous. SECONDARY FINDING, and the reason the config was reverted: MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=true is NOT USABLE on this design. Magic hits fatal 'Unknown layer/datatype in boundary' errors reading the PDK SRAM macro's internal cells (sky130_fd_bd_sram__openram_dp_cell*, layers 235/0, 33/42, 33/43, 22/21, 22/22) and LibreLane aborts the whole flow with 'Encountered one or more fatal errors while running Magic'. The DRC itself completed and wrote its report BEFORE the abort, which is how we got the number. NOT an OOM — RAM went 11G->13G at death, no memory pressure; the magic-drc step ran 42 min (21:37->22:19). Config reverted to false so future CPU runs are not broken. NEXT STEPS if this is picked up: (a) sample actual li.3 coordinates to see whether they cluster inside the SRAM macro footprint or spread across the standard-cell array; (b) check whether the sky130A Magic tech file version matches what the PDK SRAM GDS expects, since the unknown layer/datatype errors suggest a tech-file/GDS mismatch that could also explain spurious li.3; (c) compare against the Sky130 SoC run, which reports only 9081 Magic DRC errors on a LARGER die — that asymmetry is a strong clue and worth explaining.
close_reason: RESOLVED — PDK SRAM macro artifact, WAIVED. Exhaustive streaming classification of all 27,730,498 coordinates in RUN_2026-07-27_20-33-10/63-magic-drc: 27,730,498/27,730,498 = 100.0000% lie inside the 10 sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 footprints; 0 in the routing channel, 0 in the standard-cell logic zone (max y = 907.87um; logic zone starts at 917.5um). All 26 rule families are 100% SRAM-internal — none leak outside; li.3 (922,628) is not even the dominant family (diff/tap.9 3.0M, licon.1 2.6M, li.1 2.3M). Reproduced independently twice with separate awk passes. SoC/CPU asymmetry explained: SoC declares the CPU as a hard MACROS entry with MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS=false, so read_macro_lef loads the LEF abstract and Magic never touches SRAM-internal geometry — its 9,081 errors are a disjoint set (9,049 nwell.4 + 32 met4.4a), the already-documented DEF+LEF-abstract artifact class, not a diluted CPU flood. KLayout=0 on identical GDS because sky130A_mr.drc has explicit hierarchy-aware SRAM_EXCLUDE (select("-*sky130_sram_*kbyte_*") off nsdm/psdm/nwell, grouping the SRAM with I/O pad cells as a pre-verified macro) plus a working areaid:ce two-tier li1 scope — the relief Magic's COREID/coreli attempts but fails to deliver for this OpenRAM macro. Root cause: Magic's flat drc(full) engine cannot validate this dense custom OpenRAM macro's internals, independent of read path. Stage-1 sign-off stands on KLayout DRC=0 + Netgen LVS MATCH + DRT 0. Secondary techfile layer/datatype gap filed as y0w. Full write-up in memory/pd/run_state.md.

title: Sky130 Stage-2: antenna residual 154 pin / 129 net after repair (manufacturability FAILED)
description: After enabling the antenna flow (commit 86e89c1), RUN_2026-07-25_13-29-40 improved antenna from 556 pin / 440 net pre-repair to 154 pin / 129 net post-repair via 2018 inserted diodes (~72% reduction), but manufacturability.rpt still reports 'Antenna: Failed'. Stage-1 CPU achieved ~98% reduction (2849 -> 57 pin) on the same PDK, so ~72% suggests headroom remains. Worth checking: whether Odb.HeuristicDiodeInsertion/Odb.DiodesOnPorts are contributing as expected, whether the residual concentrates on specific nets/layers (e.g. long crossbar routes on the 6700x3100 um die), and whether a second repair pass or GRT/DRT parameter change helps. Confirmed DRC-safe: the 2018 diodes introduced ZERO new KLayout violations (still exactly 4, same rules/cells) and Magic DRC unchanged at 9081.
notes:
2026-07-31 RUN 5 (RUN_2026-07-31_05-13-54, HEURISTIC_ANTENNA_THRESHOLD=800) — VOLUME MODEL FALSIFIED. FINAL MECHANISM ESTABLISHED.

Cell count landed almost exactly as predicted (234,371 vs ~234k) but latency did NOT follow: 1.381585 ns, essentially identical to the 44k-diode runs, not the predicted 0.93-1.0. Hold failed at the same 5 corners (nom_tt -0.1623, nom_ss -0.1748, max_tt -0.4093, max_ss -0.5278, max_ff -0.0914). Antenna post-DRT 90/84, routing DRC 0, LVS PASSED.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — latency is BINARY on whether Odb.HeuristicDiodeInsertion runs at all:
    run        heuristic  stdcells   clk_i->u_cpu/clk_i   hold
    baseline      off     226,454        0.870159        clean 9
    run 3         off     226,952        0.933178        clean 9
    run 5         ON      234,371        1.381585        fails 5
    run 4         ON      270,217        1.410208        fails 5
    run 2         ON      272,003        1.388234        fails 5
    run 1         ON      271,858        1.439363        fails 5
Among the ON runs cell count spans 234k-272k (38k spread) with no material latency effect (1.38-1.44). Off: 0.87-0.93. Cell VOLUME is not the variable; the step RUNNING is.

WHY: the step wraps 1-odb-fuzzydiodeplacement -> 2-openroad-detailedplacement -> 3-openroad-globalrouting. It re-legalizes placement and re-routes globally after insertion. That perturbation costs ~0.45-0.5 ns at the clock root regardless of whether it inserted 7,970 or 44,742 diodes. Verified: both run 4 and run 5 show the same three sub-steps.

CONSEQUENCE — the trade-off is binary and NOT tunable. Three levers all failed for the same reason (they reduce WHAT is inserted; the cost comes from the pass RUNNING): DIODE_ON_PORTS off (run 2, no effect); clock-net exclusion patch (run 4, zero clock diodes, no effect); threshold 800 / 5.6x fewer diodes (run 5, no effect).

FOUR WRONG ROOT CAUSES over this campaign, each caught ONLY by the falsification guard and never by a run going green: (1) my cell-count hypothesis, retracted then wrongly re-adopted at run 4; (2) agent's DIODE_ON_PORTS; (3) agent's clock-tree diodes; (4) my volume model. Keep a falsifiable guard on any future claim on this bead.

FINAL POSITION:
    config   antenna    hold          LVS   routing DRC
    run 3    140/120    clean 9       PASS      0
    run 5     90/84     fails 5       PASS      0
    run 4     40/39     fails 5       PASS      0
DECISION (user, 2026-07-31): adopt RUN 3 (RUN_2026-07-30_06-42-17) as the Stage-2 result — hold clean at all 9 corners, LVS MATCH, routing DRC 0, PDN 0, 44.1 mW, 37.9% util. Antenna 140/120 documented as a quantified residual alongside the KLayout-4 and Magic-9081 waivers. Config = RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION false, GRT_ANTENNA_ITERS=8, GRT_ANTENNA_MARGIN=25, CLOCK_PERIOD=25.0, TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS=['*'].
UNTRIED LEVER, recorded not pursued: GRT-based repair does NOT trigger the legalization sub-steps, so pushing GRT_ANTENNA_ITERS/MARGIN harder on run 3's config could improve antenna without the hold cost. Run 3 already used 8/25 giving 140/120, so gains are likely incremental.
close_reason: Adopted run 3 (RUN_2026-07-30_06-42-17) as the Stage-2 result; antenna 140/120 accepted as a quantified residual. Six-run campaign established the trade-off is BINARY and not tunable: Odb.HeuristicDiodeInsertion cuts antenna to 40-90 but costs ~0.5 ns of clock-root latency and breaks hold at 5/9 corners, because the step re-legalizes placement and re-routes globally (fuzzydiodeplacement -> detailedplacement -> globalrouting) regardless of how many diodes it inserts. Latency is binary on whether the step runs: off = 0.87-0.93 ns, on = 1.38-1.44 ns across a 234k-272k cell-count spread. Three tuning levers all failed identically (DIODE_ON_PORTS none; clock-net exclusion patch achieving zero CLOCK-sigtype diodes; threshold 800 giving 5.6x fewer diodes) because each reduces WHAT is inserted, not whether the pass runs. Run 3 final: LVS PASSED, routing DRC 0, PDN 0, hold 0 at all 9 corners, antenna 140/120, KLayout 4 + Magic 9081 (settled waivers), 44.1 mW, 37.9% util. Untried lever recorded not pursued: GRT repair does not trigger the legalization sub-steps, so pushing GRT_ANTENNA_ITERS/MARGIN beyond 8/25 could improve antenna without the hold cost (expect incremental — 8/25 already gave 140/120). Full evidence in memory/pd/knowledge.md; LibreLane clock-net patch retained at memory/pd/patches/ (harmless, default-off elsewhere).

title: GH #123: CPU macro clk->Q on AXI outputs 4.55ns @nom_tt -- Stage-1 output budget far too loose
description: CORRECTED 2026-07-25 (original premise was wrong). pnr/sky130/cpu/constraints/sky130_cpu.sdc DOES budget I/O: 28 set_input_delay + 38 set_output_delay lines, 2.0ns max each side on the AXI ports. Real root cause is that the budget is TOO LOOSE: set_output_delay -max 2.0 against a 13.333ns period lets the macro take up to 11.33ns to produce an output; it takes 4.55ns @nom_tt (7.54 @nom_ss, 8.12 @max_ss) so the optimizer had zero pressure to do better. 4.55ns clk->Q at the TYPICAL corner is ~30% of the period gone before the signal leaves the macro. Second independent cause: rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585 early-accept makes arready a combinational function of araddr via decode() + priority arbitration (the 7-gate fabric cone in the worst path). FIX: raise set_output_delay/set_input_delay on AXI ports so the macro must drive outputs in ~4-5ns, re-run librelane-sky130-cpu, confirm it still closes at 13.333ns and clk->Q drops, re-stage 9 corner libs + LEF/GDS, re-run Stage-2 at 75MHz. Only if insufficient, consider registering crossbar arready (costs 1 cycle/read, needs decision + full re-verification).
notes: GitHub issue #123. NEGATIVE RESULT 2026-07-25: budget tightening CANNOT recover 75MHz. Tried 2.0->8.0ns on AXI ports (RUN_2026-07-25_19-30-52): Stage-1 failed to close, setup WNS -2.950 on apb_prdata_o[13] (APB budget untouched -- the AXI tightening ate design-wide optimizer headroom), 4826 hold-violating endpoints. Reboot killed it at 19:48 but it had already failed. MATH: need 2.052ns; have 0.241 slack; must recover 1.811ns from macro; requires clk->Q 4.545->2.734ns (40% cut) = 10.6ns budget, MORE aggressive than the 8.0 that failed. No viable value exists. SDC REVERTED to 2.0ns. REAL TARGET: crossbar fabric = 8.83ns of the nom_tt path (20 driver stages) vs macro 4.55ns -- the araddr->decode->arbitration->arready early-accept cone at rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585. Options now: (1) register crossbar arready, costs 1 cycle/read + full re-verif; (2) pipeline decode; (3) accept 65MHz. Design decision, not PD tuning.
close_reason: Accepted 65 MHz (user decision 2026-07-25). Budget tightening proven a dead end: 8.0ns failed to close (WNS -2.950, 4826 hold endpoints); 75MHz would need 10.6ns, more aggressive still. SDC reverted to 2.0ns. Real target is the crossbar early-accept cone (fabric 8.83ns vs macro 4.55ns on the nom_tt path, rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:580-585) but both fixes trade read latency against verified RTL and Sky130 caps this topology at ~100-120MHz anyway. Remaining Stage-2 gaps (nom_tt hold -0.0923, antenna 154/129, SRAM single-corner) are worth more than 10MHz. Re-open trigger: a real >65MHz Sky130 requirement.

title: GH #120: SPICE-characterize sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff corners (CPU macro DONE)
description:
SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-01: this issue is now SRAM-ONLY. The CPU macro half of the original description is obsolete -- see 'Historical' at the end.

The SoC's SRAM hard macro sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 (OpenRAM compile) provides only a single characterized Liberty view: TT_1p8V_25C. pnr/sky130/soc/config.json's MACROS entry deliberately maps that one .lib to every PVT corner via a wildcard ("lib": {"*": [...]}), so the macro's internal timing arcs are IDENTICAL in all nine reported corners. Only sky130_fd_sc_hd standard cells, and the CPU macro, genuinely vary by corner in this flow.

Consequence (bidirectional -- and note the direction was guessed WRONG once already, see below):
- nom_tt results are valid: the one corner where this macro's characterization matches the analysis label.
- ss/ff results on paths touching the SRAM macro boundary carry macro-model error of UNKNOWN SIGN. Do not assume it is conservative. When the CPU macro was given genuine per-corner libs on 2026-07-25, the earlier reasoning that ss HOLD was 'pessimistic and plausibly fine in real silicon' proved wrong: max_ss hold went -0.0708 -> -0.3997 ns and nom_tt hold went from MET to VIOLATING. The wildcard was optimistic in BOTH directions, not offsetting.
- Therefore Sky130 SoC Stage-2 timing is a TYPICAL-CORNER (nom_tt) SIGN-OFF, not a validated multi-corner one, despite reporting numbers under ss/ff corner labels. The physical gates (Netgen LVS PASSED, routing DRC 0, PDN 0, KLayout DRC 4 waived) are NOT affected by this and stand as real results.

This macro is the SOLE remaining source of that limitation.

Fix (the only remaining one): characterize sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 at ss/ff for real. OpenRAM supports multi-corner characterization natively (process_corners / supply_voltages / temperatures, nominal_corner_only=False); our compile used nominal_corner_only=True for speed during the views-first pass. Doing it properly needs SPICE-based characterization per corner -- NOT the analytical mode, which is separately known-broken for power (it emitted internal_power ~1.99e11 mW, currently hand-zeroed in the staged .lib).

STATUS: DEFERRED host-blocked. See the feasibility verdict in NOTES -- ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h total, measured from Xyce's own progress meter, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h. Not a tuning problem; no amount of PD iteration substitutes for it. Bead ujv (Stage-2 ss setup failure) is deferred for the same underlying reason and cannot be honestly closed before this one is.

Keep the two documented hand-patches on the TT lib (zeroed internal_power; max_transition 0.04 -> 0.5, required because 40 ps is unachievable in sky130_fd_sc_hd and OpenROAD hard-aborts with RSZ-0090). Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days, or with a genuinely reduced characterization netlist.

Related: separate from claude_verilog_test-0jp (the 4 KLayout DRC violations, closed won't-fix), though both stem from the same views-first macro-compile pattern.

--- Historical (superseded 2026-07-25, retained for provenance) ---
The original description asserted that BOTH hard macros (rv32i_cpu_top and the SRAM) had only a single nom_tt Liberty view, and prescribed re-running the Stage-1 CPU characterization flow as part of the fix. That is no longer true. rv32i_cpu_top was fixed on 2026-07-25: config.json now maps 9 exact corner keys to 9 genuinely distinct per-corner Liberty views in pnr/sky130/cpu/macro/, verified from each corner's own sta.log. Those views had in fact always existed -- Stage-1's OpenROAD.STAPostPNR wrote all nine; only nom_tt had ever been staged into the SoC config, which then wildcarded it across every corner.
notes:
2026-07-27 FEASIBILITY VERDICT: NOT FEASIBLE on this host, measured not estimated. Xyce's own progress meter in temp_charretry/spice_stdout.log: 'Percent complete: 17.0783 %' at 05:37:07 with 'Estimated time to completion: 52 min., 33 sec.' => ONE delay simulation ~63 minutes. OpenRAM does NOT run one simulation per corner: delay.py find_feasible_period_one_port is a period-doubling loop capped at 9 iterations (time_out=9), then find_min_period_one_port runs a BINARY SEARCH, repeated per read port -- this macro has 2 read ports (1RW+1R). That is roughly 25-30 full simulations per corner = ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h for the 3 corners, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h and where tmux does not survive. The netlist-only sram_char.py path (which removed the 3.7 h routing per attempt) does not help: the cost is the SPICE search itself. Note sram_char.py forces trim_netlist=False, and the 'trimmed.sp' from the generation run is 4.30 MB vs the full 4.17 MB sram.sp -- trimming is not meaningfully shrinking this 32768-bit array, so there is no easy speedup there. The 05:17 run also died at 17% for an unexplained reason (no kernel OOM in journalctl -k, no systemd-oomd entry, no Python traceback, timing.raw had reached 1.0 GB); that is unresolved but MOOT -- even a clean run cannot fit the search into this host's uptime. RECOMMENDATION: keep both documented hand-patches on the TT lib (zeroed internal_power, max_transition 0.04->0.5), leave the macro analytical + single-corner, and pursue bead 0ro instead. Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days or with a genuinely trimmed/reduced characterization netlist.
2026-08-13 DEFERRED (host-blocked). ~26-31 h/corner, ~80-95 h total of Xyce SPICE measured from Xyce's own progress meter, against a host that reboots every 2-8 h. Not a tuning problem. Revisit only with a machine that stays up ~4 days or a genuinely reduced characterization netlist. Blocks ujv.

title: Phase 5 follow-up: EQY/LEC sv2v output vs source RTL
description: M11 SoC synth uses sv2v-converted Verilog (Synlig can't synth the SoC SV). Correctness rests on soc_all 82/82 vs original RTL; no formal equivalence between sv2v output and source. Add Yosys EQY (or equivalent LEC) sv2v-vs-RTL for tape-out rigor. Non-blocking for indicative ASAP7 signoff.
notes:
2026-09-09 MATERIAL CHANGE — LibreLane 3.0.14 REPLACES SYNLIG WITH SLANG. Re-scope this bead
before acting on the drafted upstream report.

Found while doing the OpenROAD/LibreLane migration for bead ocm. LibreLane 3.0.14
(librelane/steps/pyosys.py:129-133) defines:
  USE_SLANG, bool, default False, deprecated_names=["USE_SYNLIG"]
  "Use the Slang frontend to process files, which has better SystemVerilog parsing
   capabilities but is not as battle-tested as the default Yosys friend."
plus SLANG_ARGUMENTS. Loading this repo's ASAP7 CPU config under 3.0.14 emits:
  WARNING 'SYNLIG_DEFER' has been removed: Synlig replaced with Slang.
So the Synlig frontend this bead's findings are ALL about does not exist in the version we are
migrating to.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS BEAD. This project's entire sv2v detour exists because Synlig
could not synthesise soc_top (CLAUDE.md M11: "sv2v frontend -- Synlig can't synth this SoC").
That detour is the ONLY reason this bead exists at all: the M11/M12 sign-off rests on
sv2v-converted Verilog with no formal equivalence to the source RTL. If Slang parses soc_top
natively, the sv2v step disappears and with it the entire sv2v-vs-RTL equivalence gap -- this
bead would close by removal of the problem rather than by proving equivalence.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DRAFTED UPSTREAM ISSUE (scratchpad synlig_issue_draft.md, still NOT
posted, still needs the user's go-ahead):
 * The unpacked-array-PARAMETER silent-garbage defect (Cause B) is a real Surelog/Synlig bug
   and reporting it upstream is still valid and still useful to the Synlig project -- but it
   is no longer on THIS project's critical path if we move to 3.0.14/Slang.
 * Its stated impact ("blocks 6 modules transitively in our EQY harness") would become
   historical rather than current. The draft should say so rather than overstate live impact.
 * Priority for us drops accordingly. Reporting it remains a good-citizen action, not a
   dependency.

CONCRETE NEXT STEP, NOT YET RUN: test whether Slang parses soc_top. Set USE_SLANG=true in a
3.0.14 config whose VERILOG_FILES point at the SystemVerilog sources (NOT soc_top_sv2v.v) and
run to Yosys.JsonHeader / Yosys.Synthesis. Cheap, and decisive for whether the sv2v frontend
can be retired. Note SYNTH_HIERARCHY_MODE's docs warn that with the Slang plugin you must pass
'--keep-hierarchy' via SLANG_ARGUMENTS separately if you want hierarchy preserved.
NOT attempted yet only because the LibreLane 3.0.14 worktree (/nobackup/librelane-3.0.14) is
currently in use by the PD orchestrator working bead ocm -- avoid concurrent use.

Also still outstanding from the earlier note: the exact Synlig/Surelog/Yosys versions for the
draft could not be extracted (neither `strings` on the .so nor `nix derivation show` yielded a
clean rev). If the draft is ever posted, that field still needs filling.
close_reason: Closed with bounded evidence on record (user-directed close-out, 2026-09-14). The question this bead exists for -- is the sv2v netlist that PnR consumes equivalent to the source RTL -- is answered to the depth this 15.9 GB host allows, with nothing disproven anywhere. Gold is the source RTL read by yosys-slang (an independent frontend), gate is the regenerated soc_top_sv2v.v. STRICT LRM: the SoC now elaborates with no --allow-use-before-declare / --compat vcs (PR #171: soc_top.sv IRQ declaration order; __pnr__ shim parameter string types), soc_all 183/183. FLAT soc_top: 64209 / 64433 equivalence points proven (99.65%), 0 disproven; depth host-capped at equiv_induct -seq 5 (seq 7/10/20 all die at ~12.57 GB). PER MODULE (tools/verif/equiv_sv2v_module.sh, strict, fresh netlist): 25 of 27 modules PROVEN outright at seq-20 induction, incl. axi4_crossbar, soc_bus, async_axi_fifo, boot_rom, pll_clkgen; sram_controller PROVEN at MEM_WORDS=16 (full size unaffordable; sv2v keeps the parameter, override verified on both sides). RESIDUE, bounded evidence only: pmu -- 39 FSM-output points induction-unproven, 40-cycle post-reset bounded miter PASS (39 post-reset cycles, enough for a full power-down/up through both domains); dma_engine -- 128 points (src_q/dst_q/words_rem_q/m_araddr) unproven even at seq-20 induction, 8-cycle bounded miters PASS from zero state and post-reset; 12- and 20-cycle miters time out. The residue is NOT depth-starved: seq-20 induction ran to completion on dma_engine without proving it, consistent with sv2v's struct->bit-slice and dropped-width-cast rewrites being equivalent only over reachable states. One PMU counterexample was a pre-reset first-cycle artefact (identical outputs for all post-reset cycles); the tool's BMC mode now asserts reset at step 1 and skips that step. Not pursued, by judgement: an invariant-constrained induction on dma_engine's descriptor queue -- high cost, and nothing points at a real mismatch. Reopen if a sv2v upgrade or an RTL change touches dma_engine or pmu.
